This is a tune I started while staying in an Airstream trailer in the woods of central California, channeling my inner Bon Iver. I spent 5 days out there making music and hiking all day. Drank a lot of instant coffee as well.

I recorded probably 30 demos in that trailer and I've been chipping away at them ever since. Whenever I get stuck or at a loss for new ideas, I crack open one of those projects and I can still feel the palpable sense of inspiration I had on that trip. 

The core foundation of this song is a sample of an old song my friend and I made about 10 years ago. I used some granular synthesis to make a bed from that old track, then structured a new song around the sample. As I often do I recorded my voice then mangled it up to make some emotive vocal chops. 

I'm hoping this one takes you on a nice little mental trip -- you deserve it ✨

Welcome to Eternal Garden.

Eternal Garden follows the story of Caius, an angel cast out of heaven by the goddess Flora, tasked with a mission to terraform a now desolate and uninhabitable earth. Though his mission was successful, he broke the singular rule necessary for an angel’s survival. Caius falls in love with an earthly being, later revealed to be a centuries old shapeshifter, and falls into a deep slumber. Locked in a daydream, he relives the memories of a thousand men, unlocking the secrets of the human condition as he experiences love, heartbreak, and resentment over and over again. He awakens to a world on fire and stripped of his angelic blessing. To reclaim his power and fulfill his promise, Caius embarks on a treacherous journey to the Eternal Garden - a portal between Heaven and Earth, and the source of their vitality. 

7 Songs, 7 Visuals, 7 Forbidden Fruits, 700 Editions.

Read more at: www.eternal-garden.xyz

Eternal Garden was written, produced, and performed by TK. Featuring additional production by Aidan Graven & Brett White, and additional vocals by Refi.

"Just Off In Our Own World" - Produced By Dutchyyy

As someone who grew up & started their music career in the mid 90's (Golden Era / Boom Bap HipHop) I've had a large portion of my long term supporters as well as new listeners stumbling on my earlier works who adore and wish I would keep creating music of the same style from those early years. This pertains to Beats (Dutchyyy) & (Rhymes) 

I went into detail about this in much greater context recently, which if you care to understand you should read thru all the descriptions and backstories here:

+ https://beta.catalog.works/dutchmassive
+ https://beta.catalog.works/dutchyyy  

Reality is, from the very beginning I've always been making music that didn't fit into any specific genre since I don't just listen or draw inspiration from a single genre.  While most of my music is rooted in the fundamentals of traditional hip hop / beat making.  I've always gravitated towards creating instrumentals that can speak for me, that aren't meant for people to put vocals over. Just genuine self expression minus the pressures of how that art will be received by others.

This external pressure reached an all time high 2012-2014 with supporters getting frustrated I wasn't releasing new music rapping, and even more so that the Instrumentals I were releasing, weren't your typical hip hop beats (sidenote: funny years later my style would become a whole genre, branded "Lofi-HipHop")  

After moving from Los Angeles, back to Tampa Bay and then Immediately to NY in 2014, I reunited with my pops after over a decade of having no communication.  

You can read more about this Arc of my life here:

https://medium.com/@SolarSounds/shawangunk-stomp-the-story-of-dutchyyys-uproot-4235a4eb66ff

Long Story Short,

My Pop's saw the pressure fans were putting on me and how I was torn between trying to please strangers and wanting to escape the boxes I was always being shoved in and told me that since I was a child, I always marched to the beat of my own drum and never cared what anyone else thought, a trait I inherited from both of Parents as we are all a tad "out there" he told me to ignore all the outside noise and let go, Because the view is better and much more rewarding when truly existing "Off In Our Own World"

My name is Toha and this is the story behind my solo genesis, ‘Relics’

This track was birthed a few months back when TK the Legend and Kits.IO released The Eternal Garden Master Collection sample pack. https://www.kits.io/packs/eternal-garden-master-collection

I started browsing it and the loop featured in his song ‘Pain’ instantly grabbed my attention. I let my Intuition guide the writing process and before I knew it, I had a finished track on my hands. 

At the time I was meditating on relics.
Relics can be categorized as souvenirs with deep historical or personal value- often creating feelings of nostalgia or a reminder of experiences lost to the hands of time. Relics can also hold spiritual power and be used as a tool to strengthen or protect the holder.

The artwork features Suyat, an ancient writing script from the Philippines. Historically it was written on leaves and wood, but also carved into artifacts like pottery or jewelry. Using this script alongside the artwork is my way of re-imagining the relic as something that can live on-chain forever. Learning to write Suyat empowers me and I hope to share that feeling through the song and artwork.

My vision for this release is to inspire new people to have fun participating in a Sound.xyz drop

All collectors will be airdropped an animated version of the cover art (via L2) (Golden Egg will also have its own special animation)

All collectors additionally can reach out to me directly and have their name written in Suyat 📝

I've also created a physical relic- a framed mixed-media version of the cover art. It will be rewarded to whoever has the most referrals/or videos using the song at the end of the mint period. 

Let’s share this moment together. 'Relics' is a seed for the future, and I’m grateful for your participation 💎

Description:
So after working with a publishing label that was treating me like I was a slave, I got stuck in form and this idea that songwriting has to be one way, I took some time to heal because I really couldn’t write for months. To help, I decided to ride my bike to clear my head, and one day I envisioned myself rapping a verse on the L.A. River. And that’s how “Joyride” came to life. 

“Joyride” is an evolving practice of free verses that are straight to it. No form, just me and me philosophies in bars. It’s a meditation, it’s short bits of me, it’s whatever you want to make it. An opportunity to just allow myself to ride the beat. To create these verses, I would start with a beat I love, rap on it and then send the accapella to Kaui to create something new out of it.

“Culture”, this first offering/verse off of “Joyride” came to me after rapping on Kaytranada’s production. I wrote the verse in a nite and immediately knew I didn’t want to add much else to it. I am very lyrical and I am realizing, sometimes one verse is enough. Sometimes keeping it simple is all you need. Sometimes just riding your own path is what I have to do. 

So this year as I’m riding my path, I guess I’m using this “Joyride” as an exercise in getting back to me, getting out of my way, sticking to my journey, continuing to create with bro Kaui who has been working with me for years, I’m really excited for how this ride will take me to more paths.  Next up “Showtime”

One of the toughest questions I’ve been asked in therapy was:

“How do you need people to show up for you?”

There have only been very few moments in my life where I’ve been lost for words and that probably lands in one of the top 3 moments. I truly did not have all the answers. I named a few things that I thought were “reasonable” and / or essential but my therapist pressed in more and said, “I didn’t ask what you thought was acceptable. I asked how you want people to show up for you.”

Prior to therapy, I was aware of some unhealthy habits I had picked up from my mother. I watched my mother on multiple occasions do so much for our family, so much for me growing up and so much for her friends that she would empty her cup at the drop a dime for people and not expect her cup to be filled in return by them. She did it out of pure love for people. 

But that caused her to be exhausted when she didn’t have to be. Sometimes too exhausted to do for herself in a personal way. 

In my course of healing and growing and raising the standard of what I expect from my friends, I remember getting into an argument with my wife about what I needed from her as one of my best friends. I remember telling her “I just don’t desire it…I need that from you.” 

Who knew that some self-discovery and an argument could give me all I needed to write this new record that I’m sure will encourage people to express what they need from their tribe.

Description:
For my genesis Sound drop it was important to stay true to the essence. I could’ve gone with another style of music but it was key for me to make history by sticking to the roots. When I first got into crypto in 2017, I noticed that the majority of the artists involved were in electronic music, a culture I was also a part of but I knew it would be an uphill battle to get Reggaeton recognition in the space. Fast-forward a few years and I accomplished everything I set out too in crypto/web3. (so far)

I made this song late 2021, I was on a hot streak knocking down about 3 records a night and “SOLTERA” was born. I needed a dope Reggaeton for the INFINXTE album and this was the one. The track is produced by two of my closest friends, Los Hitmen, a grammy-nominated production duo that have worked with heavyweights like J Balvin, Jay Wheeler, and De La Ghetto. I remember as soon as I sent the track I got a call back right away like “WTF DID YOU DO HERE?!” I knew right then we had a hit. 

The original artwork was crafted by one of my favorite artists from Spain, Diego (Paranoidme). I think one of the most exciting parts of my album is the diversity in collaborators, its completely organic and features artists from more than ten countries. Reggaeton was rejected in the mainstream for years and now its the voice of the youth all over Latin America, the Caribbean and people all over the world. Reggaeton pushes culture forward and I want to push it forward into web3.
Ol' BK Soul (Official Video) LATASHA ft. Radamiz

22 years ago, I was on tour in Japan and in one of my favorite record stores in Tokyo crate digging. I struck up conversation with another crate digger who turned out to be Kabuki - and that started a whole new world of possibility. Pretty much on the spot, Kabuki asked me if I'd be interested in collaborating on a project and less than a year later I was in Germany in studio with him and his Megashira production partner Mainframe writing and recording their next album ('At Last'). Two whole decades later, we've reconnected with each other thanks to our shared passion for web3 - the power of blockchain!

This remix came into existence thanks to our first Mashibeats community remix contest, with finalists being chosen by our discord community and winners decided by $BUYBACK holders. Kabuki's remix was one of my personal favorites but didn't end up being in the final 4. Those 4 were minted as 1/1s on Catalog and now, today, we're celebrating the release of the remixes on vinyl (!) and very limited digital (no DSPs) with bonus tracks including this remix. To celebrate the vinyl release, Kabuki and I decided to share his amazing remix with the world via this Sound drop. 

The original of this track (a future drop?!) was my creative reaction to the summer of 2020 when we were in full lockdown, BLM was top of mind for the whole planet, which raised the perspective of [joy] as an act of [resistance] and how that sounds in my imagination. I'll leave it to Kabuki to tell us more about his remix:

"... when I heard "Joyful Resistance Part I" for the first time I fell in love with the chord progression: shades of modal Herbie and "Extensions"-era McCoy Tyner conjured a magical mood. I had to figure out how Mark did this! Once I worked out the harmonies I wrote an "answer" to Mark’s phrase, starting a musical conversation between the original and remix versions. 808 drums programmed in a jazz waltz pattern and my trademark ARP2600 synth bass provide the necessary contrast. Music that transcends all styles and traditions..." - Kabuki

zone out to the vibes with us... Joyful Resistance Part I remixed by Kabuki!

The celestial theme in her music evokes a sense of wonder and inspiration, encouraging listeners to reach for the stars and pursue their own goals without limits.

Bela - 
A trip with friends will always be revealing. This song was born while I was on San Andrés island which is an island off the coast of Colombia known for its deep blue waters, warm weather and rich musical culture. This trip was about an escape, to get away from my thoughts and the people who appeared along the way made this trip something wonderful.

Xcelencia - 
I first learned about Bela promoting on Twitter which lead me to her OpenSea. As I went through her collection I noticed the versatility and knew right away she was a songwriter at heart. That definitely drew my attention since I worked on the publishing side of music for several years helping writers and producers. I collected one of the songs in the collection making it the first music NFT I purchased to support other Latin artists in the space.

We were talking about collaborating for some time and ISLA was the perfect song to start with. The Afrobeats inspired soundscape and the Rhodes driven chord progression set the tone for the song. This is one of those records where I effortlessly did my thing inspired by her writing and the production. This is the remix. 

🌴

Being a producer who has been grinding, collaborating, creating beat videos, and promoting myself as a producer first .. I thought it was time to show the world what else I have in the tool box. I believe as artists we all go through a period of self doubt and for me It was time to put that to the side! These songs that have been living in my hardrive for quite some time now just had to be released. 

So for my first drop in a year, this is SWIMMING. A record that was recorded just by freestyling in my basement as I had just made the beat a few hours prior. It slowly started to develop into what I had been feeling the last few years. In ways that many people can relate to. When life takes you on an unexpected path or some things just ain't going the way you expected it ... ya just keep swimming.

Description: We’re joined by Iman Europe to discuss her new project moneymorphosis released in collaboration with LNRZ.

The stories that we tell ourselves determine our self-image, which determines how we move through each day. NOT4ME is about recognizing and releasing the habits, patterns and stories in life that hurt us more than they contribute to our healing.

NOT4ME has been an affirmation for me throughout the 6 months since I wrote it - it is the story that I told myself to reclaim my identity and learn how to love myself despite persistent feelings of guilt and shame. Releasing these negative feelings allowed me to better show up for myself, re-center creativity and welcome healthier habits into my life.

This song is more relevant to me now than ever. It has made me more discerning of what supports my growth and what is simply…not for me 🤷🏽‍♂️

I hope NOT4ME supports your journey in some way.

I hope it makes you smile.

I hope it makes you dance.

❤️‍🔥

Lots of things changed for me in 2022.

I moved to Brooklyn, switched careers, ended a long-term relationship, quit weed, traveled everywhere from Paris to Bogotá, moved OUT of Brooklyn, released my debut single and genesis music NFTs...you get the point.

In the midst of all of this I have attempted to become more discerning in my day to day life. Every day brings new decisions. How will I show up for myself? Which relationships will I prioritize? Which habits will I direct my time and energy to?

Released on the cutting-edge Sound.xyz web 3 blockchain, this track not only represents the avant-garde spirit of A&TJJB but also marks a pivotal moment in the intersection of technology and independent music.

"Strange People" is a sonic journey that encapsulates the collaborative brilliance of pianist, composer, and producer Aron Ottignon and Senegalese Griot Bakane Seck, the mastermind behind the sabar percussion. This groundbreaking fusion marries Mbalax, Afrobeat, Afrofunk, and Jazz, creating a genre-defying tapestry that resonates with both modernity and timelessness. Drawing inspiration from Ottignon's background in jazz and Seck's Senegalese roots, the track is a unique blend of traditional sounds and contemporary production techniques.

As the rights holder and label manager, you play a pivotal role in steering the narrative of A&TJJB's musical journey. The decision to release "Strange People" on the Sound.xyz web 3 blockchain is a visionary move, aligning with the ethos of Urban Trout Records, the independent label that champions innovative sounds and supports artists pushing the envelope. This release not only serves as a sonic experience but also establishes a deeper connection with the community, ushering in a new era of transparency and collaboration in the music industry.

A&TJJB's independence shines through in this release, as they take full ownership of their artistic expression. About "Nostalgia"

This piano piece arose from a few bars improvisation. I revisited this idea four years later and varied a little around it. Finally, in 2021, I completed the piece, which was then published in 2022. 

In finding a suitable title for this track and listening to it after a few days of absence, I realised it exuded nostalgic feel. The cover art aims to represent this nostalgic approach.
I remembered a silhouette of my profile created by a street paper cut artist in my childhood and felt this form of art would be a fitting choice. After familiarising myself with how to create paper cut art using a program for illustrations, I came up with a somewhat humorous take on the composition process -with me as the model. 

Adding a "paper cut like" artwork, the nostalgic thoughts about a childhood memory, and, of course, the vibe of the composition together was the final step for ´Nostalgia´.

Description:
SRA stands for “Source Recordings Augmentations”, product of the experimentation with audio that has been reshaped many times. It embraces Blockchain technology in the form of NFTs, setting a new standard in the way G89 Records releases music. By leveraging this approach, we can offer true digital ownership, ensure fair compensation for our artists, and streamline revenue distribution through smart contracts. NFTs also provide a unique way for fans to support our art, while reducing reliance on middlemen, increasing transparency. We believe this shift marks the next logical step in the evolution of the music and arts ecosystem, benefiting considerably all parties involved.

--

Recorded and mixed by William Jourdain (Quebec, Canada)
Mastered by J. David Lucio S. at G89 Records Studios (Santiago, Chile)
Cover artwork by William Jourdain (Quebec, Canada)
Released by G89 Records (Santiago, Chile)
Cat# G89R016

--

About:

William Jourdain, also known under the moniker of Automatisme, began his music project in 2011 and since then has been publishing on various labels, such as Constellation, Mille Plateaux, and Outlines, while simultaneously being active as an art historian and curator. His generative ambient dub techno music is continually reshaped in the studio. This album is a compilation of post-produced sound archives, including stems, presets, and templates dating from 2011 to the present day.

The track combines offbeat rhythms and trap sound elements with live rap vocals, alongside a strong lyrical male vocal. The layered atmosphere, built from synths, pads, textures, and soundscapes, gives the song a dark yet high energy downtempo feel.

As a producer, I enjoy exploring different music genres I’m passionate about, without sticking to just one. I believe this journey keeps me dynamic and always evolving as an artist. I hope when you listen, you can feel the energy I poured into creating it and share that same vibe with me.

Description:
In April of 2020, separated by an ocean and 3000 miles, both of us went into self-isolation. Physically, of course -- like everyone else. But also musically.

Turning inwards, we scoured the Refs instrumental vault for our most menacing, introverted and brooding soundscapes -- and proceeded to write 12 songs in 12 days. Years later, we offer up our debut album, "New Religion".			

Set over a static, anxiety-ridden percussive backdrop, "Running My Mouth" is an expression of a repressed alter ego within.

The animated image we chose for artwork is a taste of an unreleased "New-Religion" themed collectable project. Owners of this NFTs will get advanced access and a sneak peak of what's to come.

-Dessauer and Rich

What if you could meet your past or future self across space and time. What might you advise, observe, affirm, or say to yourself ?

One truth I would reveal to my past self is: 
you will use your voice and your journal entries will become poems, stories will become speeches, and songs will spring forth into the world to become your legacy. 

“Infinite” is a dance between my past, present, and future self. If we see more limitlessly we find that time is in fact not short, time is abundant as well, life is the longest dance we will ever know.   

The world is what it is, for better or worse because people shaped it so, that being said, I believe we are in an everlasting cycle of co-creation with the universe. “Infinite” asks us to get on the dancefloor ( a metaphor for life) and tap in with self and one another to create the world we want to live in and leave behind for future  generations. 

Art imitates life and life imitates art. Dreams are sacred and I believe we don’t quit until we’ve lived each one. 

Produced by New Orleans royalty, Ciara Porter( granddaughter of George Porter Jr. , The Meters) , recorded at House of Corperning with her partner, Charles aka Winowilly ( from Philly) and mixed & mastered by Future Surf  Labs founder Cam Murdoch, the song is made up of bars, bounce, melodic house poly-rhythms, and soulful dance breaks. 

Everyday I reaffirm to present self that I am surrounded by supportive community, I can step out of my way and let the blessings flow into my life. 
Breathe now look up, look within, and look how far we’ve come. 

If I met my future self, I would encourage her to  continue to enjoy the fruits of her labor and to keep finding ways to honor all the people she has encountered along the way, they have  all mattered.

I am inspired daily and have so much love for so many of you in ways that don’t even belong to me🙏🏾

Infinite gratitude,

✨Charm

Overly caffeinated and full of road rage, she walked into a room filled with 4 strangers she would later discover were the greatest musicians she’d ever worked with. They each stood there and sat there, instrument in hand, ready to explain the day’s plan starting with NFT meets music 101. “Not Fucking Trying” she thought as they continued talking about block chains and ethereums. Then, a sultry guitar riff emerged, and they were off to the races.

Do It is a 20 minute freestyle that perfectly captured the magic in the room. Barely touched since that friday, you can feel the energy in the production, musicianship, and half intended and half gibberish lyrics encouraging the listener to go ahead and just do it, whatever “it” means. What up I'm Jamee Cornelia based out of Atlanta [eastside] by way of Fuquay-Varina, North Carolina. I'm a Experimental visual artist and Alternative Rapper known for their uniqueness, high energy and creativity. 

Pulling from Punk and Pop influences like Beyonce to M.I.A to Queens of the Stone Age to Jay Z to Pink Floyd to Britney Spears. As well as Hip Hop/Trap influences like Gucci Mane Busta Rhymes Missy Elliot and Ludacris. I am a mixed bag of sounds and aesthetics that enjoys keeping their audience guessing. 

This track is a high energy song celebrating authenticity. I highlight the duality of living in spaces that aren't consider righteous while being exactly aligned with my purpose.  Heavily inspired by Pep Rallies and "bullying" the opposition.

“ Gotta Be” was created at MeLoX old studio space in Flatbush Brooklyn. I remember it like it was yesterday. Written & Performed: MoRuf
Produced by: MeLo-X

Ever since moving to Los Angeles I've had the pleasure of doing a bunch of sessions with talented vocalists. The process has taught me how to be comfortable in a room and make people feel ready to record, all while trying to be quick on my feet as a producer and catch a vibe with the artist I'm working with.

Over the past few months I've realized that most of the music I've made has been in sessions. And while I love vocal-driven music, I haven't really had the chance to sit back and do my own instrumental production experiments. When I look back on how I got started in music, so much of it was by myself sitting in a room twisting knobs and making odd sounds.

Honey is me taking a step back in that direction - it's a science experiment of a song that serves as my reminder to let go and have fun producing and to not take myself so seriously.

“Moving like you won the lottery/ Took it to another level it’s the God in me. “

This song is super special to me. A few weeks ago MeLo-X sent me this beat and I would just have it on repeat not even writing to it yet but just enjoying the beat itself. I played it as I was driving one day and it  simply wrote itself. 

It ended up being a song about the importance of having gratitude, and reflecting on how far I’ve come but also how much further I want to take it. Speaking on being grateful of where I am but excited for the level up. Digging deep inside of myself and remembering that the power is in me. I hope that anyone who listens to this song can enjoy , 2step and also remember that regardless of any challenges you might be going through remember that the power is in you, it’s up to you to activate it. Enjoy!

Written by: MoRuf
Produced by: MeLo-X

These are the words I want to say when I float away and leave my body behind. 

Time dissipates when I am dancing. My movement encapsulates the interconnectedness of memory, instinct, emotion, and truth. But when the sweat dries and the clocks start up again, my identity can become distorted and blurred. Regret, guilt, fear, and loss flood my mind, ripping me away from the love that colors my life.

This is disassociating for me; I am no longer in control of my body, words, or feelings and I am a shell with empty eyes. My mind hovers and every conversation is empty. My loved ones feel abandoned while we are sitting right across from one another. I wrote these lyrics while fighting a dissociative episode and I managed to come back to myself through making my experience tangible and real with words and sound.

This song is a reclamation of myself. When I’m ready to become real again, patient love is always there to welcome me back home.

Chapter 1 of my journey into web 3 began with three small batch editions of Music NFTs. If you're a holder of this NFT it most likely means you joined me during that time, so welcome aboard. This is a collectors item and represents a moment in my personal web 3 history. 

The medley you hear starts with 'Meet Me On The Lake' - my first ever Music NFT, 10 editions and a national radio debut on BBC Radio Scotland. Next comes 'Low Light' a small, peaceful song from 2020 which found its way into many hearts on Twitter space performances and was subsequently dropped as 20 editions. Finally, this trilogy of tracks is completed by 'In The Smoke', my genesis drop on SoundXYZ.

"2am" is a heartfelt song that combines the inspiration from bubblegum pop sounds with early 2000s vibes, with its music video taking inspiration from the manga series "Chobits" and cam girls. The video tells a fictional story set in Neo Tokyo, where AI bots called persocoms are common, and one special persocom, the chobit, seeks unconditional love from her person. 

The song's lyrics touch on the theme of unrequited love and delve into the experiences of the artist, a plus-size Asian, who has encountered fetishization rather than genuine connections in the world of dating. By sharing these personal experiences and emotions through her music, the artist hopes to resonate with others who have faced similar challenges and create a meaningful connection with her audience. With its unique blend of musical styles and thought-provoking themes.

Description:
"Put Em Up" is the very first Music NFT released by CREANS and is an absolute searing EDM festival banger! The cover art is new original work from ANGRY TENO.

Inspired by the art, community and vibe that CREANS found in the NFT project ANGRY APES SOCIETY, he set his mind to craft something that was both an anthem celebrating the art that ANGRY TENO had created but also was about the community who grew from it.  The lyrics are reflect that experience as well from things like about celebrating life:

"From the front to the back --
Where you at --
Put Em Up Put Em Up!!" 

..and then the lyrics also speak to how community is created, the friendships made and fellowship thats created between IRL/web2 life and the emerging web3 space:

"Cos the world that we're livin in -- 
kinda hard to be fittin in -- 
so they made it just for you and me --- 
Angry Ape Society!"

In order to bring this whole vision to life, CREANS wanted to elevate both the music and the art to the same top-tier level. He wanted the art to be something people would WANT to collect so that meant he needed to partner up with someone truly great. This is where the magic and wonder of a perfect collaboration comes in. CREANS and ANGRY TENO knew each other through the AAS project and started having conversations about how to make the art contain the same freshness & energy that the song did, but also still be part of the Angry Apes Society's universe and lore. 

For CREANS, he wanted the artwork to not resemble a traditional album cover and instead be an actual collectible limited-edition NFT! In addition he also wanted the "Golden Egg" cover to be a completely different Angry Apes NFT, a true 1-of-1 Legendary Grail, raising the bar even higher for the collectors who love the exceptional art from ANGRY TENO and music from CREANS.

_______________________________

ABOUT CREANS:
Los Angeles based Electronic artist, Creans (pronounced "kray-ahnz") creates a sonic journey with each track. 

Amassing over 18,000 monthly listeners and 5 million streams on multiple platforms like Spotify, Tidal and Soundcloud including co-producing top remixes of hits like Rihanna’s “Work”, Bebe Rexha’s “Me, Myself & I”, Bel Biv DeVoe's "Poison", Sergio Mendes's "Mas Que Nada" and many more! He's also scored films and written songs for some of your favorite TV shows.

Layering lush and well-crafted melodies with hard-hitting rhythm sections, Creans expertly combines his modern production style with straightforward songwriting methods to create beat-driven music, that is just as much imaginative as it is engaging.

All Socials: @iamcreans
_______________________________

ABOUT ANGRY TENO:
Angry Teno is the artist and cofounder of Angry Apes Society.

For more than 20 years he has been doing professional art originally from the IRL/web2 & traditional methods. In discovering web3 and NFT art and communities he's found the place where he could really express himself with the feelings and emotions that drive him.

For ANGRY TENO creating a community, being part of something bigger than himself and having the possibility of sharing who he is an something that has, in ANGRY TENO'S words , "This has changed me, elevated my artistic experience and provided my heart with incredible joy and happiness."

All socials: @angryteno

Description:
Growing up I looked up to Dizzy Wright and was highly inspired by his music. I spent years working on music of my own and creating a name for myself. Taught myself how to record vocals and engineer them. After years of writing and releasing music I slowly got better and better at producing my own music. 

Everything being recorded in my bedroom with equipment I saved up for a slowly purchased along my music journey. Over the course of those years I was on a mission to once day get Dizzy Wright on one of my songs. Contacting his management multiple times and sending over song after song trying to make something work. 

After pounding the pavement long enough I found myself working on this song. Getting ready to release it, something felt like it was missing... 

So shooting my shot like any hungry artist would do, I sent the files to Dizzy's team and asked to give it a listen. 

After a couple days I got an email back saying he heard the track and he loved it. I went back to work on the song chopping it up so that there could be an open verse for Dizzy to work with. 

The rest was history. 

This song is proof that no matter who you are or how big your name is, Working hard and staying consistent will pay off. 

Do what you love and dream big

Golden Egg: A scene -by me- from the ancient temple of Habu in Luxor, Egypt, situated on the western bank of the Nile. Dive into the enchanting embrace of "Ocean Lullaby," a captivating 20 minute sound montage meticulously crafted from original field recordings I captured & processed over the course of 3 years, transcending the boundaries of conventional music composition. This auditory work ventures beyond the realms of traditional music, inviting contemplation with a thought-provoking question: What is music?

Immerse yourself in the gentle cadence of the sea as you embark on an ambient journey spanning three coastal states in America: Florida, Georgia, and South Carolina. "Ocean Lullaby" artfully weaves together a symphony of ocean waves and field recordings, creating an immersive soundscape that captures life on the coast.

For me, this conceptual soundwork challenges conventional notions of music, encouraging you as the listeners to ponder the essence of melody, rhythm, and harmony. Is music confined to traditional instruments and structured compositions, or can it be found in the symphony of the natural world? "Ocean Lullaby" invites you to explore these questions as you listen.

This piece of audio can serve as a soothing backdrop for various activities or moments of reflection. Whether you're looking for a serene soundscape to enhance relaxation & meditation, or simply looking for a calming ambience while working, reading, or unwinding for the day, "Ocean Lullaby" can provide that for you. The gentle ebb and flow of ocean waves, coupled with layers of field recordings, can transport you to the coastal states of Florida, Georgia, and South Carolina, allowing you to find peace and focus amidst the chaos of our modern lives. 

With "Ocean Lullaby", you're invited to experience the allure of the ocean's embrace and embark on a contemplative journey that transcends the boundaries of sound. It's not just a song; it's an invitation to join me in redefining the very essence of music itself.

The Beaver Jam Club is the musicians' collective focused on cutting edge music production, founded by Brandon Schroeder. What began as an interview on the Beaver Jam Club's Artist Spotlight show, episode #4 on Twitter (X) Spaces, now available on podcast streaming platforms, blossomed into a creative friendship. Brandon had a vision to create a song based on the amazing freestyle Rohan did with the infamous loop "I Got 5 On It." The song envisioned was to be inspired by the tougher, true-to-life golden era hip hop classics contrasted by the spirit-filled, melodious vocals of reggae music. Brandon teamed up with his brother Ryan and they created the music heard on the track today. Ryan Schroeder is an amazingly talented musician and was crucial in the genesis of this track with Brandon. The song was then sent to Rohan with the help of his manager @$MoneyLoooong$ on Twitter (X). Vocals were recorded by RDG at G.L.O.W. Entertainment studios in North Carolina, US in July, 2023. When finished with many electrifying takes, the recordings were sent to @MerkleyMusic on Twitter (X) with Christopher Merkley for the mixing and mastering. The final production was done between everyone involved including: Brandon Schroeder, Ryan Schroeder, Rohan Da Great, and Christopher Merkley, however none of the production for this song could have been done without the genius of Christopher Merkley's mixing abilities. Brandon is honored to have been able to work with so many truly talented artists to bring this vision to fruition. By minting this song, "Greatness Indeed," you support independent musicians who strive to survive in a world that doesn't appreciate them nearly to the extent it use to. Streaming platforms are nearly impossible to make a decent living on alone and the expectations for what a new album release can bring-in financially are marginal compared to the amounts seen just a couple decades ago. Now with the advent of blockchain tech and smart contracts, the power can be given back to the music creators as opposed to the hand's of big business. A new landscape is being built on the revolutionary minds of web3 devs, paving the way with unique and exciting ways to connect, grow, and remain independent as a musician.

The values of web3 align with Rohan Da Great's mission to support independent music and the culture of music NFTs is what inspired him to get involved, support other artists, and begin creating in this space. This is far from a one time venture for Rohan as he is already in the works collabing with other NFT projects and finding anyway he can to participate, give-back, and to grow alongside the rest of the web3 music family at large.

Rohan Da Great, son of legendary dancehall artist Curry Don, is an aspiring MC hailing from east Flatbush Brooklyn New York now residing in North Carolina. RDG is driven by one goal; to administer great music to the world. With his L.A.R. Entertainment (Leaders of the Artist Revolution) Imprint, his versatility, exceptional bar delivery and ear for music, Rohan sets himself apart from the upcoming class of MC's. Previous releases such as “Rule The World” & "Say Goodbye" have tested the waters and came out on top with flying colors. Since their release the songs have been featured on multiple major blogs, radio stations and several magazines which have all sang the praise of the breath of fresh air that is Rohan Da Great. The songs were able to touch people and evoke emotions and ideals that made them reminisce on the past and contemplate creating a better future. Nowadays versatility within independence is the key to any successful artist and Rohan Da Great exemplifies those traits. We’ve seen plenty of rappers pay homage to, and dabble in the Dancehall/Reggae genre, but not many artists can switch genres completely and still hold their own. It seems as though many artists are incapable of finding that elusive sweet spot in their artistry to deliver on both spectrums.

Rising Dancehall star RDG, more recently known for his chart-topping releases like “Fallin’,” and “Unfair Games,” which made it to #1 on iTunes and the Top 100 on Urban Radio respectively, has cracked the code. Although Rohan is currently seeing success in Reggae genres, he originally entered the game as an MC, hence his SM handle @rohandagreatmc. Rohan had a promising rap career with releases, but somewhere along the line he decided to switch it up and it worked effortlessly.

He just expanded his reach with the newly released track, "She Single" and then the longly anticipated collab song with the Beaver Jam Club "Greatness Indeed." Armed with an unmatched level of versatility, lyrical prowess, an ear for catchy beats and an unrivaled work ethic, Rohan Da Great is sure to reach international levels of success and will undoubtedly be a household name in the years to come.

Indonesia was my second release as Divorce Court but really feels like the song that started it all. It's a sultry chillwave tune that began with a few resampled piano chords on a repeating loops with lots of grain and delay. 

It's about a 6 month span of time where I lived in Indonesia with a bunch of strangers as a 19 year old and tried to wrap my head around some important questions I had. Ultimately it was a journey which brought out all of my parts at once, beautiful and miserable all at the same time.

I hope it connects with you. After 5 years, it's still really special to me, which is why I wanted it to be my first release on here. It's been sampled in a few different tracks including Dre Scot's Feelings and many other underground beat makers tracks.

Thank you so much for listening. 

Much love,

- I moved to Nashville in 2016 with my girlfriend I'd been with for 4 years. She got a job as an E.R. nurse, I came to pursue music. We moved into a two-bedroom apartment together and life was great. I was chasing my dreams and lived with the woman that I planned on spending my life with. After a few years without having any real success as an artist/songwriter, she asked me one day after a long stressful shift at the hospital, "How long are you going to chase this for?" I answered "as long as it takes"... which was and still is my truth.
- After that conversation everything changed. She changed. She wanted security, and I wasn't it. Our relationship started to suffer. That's when Baltimore called. She got offered a 3 month travel nursing assignment to move to Baltimore. She would be able to pay off her student loans and it would also give us a little space, maybe just what we needed.
- A few weeks later she packed up her car, gave me a kiss goodbye, and headed off to Baltimore. Little did I know that it would be the last time we would kiss, and the last time I would see her. After she got there, she didn't answer my texts or calls. Our relationship was over. It became clear that she had made her decision to end our relationship before she left Nashville and that maybe this was the most pain-free way of doing it. I was heartbroken, she was my first true love and it hurt to lose her. I wanted to hate her for it, but I couldn't. This life I have chosen as a troubadour is not for everyone, and It just wasn't for her. I wanted her to find happiness, even if it wasn't with me... and that is what inspired this song, "Baltimore"
- For anyone who has ever been with someone who left them without warning... I present to you... "Baltimore".

Description:
This song took more than a decade to manifest. This song's surrealistic lyrics and haunting verse melodies were born from a whiskey-fueled dream about a non-sensical conversation in a dark western bar after an ordinary night out in 2010. Luckily, the dreamer woke up with enough sense to realize the potential of this little dream diddy and immediately recorded what he remembered into his iPhone while in bed. Initial drafts of a fuller song with a chorus and bridge were soon written and recorded in the hopes of something sticking, but nothing ever did. Frustrated, the dreamer dropped the diddy and moved on with life...

Fast forward ten years later, and the dreamer woke again from a dream, floating among white, snow-capped mountains with a curious melody blaring in the sky. It was a dream that felt vaguely familiar. Drifting back into consciousness, the dreamer realized it was the continuation of that conversation from that dark Western bar. It was the same dream -- only a proper chorus was born this time. La Cita jams on this concept soon and then ensues, where the song is fully fleshed out and elevated into its current form. 

Like most things, finding meaning, connecting the dots, and looking forward are hardly natural. Sometimes, a dream doesn't end when you wake up; sometimes, it takes more than 10 years to complete a feeling. But looking back, this song is heavily influenced by a love of Spaghetti Western movies and dancing to cumbia music in dark bars. It honors the slow, mysterious, and often aimless character arc from a good Western we go through before seeing things more clearly from a higher vantage point. And yet it leaves room for the mystery and longing that often remain...

Description:
Somewhere Far Away is an emotional, bass heavy, dark electronic pop song about depression, and inner turmoil.  

The lyrics of this song spilled out of me at 2am one night in a moment of pain and sadness.  I am just grateful to be able to channel this pain into art...

When we have depression or intense moments of sadness, we sometimes feel like we want to run away from everything.  Life can feel overwhelming, and like the only escape is leaving everyone, and everything we know behind.  

Somewhere Far Away is about the impossible dream of running away to a place where everything magically feels better. 

No one knows what it’s like to be you, or be in your mind.  No matter how easy you life might seem, if you’re up at night having panic attacks, or suffering from any mental illness it can be hard to live even the cushiest, most blessed life.

Description:
Quiddity is inspired by Clive Barker's book "The Great and Secret Show." 
In the book quiddity can be accessed only 3 times in someone's life: when we sleep outside our mother's womb for the first time, when we sleep beside the one person we truly love for the first time, as well as the last time we sleep before we die. 

I've tried to encapsulate this into song.

Inspired by a moment of frustration and realized exhaustion, "VOID" came to be as commentary on how it feels to be an independent artist in a digital world. It's no longer about talent or vision, but how loud you are and how many friends you have. Yet, where does that leave the introverted, quiet types who have something to say - the ones who look and sound different from what's popular? 

Heavy, grungy, and matter of fact, "VOID" is about the underdogs, the ones who work themselves to the bone and throw it all into the blackhole called the internet, time after time. Not because they have to, but because they refuse to live a life that consistently reminds them to give up and fall in line.

Description:
‘Bipolar’ es electrónica nueva, de la que muta y crepita. De la que respira, huele y suda. IDM, breaks, dream-pop, trip-hop, bass, glichts, electro, techno, jungle, future-garage, etc. Aquí suceden cosas todo el tiempo, desde el primer beat. Suenan sintes que rasgan la realidad como cuchillos, como empeñados en arrancarnos de una distopia que, si no lo impedimos, acabará matándonos. Emergen sonidos bastardos que, desde su propia orfandad, colisionan en feliz sinergia para implosionar en lo más alto del abismo.
Temas que habitan unos dentro de otros. Solapados, pero no escondidos. Infinitas historias que convergen en una misma que siempre terminan siendo dos. La misma cara en dos monedas diferentes. Aquí no hay tiempo, ni lugar, para cruces. Y de repente, tras un drop atisbamos un destello. Y nos hace soñar. Para pronto, todo volver a empezar. En loop, como la vida. O la muerte y la locura. Vive doble y lo harás más.

‘Heavy Calm’ is the first single off of Sessions Vol. 1 — Songcamp’s debut collection of one-off releases. Sessions Vol. 1 will feature the first five Sessions, highlighting the incredible collaborative talent of 18 musicians at Songcamp.

“Best part about making heavy calm was getting to see the brilliance of both Matt and Mars; how they work and think about poetry and music. Good vibes the whole way over like a heavy calm.” — Kinney

“Going into this project my main goal was simply to make something that Matthew, Kinney and I would all love objectively as listeners. After connecting a few months back, ProbCause sent me some beats to check out. I instantly gravitated towards this one in particular (Often Told), and from there the process was seamless. I wrote/recorded my verse a few days later, then sent him the stems to do the same. The song came together very naturally. We didn't even really discuss the direction of the lyrics or message. We just started to write and let the beat lead the way.

This song explores themes of resilience, defiance, and embracing one's truth. It emphasizes the importance of remaining authentic and level headed, even when faced with moments of turbulence and adversity.

Creating this track with ProbCause was a special experience.. I remember listening to his music when I first started out, and the positive impact it had on me. He was someone that inspired me to take my music/artistry more seriously. To keep pushing and evolving my craft. So, being able to hop on a track with him meant so much.

Description:
When I was 10, my family and I took a flight from Zimbabwe to New Zealand. In a lot of ways that was their escape from a collapsing economy, to a new world and yet gripping on to the traditions of the world we once knew. We all remember our first great escape, ironically that was not mine. My escape was writing... An escape from a crashing of cultures that I couldn't seem to confront internally. Spending every second I could get in words and in worlds rather than inwards. That was before I understood that essentially they must co-exist. For one can only travel so far from their flesh before it yearns for water. 

The METAL ON MY TEETH bio below is written as if I am studying my own creative process from outside looking in.  

"METAL ON MY TEETH" is the first single off TAPZ GALLANTINO’s debut album, “ALL FOR WHAT” arriving when the stars align. The Zimbabwe native fuses his punk rock and R&B background to form his unique brand of PUNK R&B. 

Written, produced, and performed by TAPZ GALLANTINO, he brings his trademark grit and spitfire lyricism to “METAL ON MY TEETH” – a thundering foot stomper of a sonic experience with an adrenaline-boosting chorus that chants “They don’t make them like us no more...” 

The track documents his quest for peace in a world that has offered him little to none. Referencing his collective experiences as a black nomad, exploring the combination of political tension and black culture, he sings “I put metal on my teeth, it’s the only time I feel inner peace, smiling. Because the piece that they’re serving in these streets is the type to leave no peace.” TAPZ further explains, “I spent my youth predominantly in an internal culture clash, moving from Zimbabwe when I was ten to the first world created that internal complex. Rock n Roll and Hip hop culture served as an escape, the TV screen playing Jimi Hendrix and Lil Wayne was my mirror. Silver Metal Grills are poetic for me. To me they serve as the right of passage to the first metal you choose to bite, especially in a world of limited choice where we’re forced to bite or even worse – swallow the bullet.”

Description:
'Pressure' is a summer jam i wrote a few months back.
It is a song that is super catchy and easy to sing along with.

I often get inspiration from real situations when i write my music. 

When writing 'Pressure' i wanted it to be less 'Serious or deep' and 
more of an easy listen summer 'smash' but still following the afro feeling it gives especially with the drums and with me being from South Africa it was super important for me to get that feeling out of 'Pressure' the feeling of home if you may. 

My friend was going through a situation and called me mid studio session telling me about how much 'Pressure' he is feeling being with this girl and how he never really wanted it to be a serious situation and that is kind of a brief summary of where the title for the record comes from.

This vibrant track represents a significant turning point for the artist, embracing tranquility and self-empowerment as he rediscovers his purpose.

"Escalator" is a rhythmic masterpiece that effortlessly combines Ayotemi's infectious Indigo Rap flow, skillful cadences, and an irresistible blend of singing and rapping. The song's upbeat nature, coupled with its lush harmonies, creates a sonic landscape that beckons listeners to surrender to its contagious energy.

With a deep understanding of the human experience, Ayotemi's lyrics speak to the transformative power of choosing peace and prioritizing self-care. In a world that often demands conformity, "Escalator" encourages its audience to fearlessly rearrange their lives for the better, embracing vulnerability as a catalyst for growth and personal evolution.

The song's soaring melodies and rhythmic hooks envelop the listener in a sense of high-frequency peace, joy, and the irresistible urge to dance. Through Ayotemi's heartfelt delivery and thought-provoking lyrics, "Escalator" becomes a conduit for catharsis, allowing listeners to recognize the areas in their lives that require healing and transformation.

From the opening notes to the infectious chorus, "Escalator" takes us on a journey from turmoil to serenity, encapsulating the journey of post-breakup introspection. Ayotemi's talent for crafting compelling narratives shines through as he seamlessly weaves together personal anecdotes and universal themes, creating an empathetic connection with his audience.

As Ayotemi returns to his purpose, "Escalator" serves as a powerful reminder that choosing self is a courageous act, and that we all have the capacity to rise above our past experiences. With its vibrant energy and uplifting message, this track positions Ayotemi as a beacon of hope and a guiding light for anyone navigating their own path towards personal growth and self-discovery.

"Escalator" is more than just a song; it's an invitation to embrace vulnerability, rearrange the pieces of our lives, and find peace in the process. Ayotemi's artistic prowess shines brightly, offering an enchanting musical experience that resonates on a profound level with listeners.

Prepare to elevate yourself to new heights as you surrender to the infectious rhythms and empowering message of "Escalator" - a song that will leave you inspired, rejuvenated, and ready to dance to the beat of your own heart.

This is exclusive to you exactly like 'JOY' was and i hope you all enjoy it and resonate with the record in your own personal way.

ART IS BEAUTIFUL.

Description: This version was cut with live guitar as a special first release.

Every day is a battle and a struggle whether its mental, physical, spiritual, or emotional. This song was created to battle every day struggles and let the people know they are not alone, we are not alone in our battles even if it feels like it. 

This song takes inspiration from Citizen Cope's "Let The Drummer Kick". I created a simple and easy to remember chorus that's vague enough to insert ones own problems into and identify with. The verses touch on different aspects of the everyday struggle and I almost abruptly ended the song at 4:20 because life is unpredictable like that and because I'm a stoner and Mary always helps. 

Light one up and relax because its all gonna be okay, we'll all make it to our destination on time and intact.

“If you really want to be famous, change your name to Sky Bravo.”

He looked me dead in the eye as he sat up and grabbed my arm, his seriousness taking me aback. The whole scene really. His eyes a bit cold. His large and ever-commanding frame, frailed by time.

He was on his deathbed and we both knew it. 

There were times when we didn’t know what to do - when I didn’t know what to do - except sit. Except think that a young man ought to be near his grandfather during his final days on earth. 

He was not a vulnerable man, Paw Paw. Charming, yes, a smile that could melt your heart or bend your will *just so* whether you were part of the family or had just met. But vulnerable, no.

So when he looked at me - as he broke the silence that we had been sitting in for hours that turned into days that turned into weeks that turned into the passing of a generation - when he looked at me and broke that silence - to tell me a quip that crossed his mind or why he thought Nicholas Cage was great in Raising Arizona - every bit of small talk was like - have i spent my whole life really not getting to know you? not asking a single question beyond what i could see? and when he broke the silence…

“I coulda been a singer.”

Stunned, having been lost in my own world, contemplating the silence and sitting and sitting and - stunned.

“But you were, Paw Paw, you *are*.” My heart careful not to place his life in the past tense. “You have a gold medal in singing - in chorus competition - the barbershop society - a gold medal -“ my voice raising in pitch as my heartbeat quickened, pleading to the moment, “the quartets - your quartet - the spellbinders - you were a singer, you ARE - “

“No.” 

He interrupted deeply, but kindly. 

Stolidly, with his full self, he spoke again.

“Like Sinatra.” 

So matter-of-fact.

He lay back - his strong-broad-frail shoulders lay back as the life he imagined flashed before my eyes - the crowds lost in ecstasy swaying in unison, the dancing lights reflecting through the sweat dripping from the brows of the great entertainer, the bathed in gold, the showing up to play your role, the diamonds, the sparkling eyes, the grit and glamour of a public life.

Once more from the silence:

“If you really want to be famous, change your name to Sky Bravo.”

He looked me dead in the eye as he sat up and grabbed my arm, his seriousness taking me aback. The whole scene really. His eyes a bit cold. His large and ever-commanding frame, frailed by time.

He was on his deathbed and we both knew it.

        taking a look back at his life

             "What do you see?"

'JOY' a beautiful song that probably means the most to me.
I lost my uncle a few weeks go and the day i found out i went to studio and found myself writing this record with no intention of doing anything with it besides sending to friends and family and most importantly for listening to it myself to heal and feel the emotions of the ups and downs of losing someone. 

Uncle Ken was my mothers brother in law who was married to her oldest sister 'JOY' who passed away from cancer when i was very young.

So for me the title means more than the word  'JOY' 
& when writing this i had the feeling that i was talking to my uncle and asking him questions about Life,Love and meaning. 

So the feedback i have gotten from friends and family has pushed me to share 
'JOY' to all of you and i hope a few of you can relate to this special first song i have decided to share with yall.

I know he is happy with his 'JOY' in heaven.

'Luna' incapsulates the things that hide in the dark. Insatiable, chaotic, and hedonistic the darkest moments can provide some of the most powerful catharsis.

“no matter how this ends i’ll be just fine” is the final track on my EP “things i wanna text u” - a look into my life during one of the biggest heartbreaks I’ve ever experienced. A point that brought me to the lowest point in my mental health I have experienced. The song serves as a reminder to myself, mostly, that no matter how this ends, I’ll be just fine.

But, I didn’t always believe that. I remember clearly one point in the heat of it all where I genuinely questioned if it would be okay. I hadn’t ever experienced that before. I was genuinely concerned about my mental health for the first time ever.

Through this experience, I learned how important it is to take mental health seriously. i learned so much through this journey and want to use this music to help others who are going through something similar. To show them they’re not alone.

That’s why, through this drop, I am donating half of the proceeds to Bring Change To Mind - an organization that is helping to make a change and end the stigma around mental health and mental illness. If you’re struggling, you’re not alone, and I’m here for you.

“show me” was a really fun song to make, and the creative process from start to finish was unlike anything I had made before. When I first made this track, what is now the verse was actually the “drop” or the main hook, the song was much slower, and I had written and recorded my own vocals on it. It was a cool track, but I knew it could be better (i'm not a very good singer). That's when I decided to send the instrumental to a songwriter and vocalist, with no instruction other than to “have fun with it” and see what she could do. I absolutely loved what she sent back and I ended up making two different new versions of the song. I made one version with the original drop and her new vocals layered over the top, which made a sort of Nu Disco Indie-Electronic track. The second version I made was a high-energy bass house drop that used all of the ad libs she recorded and some bouncy bass lines I had written underneath them. In the end, I took both ideas and was able to mold them into one track to get the best of both worlds, and that's the tune you hear today. Hope you enjoy dancing to this one as much as I did making it! see you soon. - informal.

This song started the way many others do, with my friends throwing different ideas around with no expectations or guidelines. Collaboration is such an integral part of my process. Gaining an outside perspective and playing off of each others strengths always leads to a unique product, as opposed to sometimes getting stuck in a loop when creating on your own. 

The beat for this song first came to life in March 2022. I pulled up to the Wallis Lane HQ in Santa Monica to have a session with Don’t Trip, an extremely talented producer duo I had been working with for over a year at that point. It was maybe our 3rd or 4th idea that we made that session. They started laying down some melodies and adding layers but it really came together when they played that bright, abrasive, synth bass over everything. I believe every song should have elements that cut through the rest; ones that are instantly recognizable, and this was it. After they got that down I immediately had ideas for the drums. I was picturing driving hats and a huge snare, reminiscent of a lot of 80s/Synthwave drums. I did my best to translate everything in my head onto the track and added some toms and other percussion to really solidify the movement of it. 

After this session, the beat went into a folder for 4 months until I had a session with Kevin George in June. I didn't even send the beat out before that because I wasn't sure who I could hear on it, but I knew Kevin was always down to hear the weird, left-field beats on my hard drive, so I played it for him. As I was playing it I think the same elements that stuck out to me, stuck out to him. He told me to put it aside and later that week I saw he posted an Instagram snippet of what he had recorded. Once I heard the hook I new it was special. 

The song laid dormant for almost a year after that, until I was texting Kevin trying to figure out which song of ours I should release for my debut in Web3 and he reminded me that we still had 'Status Online' in the vault. After getting the vocal stems from him and tweaking the instrumental and arrangement, the song was finally ready for people to hear. In my opinion, one of the best parts of producing is looking back and seeing the journey an idea took from its inception all the way to its release. It really makes me appreciate the process and the care it takes to showcase a song to the world. I'm excited to continue to drop music on this platform and give y'all a chance to invest in this journey! Much love!

While experimenting with distortion, I heard a familiar timbre from my childhood. I remembered how I spent a lot of time at my grandmother's playing with her old electronics. There were radios, TV remotes, flashlights, and so on.
I was most interested in the radio; I didn't understand what it was, but I really liked the various buttons and the antenna. One day, I turned on the radio and heard white noise. I was surprised that it still worked. I was very happy with my discovery! Turning the knobs, I finally found a station with music. On that day, I spent a lot of time listening to music and the voices of announcers on that radio. The distortions were uniquely pleasant, simultaneously beautiful and dirty.

I tried to transfer those feelings to the present, to modern sound. Here, there is that distinctive distortion, curiosity, admiration, and innocent childlike simplicity.

Enjoy listening!

I’m Upper Reality, producer and artist, and I have been developing myself for 10 years.  As a longtime creator, I have grown and changed immensely and watched the industry do the same.  “Rise,” is a reimagining of the exhilaration, appreciation, joy, pain, and ultimately, exhaustion, that I have garnered following this life path.

I have an Economics degree from the University of Texas at Austin.  I used to not mention it, because it didn’t seem “cool,” but the more I traversed my journey, the more I began to see how cliques, identities, buzzwords, and other superficial considerations go into valuation of a person and what they do.  This understanding has led me to have a more active, intellectual role in my work, just in time for the intersection of music and fintech to make a place for it.  There is a sociological and spiritual revolution happening with my work that I seek for all listeners to feel and understand when they listen to what I’m creating.  This is all my production, all my music theory understanding, all my vocal training, all my Ableton practice, and all of the closed doors that have never recognized what I have felt to be a gift that I have.  See, “Rise,” is not just about a vacant, toxic-positive chant to peace and love—it is a proverbial snatching of the goalpost—a declaration of “sleep on me, I’ll sleep on you,” to all of the times that I have had my core wounds invoked by organizations, groups, systems, and people, that I wanted to value me, accept me, etc. only to be rejected, humiliated, abandoned for superficial reasons, yet told it’s something that I’m lacking.  “Rise” says “Nope, I was never the problem.  And now, with the joys I reach on my own terms, you all will see that, from afar.”

I am at a point of detachment to the outcome, as to whether or not I will be heard, recognized, celebrated, or valued.  As of now, this is just a special piece, that means a lot to me, and means a lot that the Sound audience would be keen to listen.  I enjoy the piece very deeply, but I have left it in it’s raw, early stages, before tweaking it to see whether DSP’s will bite. So this is a special, limited edition, that won’t be released anywhere else.

For more information of the entire context of what I’m wanting to do in Web3, please check out my proposal video:

https://youtu.be/Xxp1Y8iKaI8

“ghost” was made over a series of discord video calls late last year. Darby and I had been discussing the healing journey, and how someone (or something) can leave a void in your life after they're gone. This echo can't be moved on from until you confront your past. Sonically, we wanted this track to be layered with texture and ambience, and have chords that gave you the feeling of that emotional tug of war. Clover's speech (the spoken word intro) represents the resolution to this- that you need to make peace with your past in order to move forward and heal. Our goal was to make something that would uplift and inspire people going through similar struggles.

We made this song at some point during the pandemic and had a blast doing it. It was a reminder to us and everyone who hears it that despite everything going on, we are gonna be alright. Please listen at full volume and dance :)

Description:
Nvak Collective is a next-generation record label and artist advocacy collective that fully embraces web3 to uplift creators. Our mission is to build a more equitable, profitable, and diverse music industry that puts the underrepresented first, recognizing that the current system is in need of major disruption. Our small team has already discovered talent from remote regions around the globe and launched them to billions of streams and hundreds of thousands of fans, all while providing artist-friendly deals and artist care. 

With a focus on signing and developing women, non-binary, and LGBTQ+ artists from emerging markets, we see web3 as a tool to better help these creators tell their stories, earn new revenue streams, and connect with their biggest fans. Since June of 2022, we’ve worked hard to bring rising artists such as Annika Rose into the web3 space, and will continue to bridge the gap in web3 education and onboarding for artists seeking to take the leap.

Rosa Linn began her journey with Nvak Collective back in 2018 when she was discovered by Nvak’s local A&Rs at a small music festival in Dilijan, Armenia. She became the first artist signed to Nvak Collective in 2020, and has since surpassed over 1 billion streams and will be opening up tours for Ed Sheeran, Young the Giant & Milky Chance this summer 2023.

Rosa’s latest single “Hallelujah” puts her powerful vocals on full display as an ode to the life-changing year she has experienced since competing at Eurovision for Armenia and signing a major label deal. She says, “This past year, my life has changed so much. It can be hard to put into words how grateful I feel, but I hope this song helps you understand.” This “Hallelujah” R3hab Remix offers a dancier twist to the already uplifting track, and we’re excited for it to be the first of many curated drops from Nvak Collective. Play it loud.

The original song was created to be the soundtrack to a great day, and inspire you to take life “Lightly”. The og song was made at the tail end of 2020 with Lani Rose. As we all know that was not a great year, and there was a lot of anxiety and negative feelings surrounding that time. With all the negativity and bad vibes happening I wanted to make a song that could inspire a positive feeling, and perspective. 

The OG song got featured in NBA2k22 and has over over 1 million streams on Spotify. First of all I wanna say John - “ThaKracken” is one of the most kind people I’ve encountered in music, for over a year he would just send me deals and freebies on audio plugins that I would’ve otherwise never knew about. One day ThaKracken sent me this CRAZY dope song he finished, and at the time I was looking for a more electronic, hype version of “Lightly”. So I asked ThaKracken if he would be down to do a remix. 

The original song was a more chill but vibey approach to Lightly, but this remix is the hype version that really reflects the positive energy of the lyrics in the production. I hope you are enjoying your day, and taking it lightly.

"Don't Take Your Love" was released on May 22, 2020, roughly two months after "15 days to slow the spread". It was my last release of 2020 and my final solo/pop track before fully entering the EDM space in 2021. 

The song first came to life while I was messing with a vocal plugin I recently purchased and experimenting with stacking a lot of vocals together to make a choir/gang vocal. The line that started that experiment was, "No, don't take your love from me." 

The lyrics were inspired by a relationship on the verge of collapse, and the feelings of experiencing someone's love slowly fade. It's interesting and kind of poetic, though, that the song lyrics are beautifully and tragically paralleled with the love of the world gradually being replaced by fear. So I'd say "Don't Take Your Love" is also a song about the desperate plea to not lose love in the world during one of the most extraordinary times of our lives. 

"Don't Take Your Love" is one of the few songs in my career that is 100% written, recorded, produced, mixed, and mastered entirely by myself. This style of song is the kind of music I want to return to making in the future. 

This Music NFT release with Sound is a brand new endeavor for me in the Web3 space, so a massive thank you to them for reaching out and another huge thank you to everyone who mints this song. 

From the bottom of my heart, it really does mean the world to me when anyone finds a connection with something I've created. 

Much Love and God bless, 

Zack Gray

Description:
In honor of Pride Month “Freedom Bass” is a celebration of the radical and connective power of dance music. A disco-house track and call-to-arms for the queer and dance communities alike. 

A nostalgic, yet forward-thinking track, “Freedom Bass” a lyrical call to action for resistance and change set against a mashup of disco and 90’s house. Written during the pandemic, in the heart of lockdown, the song is filled with melancholy and a desire to return to the dance floor, surrounded by joyful crowds and uninhibited self-expression. 

“Freedom Bass was the first song that we ever wrote together in the basement of Boy Untitled's LA home during quarantine. This was long before we decided to become a boy band (lol) and like most first sessions, we were just feeling each other out to see if we would catch a vibe. We put the track down only to return to it a year later. Little did we know that this would become the thesis of BOY2K: 'The dance floor is the revolution...this is Music For The People.' Our mission as artists is to create spaces for people to come back "home" to. Spaces to find ourselves. Spaces to connect. Space to riot against systems of oppressions. Spaces to imagine the new world that we want to create together."

BOY2K’s mission is to make “Music For The People,” that is, music that celebrates the power of community. A community built in mutual support, love, acceptance and music that begs the listener to get up and move!

Learn more about BOY2K at www.boy2k.com.

Stuck was written on a day when I was trapped in a condo at mammoth mountain, unable to snowboard or leave at all. So I closed myself in the only bedroom and made this song using voice memos and my laptop while my friends binge watched anime.  The track is about being both physically and mentally stuck while watching the seasons pass your life away.
Today we are joined by Keyon Christ of Spores as we discuss the Sporeᵒⁿᵉ - a new tool that allows you remix songs on your phone.

Minimum wage is about the day that I understood that he bare minimum of absolutely anything is simply not going to cut it anymore (wage, love, time, loyalty, energy, you name it). This record was born in my writing sanctuary, the castle in Bordeaux, France, in a writing camp with 3 incredible producers. It is an anthem of all of our early twenties, a time stamp of my many day jobs - selling printer ink to the US army, assistant to an interior designer, party planning, waiting tables, singing at steak houses to empty rooms, you name it. This song is an ode of gratitude and respect to those choices in the pursuit of the dream - running to sessions and rehearsals after an 8-hour minimum wage paying work day. It is also a farewell to hustling for anything that is not the gift of music. This song is part of the "Queen George" chapter of my music that will include my recent releases.

Description:
When we think about “Chaos Theory” the first thing that comes to mind is control. We think about how all of us navigate the world looking for a little semblance of control in this chaotic world we live in. We want to believe that we somehow have an external reach beyond us that protects us, that guides us, that gives us the power over our lives that we are looking for…maybe we do. Maybe the music and the art, the creativity, the words, maybe that’s how we exercise control in this chaotic world. It is our little mark, we own it. We didn’t go seeking the name “Chaos Theory” it found us, all we did is control what we could control and that was the creation. We kept coming back to that river and drinking from it, slowly carving out a space for something bigger than both of us.

- Daktyl & Benni Ola

Ahead of his US Tour, we've been blessed with the first Drum and Bass track he ever created. Here's a quote from Rohaan about the song...

I adore the world this song paints when I hear it, it seems hopeful and wrapped in nostalgia.

I hope this track can mean something to you also.

R. xx "

“CUFFED”  - one of the four singles leading up to my sophomore album “ANGEL OF SADNESS”, self produced and written by me. The whole project is a set of love songs, not only to people but to my head and heart. 

In light of May being mental health awareness month, CUFFED is the love child of whacky, whimsical sounds and . . . ha ha . . . severe mental illness :’) living with mental illness has been a painful life, especially with a diagnosis including the most stigmatized and misunderstood disorders, and it is something I am aiming to be more open/vocal about. I’ve been in a never ending battle trying to get better with treatment centers, psychiatrists, therapists, and medication cocktails for as long as I can remember, and falling back in not only love with a partner but with creating music again after a production hiatus has taken every ounce of mental jiu jitsu possible for someone like me!! however, I’ve never felt more creatively liberated than I do now that my brain is set on the right path and in recovery, and this project truly celebrates getting out of the artistic rut I’ve been in for so many years. 

mixed with my wonderful partner in crime, who also inspired this project, rob <3 (peep our duo project GLOWSTONE if you haven’t)
