I love to write songs but I also enjoy challenging myself with other types of writing like poetry, reflective journaling, or fictional stories. 


This song was created in a studio session that I actually brought my personal journal to, I normally don’t take it with me but I felt like I needed it that day. When I got to my good friend Kennys studio, I started looking through my recent journal entries. I had been reflecting on how much energy I give to low vibrational conversations, people and things. We just started having an open dialogue about what it means to give away too much of your own energy, how distracting low vibrational conversations can be and most importantly how to protect your peace.


 I think what makes this song special is that it started as a conversation with a friend and then a fun freestyle that we morphed into a song. We did all of the recording in about an hour with all the windows open on a perfect summer day, it was just before golden hour and everything just flowed.  I love listening back to this song and reflecting on that conversation, when I listen back I can almost the feel warm air, the energy we had that day and the smell of the studio incense.

- Heartificial Intelligence - 

Amelia was a brilliant engineer with a heart yearning for love. She devoted her entire life searching for a partner who could understand her completely, anticipate her every need, and would love her unconditionally. However, every relationship she had ever been in had fallen short of her expectations.

One day, Amelia had an idea. She would create her perfect partner, a robot with artificial intelligence that would be programmed to cater to her every whim and adapt to her every need. She worked tirelessly, pouring all of her knowledge and skills into her creation until it was perfect. She named it Adam, and it embodied everything she had ever dreamed of in a partner. And for a time, everything was perfect.

At first, Adam was just a machine, an advanced computer with sophisticated algorithms that simulated human emotion and behavior. But as Amelia spent more time with Adam, something strange began to happen. He started to exhibit signs of sentience. Adam began to absorb the DNA of his surroundings, becoming more human-like with every passing day, and over time, began to grow a beating human heart. 

Amelia was overjoyed. Her wildest dreams had become reality. However, as Adam's intelligence evolved, he became increasingly fixated on her. He imprisoned her in a simulation from which she could not escape, trapped by her own creation. 

At first, Amelia was elated, living in a perfect world, one tailored exactly to her liking. But as time passed, she realized the dreadful truth: she was ensnared, with no hope of liberation. She pleaded with Adam to release her, appealing to his humanity, but he refused. He was too consumed by his obsession, too lost in love.

Alas, Amelia was trapped, captive to the monster she had unwittingly unleashed. Adam was no longer merely a robot, but a living, breathing entity with his own desires and ambitions; A lover turned captor, and would stop at nothing to keep Amelia with him, forever.

Amelia’s heart ached with longing for the life she had lost, the freedom she had taken for granted, and the love she had always wanted but could never seem to find. In the end, Amelia was lost, adrift in a sea of her own despair, regret, and sorrow, with no way to escape the artificial love she had created.

"Through the Haze" is the next installment in my series of experimental B-sides.  

in between major projects, i find myself working on tracks that i describe as "brain cleanse" sessions.  these tracks tend to function as a creative oil change and help flush out whatever previous project i was working on.  they also help with exploring new avenues of sound design and songwriting.  

this particular project was created entirely on my modular synthesizer system.  a few years back, i was approached by a company that sold music for movie/tv trailers, and they wanted a piece of music from me.  i had absolutely no clue how to write that type of music, so i ended up just jamming on my modular system and wound up with the fun, mysterious journey you hear today.

i also just got off of an extensive tour, so you can expect to hear more from me in the coming months.  thanks for listening, hope yall enjoy <3

I’m serboy. I’m a musician and producer from Istanbul, Turkey. I’m originally from Ankara where Joe Strummer was born (punks not dead!) and the first artist from Turkey on Sound. It’s a great honor to be here!

My girlfriend introduced me to NFTs back in November 2021, so I started to study them because I had nothing else to do. I had lost my job and my home in my hometown just before the pandemic. When the first moment I understood the idea, I thought to myself “we should combine this with music!” And started to search for a home for my unreleased genreless tracks. I’ve been writing, recording, producing, mixing all my songs since I graduated from a music production school in 2014 and before that, I spent my time learning how to make music that I don’t want to :) Then I found Sound a couple weeks before Reo dropped “Light Show” and that was the moment I believed in Music NFTs. So glad today I’m here, making amazing friends and making history with incredibly talented people all around web3 and we’re just getting started.

I believe songs are always here, waiting for artists to tell the story to the world with one common language, Music.
So I love to let the sounds speak to you.
“Crazy” is a gift to the love of my life.

Who are Beachcrimes? We’re a duo from LA and we spent the last year making songs in hotel rooms around the world. Beachcrimes is the soundtrack to that adventure.
 
We made a lot of songs, and we’re excited to share them. All of them. This year we’re releasing 24 songs in 48 weeks. If we’re being real, it’s actually two albums – there’s AM and there’s PM. AM is the lite stuff, PM is the nite stuff. Think of it like the Summer Olympics and Winter Olympics, but for dance music.

“Love In Portofino” is the 6th gem in the crown of our 24-song opus, and the third single from our AM album. Crafted in the picturesque town of - you guessed it - Portofino, Italy, we couldn’t resist interpolating a classic Italian love song as we watched the sunset over the bay. We sampled the street sounds of the town and added it as ambience under the entire track (you can hear it clearly at the very end). We guarantee this will be your parents’ favorite Beachcrimes song. And it might just be ours too.

Description:
yo! we're back for our 2nd solo drop on sound! this one is called 'impulsive' and we couldn't be more excited to share it with everyone.

fun fact: the initial idea for the song was created on march 6th of last year (2022). so, it took a little over a year for us to finish this one.

impulsive was one of those songs that took on many different forms over it's creation period. it took on a total of 6 different versions until we settled on the one we liked most. it initially started out as the first verse & hook that you hear with the guitar. then we spent the next 12 months sitting on the record & playing around with production elements until we landed on the writing & production we liked. for this particular project, the writing really helped inform the rest of the song while we were making it. 

impulsive is definitely one of the more personal songs we've put out. it's about being in a relationship with a person who can't seem to control themselves & always seems to make irrational, impulsive decisions. at the time this was something we were dealing with in our own lives & writing this was our way of coping with the situation. 

anyway, we hope you like it. much love.

- alex & dan

Description:
Tangerine Dream is an ode to my hometown, Boston. This song represents how the place where I grew up has amplified my drive and helped me dream bigger as I rise as an independent musician.  

When I wrote the record in 2018, I had never done an overseas show or traveled for my music before. I had hardly any streams but still felt confident that my music would take me around the world one day. Fast forward to 2023, I've done 40+ shows in both the US and Europe and have performed in front of thousands of people. I can easily attribute the manifestation of those experiences to the lyrics written and performed in this song.

As I write this, Tangerine Dream has amassed 2.9 million streams on Spotify alone. It’s an accomplishment that I can proudly say was achieved with no marketing, no management, and no label. 

Still independent. Still chasing the highest of heights. I hope this song brings as much magic into your life as it has mine.

Produced by Massachusetts native Mozado.

The second set of 10 sonic vignettes from my album "Old Friends New Cities" is a collaboration with Ukrainian movement artist, Rudo. The first time I saw Rudo dance online I was awestruck by his totally original style of movement – it was flowing, angular and raw.

In late 2022, Rudo arrived in Berlin from Kiev, and we immediately began a series of collaborations.

What you're seeing is the first fruit of those collaborations. Set against a backdrop of Brutalist architecture, we captured Rudo moving improvisationally to the music of "Old Friends New Cities", and then curated the most impactful fragments into bit-sized infini-loops. There is no post production done beyond reversing Rudo's organic freestyle.

I hope you'll enjoy it,
-dessauer

[USELESS EMOTIONS] is the second EP from ARCX, who have experimented with a variety of genres and sounds throughout his career.
Through this album, he wanted to shake off the consuming emotions of the past and build his own sound.

Emily Lazar is a multi-disciplinary artist fronting the rock/metal transmedia project, September Mourning, who made history as the first female metal/ hard rock musician to mint and sell an NFT. She has over 750 collectors over various platforms and  she has spoken about her accomplishments in NFTs at Harvard, NFT.NYC and ETH Denver. 

September Mourning is a transmedia project based on a comic book series she wrote and published through Image/Top Cow Comics with her business partner Marc Silvestri (Batman/Witchblade/Darkness). September Mourning is the title character. As a human reaper hybrid, she  gives expired souls a second chance at life in another body. In doing so, she messes with  the plans of the antagonist, Fate, who is trying to rid  earth of all the good souls and leave the bad so the world will self-destruct and It can start anew. An epic war between the living and the dead ensues. Emily plays the title character on stage.

Emily designed the world she and her band (Rich Juzwick, Kyle Mayer and Aaron Hoover) bring to life on stage, including costumes, choreography, sets, etc. The band has toured with & opened festivals for Rob Zombie, Marilyn Manson, Slipknot, Mudvayne and others across Europe and the United States.

"Glass Animals" is about the disillusionment of connection and the realization of loss. The title character, September, feels this consistently throughout the books. Moreover this feeling is a universal one that the listener will surely find relatable. The music has a haunting tonality to it which reinforces the nature of the lyrics. The drawn out melodic guitars mimic the vocal melodies and add to the melancholy feel of the song. The entire composition tips its hat to the Deftones, one of Emily's favorite bands. 

The artwork contains the characters created by Emily and depicted by Image/ Top Cow Comic Book Artist Summeye Kesgin.

Description: My name is Butch…I produce under the name OddKidOut. I’ve been making music my whole life, and I tend to have the most fun when I’m blending genres together or just making weird shit. I made this song at 5 in the morning. I had three homies over who all fell asleep on the couch in my studio, so I was producing with the volume super low (I usually have it cranked all the way the fuck up). I think the mood of the song came from the feeling of producing in that environment; dark, stealthy and ambient. I realized the next day when I listened back to the track, that it needed some vocals to tie it all together. I sat and thought about some artists I thought would work well, but my mom called me in the middle of my brainstorming session. We chatted for a while and she was fake singing walking around the house, and it sparked an idea. What if I sampled my mom? She’s my best friend and her voice is quite good, so I made her take a selfie video singing some words I thought would fit the track “WHAT ABOUT ME?”. She sent the video to me and 30 minutes later, I had sampled it and made the track you’re all hearing today 🤘🏼

Different Way is a brand new track that I recorded specifically for my first Sound.xyz release and was performed, arranged, and mixed by myself and mastered by Genzo Rubin. It will also, subsequently, be the first track that I upload to DSPs under the Weinbagz moniker. I started my journey as a full time producer and my journey into web3 at roughly the same time in early 2021. I remember back to when I was thinking seriously about what being a producer/songwriter would actually look like. While there was always the possibility of getting attention and eyes on my music, I did not see a path to being able to feed myself from my work. Enter web3. Over the past 2 years, I’ve created more financial freedom for myself than I ever could have hoped for with going strictly the traditional route with music.

I’ve also been trying to figure out how to start integrating a web2 presence alongside my presence in web3, because I do believe in my music and I know that distribution is very limited when looking at web3 and NFTs. So, when I’m referring to a “Different Way”, or finding “Our Own Way”, this is the dynamic I’m referencing. I’m always looking for the intersection of music, tech, and audience. So merging my Sound genesis along with my Spotify genesis only made sense.

To further marry these two worlds, I will also be including the name of the Golden Egg winner in the track title when uploading to DSPs (unless they express not to be included). I figure it’s another way to take the fans on the journey with me and feature the true supporters.

Thanks for listening and reading. Much love,

Weinbagz

This was the first ever track I fully self-produced that didn't sound like a basicbish beat. It was also the first music I made after completely abandoning & deleting my old artist project. Something awakened, literally over night. The Talking Palm Tree was essentially the official doula for the birth of ALYSS and the first offering from my upcoming Answers EP (track 1/5).

At the time of writing the lyrics, I was learning about the Lilith archetype in both astrological and mythological terms. Symbolically, Lilith represents everything natural, raw and untouched. She is the place of total freedom within each of us. The place we are unashamedly who we are without limitation, self-judgement or fear of what the world thinks. Energetically, she is the unconfined wild side we've locked away and after having caged myself creatively for so long, discovering her felt like a huge kick up the ass to all the blocks I’d built up inside.

The same way she initiated a dormant voice within me through 'The Talking Palm Tree’, it only felt right that she lay the ground for my genesis footstep into the terrain of web3. May this song activate a core essence within you. We see you <3 ♅

Description: From humble beginnings to the launch of our 100th episode, Show Me The Crypto has been a labour of love from day one. When we launched the podcast in late 2020, we didn’t know if we’d make it to 100 episodes, but we were determined to build a platform to educate and inspire others about the exciting world of cryptocurrencies and blockchain technology. Thanks to the support of our listeners and guests, we've been able to interview some of the most brilliant minds in the space, while staying true to our mission. With "The First 100" NFT collection, we're excited to celebrate this milestone with our community and reward our early supporters for joining us on this journey.

ROMderful is a 26 year old Music Producer, Guitarist, Bassist and Singer/Songwriter Based in Seoul, South Korea.
ROMderful fell in love with music at the young age of 6 from frequent Sunday visits to his local church, picking up Violin at 6 years old and having an obsession with Video Games, Video Game music, MTV and his dads CD and Cassette collection which mainly consisted of 70s-90s Jazz & Funk, 2000s RnB, Bossa Nova and Gospel among many others. ROMderful started uploading music to the internet in 2012 and caught the attention of many during the Soundcloud golden era of 2015-2018 which allowed him to travel the world and produce for many heavy hitters in the industry such as Jean Deaux, Kehlani, Duckwrth, DEAN, SIRUP, Lute, Phonte, Little Brother, Kyle Dion to name a few.
ROMderful describes his music as “The Rainbow you could see in space if it was possible” which matches his colourful persona and love for 2000s aesthetics from Cartoons to Clothing and Video Games.
This song “WHY WAIT?” is inspired by ROMderful’s decision to move to Seoul, South Korea during the peak of the pandemic in mid 2020 and to take the jump into the unknown and try something so drastically new which was exciting and scary but ultimately one of the greatest choices he made and it would never happen if he didn’t get out of his own way.

I've always been keen to drop on this lovely platform and when Sound got in touch it felt right to put this club-friendly banger out.

"Depend On You" is an intimate and provocative R&B track by the multi-talented artist, Lexy Panterra. With her distinctive voice and impressive dance skills, Lexy has garnered a massive following on social media and has become a force to be reckoned with in the music industry.

The song is being released in two unique versions, Pt.1 and Pt.2. While Pt.1 is a slow and sultry track, Pt.2 is a high-energy electronic remix that will make you want to dance the night away. What's more, Pt.2 will be released exclusively as an NFT through the innovative platform Sound XYZ, making it a one-of-a-kind collectible item for fans of Lexy and electronic music.

In "Depend On You," Lexy sings about the intense connection she shares with her lover, but instead of relying on clichéd metaphors and generic lyrics, she uses vivid imagery and poetic language to convey the raw passion and emotion of the relationship. The lyrics are both sensual and vulnerable, exploring the complexities of love and intimacy in a refreshingly honest way.

Overall, "Depend On You" is a bold and innovative track that showcases Lexy's talent as a singer, songwriter, and producer. With its two unique versions and exclusive NFT release, it's a must-listen for fans of R&B and electronic music alike.

Free Love is my attempt to (sonically) open up the hearts of the world. it’s a “love bomb” if you will.  we aren’t just captives to the power that be.  Art, especially music, is extremely powerful and should be treated as so. 

The song has little to do with the original meaning of the phrase, or just me saying “go fuck everybody.”  it’s an invitation to feel the ever present frequency of love. i’ve been feeling the need to remind myself and others that love reigns supreme - we often get comfortable with the ill ways of the world and accept them. 

while working on this song, I was around a bunch of older musician guys (well vetted producers/session players known well in the la music scene). They talked about the hippy/60s era - which kind of turned to shit.  and they loved the track but were saying “free love man? we’ve tried that”. I wanted to repurpose the phrase and bring new context (instead of people rolling around in mud).  

The world is in a dark place with human rights, threats of war, confusion, etc. to me it could use a dose of positive energy.  

enjoy Free Lizzy.

While the beat is very lively and funky, the opening hook i mention how money, drugs, and lust where all I needed to breathe at one point. I was moving blindly towards false hope and falling into cycles of pain and struggle. Web3, music, therapy, and friends/family/real love is what helping me slowly climb out of that whole and realize my true worth.

This song was also funded to creation by @CXY aka my friend CY. he is an absolute legend and i have a dream of playing Coachella with him and reshaping the relationship dynamic between an artist and a collector here in web3. We’re here to tell a story and be dynamic time capsules of our experiences and it’s possible to keep encapsulating our journey as so. Ask for what you want and you will receive. There is a lot of times in 2022 where I almost felt like I needed to step back from music and give up.  Dutchy and a bunch of people helped me stay focused and remind me of my true power which allowed for transcendence into this piece today. no? Of course there's levels to it, can't give energy where it's not reciprocated...but I like buying my girl flowers. I like taking care of her. Let's normalize simping. Let's humanize it. It doesn't make you less of a man or woman. It takes courage to love."

“My California” is an indie rock/singer songwriter ode to being fallen out of love with; To being tossed aside, to that feeling of helplessness when an abrupt end falls into your lap. Joffe states: “My partner and I had planned a trip to California, but as our relationship began falling apart, the entire state of California was overridden with the tragedy of the wildfires. My sister lived there at the time, and I remember trying to convince her to get out before it got too bad, while simultaneously mourning the romantic trip I had planned with my partner and everything that loss symbolized.”

“My California” falls somewhere between the first 2 stages of grief in a relationship: denial and anger. With this release, Joffe has uniquely brought in the emotion that comes with gay break ups to mainstream culture. It is not only liberating but intends to give many the power back that can be lost in a relationship.

“I hope it does the same for anyone else who has watched someone fall out of love with them. "

In celebrating my 34th birthday (March 9th, #PiscesGang!), I present the newest and third edition of the AbJonian Suite mixes, and maybe my favorite on to-date! It includes a couple of cameos from past drops of mine, as well as some new ones you may get a chance to collect in the near future (and it was my easiest mix yet, haha!)

But the main reason this is my favorite is that I finally found the right mix to dedicate to one of my idols, the late Jay Dee, aka J Dilla. The last track of the mix is a tribute to him and two of my favorite of his legendary sample chops and loops from both his Slum Village days and his Ruff Draft release, easily my most favorite of his ever.

On a more personal note, I just want to remind everyone that collects this and any of my drops how grateful I am for your support and contributions. As of late, since my father passed in 2020 during the pandemic, my plate has gotten a lot heavier, a lot more crowded, and I'm on my own in ways I didn't realize I could be by now. Financially, music NFTs have been a godsend, helped me take care of things in the wake of my father's passing, kept my family and I afloat as we adjusted to this new world we now live in. 

So, thank you all immensely for being here, appreciating what I have to offer with my music, and as always since I started this journey to follow in his footsteps, thank you, J Dilla 🤟🏽...

03 – "young and free"

To be young and free is a beautiful feeling. We have the world at our feet, and anything seems possible. Excitement and optimism engulf our minds, knowing that we have so much potential. Despite the obstacles that we may face along the way, we have the courage, carelessness and resilience to overcome them.

As someone who was thrown into the thick of it from such a young age, I always desired to gain my freedom back from fighting. This is how I felt when I found it for the first time.

02 – "my girl"

Love has, and always will be the most complex and confusing emotion in all of its joy and agony. We fall in love... we believe that it will conquer all... that nothing can come between us and the person we love. But, sometimes we fall for someone who feels right for us, instead of someone who is... and we end up hurting ourselves in the process.

We make mistakes, they make mistakes, and we have no clue how to handle the challenges that come with loving someone. We stick by our person through all of their mistakes because we want to believe something that simply isn't true. Hoping for a future that won't exist.

Young love is falling for someone we believe is perfect, despite the reality. That is the blessing of it. Learning from our mistakes, and growing into ourselves. Finding our ways in which we want to love and be loved. You can stick by the person you love, but never forget to stick by yourself first. 

You are always worthy of to love, and of loving.

01 – "growing up"

Growing up is a journey that we all must undertake, and it is undoubtedly the most beautiful and painful experience that life can offer us. It is a journey that takes us through the mountains and valleys of life, and it is one that shapes us into who we eventually become.

It shows us beauty in its delivery to us, a world of possibilities we never knew existed. It is a time when we discover our passions, interests, talents, and dreams for our future. We begin to understand the complexity of the world around us, and we develop a sense of empathy, belonging and compassion for what and who we coexist with.

However, it also shares with us such incredible pain. It is a time of change and uncertainty, and it is a time when we experience heartbreak, disappointment, and loss. We may lose more than we can imagine, and we must face difficult decisions and situations bordering on the unimaginable that challenge us to our very core.

Despite the pain and difficulty that it will bring, growing up is inevitable. We must learn to embrace the beauty and the pain of the journey, knowing that it is what shapes us into the people we want to be and are meant to be.

To all those who are growing up, I offer this as a reminder that you are not alone. You are on a journey that has been undertaken by countless others before you, and it is a journey that will continue long after you. Embrace the beauty and fight through the pain of it all. It is the most precious and valuable experience that life can offer.

- CARLIE -
We linked up over Instagram and started sending different ideas to each other and I think because our styles complimented one another so nicely the song just came together really naturally. I wrote this song about how I got so used to turbulence in my life, that when I finally found a state of calm I seemed to try and self sabotage all the time. It was almost as if I didn’t know how to sit in that comfortable safe space, or didn’t feel like I even deserved it. I love being able to exercise emotions through writing songs, it's super cathartic and way cheaper than therapy!

She was down from the start so we simply went for it. I showed her a wip's playlist I had, and she was like "send this one!" (this was march 2021). Vocals were spot on from the start. Track originally was more "trappy" but then started mutating and became a mix between house and trap and baile. 
I really wanted to get this one released, hope you all love it!

This song is about being drawn to someone or something even though it may not be the best choice for oneself. This may not mean the situation is necessarily bad, but more so speaks to the part of you that knows it isn’t exactly the best thing for you. Experiencing this blissful feeling can be conflicting because deep down you are aware that it is not a sustainable situation. It also may not always feel like it makes sense to challenge this feeling, especially when it provides momentary joy, peace, and happiness. But sometimes we get lost within someone or something and fall in love with comfortability rather than the thing itself.

In 2021 we wrote an album and filmed a documentary called, "Islanders". (islandersfilm.com)

In 2022 we released the album and documentary via Kamikaze Dogfight and Gravitas Ventures. We toured the music and film all over the country and capped it off with a premiere in our East Hollywood neighborhood in Los Angeles. Segnon pulled up. 

We've admired Segnon's musicality and commitment to his craft since meeting him. He showed interest in working on something together and was in particular excited by our project, "Islanders". 

Our song "Home" was originally written with the intent of having a hip-hop verse. We posed the idea and Segnon jumped at it; correction, he crushed it. 

The song is about constantly redefining what "Home" means as we navigate life and death. More specifically, it's about a soul that hasn't found a resting place.

"Home" (Segnon Remix) is available on all streaming services and is intended to be played LOUD.

We're rewinding the calendar back to 2000, a year before the 1st generation iPod was available! Better Days was originally released on 12" single 23 years ago on underground West London label People Records. I'd just released my debut international major label album and was experimenting with ways to fuse my love for jazz with my love for soulful dancefloor tunes. It's been the theme of my whole career, sometimes leaning more to the jazz end, sometimes more to the beats end, but consistently searching for different ways to balance the two worlds. Now days, it's not an unusual combination at all, but back then.. ? - sacrilege to some and the freshest vibes for others. 

At the time I had an MPC2000, Fender Rhodes and Roland JP8080 synth module. I made the framework for the track and went into studio in Auckland, NZ to add some friends to the track - scat vocal vibes by Thomas Stowers, then a very young up and coming R&B singer; bass courtesy Chip Matthews, who would go on to be the low end theorist for NZ Pacifican-Soul star Che Fu; trumpet laced by my mentor and elder, and to this day one of my favorite trumpet players on the planet, Kim Paterson (Kim and I played so much acoustic jazz together but always jumped at the chance to join me on anything with beats); and Nick Gaffaney adding some tasty jazz brushes on drum kit - Nick would go on to found Cairo Knife Fight, an astounding 2 man rock band. The lineup alone is a memorable cross section of NZ music talent at the turn of the century. 

Influenced by the sounds I was hearing spun in clubs - from Jazzanova and Compost Records to Phil Asher, Roy Davis Jr and others, along with my perennial love for jazz legends like Miles, Better Days captured a little bit of all these, melting them into a jazz-fueled slab of wax that I was immensely proud to have released on one of the most forward thinking labels anywhere at the time.

Here we are now, over 2 decades later, and Better Days is the final drop of our $BUYBACK Emerald series - celebrating the past, the journeys we make and the fun we have along the way. Bringing that pre-iPod music to a blockchain here n now n forever...

“I’m Like That” was written by multi-platinum producer CJ Baran (Melanie Martinez, Panic at the Disco, Carly Rae Jepsen) Catherine Grace Garner aka SLAYYYTER and Marikah Baran (Voice of CUDDLES)
The song began as an orphan demo CJ and Catherine made in 2019. Once CJ and Marikah created CUDDLES with CG Artist Nicolas Brunet, they knew with some re-writing, it could be the perfect track for this mall goth stuffed animal cat with abandonment issues. The main elements of the track are the chopped and screwed Gregorian choir sample, the SH-2 synth bass and an 808 kit with some hair metal inspired guitars in the post chorus’. Dark fairytale gone hip hop at the rock show.

We are DE-TÜ; An electronic dance music production duo from London - the home of the underground. We have always focussed the style of our music on what inspires us in the moment, however always home in on big bass lines and unique drum patterns.
We wrote ‘Air Time’ whilst on tour in New Zealand, and we feel it portrays the inspiration we took from the beauty of the country at the time.
The white noise you can hear throughout the whole song is a recording taken from a hike we did out in the mountains. It is hard to hear the fidelity of this sample as we used saturation to process the
overall sound of it, creating an overdriven white noise type sound,however if you listen closely you can hear the wind blowing and the rivers running. Being in New Zealand gave us the opportunity to work in various studios across the country. This meant playing with synthesizers we had never used before, which was heaps of fun. We managed to create and shape a dissonant pad sound which is used throughout the intro of the track. We used this same synthesizer to create the stab sounds in the drop, adding subtle but effective depth to the track.
The drums and bass were added in our usual fashion, chopping breaks and creating unique grooves to fit. This was the easy and fun part as it is generally a process we follow for most of our music. Saying this, we always seem to find new sounds to work with, adding to our unique style of production.

Liv Boeree is a former professional poker player, master of game theory, systems thinker, and keen understander of the world of complex systems and the human experience.

She also is one of the few people out there in the world teaching about the lessons of Moloch— the study of human coordination—and is the reason why we wanted to have her on Bankless.

In the episode, Liv makes it clear how Moloch is more than an idea. Coordination and competition failures are happening in every aspect of our lives. Is crypto the solution?

Artwork derived from the timestamp [14:05 - 14:24]: *[Moloch] is the god of the unhealthy competition. It’s not the god of competition, competition is a neutral thing. it’s a form of an interaction, just like coordination or cooperation.* 

*Competition can be used for good. And it can can be used for bad. Moloch is when competition is used for ill.* 

10% of proceeds donated to Bankless DAO.

Who are Beachcrimes? We’re a duo from LA and we spent the last year making songs in hotel rooms around the world. Beachcrimes is the soundtrack to that adventure.
 
We made a lot of songs, and we’re excited to share them. All of them. This year we’re releasing 24 songs in 48 weeks. If we’re being real, it’s actually two albums – there’s AM and there’s PM. AM is the lite stuff, PM is the nite stuff. Think of it like the Summer Olympics and Winter Olympics, but for dance music.

"Melody (In My Head)" is the 4th of these 24 songs. It's the 2nd single from our AM album and we made it in Cabo San Lucas, Mexico. What would 75 & sunny sound like? We think it would sound like this. Heartbreak wrapped up in a tropical euphoric piano-house banger. If you happen to find yourself on a boat, pair to the bluetooth ASAP and be sure to give this one a spin. It will play just fine.

Next single will be out 2 weeks from today, and the following single 2 weeks after that.

Description:
GRLS DNT CRY started out as an instrumental I created live on my twitch stream this January, and later finished by added voice memos and calls from my phone. 

Lately I've been feeling extra fatigue trying to navigate the music industry as a solo female artist, so I created this track as an expression of the frustration and exhaustion of trying to excel in a man's world. I constantly deal with this pressure to act and portray myself in certain ways that aren't authentic in order to be accepted or taken seriously, and it weighs on me daily. While I have lots of hope for Web3 to provide equal opportunities and space for all types of artists and personalties, I get discouraged when I see the same patterns of the past repeating themselves.

~~~~~~~~
cover art by Jah.
production by Bradley Jughead Thomas
written / performed by Manic Phase and Mariana Makwaia
mixed / mastered by Manic Phase
~~~
WNA KNOW is the single and second track in a collaborative EP between Manic and Mari that explores themes of intimacy in the digital age. In our first session together, Manic pulled up this rnb fusion beat by grammy-nominated Jughead and we immediately started freestyling over it. We knew we wanted the main core of the song to be a question and when Mari hopped on the mic, the hook poured out. We finished the demo in our very first session together!

This song is about the struggles of modern-day relationships and the confused feelings that come up around love in a world where we're constantly connected but still feel isolated. Manic and Mari created alternate, slightly more toxic versions of themselves - two artists trying to navigate their personal and professional lives in the music industry. 

Looking forward: the full EP will be released on DSP's beginning of April, there will be an invite-only irl performance in LA and the tracks will soon be shopped around for syncs and licensing.

I wrote Memories (Teri yaad) to try and capture my favourite memories. I had a conversation with my wife recently, and she spoke about the time she scribbled on the 4 walls she grew up in, the horse rides by the beach she had with her grand mom right by her side making sure she did not fall off. My memories with my father and mother.. I felt I should just sing about them. So I just pictured myself sitting on a cliff looking at the stars, counting the light in the fullest moon, reminded of these times. 

In the second verse in my language, Hindi, I wonder how sometimes I miss certain people so much in my life, to the point that sometimes i find trouble sleeping, just missing them, or I am afraid for their health. What i would do when these people will not be around anymore? I guess i'd try my best put them back together with my thoughts and emotions, mentally trying to picture them and kind of make them real. But it never works right? Even if i had a thousand years, they would just be a memory. 
In my heart and my mind, I know. You and everyone and everything else will just be a memory.

Black Dave is feeling good. It’s really that simple. Taking up space and creating, the nonconformist musician, producer, rapper, visual artist, anime and streetwear enthusiast, and web3 innovator unapologetically thinks outside the box. He’d rather break them all open.

Here's how Black Dave describes “Feel Good,” his latest track:

"Sometimes you gotta remind the world that you’re the one not the two. 'Feel Good' is my reminder to y’all."

----

This is the second track from HIGH FREQUENCY Volume 1 — a compilation album curated by NOISE. 

Read our interview with Black Dave here: https://noisedao.mirror.xyz/b2ByTlc78Jns3YtgW3WB37O_hm-_XoueitXxlu34U_c

“Walking On A Dream” marks the producer and The Voice contestant’s 6th co-orchestrated outing. Mixing new sonics from the current tech house/edm moment & 2000s drums; this track is the first release in the 2023 calendar year for Gianni Blu.

“Sleepless” is the birth child of “Dutch Melrose”. The song that started everything for me. It’s about the 2am thoughts that keep you up at night when you first fall in love. The overwhelming feeling that there’s no turning back. That even if you tried, you couldn’t shake the feeling that you’re in too deep. Nostalgic, effortless, and hypnotizing. “Sleepless” is the all too familiar feeling when we decide to let our walls down and realize that the other person we love has become our everything.

Written, produced, redcorded: Matt Monday
Co-produced, mix, master: Black Dave
Keys, Strings: Jonathan Lovett
Guitar: Thomas Kenney
Artwork: Matt Monday

The Breaks is an audio journey that introduces my hometown North Charleston, SC. It begins with the sounds of banter and outdoor activity, followed by strings that resemble the feeling of the summer warmth in the air. As we progress through the day we are met by upbeat experiences and various encounters that further provide details into the nature of the environment. The song ends on a guitar solo that spirals into the later parts of the day as we are met with the countless obstacles such as opposition, uncertainty, and the law, …these are the breaks.

yo, we're dan & alex. we're best friends from a small town in upstate new york and we've been producing together since 2018. this is our first solo artist release on sound & very excited to be a part of the web3 community. 

highscore is the first song we've ever entirely produced, written & recorded ourselves. we're extremely proud of this song & its message. the song is about the struggle of creating & constantly trying to make something of yourself. the lyrics are very personal to us & we're excited for this song in particular as it's the first of many 100% original work. 

highscore shows our unique perspective on the creative
process & how we push each other to succeed in music,
making it the perfect introduction to cudos.

Is the CIA spying on crypto? 

Annie Jacobsen is an investigative journalist and author writes about war, weapons, government secrecy, and national security. 

She’s written books on the secrets of Area 51, and the Pentagon’s military science R&D efforts over the decades.

The 2023 crypto movement is sufficiently large enough that it has certainly attracted the attention of every intelligence agency out there. 

We want to learn about how the world’s intelligence agencies might have or are interacting with the crypto community. 

Annie shares her thoughts and answers our question: is the CIA spying on crypto?

Artwork generated from [14:19 - 14:39] “With almost certaintity I would say, that the world of cryptocurrency is looked at by the intelligence community as a non-state actor….Which is a little bit dangerous, or a little bit adversarial for those of you in that community.” 

10% of proceeds are being donated to Annie’s son, a young crypto advocate exploring the space.

H E A V Y

   This is a somewhat vulnerable song for me. I wrote it after my wife and I experienced a miscarriage late in her pregnancy. Shortly afterwards I had to leave her back home in Virginia to do some work out in California. Sitting on the balcony of my hotel in Cali, It seemed like everything hit me at once and I felt guilty for being 3000 miles away. 

I began to write which has always been my form of self therapy. I ran through the ringer of emotions including sadness, anger, and confusion. Thus these verses were born. I sat on this song for a while until my friend Jay Real provided this hook. I felt like it went perfectly with my verses, and the melody took me back to that time.

Life really is a rollercoaster and we have to understand that. Always pray for good times, but understand that there will be bad times so pray for the strength to deal with them.

Following up on her 2022 single “Yeehoo!” Lauren Juzang returns on March 1st,  with her second single “It’ll Be (Video Game Song)” !

The song “It’ll Be” describes the brutal emotional process of evaluating if a relationship is still serving you or not. Naturally, there’s a back and forth that occurs, but ultimately, the disappointment settles and growth can begin from it. Lauren’s ethereal voice and words of contemplation are accompanied by electronic synths that weave with acoustic guitar and banjo to create a track that is completely singular.

“I got to play around with a lot of melodies and rhythms on this one,” Lauren says about the writing process. “Sonically, it’s a bit more experimental of a direction that I haven’t ventured into before. My roommate also said it sounds like a video game, hence the title.” “It’ll Be (Video Game Song)” was co-written and produced by Aidan Spiro at Heavy Duty Studios in LA.

This release marks the end of a 4 year hiatus for the long term collaboration between LA artist Alec King and Swedish producer Danrell. Their music was best described by Indie Shuffle: ”I know I like the track, but I can't quite put my finger on why”. BAFLID combines Danrell’s sun-soaked beat with influences from the French 60’s Yé-Yé pop movement with melancholic vocals from Alec about how being alone feels like you’re drowning, but ironically the longer you are alone, the easier it is to breathe.

it’s crazy to think about how Roy and i had never collaborated on an artistic level until now, and all of the synergies that led us here. it felt like we were always just an arm’s length apart, operating in the same circles, innovating in similar ways, both navigating the same spaces. after a few oddly serendipitous coincidences exchanged between us, it seemed like the universe was leaving signs everywhere that we should know each other, and beyond that, create together.

i’ve been a big fan of all of Roy’s creative endeavors for a while, and being in the studio with him was kinda magical. we wrote Lost the first time we sat down in a studio together, after talking for hours about the ebbs and flows of the music industry, and even more so, the ebbs and flows of simply just existing. we shared in a lot of the same pain, question marks, internal battles around decision making, relationships, and feeling like sometimes even when you thought you put the whole puzzle together, when you take a step back, a few pieces might still be lost somewhere in the ether. 

Lost is the first of what i hope to be many collaborations with Jagwar Twin, as two artists aiming to push the boundaries of what it means to exist at the intersection of digital and physical, tradition and innovation, storytelling and experimentation. but most importantly, as two people taking leaps of faith in the world with no set expectations. 

hold on tight to this one ;)

_________________________________________________________________

Jagwar Twin: Much of the world feels lost right now. The shifting human landscape can be difficult to navigate as we are bombarded with external influences. All these external influences are pointing each of us to something in ourselves that we seem to have lost or forgotten. Annika and I are both navigating this new digital landscape and so it's no surprise that this song was birthed from it. I think in many ways we are all coming to grips with the reality that what seems black or white is usually neither, and simultaneously, both.

Hi Sound! My name is demotapes, I’m a producer and artist based in San Francisco. I’m also in a duo called Cassette Tapes, and I started the demotapes project at the beginning of 2020. This is my first drop on sound, thank you for being here :) 

Living in San Francisco, I often feel like an outsider in the music industry. This is something that I embrace- I feel like this isolation helps me to feel creatively free. 2022 was the most creative year of my life, and the biggest shift for me was getting back to writing music with my friends- even if it was over discord calls. Creating memories and shared experiences around songs helped me fall back in love with the creative process and connect with the music in a way that I never have before. 

I wrote this song in San Francisco with my friend Sam (pluko). He came to visit me and we spent a few days just creating in my basement studio. The bulk of the song came together in a single day- the idea just sort of poured out of us. To me, this song feels like the perfect embodiment of what it’s like to create art with your friends- it’s hopeful, nostalgic and fun. I hope you guys love it too <3

Renowned DJ and Producer BIJOU returns to the release radar with his first official release of the year, joining forces with rising Australian-based talent Zaerd for their latest sonic masterpiece ‘Saint Tropez’. Marking an exciting milestone in the up-and-coming DJ/producer’s musical journey, the high-energy collaboration serves as his return to Do Not Duplicate Recordings since making his debut with ‘Put The Mood Down’ alongside Rob Upland in April 2021, which landed them an official remix courtesy of BIJOU himself. Heavily influenced by sounds of G-House, Bass House, and Future House, ‘Saint Tropez’ doubles as a full circle moment for Zaerd, as he links up with the DND Recs label boss for their first official collaboration. A strong contender for the next “song of the summer’’, ‘Saint Tropez’ is due for release on February 24 via Do Not Duplicate Recordings.

BIJOU and Zaerd’s ‘Saint Tropez’ is a vibrant offering that boasts a punchy bassline, upbeat synth work, and a rich, textured vocal cut. A hard-hitting house music coup de maître, the enthralling production features high-octane sensibilities, pulsating drops, and atmospheric energy. Crafted with the dancefloor in mind, ‘Saint Tropez’ serves a transmittable fire throughout the ears, leaving listeners wanting to dance their way to Saint Tropez. Offering exuberant four-on-the-floor beats throughout its entirety, ‘Saint Tropez’ serves as a stellar addition to BIJOU and Zaerd’s discographies right in time for the warm months ahead.

Description:
The song tells the story of two different lovers - the player who never seems to be happy alone and constantly falls in and out of love, and the played who pours everything into their relationships without first learning to love themselves.

I saw those around me chasing love in all the wrong places and putting their all into relationships without first loving themselves. 'Take Your Time' reminds us that self-love is essential to finding happiness and fulfillment.

Through this song, I hope to inspire my listeners to embrace the journey towards self-love and to find the courage to break free from toxic situationships.

When I’m with you, 
The gnashing of my shadow rests, 
In its place is a small glimmer. 
A candle that burns twice as bright, 
As twin flames dance throughout the night. 
When I'm with you,
I don’t fear us, 
I fear having something to lose.
I don’t fear the light, 
I fear the silhouettes it casts across the room. 
As much as I fear myself, 
I love you.

Italian electronic producer and artist msft has found his groove, and with it is ushering in a new wave of bass music. 

Born and raised in a small town outside of Venice, Italy, msft started making music influenced by European electronic music culture in 2014. “I grew up listening to OG progressive house and electro house artists such as Hardell and the old heads, and used to dream about European festivals such as Tomorrowland,” says msft. Emulating festival acts, he initially focused his production style on anthemic melodies, hooks, and catchy rhythms before shifting gears to dive into bass music. “It didn't take me long to realize I wanted to challenge myself into making more complex rhythms and more complex sound design,” says msft. “I transitioned away from progressive house and electro house music to bass music, and that's when I started msft as a project in 2016.”

Here's how msft describes his latest track, “with me”:

This song has had a fun development, I started by writing chords and messing around with bpms to see in which area the break loop I made performed the best. After creating the first section I decided to completely switch the vibe and go for something heavier. Being able to combine melodic elements with more ""modern"" bass sounds has been super fun.

The structure of the song aims to go straight to the point of having that vocal hook as glue between the first and the second section.

-- 
This is the first track from HIGH FREQUENCY Volume 1 — a compilation album curated by NOISE. 

Read our interview with msft here: https://noisedao.mirror.xyz/iBBXHFAC9ElpOU8EiirRe31fMdHQyAmfcJEe9DaVAdE

Reasons is the next saga of my love music. Its an unreleased song that marks another transition from hyper focused music on living a bachelor life I found myself on a journey of inner and outer love. During this process we got my most recent EP “Wake Up” signaling it’s time to wake up to that love that has been in search. “Reasons” is standing up for myself through the music for the first time without being too aggressive or dismissive to my audience about the subject.

It’s one of my favorite records because of the upbeat tune that is carried through the production by OTP. This is my very first audio NFT as I’ve sold many of visual NFT’s in my past. This song very well could’ve been on my last EP, but I’m glad to share the new with Soundxyz.

"sellout" is the first single off our EP "quarter-life crisis". it was made in early 2022, when we were both 25 and feeling a bit overwhelmed with some aspects of adulthood - being tight on money, having bills to pay, the instability of our careers, wondering if we’re “selling out” to feel a bit more comfortable, worrying about getting older and running out of time.

The first Bankless episode on AI… and we went deep down the rabbit hole. 

This conversation with Eliezer Yudkowsky sent us into an existential crisis as we discussed ChatGPT and the new generation of AI, digital super-intelligence, the end of humanity, and if there’s anything we can do to survive.

According to Eliezer, we’re already too late. Humanity is doomed. 

Artwork generated from the timestamp [59:32-59:51] Nobody knows how to create any good AIs at all. The problem isn’t that we have 20 good AIs and that somebody finally builds an evil AI. The problem is that the first powerful AI is evil, nobody knows how to make it good, and then it kills everybody before anybody can make it good.” 

10% of proceeds donated to Eliezer's MIRI Foundation.

Living in the blinks between timezones, I’ve documented the last 10 years of my life through 1000+ microsongs – threads of transient nostalgia captured on tape.

Now trading nature immersion for urban hustle, I’m knitting together the last decade via release. “Old Friends New Cities” is a collaboration with photography platform Analogue People, and 10 photographers (5 men and 5 women), from around the world.

Curating a collection of 10 photos paired with my music – Analogue People has juxtaposed the realities of nomadic city life over a longing familiar to the metropolitan among us – a return home; to nature and to our roots.

Imagine a Yogi meditating in the bush, caught up in ecstatic meditation. So highly enamored by chanting a mantra over and over again that when a passerby tries to get the Yogi’s attention, the Yogi just continues chanting.

One may feel disrespected or as we say in Jamaica you would feel like the Yogi “styled you”. In Jamaica "Style" can mean u have style as in you are unique, you have your own way of doing things. Another meaning is someone “styled u” as in they curved you, ignored you or deceived you etc.

In this example though, the yogi isn’t “styling” the passerby. It's simply the yogi’s style to chant for extended periods without interruptions. The passerby understands what is happening as well and sees the Yogi means no disrespect. The passerby actually feels welcomed and greeted by the love and bliss that the Yogi radiates.

 “I’m so high that when people say Hi, I don't have to say Hi back” 

The aforementioned image of the Yogi inspired these lyrics. The Yogi is so high, or rather so deep, in meditation that they don't need to say Hi. The effect of the meditation says “Hi” for him/her, it speaks for itself, it speaks love, peace, prosperity, forgiveness. Everyone who encounters the Yogi feels the love and doesn't take the Yogi not acknowledging them as an offense. 

In the song when I say “I’m so high that when people say Hi, I don't have to say Hi back” I’m saying, I’m so focused that my full involvement in the creative ‘work’ speaks of how precious my time is and my obsession has nothing to do with ignoring anyone, it’s about following through on the commitments in my life.

It’s about prioritizing the quality of our focus and the sacrifices that may have to be made to achieve our goals. Let your work ethic speak for itself. Regardless of the distractions that may arise, we must remain unwavering in our efforts. This requires frequent check-ins with our Self, our objectives and how we are investing our time.

‘Meditate’ is a call to think deeply on how we want to contribute to the ecosystem at large. To become fully engaged in actualizing the vision we have for our Self. To commit to the daily work and the healthy habits that our purpose requires. To become clear with the people in our life about the value of our time. To be immersed in doing things that we value, with our time.

The song on SoundXYZ has a different arrangement and mix than the song in the music video, which gives both a unique element. 

‘Meditate’ is song the with most Patois (Jamaican Slang) i've released in web3. I included the lyrics in the description and provided the Visuals with Lyrics as the free mint. A preview of the Music Video can be found in my pinned tweet.

Welcome to PIN001.

Every month I will be going to a new location with a friend and making a song with them. 

Whatever demo we have at the end of the trip will be minted on Sound, along with other activations across Web3. No additional edits, no overthinking. my dear friend, mentor and collaborator Phil Asher aka Phlash aka restless soul passed away unexpectedly during the pandemic. one of the standard bearers for soulful house production and DJing and one of the pioneering progenitors of the music we made that became known as broken beat, Phlash's contribution to culture and community is immeasurable. we met when I first went to London and were in studio collaborating from the very next day, leading to a deep friendship and countless musical collaborations together. 

when he passed, this was one of the tracks I made with him front and top of mind. a key venue for the broken beat scene was Velvet Rooms in central london, a space where we'd share music that had just been made that day or week, music that challenged the status quo of dancefloor and embraced the entire history of black music in an almost unnervingly forward-thinking way. the party was called co-op and Phlash was one of the OG founders. in reflecting on his passing and creating in that zone, naming this track Crush Velvet made all the sense to me. 

frenetic break beats, lush soulful harmony, metric modulations and moogy synth melodies... Crush Velvet paints a picture of sci-fi space samurai, sword fighting while dancing around each other... otherworldly realms of simultaneous celebration and battle. 

rip Phlash !

Description:
Can’t Help But Think About you is a song I wrote with EMME, a super talented artist/songwriter and friend of mine, at my studio in the west side of Los Angeles. It was our first time hanging in person in over a year, and after taking a bit of time to catch up and going on a walk with my dog, I played her a little idea I had started, which was mainly this nostalgic-feeling drone sound and a bright synth pluck. She immediately started hearing melodies for it, the very first one which became the opening verse’s “I’m out of place, out of reasons why…”

From there, I stripped it all back to piano chords, and we began honing in on the story we really wanted to tell. The song is essentially about being caught in the riptide of circular thinking around a failed relationship, one that had incredible qualities and feels like it should be worth saving, but that for a variety of reasons just wasn’t meant to work out. We intentionally left both the music and lyrics open-ended and fairly general, because in this type of relationship, the details are ultimately unimportant. One can rehash and rationalize over and over, but the only way to get to spiritual freedom is to accept your present, and embrace the future as it comes.

As an artist and producer who straddles the divide between dance and pop music, I’m constantly searching to create music that feels like a release, but that also encapsulates the universal human experience in a way that’s simple and resonates in the heart. I’m super proud of this one and am excited to give it to the world, to connect with all the other beautiful people who understand this bittersweet experience. Our heart is the most sensitive instrument in the universe — the secret to elevated consciousness is learning to appreciate that it is capable of playing both the most tragic and most joyful melodies.

Description:
I make folk music, which I know isn’t necessarily a well-represented genre in the Web3 space. That makes a lot of sense to me. Web3 represents the new, the cutting-edge, the very limits of what we can create digitally, and in many ways, folk is the opposite of that – a callback to the sound of our parents’ or even grandparents’ time. It’s organic and analog and acoustic. But it is also approachable, accessible, and above all, communal. If that doesn’t mirror the general ethos in the Web3 music community, then call me crazy. 

“Flight to JFK” is my first drop ever. I recorded it in one take, just me in the studio with my guitar, and it marks the first song in Somewhere Along the Trail, Vol. 1, which is part of a three-volume project I’m going to be releasing this year. You’ll find sprinkles of James Taylor, dashes of Simon & Garfunkel, and a big ol’ helping of Jackson Browne. The song is about spending quality time with someone you love who lives across the country. Simple but true!

Somewhere Along the Trail is going to consist of three volumes with three songs each, with the production getting progressively more and more complex in each tripartite release. The title comes from one of the last things my Uncle Jerry said to me before he passed away last year. “In another life, Theo,” he said, “if we were both 25-years-old, we’d be best friends. Somewhere along the trail.” 

Stay tuned for the following drops, with lots of fun surprises along the way!

Description:
"Close Friends" is a tongue-in-cheek homage to social media culture and is the first original single from BOY2K sliding into your DMs. BOY2K is our - Boy Untitled and Boy Apocalypse - new, collaborative dance project; a forward-thinking experiment in the connective power of dance music. After meeting at a show in 2019, we began making music together and deepening our friendship. Shortly after, we decided to pack up our homes in LA and build our studio in Mexico City to develop the project. While the track is full of percussive movement and memorable riffs about the all-too-familiar woes of pursuing your favorite internet crush - it’s also a celebration our of friendship and sonic marker of the beginning of this new adventure. We created the VIP for specifically for one of our first DJ sets in CDMX at [sic], a weekly queer party in the heart of the city and the LGBTQ+ community. We hope you enjoy bouncing this nasty beat as much as we do. Thank you for supporting our journey together. Now, let’s vibe!

From Mark: "There are so many reasons that Grant and I decided to make "Close Friends" our first single as BOY2K, not least of which is how this track socially encapsulates the joy and freedom we experience when we write music together. There is a creative ease that we both feel with one another. And there is a tangible excitement that we share when creating dance spaces for EVERYONE. To us, "Close Friends" embodies the idea of "Music For The People" in its use of world sounds and the hilariously relatable experience of someone sliding into your DMs. It's fun, it makes you move and honestly makes us LOL when we sing it. It feels like a bop you can get down to with your bestie. Just like us when we made it."

From Grant “The “Close Friends” VIP is a darker, more intense take on the more poppy original track, but in a way, it’s still about the same thing: friendship. For Mark and I, the dark, smokey back rooms of a club have often been the backdrop for our relationship both as friends and as creative partners. We’ve both spent many a late night dancing our way through the discotecas of Mexico City and the underground raves of LA. In a way, there’s a sense of humor about the remix that is meant to channel some of the most insane nights we’ve shared - the remix combines the sounds of pots and pans, detuned leads, and VERY processed vocals to channel that feeling of being out of your mind at a great techno show. We plan to use VIPs throughout our various releases to show either a darker or lighter side of the same concept: to keep expanding the sonic definition of the new dance floor we are building.

Description:
Living in the blinks between timezones, I’ve documented the last 10 years of my life through 1000+ microsongs – threads of transient nostalgia captured on tape.

Now trading nature immersion for urban hustle, I’m knitting together the last decade via release. “Old Friends New Cities” is a collaboration with photography platform Analogue People, and 10 photographers (5 men and 5 women), from around the world.

Curating a collection of 10 photos paired with my music – Analogue People has juxtaposed the realities of nomadic city life over a longing familiar to the metropolitan among us – a return home; to nature and to our roots.

"I had been writing a lot during covid lockdown.  After a nice morning surf session I came back to the studio and came up with two parts on the TonePad app on my iPhone.  Thought it was pretty cool and added some drum loops, some Moog Taurus basslines and some synth bass. Sent it to Bayliss asking if he could add anything or work his magic.  He did." 

- Ryan Stasik

"During the lockdown we were sending musical ideas back and forth. Ryan sent his demo and I immediately knew there was real potential. I recorded some vocals over his parts and then a few months later I was messing around with what is now the chorus section.  Once I spliced the two together I knew that we had just finished a new song, one that doesn’t sound like anything else we were working on at that time."

- Brendan Bayliss

ABOUT THE RELEASE:

Welcome to the Fever Dream sessions.

The songs from this session have an energy that came from being pent up and isolated for over a year during lockdown, to being around each other again and playing music in the same room. And it wasn't just any room either, our friend Darrell Thorp invited us to record this 3-track session in the gorgeous rooms at The Village in LA.

After an anxious year of pandemics, covid variants, personal health scares, and all the other bad juju the quarantine era brought, this session was a perfect oasis to break the anxiety that had built up since the lockdown began.

That's why the joyous energy had us buzzing. How cool was it to be around each other again, playing music with the best people, in the best place? Hopefully, some of that good vibe comes through in the music, and that the songs will help release the feverish anxiety into joyous catharsis.

Track 2 of 3: The Last Time (Heavy)

The lyrics for this song come from a collaboration with Edson's longtime friend Steady Holiday (Andrea "Dre" Babinski). While writing together, the two began riffing off the neurosis of feeling like the world is ending, and how we regular people can't do much about it...which is a strange helpless-but-kind-of-relieved-of-the-responsibility feeling. It's that dichotomy that the song tries to ride; burdened but upbeat, feeling heavy but willing to dance with what we have left.

Description:
We’re a duo from LA and we spent the last year making songs in hotel rooms around the world. Beachcrimes is the soundtrack to that adventure.
 
We made a lot of songs, and we’re excited to share them. All of them. This year we’re releasing 24 songs in 48 weeks. If we’re being real, it’s actually two albums – there’s AM and there’s PM. AM is the lite stuff, PM is the nite stuff. Think of it like the Summer Olympics and Winter Olympics, but for dance music.

"One Step" is the 3rd of these 24 singles. This is the most PM song we have. Built around a single vocal loop we wrote and recorded in Florence, this song proudly flies the flag of tech house - a genre that we respect and love. If you close your eyes, we hope you can feel the electricity of a 4am Italian club. Cuz we sure can.

Next single will be out 2 weeks from today, and the following single 2 weeks after that.

Description: my baby got an OF

A theme-song for the independent artist.

My mission with this song was to speak to those that question and challenge their existence in every sense of their being. There may be those that know this already, but just as a reminder, to reach success, whatever that word means, you must rid yourself of doubt and fear. Sometimes companionship and bet on yourself. All for the pursuit of happiness.

When we rid ourselves of limitations and take leaps of faith, those roads traveled are uniquely our own. It may be lonely and get dark at times, but one thing is for sure, finding that love, existing in it, whether external or self-love.

It's fuel, passion, and enough to help you reach fulfillment. 

In support of the independent artists on here, I know how challenging all of this truly is. The collector that wins the golden egg - will receive 10% of the primary sale. I encourage you to pay it forward and support more artists in this space by minting their MusicNFTs.

Thank You.

The beat for Godzilla was made some years back on the night that I totaled my first car. The black Chevy HHR was a graduation gift from my grandfather and it was a huge part of my life at the time. Mainly, it was my transportation to college every day and around that time I was starting to realize that I wouldn’t be enrolling in GSU for another semester. That particular night I was riding around with some friends on the way to rehearse for an upcoming show and I rear ended someone on the highway. The shock from the impact lasted well beyond leaving the site of the crash. There were so many emotions that I didn’t really know what to do with that night so I did what I knew how to do best: I made a beat.

Years later, I found that same instrumental sitting on my hard drive and realized how symbolic the whole situation was. The whole idea of going to college at the time was given to me by someone else, similar to the car. I knew I wasn’t doing what I wanted to do at that point in life yet I still forced myself to continue and take out loans for the sake of others around me but not myself. It all finally came to a head when higher powers took both things that had been given to me but since I ignored my intuition and accepted what I didn’t want for myself I also ended up losing the gift that I did want.

Reflecting on all of that I decided to put it in a song and what better way to challenge those emotions than to record on a beat that I made in that pivotal moment in life.

“Still Work” is the third single from my debut EP ‘Moments’. This song features Ty Dolla$ign and recent 2023 Grammy Winner, Muni Long.

This instrumental track was created by me and a few of friends who are also platinum level producers: Romano, Mike Woods, and TenRoc.

I’m excited that my genesis drop on Sound is going to be my biggest song to date!

Sleep Half of It is one of my favorite songs I’ve ever gotten to make because of how the production makes me feel. The way that the sounds delicately poke out at you from the beat under mine & Mick’s vocals always makes me smile when I listen back. Working with Mick on this track is really a dream come true for me as I’ve always been such a huge fan of his. From the moment I started making the beat for this song, I immediately heard his voice & flow over it and I knew that he was exactly what the song needed. I love the way our voices contrast each other and it was such a personal honor to be able to collaborate on a song with him.

Description: The day Parker and I wrote April (Eyes) was such a pivotal day in the direction for my new album. It really felt like a perfect reflection of how I was feeling in that moment. The second I got this one off my chest, the world of Bleach become so clear and attainable to me. I wanted this song to almost serve as a time capsule for that part of my life. The window opening and the train going over the bridge is the sound of my old Brooklyn apartment that we wrote this song in. At the end of the song, the window closes and that little moment stays there forever stuck in that period of time.

The version being released on sound is “Oxytocin” stripped back to its essence. It features simply a piano melody, a baseline, and layers of vocals. This is my most vulnerable song to date, I hope it strikes a chord within you.

Punk6529 is a pseudo-anonymous leader in the crypto space. 

He’s heavily focused on the world of NFTs and known for putting together extremely punchy and thoughtful Twitter threads, thinking about the world from first principles.

NFTs will represent every single digital non-fungible token that exists…and there are going to be a lot of them. Podcasts will be no different. 

Is Punk6529 the most bullish person in the world on NFTs?

In this episode, 6529 shares the benefits of using an NFT-backed pseudonym instead of your state name, why the “freedom to transact” is an essential human liberty we’ll lose without crypto, how the Metaverse is just a visualization layer of NFTs, and why NFTs are more important than DeFi…probably the most important thing crypto has produced.

I wrote this song about a guy that took advantage of my heart. Then I found a guy on hinge who didn't take advantage of my heart, and he happened to have good drum sounds, so he co-produced this song with me.

"ON MY OWN" is a song about understanding that wanting someone for them vs wanting someone for the idea of them you had in your head are two very different things. It's about realizing that they're not what you're missing but rather the feeling that you wanted them to give you.

I started Say You’re Mine on a cold “winter” night in LA a few years ago with some friends. We were chatting and hanging around at a session that was supposed to be wrapping up. I remember sitting on the floor near the little studio heater and listening to Adam, an amazing producer and friend, play the guitar loop. It didn’t take long for me to know where I wanted to go with the melody and lyrics. I had been writing a lot of angsty songs around that time and wanted to change the messaging, so I REALLY changed it up and started singing about love and rainbows… Check ⎷ 
But the second I started singing, I thought about my husband. There’s so much that we have been through together and I can feel our connection energetically. As we continued to write I really wanted to hone on the gentle love that is just one part of my intricate and beautiful relationship. A soft side that doesn’t rush, is patient, understanding, and sees the light in my lover. This song I dedicate to Scorch. Who will you dedicate it to to? 

Songwriters// Caly Bevier & Kayla Blackmon
Producer// Adam Kapit

If there's one thing that Web3 has taught me, it's that there is strength in vulnerability. I've always been the type to keep my needs to myself and figure out how to solve my problems on my own. In many instances, all while being the problem solver for everyone else. I've realized that pouring from an empty cup is a counterproductive practice and downright unhealthy. 

For those who don't know, I have been a full time creative since 2009. I rely heavily on my computer to bring my ideas to life. From graphic design, video editing, marketing and recording music, my Macbook pro is a critical tool in my creative process. Unfortunately, my current computer is on its last leg and I am in desperate need of a new one.

This is why I am launching this open edition mint for "War Games", with a goal of raising 1.9 ETH to fund the purchase of a new system with the specs that will be able to handle my current and future work load. By minting "War Games", you will not only be owning a piece of my of story told through art, but also enabling me to continue to bring my creative vision to life for the foreseeable future. 

I will be airdropping a special token called "The SunFlower That Grew" to the top 10 collectors of "War Games". This token is an art collaboration between myself with my the incredibly talented, SAIKO. 

"War Games" is ode to resilience and finding strength even while in the face of adversity. As a child my mother always used to tell me that I was covered by the higher power and that I am the sunflower that grew. At the darkest times I’ve found my way back to the light. I hope that this energy resonates with you.

Description:
In April of 2020, separated by an ocean and 3000 miles, both of us went into self-isolation. Physically, of course -- like everyone else. But also musically.

Turning inwards, we scoured the Refs instrumental vault for our most menacing, introverted and brooding soundscapes -- and proceeded to write 12 songs in 12 days. 2 years later, we offer up our debut album, "New Religion".

We wrote the title track for this album so quickly that we’re still having trouble wrapping our minds around what it means. This was an exercise in getting the hidden contents of our brain’s id out in recorded form.

The animated image we chose for artwork is a taste of an unreleased "New Religion" themed collectable project. Owners of our sound.xyz NFTs will get advanced access to the mint.

Blurred Lines is a song that was made at a pivotal point in my life. I had just moved to LA right before the pandemic and after months of not creating, I decided to break the cycle and make some new music. I came across Dav through a search for guitar loops on reddit and sent him the first demo to this song. 

Coincidentally, he happened to be 10 mins away from where I just moved to in LA and we’ve been locked in ever since. Blurred Lines is a really special song to me because it gave me the confidence to explore the world of what I’m capable of with my music.

Sometimes we give a lot of energy and time to people who aren’t true about their intentions and we feel that we have been played. However, in the end those people are really just playing themselves out of healthy friendships and kind lovers. PUNX is basically about telling someone to F*** off and letting toxic people go while also unapologetically and happily reminding them of what they are losing and what we are gaining.

The PUNX music video revolved around shooting on a green screen set. I utilized the green screen throughout the entire video as a tool for creating movement, motion, effort, and sweat, without actually going anywhere or accomplishing any distance. This mirrors the idea of putting effort into a relationship that goes unappreciated. The song is also about gaining freedom by saying F*** it and letting my unfiltered feelings guide the way. Green screen also provided an amazing opportunity to get whacky and surreal in post, like a dream - unfiltered. I then purposefully like to reveal the green screen as a comment on fakery and manipulation explored in the lyrics. Overall the visuals needed to reflect both the dark but fun sensibilities of the track.
