Description:
Deja Vu was my first record to cross 100k streams on any platform. 

This was an effort

More about PAISLEY....

In 2017, I had a thought, “patterns prevail”. It was derivative of a quote from my best friend and frequent collaborator, Sky Welkin, which read “passion prevails”. Sky is a talented cartoonist that embeds profound messages like this throughout his work.

During our college years, he’d often come by and draw while I made beats, this was our ghetto co-working era, and in these sessions we’d smoke, engage in discourse, and share ideas about the respective worlds we were building in our art. In fact, I was very much into doing something new each album, but Sky was the primary influence for me to get into world-building and having a particular sense of style that was cultivated over time.

In one of my college apartments, I decided that to let Sky use all of the walls in my room as a canvas - the few hundred dollars that I’d spend to have the room repainted when I moved was minuscule compared to the living art piece around me. Every so often I would discover some new character scene or phrase that he’d drawn without me noticing, but one of these phrases was placed in such a way that I couldn’t miss it as soon as I woke up, “passion prevails”.

Web3 has offered much in the form of expansion for the experiential qualities and monetization of my art. We always say things like, “time passes quickly in web3”.

As much as I agree, I find it interesting that time also seems to stay still - art is appreciated for it’s beauty regardless of age and with the possibilities available to me with NFTs, something like my debut album, can no experience a new form of appreciation.

As I begin to release works from the PAISLEY collection over time, it was only fitting that I began with the short film.

When I was working on the album, I connected with my friend and collaborator, Dawit N.M. to share the pattern theories I was creating from and what I was aesthetically into at the time. Dawit went on to handle the art direction for the album, as well as bringing my convoluted story concept to life as a film.

The story of PAISLEY exists in a universe in which we've all been made to forget true selves. Though, there are those of us that break free and reawaken, remembering all the knowledge of self that was once lost. A human that knows who they are can no longer be controlled and is thus a threat to those in power.

This is the case for our protagonists Figaro and Paisley. The pair, bound by fate, seek each other out in parallel universes with the hope to awaken their companion and continue their journey towards freedom. Our short film finds Figaro, moments after being awakened by Paisley, and follows them towards their attempted escape.

The PAISLEY album and short film are an allegory for patterns at every level of life. Just as cells make up organisms and organisms make up the planets, and the planets the universe, and so on - patterns, appear, reshape, and reappear until their purpose in your life is realized. In my album I explore the different patterns in my relationships and my relationships as patterns, that were required for me to grow individually.

This year marks the 3 year anniversary of the PAISLEY collection, with the short film has only been screened at live performances and intimate talks. Now it will all be immortalized on the blockchain.

When I was working on the album, I connected with my friend and collaborator, Dawit N.M. to share the pattern theories I was creating from and what I was aesthetically into at the time. Dawit went on to handle the art direction for the album, as well as bringing my convoluted story concept to life as a film.

The story of PAISLEY exists in a universe in which we've all been made to forget true selves. Though, there are those of us that break free and reawaken, remembering all the knowledge of self that was once lost. A human that knows who they are can no longer be controlled and is thus a threat to those in power.

when i wrote ‘In My Head’, it was a message and reminder to make ur mind a safer place; to not let each and every thought that floods you distract you from your internal & external reality; to focus on who you truly know yourself to be at your core. 

i wanted this song and what it means to me to be shared stripped back to its rawest form, to fully convey the message behind it and how it was first written. so this a special acoustic version to do that. <3 

it’s a free gift for the holidays this year and as the first of many drops that will be paying it forward to different causes, secondary proceeds are going to Nvak Foundation’s Artist Care Program to bring resources like mental health care to a musician in need, who will be selected by the golden egg winner.

Half Life is about struggling with depression. It’s about looking at my life and being afraid that I wasn’t living up to my full potential. About feeling like I had worked so hard and been through so much, only to feel like I still wasn’t living up to the expectations I had for myself. About the kind of hopelessness that settled around me when I felt like I was failing at living my purpose.

The depression was trigged after getting traumatized by web2 pressures - how empty and inauthentic I felt trying to go viral on TikTok; how I had hired a TikTok coach and posted every day for a month, but none of my videos took off; how I felt cringy and embarrassed of some of the content and started making them private; how I had to spend my time making covers for YouTube instead of making songs that meant something to me; how social media made me feel like shit, but I felt I had nowhere else to turn when everyone in the industry was saying I didn’t have a choice; how I felt like my experimental and boundary-pushing music wasn’t bite-sized enough and I was being asked to water myself down. 

And then one day, scrolling through Instagram, I saw a story from Matthew Chaim. He posted an article Time did on Songcamp’s songwriting camps and I felt a spark. I had followed him a while back because he was one of the few artists I knew of at the time that was doing experimental pop music and getting Spotify editorial support, and I was mad inspired. As someone who made up her own genre-blend called deep pop, his experimental pop music was a north star. I didn’t know him at all then, but I got a bit of courage, and DM’d him to see how I might be able to get involved. He responded, and told me Songcamp meets every Monday, and to come to a call. I remember running to tell my mom after getting the DM I was so excited. I joined the call the very next Monday, and fast forward to now, the Songcamp community is filled with people I call dear friends. 

In contrast to feeling so abandoned and isolated in web2, everyone on the Songcamp call was immediately warm and welcoming. I felt like they saw me and accepted me for who I was. They were kind. They loved pushing boundaries and exploring new tech. For the first time in my life, I felt like I had found my tribe. From there I was a part of Songcamp’s CHAOS project, met friends that eventually would form cornerclub together, and was introduced to the promise of web3. That one DM literally changed my life. Finding web3 is what gave me my hope back and helped pull me out of that depressive episode. 

It’s funny the way things work out. The song about web2 trauma and feeling so far away from my dreams turned into my genesis drop on Sound - a dream of mine since finding web3. Not only that, but it’s the very first Atmos drop on Sound (Tip: This is a binaural Atmos mix, so def listen with headphones :) I’ve dreamed of exploring how pop music could move in a three-dimensional space since college. Back then the tech was called spatialization, and could only be done with hard code. Now, Dolby has made the tech widely accessible by launching its Atmos software, and I was finally able to mix one of my songs using it. I think the wide-eyed college student version of me who dreamed of somehow producing music with sounds that swirled around her head would be so proud. So thank you Sound for this opportunity. And thank you web3 for giving me hope when I felt pretty hopeless. 

As a nod to all the communities that so warmly embraced me on my web3 journey so far, I’ve put everyone that has purchased any of my previous NFTs on the pre-sale allowlist, which includes collectors of There Used To Be Four, CHAOS packs, CHAOS songs, and cornerclub’s Dance Music For Introverts Vol. 1.

“SUP” is an unveiled glance into male vulnerability in the digital age — a minimalistic love song for the hopeless romantic trying to express deep affection in an age of brevity and emojis. “Sup” can mean so many things depending on the tone and context. The goal behind the track was to show the many iterations of “Sup,” and poke fun at how difficult it can be to express the simplest and most profound emotions.

The song was produced by my in house dream team: award winning composer/producer Lyell Evans Roeder and Kirk “KJ” Follette  — a process that was rather quick to compose but took months to mix and refine to our liking. Sonically, we stuck to a formula of melding contemporary drum production with a simple yet textured melody — sophisticated ignorance. 

This is my first legitimate release as an independent artist since leaving my record label during pandemic, it means the world to be so vulnerable on so many levels in this web3 space that’s redefining possibilities for working artists. I have two full length projects almost done being mixed and mastered for 2023, consider this the first official crowdfunding effort in this new independent chapter! Your support means the world.

I created TREBUCHET to tell - and write - my story from here going forward. Earlier in my music career I had the opportunity to sign to a record label, and I did. I seized what was (at the time) the best option I had to take music seriously (and convince my family that it could be taken seriously…). Signing that deal opened so many doors, and taught me so much about who I was, who I wanted to be, but most importantly who I was not. As time went by I wandered further and further away from why I started creating in the first place, eventually arriving at an unrecognizable version of myself. 

I spent much of the pandemic questioning who I was (as a human and as an artist), what I was creating, and whether or not it was worth continuing. But through time and sustained chipping away I started to remember and re-recognize the kid who first started creating - the one who rushed to open Ableton in any spare free time and express himself honestly and openly - before all the expectations and extra cooks came into the kitchen. This song is my most honest return to that, and I think sets the tone for all of my music that will follow.

I provide this context so that you might better understand TREBUCHET as a song and metaphor. I made this record exactly as I wanted to - with its weird, yet super personal sonic choices, somewhat nebulous lyrics, and a key change at the end (among other things) - because for so long I wasn’t free to create in the way that I know I’m supposed to: following only my own ideas, experience and intuition. The song feels right at home with some of the records I’m most proud of from my past, and combines my newly rediscovered creative drive with my last few years of production and songwriting experience for something I’m finally proud of once again. 

I hope you love it as much as I do.

Our Sound.xyz debut, “Vapors” is the first track in our new “Singles” series, featuring stand alone tracks that are paired with a visual.

The collector of the golden egg will receive a separate bonus 3D object NFT of the sculpture featured in the image for this piece. Most of our pieces have associated sculpture NFTs.

This chill new song mixes melodic production reminiscent of a nice breeze on a Sunday afternoon with a smooth flow that that fits the vibe right. 

Inspired by everyday life, the lyrics to this song express how music provides the soundtrack for artists to create audio experiences based on their environment & the score of reality.

6 years ago I received a package from 5,000 miles away. My ex-girlfriend from Buenos Aires had shipped me a shoebox full of mementos from our relationship and a goodbye note. I remember receiving the package and sitting with it for a few minutes in silence before picking up my guitar. I sat on the floor at the base of my couch, and this song came out in a matter of 15 minutes or so.

Disposable is the first song that I wrote and released as a solo artist in 2017. Throughout 2017-18 I hosted artist showcases in my basement to spotlight student artists at my university - the cover art for this drop is a photo from one of the first of those shows where I debuted my EP "Purple Line". The golden egg is the album artwork of that EP - my first and only release as Oddentity. That night was my first time ever performing original music - it was an intense and beautiful moment that I will never forget.

"After" is the first edition of our new project called Koastcards. Each month we will be traveling to a new location to present 4 new releases that will drop each week: 

Week 1: Electric Oyster (Mix Series) 
Week 2: EDM song 
Week 3: a remix 
Week 4: pop song

Koastcards is a check-in with all of our fans, to catch them up on our travels, our releases and our journey - an invitation to come alongside us in experiencing the good times we haven't had yet. 

For this first episode of Koastcards we are traveling to San Onofre, CA - a staple in Southern California for its remote surf beaches and untouched coastal landscape. This marks a perfect spot for us to debut this new project debuting officially in January 2023.

This track is for me and my ailments. My body is starting to fail and struggle in various ways, and this is the sound it makes. There is beauty in the decay.

I wrote this song while in a considerable amount of physical pain. It’s not usual for me to want to create when I am not feeling my best physically, but this was a chance to make a change in my writing process and challenge myself. I usually hit pause on my entire life when I’m sick. I  just sort of dissociate and consume in bed until it’s over or I’ve healed, but this time I chose to actually create something in this state. I wanted to process my emotions in real time. The pain is gone for now, but the feelings remain in this piece of music. I listen back and it helps remind me that everything is temporary and there can always be light even in the darkest moments.

LikeSo was created on December 13th, 2022. A tempo of 68.19 beats per minute was chosen because it was less painful to move slow, and the key of G minor best represented my emotional state at the time. The song features a one-take performance of rhythms that were designed on an Octatrack MK II and the rest of the melodies and pads were created using a Prophet ’08 PE running through a Microcosm delay pedal. The song crescendos into warm keys from my Wurlitzer 200A which is hands down my most cherished instrument and where most of my writing either starts or ends.

I keep my tears in the keybed.
Music can alleviate.

"HOLD ME DOWN" is about finding that person that actually makes you picture a future together.

Have you ever been so down bad that you find yourself doing things that you'd usually think INSANE. Ignoring all the red flags, texting 4 times in a row, making a mixtape at 3am, etc. Well, I've been there and I've done that (multiple times). 

This track is following a whirlwind of emotions that were felt at the beginning of most affairs. Being someone who craves steady ground and consistency, I created an illusion in my head that this specific person would be that for me. 

Luckily that's behind me now, hence the rear view mirror artwork.

Must Admit is my most transparent track to date. On this track I leave it out in the open about a past relationship that ended in way that left me wounded. Le Mav produced the track with me in Lagos Nigeria last year. The sonics on this track is our signature sound. I immediately found the hook. "I must I must admit I must" The verses took me time to write. Through out the verses I breakdown the honesty of leaving someone you love but shouldn't be with. The song was very therapeutic to me. I feel like there's a point in life where you need to let go and just admit EXACTLY how you feel no matter the repercussions.

More about PAISLEY....

In 2017, I had a thought, “patterns prevail”. It was derivative of a quote from my best friend and frequent collaborator, Sky Welkin, which read “passion prevails”. Sky is a talented cartoonist that embeds profound messages like this throughout his work.

During our college years, he’d often come by and draw while I made beats, this was our ghetto co-working era, and in these sessions we’d smoke, engage in discourse, and share ideas about the respective worlds we were building in our art. In fact, I was very much into doing something new each album, but Sky was the primary influence for me to get into world-building and having a particular sense of style that was cultivated over time.

In one of my college apartments, I decided that to let Sky use all of the walls in my room as a canvas - the few hundred dollars that I’d spend to have the room repainted when I moved was minuscule compared to the living art piece around me. Every so often I would discover some new character scene or phrase that he’d drawn without me noticing, but one of these phrases was placed in such a way that I couldn’t miss it as soon as I woke up, “passion prevails”.

Web3 has offered much in the form of expansion for the experiential qualities and monetization of my art. We always say things like, “time passes quickly in web3”.

As much as I agree, I find it interesting that time also seems to stay still - art is appreciated for it’s beauty regardless of age and with the possibilities available to me with NFTs, something like my debut album, can no experience a new form of appreciation.

As I begin to release works from the PAISLEY collection over time, it was only fitting that I began with the short film.

When I was working on the album, I connected with my friend and collaborator, Dawit N.M. to share the pattern theories I was creating from and what I was aesthetically into at the time. Dawit went on to handle the art direction for the album, as well as bringing my convoluted story concept to life as a film.

The story of PAISLEY exists in a universe in which we've all been made to forget true selves. Though, there are those of us that break free and reawaken, remembering all the knowledge of self that was once lost. A human that knows who they are can no longer be controlled and is thus a threat to those in power.

This is the case for our protagonists Figaro and Paisley. The pair, bound by fate, seek each other out in parallel universes with the hope to awaken their companion and continue their journey towards freedom. Our short film finds Figaro, moments after being awakened by Paisley, and follows them towards their attempted escape.

The PAISLEY album and short film are an allegory for patterns at every level of life. Just as cells make up organisms and organisms make up the planets, and the planets the universe, and so on - patterns, appear, reshape, and reappear until their purpose in your life is realized. In my album I explore the different patterns in my relationships and my relationships as patterns, that were required for me to grow individually.

This year marks the 3 year anniversary of the PAISLEY collection, with the short film has only been screened at live performances and intimate talks. Now it will all be immortalized on the blockchain.

Save Yourself was one of two songs on this album that I wrote from a very real place of fear. At a time where I believed that I'd lost faith, and was ashamed of doing so, I felt it was something to be earned back. 

In retrospect, the sheer belief in myself having the power to right my wrongs and redirect my path was maybe the biggest show of faith I could have displayed at the time. 

God has given us everything we need.

10% of the proceeds for this collection will go towards funding web3 education and community building efforts in Virginia.

My very first house track, dated pre-Soulection, that started my journey and transition from mere bedroom/dorm room beatmaker fawning over FlyLo's "Reset" EP, to electronic music producer trying expand his horizon past the then-overly popular J Dilla aesthetic, aspiring to Daft Punk more than Slum Village (the funny part being my favorite track the time was a Dilla/Slum Village remix of "Aerodynamic", lol).

That was the scene that set up this track, which I've revamped countless times after to feature in mixes everywhere, on Soulection, on BBC Radio 1, but never officially released; until now, of course.

Though this is a rare one, I want as many people as possible to listen to it AND have a chance to get what is possibly, literally my rarest gem drop yet out of my vault. This one is just pure vibes, but I meant it to really just take you somewhere, but nowhere in particular either; distanced from this reality into another, if that's what calls to you...

This is my second release on Sound.xyz and my final drop of 2022. 'December' feels like the perfect conclusion to my year in Music NFTs. Originally released in 2019 as part of a Winter EP, it is now exclusively available on Sound. 

'December' is a small, intimate song that hints at the colder months and a longing for a time and place where all of life's worries, regrets and complications melt away. A song to remind you to live in the moment. I hope it reaches the ears of many people and finds homes in the hearts that connect with it the most.  

This month, my heart swelled with pride at the collective coming together of artists, creators and our community as we shared our thoughts around this new landscape and considered what it means to release music on the blockchain. As an independent artist, I choose how I move through the space, who I work with and where I want my music to exist. What I value the most is being empowered to choose for myself. I choose to be a part of the Sound ecosystem and I'm proud to be a part of their community of artists.

Description: Alprazalam’ references Alprazolam, the generic name for Xanax. The lyrics allude to both my friends, as well as a woman I grew up around who struggled with tranquilizer/opiate abuse. A Cancer, the sensitive crab who would never leave her bedroom (her shell) and was largely absent during my young childhood. Aside from taking inspiration from that astrological archetype, I am without hands during the entire video. Not “of this world” and trying to escape that painful reality. The visual is playful and absurd and punky, but there is a dark and melancholic undertone to both the video and song itself.

a song about growing up feeling stuck

I love heartbreak, to be honest. I often find inspiration in memories or images stuck in my head; very visual, and very vivid.

When I reached out to Sara, I remember telling her about this idea of being in a new relationship while still dreaming about the previous one. It’s a tough spot you know? It hurts. I guess we all have that past relationship that hasn’t really allowed us to move on, that messed us up. As a result, we end up unconsciously looking for that person in everyone we meet, which most likely won’t happen and will end up hurting the other person.

So this song is about that, how cold and lonely it feels to be with the wrong person. How painful it feels to hold on to one and not have the courage to let go. How we lie and say we are fine, hurts like hell.

Special thanks to Sara for making this vision a reality and putting it into words, it means the world to me. Also, shoutout to Jack Hentosh for mixing and mastering, and Nicolas Melo for the amazing artwork.

With love,


Charlie Crown

This holiday season a lot of us are blessed with the opportunity to spend time with our loved ones. Whether it be lighting the candles together, decorating the tree, frosting cookies, or tearing open gifts like there's no tomorrow. The holidays, as we know them, are a time of love, joy, and bliss. They are a time to put all your worries and fears aside and just be happy. 
The families and friends of the 41,477 people lost to gun violence in America this year alone, will not have that. Their holidays will be filled with grief and times of remembrance. There will only be the pictures and videos of their passed loved ones from past holidays, as they hold onto their laughs vibrating through the speakers over and over again. 

I wrote America after the Uvalde Elementary shooting. I remember waking up to twitter threads of kids faces who died and rage tweets from all of the people who are over the fact that this can happen due to our lack of gun safety and control in America. Even now as I recount that morning I can feel the sadness from that memory seeping through me and trying to escape. But we can’t let go of these feelings until there is change made. I will stay sad, and I will stay angry until our people are safe. As of October 2022 there have been 257 SCHOOL shootings alone in America. That is an increase from 2021 at 250 school shootings. So things are NOT improving as the stats are showing.  And a direct quote from Snopes states, “Many of these shootings were not the mass killing events that schools typically drill for. Rather, they were an extension of rising everyday gun violence." 

I know we all have busy schedules and as much as I know a lot of us wish we could constantly be doing research and hands on help after these shootings take place, it’s just not reality. That’s why I have decided to donate 75% of proceeds from “America” to Brady. Brady is a foundation with their hands deep in making change around gun violence. A direct quote from their site being “Brady emphasizes education, litigation, and legislation to ensure that every community is safe, not only from mass shootings, but also from the daily toll of gun homicide, domestic violence, suicide, unintentional shootings, and police violence that plagues so many communities.” 

I hope with my full heart that you listen to the lyrics of this song and want to do nothing more but to help with a small yet such LARGE part in making change and that is donating to the cause. As an independent artist, honestly, it is difficult to find balance in making change in the world and focusing on developing my own personal life, but thanks to web3 and these new ways of sharing digital art we can do both. I am able to value myself and at the same time make positive change in our country that is so quickly being divided. I once had pride for the place I live, now I just want to help get back to those feelings.

https://www.bradyunited.org/about

Behind the song DANUBIO:

I love to travel, especially if they are ecological destinations. I have a special connection with nature, essentially with water. For this reason, many of my songs are inspired by travel, because every time I come from one, I come back with a new learning, with my mind more open and my creativity refreshed. In 2021 I took a trip to Danubio, which was full of challenges in every way! take the popcorn, because the story is long.

Danubio is a beautiful river in Valle del Cauca - Colombia, which I had wanted to visit since 2020; however, in December of that year I got COVID, and I gave it to my dad. He seemed to be fine, I recovered and we both did our isolation days and decided to continue with the plan to spend the final days of December in Roldanillo, his hometown. We were already in Roldanillo, and I remember that I was with my sister, packing the suitcase to travel the next day to Danubio, and my mother came over and asked us not to leave, because she felt that my father was not well. We decided to stay (I thank the universe very much for making us stay) and the next day my dad couldn't even walk because he was in such a bad way: he had hidden from us that he had difficulty breathing for more than 3 days because he didn't want to worry us.
At that time in Colombia there were not enough ICUs, not even in the best hospitals! and we were in a town where there was not even an ICU. In short, my dad was about to die in the local hospital because they couldn't do anything for him, since they didn't have the equipment to care for him. Also, they couldn't transfer him to any other hospital because the hospitals with ICUs were full. Fortunately, a miracle happened and an ICU was vacated in a city an hour away, and after 20 days hospitalized, my dad survived... That was my first attempt to visit Danubio... I was left with a great blessing that I have my father alive.

My second attempt was in December 2021, one year after the first attempt. This time we did manage to get there, but not before going through some scares...
Again we were in Roldanillo, every December we travel from Medellín to Roldanillo to spend the end of the year together. I managed to convince my parents to go with my sister and me to visit Danubio, so we went straight to Queremal, a town in Valle del Cauca 3 hours from Roldanillo, where we were going to spend the night, to get up early the next day towards Danubio. Going to the Queremal, we decided to make a stop at Lake Calima, and when we got out, it was already getting dark. My dad knew the route, but we passed a turn to the right and we didn't know how to go back... so we put on waze and started to follow instructions... but we got even more lost. We were all worried because it was getting dark and we didn't know how to go back. We asked a man from the area, and he gave us some instructions that we followed. Suddenly we had no signal and we were on an uncovered road in the middle of two mountains. Nobody said a single word in the car, we were all afraid because we didn't know the area and we couldn't go back. We began to see signs on the walls of the few farms that were, there, saying that we were in the territory of the FARC dissidents. We all looked at each other, no one said anything. We were around 1:30 hour on an unpaved road, but everything went well and we were able to reach Queremal.  

The next day we got up early towards Danubio and we were able to see this natural wonder. Once again I was amazed at the beauty and biodiversity that we have in Colombia.

The song talks about how everything around us is magic, about how much I want to feel at peace with myself and know freedom from the depths of my being, cultivating love and forgiveness, and making  a conscious choice, because in the end everything in life is a decision. This trip made me confront myself, it made me value the lives of my loved ones... with the natural wonders I saw, I remembered that everything around me is magic, and while i was in silence in the car, scared to death, I began to reflect on the power of love and forgiveness, and how they can transform the world.

This track was inspired off of a conversation me and my engineer Matt Cody was having in the studio one day. It started off with us speaking on having multiple streams of income, then some how lol the convo maneuvered its way into us both looking back and realizing how far we've come.

 "Damn the shyt is so true/ these the days that i prayed for swear everything is so new" . It represents me taking a moment to be present and actually reflect on where i am in life as well as how excited i am for what's to come.  A mix of the past, present and future. I'm a big believer in manifesting things that you would want in life and this song 5ways represents speaking all of your wishes and goals into existence. Enjoy and share with the homies. Much love and it feels good to be back.

Big Blesss!

- MoRuf

this is a remix of one of the very first midnight snacks - i made the original early 2020, right when touring came to a standstill and i was missing that feeling of flying at cruise altitude across the planet to visit faraway places, and share music with friends old and new. my sonkei ('respect' in japanese) remix is inspired by, and in memory of, the late great nujabes - the legendary japanese producer who left us way too soon (if you're not familiar, samurai champloo is a great entry point to his music via a classic anime). 

I've always loved how nujabes is the consummate improvising b-boy musician, flipping jazz, breaks and samples. i tweeted recently reflecting on how we were born the same year, have similar musical dna, were always barely even one degree of separation from each other, but despite all the time and community i've had in japan, never had the opportunity to meet. he's someone i would love to have had a chance to break bread with, vibe and create with.

with all that in mind (!), fresh out the lab, here's the new sonkei remix, slowing [37,000 feet] down to a jazzy head-nod and sending peace and love out to nujabes - RIP 🙏 ✨

East Side is a record I wrote with Oliver Malcolm, one of my best friends and also one of my favorite artists.  He's produced songs for me like Heartstrings with Carlos Santana and Ghosts Around Midnight.  We made it in one day and wanted to capture minimalism within a record.  There were so many opportunities to over produce this record, to add booming drums, to do the most...  And after playing with it for months we all agreed that the first day's version - which just features me playing and singing on the guitar, my brother Sol's infectious bass line, and Oliver's short appearance - was the one.  The song is about precisely what the lyrics are talking about.  Growing up on the east coast in Trumbull, Connecticut, I spent a lot of months admiring the ruthlessness of the winter and the feeling that winter has left me with has lingered in my sounds for as long as i've been creating.  Even after years of being in the California sun, the cold wevva on the east side has left its imprint on me.
This is the first song of my many sound releases. all of the music sounds a little different than the last drop. I sing and I rap. hope you enjoy.

I wrote Paint in the Dark because I needed the reminder that relationships can be playful and colorful instead of defining them by their mistakes. Over the past few years, this song has become a guide back to my emotional center in both my relationships to those around me, as well as in the relationship I have with myself. It has also reminded me how to believe in the joy of relationships again, and I hope that it can be there for anyone who needs that reminder too. 

I cowrote "Paint in the Dark" with one of my best friends on the planet, Dean Woodson, in his bedroom in North Hollywood in late 2019. There was something really special in the air that day. We got together to finish a completely different song, and in the process of recording a guitar part for that song, the guitar part for PITD popped right out. It was as though lightning struck and we could feel it; the static in the room drew the lyrics and melodies out of us effortlessly in a matter of minutes. All of a sudden, the song was done and we celebrated with a burrito from Cilantro Mexican Grill (our favorite local spot at the time).

As the pandemic slowly closed the world, Dean flew back to Paris and we decided in late 2020 to begin producing Paint in the Dark long-distance. We spent countless nights staying up late producing with one another over zoom and facetime, and we were constantly sending texts and voice memos of ideas back and forth while the other slept. It was a beautiful way to continue our friendship and keep ourselves inspired during a moment when the earth felt like it was at its darkest. When we had a good picture of the final song, we brought it to our mentor, Rob Cavallo, to help us over the finish line. 

"Paint in the Dark" released in late 2021 along with an amazing music video shot by one of my best friends Vinsint (@vinsint). I hope you enjoy listening, and as always, thank you for collecting <3

Description:
I took a lot of trips to NYC over the last year to work on my second EP and to live a little life outside of my suburban bubble. During one of these trips I was on the bus to a friend’s apartment when an old drunk man began reciting bible verses while waving a kitchen knife. I was already deep in this weird, reclusive funk - and this whole drunk Jack Sparrow wielding blade situation made me feel like Brad Pitt in Fight Club or DeNiro in Taxi Driver - like I was caught in the middle of some larger plot being poked at by the universe. I marched around NYC that day imagining I really was the main character - and that every crack in the concrete and every character on every bus and every piece of graffiti on every subway platform was deliberately placed to remind me of a past relationship that I couldn’t shake. I wrote the first verse and first half of the chorus on a bench in NYC over a short piano loop I made with my little OP-1 synth. I brought these orphaned pieces to my dear songwriter friend Jesse Fink. He suggested the lyric that drives this whole song: “the writing on the wall is just graffiti with your name” and the whole song clicked. My friend Sean Cook added some guitars and synths and his brother Ryan Cook laid down some real life tasty drums to bring the whole record together.

I wrote this in June. During that time I was getting over someone, writing a bunch of songs about them as a way of venting. And after many short lived voice memos and poorly played guitar songs, I created this one. This is probably the final song I’d written and recorded about them, and a great ending to that chapter. 

I love this song with all my heart. I’m in love with the story that progresses as you listen. It starts off painting the picture of seeing someone again for the first time in a while. That feeling where your heart isn’t fully healed from whatever had happened previously between you both. The chorus talks about a part of that person that you can never fully get over. “Those beautiful eyes will never let me go”. 

True. 

I love the back and forth between me describing my feelings and contradicting them with the idea of it being pointless to write songs about this person, because they don’t care. And as you continue to listen, the story evolves. The second verse reminisces on old memories. Staying up till 6am. It compares these memories to how things are in the present: “Now we act like none of it ever happened”. I mention the fact that they won’t get the satisfaction of seeing me hurt, because I’d already given them so much before. 

And the last minute reflects on what could’ve been and what actually happened. It ends off by mentioning the whole point of this person toying with my emotions while I’d been in the process of writing about them. Hence the title, 

“While I Write About You”.

Description:
Long Story Short, I've been producing & rhyming since 1995. The Golden Era of Hip Hop and the inception of the internet musician, from irc's to aol, message boards to myspace, to blogs,  The internet was once a much smaller pond where if you curious, passionate and slight tech savvy it was so easy to find like minded people & find resonance. Released a few singles on Vinyl while still in Highschool and blew up from internet rumor that Bill Gates was suing us, "Equilibrium" for sampling the Windows 95 startup music for one of our b-side tracks titled "Windows 98". During this time I also began recording my first solo album as Dutchmassive - "Junk Planet" (recorded 1997-2002, released 2004) by the time the album was released world wide, I was in my 20's and had long pivoted from the fun, ego driven battle raps after realizing I had so many people hanging onto my every word. Like The Pharcyde said, "I gotta say something that means something".  I took having an audience with more responsibility and did my best to be introspective and inspiring .I began recording my sophomore solo album titled "Crush Your System" which was originally supposed to be a double album, the 2nd disk containing my Instrumental album "Music 2 Sleep To" but in 2007 I was approached by Rawkus Records to release the album as apart of what would be the world's first large scale digital campaign "The Rawkus 50" with production from ILLMIND, Samiyam, 14KT, Dela, etc.  It didn't make sense to release my old beats next to such dope producers. 
 
This was also around the time,  Instrumental HipHop without any vocals began taking off with events like Beat Society, super crews like Beat Fanatic and countless blogs dedicated to showcasing instrumental albums but still,  Instrumental only releases were by no means normalized or acceptable to most people but the production was always the first thing that captured my heart.  After both of my Major releases met the same fate of 3 months after release, the labels filed for bankruptcy and no one got paid. I decided to take a break from recording records and focus mainly on production.  I was always Producing alongside emceeing but I was mainly known as a Rapper.   
The Long Story Short isn't as short as I thought so lets truncate as I explain the intentions of "Metropolis Jawn"

My Production was always a hybrid of 90's boom-bap, Jazz, soul with a touch of Video game OST sprinkled in and occasionally some deep house.  Like if Pete Rock, Dj Premier, J Dilla, Portishead & Nobuo Uematsu fell into a blender that time traveled to the year 2090 and still tried to hold onto nostalgia.   My Production was never intended to rhyme on, so back then, people didn't know how to categorize it.  Like I said,  Instrumental albums that weren't intended to be rapped on were not very popular.  Fast Forward to recent times, the type of music we have been making since the mid/late 90's, early/mid 2000's would now be classified as "Lofi HipHop '' and Dominates streaming charts and has become background study music.

After years of releasing cohesive, somewhat conventional instrumental albums, combined with Algorithms, the Pressure of content and super short life span and attention span that music gets since around 2016.  I needed a shift on how I approached music and began live streaming on twitch.  10 hour streams of creating in real time led to me completely shifting how I created.  Instead of trying to create and sequence a song,  I became super addicted to recording the entire process from start to end with more of a improv Jazz approach,  Constantly pushing limits of experimentation and getting as weird as possible with it, purposely making stuff sound off, just so I could solve puzzles in real time.  This led 2-6 hour sessions all recorded live and would become the series known as Evolving Portals.  

   We already mentioned the world's attention span has shortened so I basically pivoted to an unmarketable way of creating music haha. A Lot of people fell in Love with these sessions and they became long form meditative / journey soundtracks,  but most people just wanted me to make and release normal beats.   I'm not really big on modern pop or modern hip hop (autotune/trap) which pretty much dominates and has been dominating for a while now so Metropolis Jawn was my compromise and challenge to "get with the times" while still retaining my signature sound.   
 
I know this was a long backstory and 98% of it didn't even cover the actual song but I felt it was important to give some history since I know web3 and web2 history don't necessarily cross over to well yet. =)

The feeling of "the wait is over" is one of the best feelings in the world, isn't it?

"Waiting" is one of the records I made while in the US this past July of 2022, I was super inspired, but at the same time with a bittersweet kinda feeling. Imagine you could go back and tell your 17-year-old self “I’m good enough as I am.” Imagine what could’ve been one of life’s biggest failures turning into triumph.

Many moons ago as a senior in high school I was given the task of completing an exit project, where I would research poet Elizabeth Barrett Browning and one of her works and write about it. My English teacher was very vague with instructions and it left me feeling lost. So I procrastinated. Why? I started reading at a year and a half, I went to gifted and talented schools my whole life, why was this challenging? The me of today (post a late stage ADHD, Anxiety disorder diagnosis) would reach out for clarity and understanding of expectations.

But the me then who knew more than I gave her credit for, turned to music. The one constant, the one bit of clarity even when nothing else fell into place. I thought I knew the person I’d love forever and while that is not true- I did know then how profound, forgiving, patient and other worldly love was and still is. 

So I wrote Love Again but never turned in my project OR the song. I just knew it wasn’t good enough. I Technically flunked high school. As a result I had to do a semesters worth of English projects in one week to graduate on time. And did.

This recording was created 2years later @ 19 years old. The first song I ever wrote recorded, vocal produced, and co produced with my brother B. Sharpe. I was good enough then. And I’m good enough now.

It takes tremendous shadow work, to reach back into the past, and soothe the pain of a younger self. That is the point of life. That is the point of love.

Peace! You can call me Jack, and I’m an artist from the DMV. My creative style embraces all mediums for the sake of passionate storytelling, transformation, and awakening. Just as I have been finding my way within this world creatively, I can’t help but notice a sense of being found: the absorption into something bigger, more expansive, and often beyond words.

WAYSPACE is the name I’ve given to this bigger dimension of awareness that lies within us, both collectively and individually. It also happens to be the name of my debut album, which was released on Halloween 2022.

This new song, Saw, serves as a prequel to the album. It represents the mess, the breakdown, the disappointment, and the suffering aroused by loss, grief and nostalgia. Saw also reveals a quiet willingness to see the beauty in every difficulty. When we hear the words “Could it be that we’re just on the scenic route? Seeing tears on everybody coming down” we are offered a chance to embrace the suffering and understand that it connects us through compassion.

This was one of the first songs that my closest collaborator, Fabrizio, and I ever made together. Fabrizio is also the main producer on the album, so it means a lot to be able to share a song that is so dear to both of us. I’m grateful that it now has a home right here.

The easiest way to introduce myself to you all is to start exactly where my life began. Old Orleans is an embodiment of where I come from; New Orleans. It is the place that taught me all that I know, and I owe it so much.

The universe works in the wildest way, being that this is my golden year (29 on 12/29), and I’ve been in the space of reflecting on everything in life. The ups and downs, the lessons learned, the hardships but also the joy life brings and being able to move through it all. I never saw myself making music or even being in this position of calling myself a “rapper” to be quite honest. I just needed an outlet to use my voice to amplify what it is I feel to the world. And here I am.

ECLIPSE29 is a piece of art producer Aston Woods and artist/vocalist Brooke D. came together to create. Timely enough I feel as though we all were in a space of reflecting on growth in life, so it was only right this record be filled with our love to be able to express the things we’ve come from individually that we may not even be aware of collectively. To speak for myself, this record is me. It’s my life from a child to a man and beyond, and I hope it lives on and speaks healing to anyone it touches in the future.

Description: LOW TIDE is about dealing with that feeling of being out on your own and wondering if everything all came crashing down and you had to pack it all up would anybody even notice you were gone.

"All you left me with are these memories, that I'm drowning out with this Hennessy, just to hide the fact that I'm too afraid to move on."

The song is written like a sad break up song but for me it's a lot deeper than that. For me it isn't really about a relationship at all.
I could bore you with the sad details but it's pretty personal. If you enjoy the song and are curious,  feel free to reach out to me on Twitter and I'd love to talk about it.

(Clears throat) Ladies and Gentlemen, I am honored to introduce 2 new talents to web3! TyBass and DJ Mutaal! 

TyBass is a founding member of NXGN CBNT a collective of creatives based in New York— with in house original music, production, multi media and art, mostly known our work with MeLoX and impact in the underground NYC music scene. 

A major source of his inspiration for his music is his Caribbean background and experience coming up in New York the foundation of Hip Hop. With my parents being of Tanzanian and South African descent, we found a lot of commonalities in our upbringing and musical tastes. 

DJ Mutaal is a record producer and engineer hailing from Jamaica!

"Di Gyal Dem Song is one of several tracks my BrØdy AK and I made during his stay in NYC. This is the first time it's ever being heard. Within a span of a couple days we hit multiple sessions and naturally created a EP’s worth of chunes. This drop is special to me because it captures the natural musical energy AK and I share complimented by Mutaal’s original production & engineering." - TyBass

"FEEL IT ALL" is a song about chasing the feeling that something once gave you when it isn't quite making you as happy as it used to. It's about for one night trying to forget everything thats going wrong and just having a good time doing whatever it is that gets you fired about life.

"MOVE ON" is a song about knowing you've come to a point in a relationship where it's not what you want anymore and you no longer get those same feelings that that person once gave you. Rather than stay in a situation that isn't right for either of you anymore it's about saying it out loud so each of you can move on and find what's right for you.

Description:
In April of 2020, separated by an ocean and 3000 miles, both of us went into self-isolation. Physically, of course -- like everyone else. But also musically.

Turning inwards, we scoured the Refs instrumental vault for our most menacing, introverted and brooding soundscapes -- and proceeded to write 12 songs in 12 days. 2 years later, we offer up our debut album, "New Religion".			

Our song "I Should Be Alone Right Now" featuring our friend Kevin Garrett mirrors the calm-before-the-storm state of the world circa April 2020. In some ways, it holds even more water now, in light of ever-present systemic and cultural decline.		

The animated image we chose for artwork is a taste of an unreleased "New-Religion" themed collectable project. Owners of "I Should Be Alone Right Now" NFTs will get a sneak peak of what's to come.

-Dessauer and Rich

Description:
Me and my Gang was written with a friend of mine named Dwayne who is from Oklahoma.  Dwayne has a natural southern cadence.  An old-timer rhythm to his speech.  Now I come from more Northern tongues - but I've evolved my slang into a blend of North American phrases...creating some form of new age broken down, gen-z english.  We love folk music.  But we like going to the clubs.  We like strippers, but we also like fire pits.

Me and my gang was written after a night of driving around Los Angeles looking for something to do.  Hanging out with friends and pretty women and coming home unfulfilled. An LA tale that seems too familiar to even the most clouted.  

This was a record that wasn't supposed to be on the upcoming album, Bad Radio.  I really had no intentions of writing for the album/ and thought it was done. But after writing this one late summer night, and recording it the next day, we started to feel the untamed honesty that the song mirrored back to us.  While playing the song back, Dwayne recommended we go to his spot in Oklahoma to do the video.  Two weeks later we're at a rodeo at Cowboys Oklahoma City with a film crew shooting one of my now favorite visuals.

If you're reading this, the song and video is out.  
On the cover, you'll find Callie.  A sweet girl from OK who helped us film the video.

Thank you everyone for the support.  Album dropping December 9th.

-felly

When I write music, I like to tell a story. I don't go through enough in my life to write songs that pertain to me so I usually draw inspiration from outside sources.

The concept of "Get Involved" came to me when I was listening to love songs about cheating but they were always either "breakup songs" or "take me back" songs. 

I wanted to write a song about how the cheating went down and what transpired through it all. What was going on through this characters mind as it was happening. Hopefully none of you guys can relate haha!

Hope you like it!

Moving from England, to New York, then Los Angeles gave me my fair share of being out of my comfort zone and feeling lonely, so much so that it became a pattern. The only consistent thing in my life up till now was uncertainty itself and my music career. This pattern conditioned me to keep my friends and loved ones at a distance so that I could focus on the one reliable thing, music. 

I created this piece literally on the plane back to LA from being in England over the most part of covid living with an ex. I think writing this song came at the perfect moment, as I was feeling frustrated by how much time I was spending on a person who ended not working out when I could have been putting that energy back into my music. It felt as though he was living proof that the no one in my life was going to be consistent (as depressing as that sounds). 

Now that I am fully settled in LA I still find it hard to let myself completely get attached to anyone because of my past. I wrote this song as a sort of “apology” note to the people in my life who I push away. A sort of explanation as to why I act the way I do and that they should not be taking it personal. I also want this to be a song to those who struggle with attachment based on their past. What better way to explain yourself then through a song?

Hero is about a powerful person feeling powerless. Hero came to me on a run last summer in rainy Paris amidst the demise of my first real romantic relationship (right around when I wrote Boded, my other sound drop). Directionless and phone-less, I ran, ran, and didn't stop running until I reached a soccer field where I sat on the ground cinematically asking god and the higher powers to show me the way. In my head, the phrase "I'm no hero, I'm no hero..." was on repeat, haunting me until I entertained it. In the midst of feeling truly average, "just a sovereign waiting for the bus, I'm no hero" came to me and I stepped into the powerlessness cause I knew the song existed there, in the surrender to what seemed like weakness. What I only figured out in retrospect is that this "low point" swerved me into a lane that gave me a simply complex song about crumbling in order to build again. This song heavily references things that have made me who I am - Paris, Back to Black by Amy Winehouse, Miles Davis trying to stay relevant after his peak, needing a spaceship to dance cause I take up space, me being a full time artist with other jobs, being my parents pride and joy even when I don't feel like I am worthy, and bleaching my hair only to see the my natural hair come back in relentlessly (this timeless feat is as literal as it is metaphorical). This song was written as a freestyle over a Dolceola line and a hip hop inspired drum beat, layered with ethereal background vocals. I hope it finds you as much as it found me.

Welcome to a new ERA in MAiWORLD. 

WORLD 1 (a 7-song origin story of how MAiWORLD began) was my first Web3 release across Catalog, Audius, Emanate, and my custom contract. I even turned the storyline of WORLD 1 into a playable Gameboy game that mirrors MAiWORLD's creation with playable levels based on the songs. Although, to be honest, GARAGE TAPES VOL. 1 was originally going to be the first project I ever released as an artist. 

GARAGE TAPES is a catalog of songs initially made in my garage. In the earliest stages of MAiWORLD's creation, I made an entire ERA of music from MAi garage.  I experimented with making many different songs during this time, and a relationship I was in at the time was one of the biggest inspirations for me. "GLORiFiED" is a song about that relationship. 

Initially written and produced five years ago from the garage, "GLORiFiED" has been reproduced/mixed countless times; this was going to be one of the first songs I released as an artist.

The song starts off with a raw (and real) voicemail that leads into the lyrics that paint a scene from that time.

From the relationship I was in, to the music I was making, I didn’t want to give up on either; but I felt like I was giving my all for something that I could never do.

Welcome to GARAGE TAPES VOL. 1

Son of a Gun.  One of my favorites off the upcoming album.  Something that feels like it has centuries of history behind it.  It was supposed to be the intro, then the outro, then found itself at track 10.  This song is probably the most New England//CT thing I’ve made.   I was scared of it for a while because of this reasons - it's out there. It has a lot of “Christian Felner” (my real name) in it.  Felly takes a seat for this one.  But it has this dark tone to it that I think is sacred and true to me. It feels like a horse.  You ever look into a horses eyes?  Feels like you can see hundreds of years in there.  I don’t think many people understand this song and I always look at people after playing it and just sitting with the fact that, from where I stand, it seems it went right over their head. The song is sort of about only being here for a period of time. The fragility of life, and how we're all alone.  And that feeling you can reach in life where there is no place to actually call home.  Being cast into the world alone…pretty much.  It comes from touring, from meeting so many strangers, and ultimately feeling like its still just me.  If you get this one you get it and if you don’t that's alright with me.

My name is Mazare and I am a drum and bass producer from Italy. 

My creative process usually revolves around writing an instrumental and then looking for the right voice and lyrics to convey the feelings I experienced while producing.

Excited to share my genesis drop on Sound.xyz titled “Kola Champagne”. I made this track during the winter of 2017 when I first started learning how to produce music.

I spent a lot of my summers growing up in Jamaica. At an early age I was exposed to large music events, that would later inspire me to want to make music. Too young to drink, 'Kola Champagne' was a staple beverage growing up, and holds many memories.

 I wanted to create a song that brought the warmth of the tropics and fuse it with a Northern touch. This song allowed me to experiment with writing styles, production styles and vocal techniques and remains one of my favourite songs.

Emily Lazar is a multi-disciplinary artist fronting the rock/metal transmedia project, September Mourning. She made history as the first female metal/ hard rock musician to mint and sell an NFT on the blockchain. She has spoken about her accomplishments in Web 3/ NFT's at Harvard (2x), NFT.NYC and ETH Denver Conferences.

September Mourning is a transmedia project based on a comic book series she wrote and published through Image/Top Cow Comics with her business partner Marc Silvestri (Batman/Witchblade/Darkness). September Mourning is the title character. As a human reaper hybrid, she  gives expired souls a second chance at life in another body. In doing so, she messes with  the plans of the antagonist, Fate, who is trying to rid  earth of all the good souls and leave the bad so the world will self-destruct and It can start anew. I don’t always like the world I’m in so I build my own. Wherever I go. I’ve always found escape in music when the world around me got scary or disappointing. My earliest memories are of being alone with my CD player and imagining things in my head — like playing shows with giant crowds and my guitar. I felt a lot of pain and rejection, and created my own reality where someone like me is a superstar. 

I created Krash World, a magical world made in my own image loosely based on reality, back in 2019. It’s a world for anyone feels out of place to be a superstar. I want to show kids and adults alike that they don’t have to fit into anything, they can carve out their own space.



“how do u feel?” is my take on 80s synth pop/rock. my most recent explorations have been with four on the floor kick patterns, simple dance-inspired drums, groove and lots of room for vocals to shine. 

i made this song reflecting on myself and failed relationships, desire and love addiction. if you ever felt like there’s a person you just can’t seem to shake emotionally even after a breakup, this song is for you. i reflect the idea that you can become addicted to a person just like someone might be addicted to drugs or alcohol or caffeine, and what that feels like. 


there’s a desperation to these feelings that is equally intoxicating and irritating. there’s a lot of double meanings throughout the song, reflecting the dual nature of love, desire and love addiction. red is the color that came up when i listened back to the song and it was the perfect tone for the feeling i got. red can mean STOP, danger, anger, and blood or it can stand for love and desire.

two sides of the same coin.

My second song on Sound is another oldie.
Written in 2018, during a time where all I was writing was melancholic tunes, "Your Mother" stood out as a little tongue in cheek gem, ironic and direct at the same time.

This is a one take acoustic recording of my song "Your Mother" with my friend Ed Prosek on trumpet. 
Once again I feel so blessed that web3 allows me to put out songs that were written such a long time ago, and were never given a chance to see the light of day. Well now they can shine, and find a home with you guys.

Description:
I’m Glassface. I’ve been creating music my entire life. I’ve spent the past 10 years working as a music video / commercial director and visual artist, moonlighting as a producer & songwriter for other artists. In the past few years I’ve come to realize the importance of sharing my music with the world, putting my head down to finish some of the myriad of demos I have in the vault. Putting everything into the music. In the past 3 months, I’ve released 3 new songs with accompanying visuals. “There’s No Other One” is my 4th release this year, and is truly special to me. Oh, and I’m just getting started.

There’s No Other One is a mix of some of my favorite things. Produced by Matti Free and me, we brought together live guitar and drums, pitched toms, analog synths under a cutting vocal. Minimal 80’s-inspired pop rock leading into a crescendo of maximalist electronic production.

Nodding to favorite artists of mine including Daft Punk and Francis & The Lights - the song is an amalgamation of influences. It’s really important to me to make the music that I want to hear. Lyrically, it’s about a moment of clarity - that feeling when everything comes together and makes sense. A somber night drive of self-discovery. The electricity you feel after a life-affirming realization. Disguised as a love song, I’d say “There’s No Other One” is more of a self-love song. When I realized I was the only one who could accomplish my dreams, it empowered me, and I knew I was unstoppable. It’s about staying the course and letting that feeling be a North Star. I really believe in what I’m doing. This song is for anyone who has had that realization that they are that one.

Description:
IIWII (It Is What It Is) is the debut collaboration between producers BRUX & The Kite String Tangle who are long time fans of each others work & friends who came up in the Australian electronic music circuit.  

Danny Harley aka The Kite String Tangle is a Brisbane-based electronic/pop producer & artist with a string of gold certified releases (Arcadia, This Thing We Got) & awards (+ ARIA noms) under his belt. He is relatively new to web3, with this being his genesis collaborative drop on Sound.xyz with more to come..

Liz Maniscalco aka BRUX is a New York-based electronic producer & artist with a prominent web 3 presence and impressive catalog of collaborations (Kimbra, Flight Facilities, Pat Lok) including recent cosigns on her BADBOI ep from Boys Noise, Busy P & Modeselektor.


The track was written & produced by the pair, spawning from a jam session & synth nerd-out in Sydney, 2018. It was later finished off in Brisbane in between tour with a session at Dannys' music studio. 



IIWII is a comment on the climate inaction, conceptually stemming from conversations about being on the precipice of great change & empathy fatigue over the constant barrage of nihilistic news coverage. The magnitude of the climate issue is so overwhelming that it's easy for us all to disengage & feel like our contributions are just a drop in the ocean.


“Never doubt that a small group of thoughtful, committed citizens can change the world. Indeed, it is the only thing that ever has.” The above quote is from Anthropologist Margaret Mead (1901-1978)"




10% of the sales from this collection will be donated to Green Music Australia - a charity dedicated to eco sustainability within the music scene, working closely with artists, venues, events & fans to create impactful change. The Golden Egg winner will have their name on the donation.

I started making music in my childhood bedroom when it was just me and a cracked version of logic. Back then, I released about a song a week on SoundCloud, but after signing with a label, I had to distribute my creativity between creating a brand and making music. I've got great people around me helping me get back to the process I fell in love with; conceptualizing, recording, and just putting it out there. 

The eeriness flows from those intrusive thoughts, you know, the ones that hit you late at night and send you in a never-ending loop. Finding something to hold onto, whatever that may be brings you back to the reality that you are in control of how you deal with shit. Being able to embrace the ebb and flow of making music in a digital world.

“HOLD ON” started with this gritty guitar riff which got me thinking about my experience in the cycle of highs and lows in the music industry. We wanted this darker tone with dryer vocals but to also have fun with it. When the lyrics started flowing, it created this dance between the lyrics guiding the beat and the beat driving the lyrics.

Description:
When the pandemic hit in 2020 the scope of music changed.

Many artists and creatives didn't know how much it would impact us beyond not being able to do shows but it really forced us to be inside and reflect. This alone can kill creativity because many of us thrive off of the outside experiences in life.

However, I saw it as an opportunity to push myself to hone my skills. Not just as a writer and rapper but also as a visionary. I took upon myself to start a freewrite series called "The Takes" where every track had a beat switch and every title had a number next to it that was significant in meaning (I love numbers and codes that have hidden meanings).

This mint is also special because it was the last track I recorded before I evolved into my current gold bearded state (haha).

The Gold Fang Society Comms are now active and this mint free mint will get you access to the guild and Telegram chat where I'll be sharing new music and content early, hosting Zooms to connect with my collectors and more.

https://guild.xyz/gold-fang-society-comms

Take 99 prod. by Southpaw Swade & Chop

we want to show you something..

this is our song die for you... but the 1st version of the idea...

we did this because we wanted to show how art changes. as we bring more brain power into something, creations evolve and this is a beautiful part of the process.

why are you guys dropping old demos as NFT’s instead of new finished music you might ask… 

being an artist is by no means an easy feat. Your product requires vulnerability in its rawest form, generally in an attempt to reach masses. that said, often times so much of the musical process gets overlooked as the consumer is generally receiving the final and most polished version of the music.

as a band we believe in pushing boundaries, exposing all the layers of our artistry, and showing you every aspect of what’s it’s taken for us to get to where we are now to give a deeper look into our work.

this is exactly what sparked our collection WORKS OF PROGRESS.

Description:
Sometimes, as artists, and simply as people, we go through periods where nothing we create feels quite right. These periods normally expire within a relatively short timeframe, but can feel like an eternity. We bang our heads, over and over again, trying to find the perfect sound, paired to the exact feeling we mean to convey, and while this may seem fairly straightforward, it can feel like a truly insoluble puzzle. 

It had been a few months since I'd made a song I felt connected to, and I had been operating within said headspace throughout these months. Life just felt a bit lackluster, as it always seems to do when the one thing I care about most becomes the hardest to make; music. I'll never know whether it was due to the personal affairs of my daily life, or something indescribable much deeper inside me, and truly I'll never care. The reason for this is, I view these periods of dullness as essential for artists. In the same way that happiness is hard to understand without a grasp on sadness, an artist cannot create their absolute best without experiencing their worst.

Entering this mode of uncertainty always seems to be a slow trickled effect, while exiting it is usually quite sudden. Many times it's an experience which wakes the artist up, other times it is a new song or album they hear. For me, it was a person, another music creator, who took me out of my creative hole, and helped me create this art.

I made Evil with my close friend and collaborator, Jason (JVSE). His style of music creation is extremely unique, and from the very first time we worked, I could tell my days of uncertainty within my own music creation were over. We have created quite a bit of music together, but the night we made “evil,” we both knew it was special. The song was unlike anything either of us had ever made, joining elements of both of our individual styles in a way we could never imagine without actually putting it on the paper. I truly believe being in the headspace I was in gave the song room to be authentically sorrowful, and Jason always understands how to create a perfectly represented production for whatever my lyrics and melody ask for. So to simplify things, “evil” is really a marriage between the dullest and most difficult moments in my life, and the highs and inspiring moments. Without experiencing the contrast of both, there is no evil, and truthfully, there is no lilspirit.

I was overwhelmed with support on my latest free drop 'promises', which landed on the trending page on Spinamp, and generated over 13 secondary sales. For a free drop I think that's incredible, so thank you to anyone who messaged me kind words or collected.

This track (bubbles) being one of them. I grew up listening to trance and was one of the first genres that introduced me to dance music, so it only felt natural to draw from the genre with this one.

Enjoy! Thanks again for your support, it means the world and is pushing me to write more and more. <3

I remember getting this song idea from dilip while I was in Austin at CabinDAO’s node 0. I knew that there was something to this song, but not sure how I could fit my style into it. It wasn’t until I got back home to Toronto and pulled up the song during Xmas holidays that the magic began. I infused a little of the Toronto darkness into dilip’s original idea and the rest you’ll get to hear on the song. 

This drop is just the start of a musical history together. If you want to know what else we’ve got cooking up our sleeves, you definitely want to get tapped in.

Description:
Have you ever found yourself metaphorically staring at the mountain of things you have to do and becoming anxious?  Has fear ever stopped you from following through? I know I have.  The very appearance of my lofty goals can sometimes paralyze me.

Paramount examines this paradigm between two perspectives: first from a third person’s rhetorical vantage point and then from my own personal experiences with complacency, procrastination and failure.

I’ve learned in this life, you can’t be afraid to fail.  Every great anything/anybody has failed, often times, more than they succeed.  I’ve come to find that the true secret to success is not being afraid to risk not obtaining it.

As a listener, I hope this song is your new anthem to get things done!  Remember those things that are paramount in your life and keep climbing!

👀👀👀👀👀👀

Enjoy.

There seems to be a theme in my music where I get into a relationship and fuck it up... 

Well this one was written about a time when I thought I was about to lose someone to another guy. I couldn't  stand to see this person with someone else so I put it in a song. 

Long story short, she chose me!

'nobody loves you' explores the themes of isolation and loneliness, as well as a personal struggle with mental illness. This record was written after a string of tragic deaths of peers in the music industry, as well as the loss of a family member. 'nobody loves you' delves into the idea that we often wait until it's too late to really show our love, appreciation and respect for each other. 

It was written by Sara Phillips, and produced with Mike Daley and Mitchell Owens. 

10% of all primary sales of this record will be donated to the The Trevor Project - focused on suicide prevention and providing 24/7 crisis support services to LGBTQ young people. Thank you so much for helping this incredibly important cause.

I grew up in the church. I learned the rules, the christian lingo, the do's and don'ts, ALL OF IT. As i've aged, i've come to believe love is what matters, not a set of religious rules that we must all abide by. I am not spreading hate towards any religion, i'm only shining a light on my experience with it. This song is hard for me to write and release... i'm clueless as to what my family will think of it and how they might see me for it. I'm just sick of watching religion breed hate and, equally so, all the hate people have towards religion. There is such a massive divide in the world and we forget we are all one. I hope you all can take time to truly listen to the lyrics. This is exclusively on sound.xyz for the next week!

My team and I are committed to growing in the Web 3 space and are confident that your investments in my music will be more than worth it! In The Smoke is my genesis Sound.xyz drop and my third music NFT, following two sold out collections earlier this year. It’s a self-confronting song about choosing to leave the life you have in pursuit of the unknown. It’s from the perspective of a woman on the edge, where it’s uncertain if she’s having a breakdown or a break through. Perhaps a combination of both. 

Growing up in a small town in the north east of Scotland, I’ve always been exposed to the great outdoors, bad weather and a kind of social conditioning that you shouldn’t ask for too much in life. Much of my music takes influence from those themes, of wondering what it would mean to take a certain fork in the road and what my place is in the world. Since discovering web 3, I can feel my own internal changes taking place as new paths present themselves. The music community, specifically, has provided me with all the tools, unwavering support and cultural values I was struggling to find elsewhere. To be looking out towards a future where I’m able to exist in this space as a full time, independent artist is something I still can’t quite believe. I’m wholeheartedly embracing it.

Although I wrote and recorded this song here in Edinburgh, I also brought on my longterm producer Lucas Mendes to make his web 3 debut from his studio in London. We wanted to be fairly restrained in our approach to this song and to capture its uneasy nature. Lucas intricately layered guitars and plucked strings and provided the texture, detail and depth that the song required. He also mixed the song remotely with me - one of my favourite parts of the creative process where you can map out every nuance. He is my wizard.

I hope my music will provide a little salve to your wounds and act as an outlet for whatever you need it for.

emma xx

Description:
It all started when I picked up my father’s guitar and taught myself how to play some chords on Youtube. That moment alone led to me writing original songs and finding my true identity.

After making it to Top 200 on American Idol but later getting rejected, I found the courage shortly after to drop myself out of University and make the 14hr drive to Music City aka Nashville, TN, where I found my calling. I knew when my windshield met the Batman building in the skyline, that’s where I was meant to chase my dreams.

As a Cuban-American singer/songwriter, my purpose is to represent the Hispanic culture in Modern Country. I didn’t see any other artist filling those boots so I saw that as a great opportunity to start a movement and bring awareness to the genre by combining my love for Latin music and the storytelling element of Country Music. 

After 13 years of writing thousands of songs, working with many other writers and even being signed and dropped by Sony Music in 2017, I continued strumming along and found some hope on Spotify and TikTok. I dropped by debut album Oct 2021 and found some success on TikTok and Instagram Reels, gaining over 40M independent music streams and over 100M video impressions in under 2 years. This led to nationwide tours, incredible brand partnerships and way more…

In Nov 2021, I was introduced to web3 and NFTs by a close friend from back home in Miami, FL. Little did I know, this introduction was gonna change my career and my life forever. Since starting my NFT journey, we have sold over 6500 Music NFTs and proudly stand as the founder of 3 Music NFT collections -  METAGIRL, Pulse Pass & PIXELATED. These were all released on my own smart contracts and were organically minted via Twitter Spaces and rigorous hours connecting with the community on Discord. 

My genesis drop on Sound is “WTH” (What The Hell). This song was inspired by stubborn love and chasing someone knowing that it’s only gonna end in heartbreak. 

As someone that considers himself a hopeless romantic, this song definitely means so much to me. I look forward to releasing this one out in the world and hope it resonates with other hopeless romantics hopelessly loving someone as they hear this song.

- SAMMY
