Description: I wrote ‘worlds heaviest shoes’ based on the idea of someone who’s completely moved on while you’re still in the same place, reminiscing the memories you had. In the writing session, the writer i was with had mentioned the line ‘worlds heaviest shoes’ as a metaphor for that feeling of being stuck and it felt like the perfect way to describe it. The chorus is almost a plea for help, wondering why no one’s paying attention. I like how it ends desperate and angry, almost shouting, because you’re left without answers.

While working on this record I was aware that this didn’t sound anything like how I’m supposed to.  But I guess that’s why it excited me.  I always talk with artists I work with and we frequently get on the subject of how their music never sounds like what they actually like to listen to.  I always thought that was odd, almost wrong.  Mirror sounds like the type of music that I…usually listen to.  Not all the time, but if I’m on a plane or just cooling out…I’m playing stuff like Bon Iver, the Shins, Modest Mouse… Almost calming, soul nurturing records. I was laughing with a friend about how everyone’s always trying to make the hardest most in your face record (which I’ve done dozens of times), and about the power in the opposite.  

I’ve been working on this record for 2 years and always knew it would eventually come out, just needed to find the right time.  I played this last week for my friend Rey, who is one of my favorite painters/artists probably living, his response was “I can’t believe you made this”.  That’s probably the best thing I could have heard.

The songs about being honest with yourself, even about the ugly shit.  It’s a tune of ambivalence.  And is sort of on the subject of not knowing.  Not exactly being sure.  Trying to face yourself but the image keeps changing.  Trying to see what is actually there, and what you’re just dreaming up.   I think today people can toxically be like, “Face your demons! Change your life! Get your act together!”  I think it’s way more complex than that and that we are constantly shape-shifting.  Sometimes you’re the fool, sometimes you’re a genius, sometimes criminal.  The song sort of deals with facing all of these sides. 


My good friend and touring partner Sol Was played bass on it, his brother Henry played the drums. Johan Lenox did the strings and backgrounds.  Hope you enjoy.

Description:
to celebrate my 1-YEAR ANNIVERSARY in web3, i am sooo excited/proud/honored to release this celebratory anthem, FWM! this song speaks to the joy and liberation that web3 has brought me in this past year. 

i released my first NFT in November of 2021 and didn't know what the hell i was doing. “what is a mint? wait, it means to sell and to buy?” “what is gas and what am i putting it in?” “why is everyone saying ‘GM’?” i was lost for a long time, yo. lmao. but with time, support, and a strenuous amount of studying, i grew to know and love this incredible space that we're in— a space that allows artists to finally see the value of their work, to actually make a living off of their art, and to create communities with people who genuinely care about them and want them to win. coming from web2, this was so new for me. it was the breath of fresh air that i prayed for, and i'll always appreciate this space for that.

fast-forward a year and i'm the Head of Artist Relations for the very music NFT platform you are on right now! helping artists everyday experience that same freedom and joy that i've experienced! learning to teach, getting to give. i couldn't have planned or even imagined that a year could change my life the way that it did, but God did, and i'm grateful for His grace everyday.

our first music showcase Sound Lounge Live is this Wednesday, 11/16 and Art Basel is right around the corner, so i had to make us something to dance to okay! something to celebrate ourselves to! i know that every day in crypto isn't a pretty one, but we've got so much to be proud of and i really need us all to know that.

i'm scheduling "FWM!" to go live at 11pm pst on 11/16 because— yes—  I'M DOING A LIVE MINT AT THE SOUND LOUNGE LIVE SHOW!! if all goes according to plan (*fingers crossed*), i'll be on stage and we can all mint this at the same time! I started working on a project called OG Cool (Only Good Comes Out Of Living) in the fall of 2013 with one of my best friends, super-producer, Nash B. During that period of time we recorded 30-40 songs towards what I thought would be the final album. The summer of the following year I lost the only hard-drive that had every session file/track-out and bounce for my entire catalog of unreleased music (1200+ songs/production/demos) to that point, (OG Cool included). A few years ago I began to recover some of the music from that hard-drive (Thank God for clouds and email accounts lol) One of my favorites from those album sessions (and closest to me) is a song called "Brothers Talk".

Growing up in the states as a child to an immigrant family, I grew used to not having a lot of blood-related family around me. It was always just me and my little brothers. This upbringing conditioned me to value the people closest to me as family and not just friends.
"Brothers Talk" was a chance for me to hold a conversation with two close friends (that have always been brothers to me) during their times of need. One friend lost a father and the other lost his way.
I originally intended on placing this on the album but for now this is a just a marker for major moments in time. This is the last bounce I did after I originally recorded the record at my home studio.

Much love to the good homie, Myles Stefan for the amazing guitar solo at the end and my lil bro Nash B for supporting me getting back to my production (I made this beat). This song is in honor of my blood brothers Chris and Thorence (Long Live Baby Thor). I consider the people who care enough to listen to and support my music my family. As I work on my album (among a million projects lol) and we continue to build up this VibeHaus family, I wanted to offer this song as an invitation to join the Tribe. 

This is me, no final mix, just soul & love. I appreciate you for walking on this journey with me. The way is just a little bit longer but we're almost there.

Description:
We wrote Snow Globe after being hit with the first major snowstorm of the season in 2021 while writing our record, Islanders, on Mackinac Island. We’d anticipated being snowed in prior to moving into our Island apartment and setting up our studio. When the snow started falling from the thick clouds, engulfing the island, we knew it was time to start in on our song "Snow Globe".

Weather can change on a dime on Mackinac Island because of its position nestled in Lake Huron and north of the 45th parallel. The aim was to capture the other-worldly phenomenon that only this small island can experience; existing in a real-life snow globe.

"Snow Globe" was produced by FINKEL and Josh Stadlen, mixed by Khushi, and mastered by Dale Becker. “Snow Globe” is the last song of our album, Islanders, which also serves as the score of our feature-length documentary also titled, Islanders. To watch the documentary, head to islandersfilm.com.

Description:
friends was sort of a song that came from an experience i had during summer of last year where i was with this girl but i didn’t want to make anything official or have to deal with labels or gossip - it was basically just a situationship. of course i didn’t think to call it that at the time so ended up writing about being “friends” that make out sometimes.

the writing/production process was pretty straightforward; i wanted that indie-pop, COIN, backseat lovers sound i had heard before and this was my first time ever trying to replicate something like that in my own song which was interesting to figure out on my own. but honestly the song already had that perfect hook so everything afterwards just came naturally.

so it wasn’t much of a surprise when in november 2021 a snippet of the song went viral on tiktok and caught on with indie-pop lovers — who regrettably waited 6 months before the song actually hit streaming platforms — regardless, i knew people would come back to hear the full song. so after going back and forth with mixing/mastering for a few months the song was finally ready and dropped in february of this year.

You love to talk, but you don’t listen. This is one of the tracks that early on started to shape the upcoming, now completed project.  I was looking for a bridge between hip hop and live instrumentation, and also reggae?, and also Beatles-inspired grooves, and also something lighthearted that you could dance to.  Listen was the result.  I think music is a melting pot more than ever and I hope when people listen to my music they can references dozens of influences because that’s essentially how these songs are made.  But at the end of the day, the song feels like me.  If it didnt, we wouldn’t be here releasing it. 

Listen is track 4 off the new project, which I haven’t officially announced to the public.  But it is coming in December.  The project is a journey, almost feels like a road trip, reminiscent of a kerouac novel - but tinted by the strange, modern, polluted times we are in now.   

I remember playing this record after previewing Young Fel 2 to my label at the time.  We had just finished playing a lot of the darker records off of YF2 and some of the label heads had stepped out to take calls, and finish their business.  I continued playing unreleased records of mine and Listen was the first one I played after the album.  It lit up the room.  It felt like the light at the end of the tunnel and I remember my friend Clay (who did the artwork for this nft as well as all the upcoming ones), giving me this look of…shit, well when is that one dropping?  It didn’t fit on Young Fel 2 but I knew it’d find its place.  To me, its home is on this upcoming project.  Hope you all enjoy and thank you for listening and supporting.

This song is the title track for my album. This album means everything to me. I have never poured out my heart the way I did with these songs. I have a fear of not making the best music I am capable of making before I die, so I push myself as hard as I can everyday to try and achieve that. For every chip on my shoulder that I have gained, this album is in retaliation for that. Every time I have been pushed and shoved to be a certain type of artist, it has brought me closer to this. I once had a manager threaten to ruin my career, and told me I'd be singing songs in my room for the rest of my life. My career hadn’t even started yet. When I was with a major label, nothing I made was good enough. I was never good enough. I went on a TV singing show and I was told I wasn't good enough in front of millions of people, and was bombarded with so much hate on the internet, it made me throw up. I have had my indie managers that told me I was "way too basic and nothing about me was special", and my pop managers told me "if it's not a hit then throw it away. You have to be perfect." I was born and raised in West Hollywood, so maybe these are years that I couldn’t have avoided. After dealing with that for 6 years, after feeling like I was a piece of dough for everyone to mold, I finally snapped. I shut all the voices out. I’m not impressionable anymore. The freedom I feel to finally be creating whatever I want, is the most incredible feeling in the world. Produced, written, & mixed by me.
I think the Medicine might be working, I feel kind of powerful. #FEVER

Description:
I am a Jamaican Reggae Fusion Artist, a peaceful warrior always looking on the bright side. Elevating collective consciousness one idea at a time, serving the SkyStarter community. 

SkyStarters are tenacious, creative, optimistic, compassionate and empathetic. They can also be misfits and misunderstood. The only requirement to be a Skystarter is that We Never Give Up. Within us is an innate power that comes to the aid of the resilient and weaving through the SkyStarter fabric is an unwavering tenacity to Never Give Up 

Wake up created a portal that reminds me to always step into the NOW. Regardless of the past, what matters, NOW, is that I must pick up the hammer and get to work. This song is me coming to terms with the past and even the future. Realizing all I really have is NOW. 

I wrote this song looking for a new path to the same destination. I knew where I wanted to be but I know I wasn't going in the best direction to make it a reality. I became self-aware about the stories in my head and felt the courage and faith to wake up and create a new story

Wake Up is a call to take a hold of life and take our goals seriously. To be present despite the past, despite the future. Be present with all your mind, heart and soul. 

To Wake Up everyday with a picture and a purpose, with intention, with gratitude. Wake Up is an ode to nature. An anthem for more love, for the hungry to be fed. A celebration to embrace who you are and Never Give Up.

Each holder of Wake Up gets a free mint from the upcoming album collection, a private link to the album and access to a token-gated performance of tracks from the album.

i wrote “In My Head” after beating myself up for having the most outlandish thoughts.  humans think over 17,000 thoughts a day, on average, and often times we let those narratives drive us to some pretty insane beliefs.

your own mind can be your biggest enemy; flooded with wild ideas around the what ifs and how’s and when’s, or even "what would happen if i just stopped my car in the middle of the freeway right now?"

our mind can be more dangerous than the outside world; dictating your belief system about yourself & the world & persuading you to believe scenarios that are far from reality. “In My Head” was a response to the recognition of how important it is to not identify with each and every thought that infiltrates your brain, & to remind yourself of who you know u are at ur core <3 i hope you like it :’)

Description:
AmbieNFT is a generative modular synth music NFT project that has topped the top of the blocks and plumbed the depths of synthesis depravity. Over the past year sixty-two pieces have been generatively created and human refined … their traits, modules, tempos and keys governed by an all-seeing hexadecimal hash.

On this Sound of Fractures remix I worked backwards from the shuffled chorus shaker, anchoring the track around it and introducing some polyrhythms by displacing elements of the original beat. Some house’y arpeggios quickly materialized and before long I had worked my way backwards all the way to an ambient rhodes + modular synth introduction that laid a nice foundation for a verse vocal feature.

Hip Hop, Jungle and UK Bass are musical siblings, eternally connected through their cultural roots. So it is no coincidence that the heart of Kabuki beats for all of these seemingly disparate genres. For more than 20 years his music productions covered the full spectrum of beat science, but misty-eyed nostalgia isn’t Kabuki’s thing. Instead, he is more interested in the present and future of electronic music. And more than style and aesthetics he is in pursuit of the elusive element that keeps it all moving: the soul

For me a good remix should showcase an aspect of the original that went by unnoticed. So my first course of action was to familiarise myself with the source material in search of a creative spark. I eventually found a background vocal which became the nucleus of the track, adding a completely new twist to the melody by means of reharmonisation. I also wanted to expand on the UK Garage vibe of the original by adding a Jungle twist and paying homage to my. roots. The end result stays true to the original while sitting comfortably between all genre definitions.

Description:
I released the official production of “Grateful” a few weeks ago, and I wanted to try something new on here. First off, as a thank you to everyone who collected the first edition, you are all receiving this drop for free! And to anyone who wasn’t able to collect the official drop (*cough cough my dad*) this one is for you. This release is actually the first demo that I made of “Grateful” back in 2020. The execution of the vocal is emotional yet super raw, and the lyrics aren’t quite as locked as the official drop, but there is a magic to it that I am so in love with and I think deserves to be appreciated too. Which, of course, made me think of you all! I love the idea of web3 setting the standard for a new artist/fan/friend relationship, and I want my work here to reflect that. This drop for me represents the opening of my green-room, and a welcome to my studio, where I get to share all the mistakes along the way, all the lessons learned, and all of the fun behind writing and producing music I love. Y’all all the first to hear this version of the song, and if you feel inspired to collect it, thank you, and I appreciate you so much. Cheers to getting to know one another!

-Nico

"Grateful" is about how to ease the blush of unfamiliarity when entering a new relationship. I wrote it when I made friends with the feeling of having just enough fuel to jump AND just enough fear to shut my eyes when I do it. This song is quite a bit more specific than my previous releases. As “Stuck” talked about trusting the feeling over the circumstance, and “Paint in the Dark” described the over-arching agreements that I have observed in the healthiest love, “Grateful” exemplifies these themes using the intimacy of a pillow talk conversation. It is about putting what I’ve learned into action and trusting what happens next. 

"Grateful (Demo)"
Written by Nicolas Cyril De Luca-Verley (Nico Franc)
Produced, Mixed, and Mastered by Nicolas Cyril De Luca-Verley (Nico Franc), and Dean Woodson
With additional vocal production by AJ Jenkins

Description:
OTHERSIDE –

This song is a perfect example of why nothing created is ever useless. Pieced together from 4 different songs I created over the past 3 years. Lyrics that never felt connected, spliced and crafted to make what I had tried to accomplish with each song made. Production elements from songs I have released, and songs I haven't.

This one is incredibly special to me.

Trying to explain the meaning behind it would only be doing it a disservice, but what I will say is that in life you are often given a choice and those are what make or break us. Time and happenings make those choices harder for some, and for a long time I chose wrong. I don't want to die young.
A special one from the vault - one of the earliest tracks I made for the BRUX project but never released.

Who is right or wrong?

We all need to decide what we value and what love we accept. Too often people don’t stick up for what they truly believe at the thought of not being accepted. 

The proceeds from this song will fund a nonprofit DAO that gives free studio time to musicians in the web3. Holders of this song will get to nominate and help determine the artists. The studio space is located in Los Angeles to start and will be looking to partner with other studios around the world.

Description:
“Encarte”, tiene un sonido fresco electrónico, pero con un trasfondo íntimo que contrasta el sonido de la canción, aquí se habla sobre los problemas de ansiedad, y ansiedad social que enfrenta todo el tiempo una persona, estos problemas le hacen tener miedo a enamorarse y dejar que se enamoren de ella, haciendo que su primer pretendiente entre en alerta antes de decidir entrar en una relación amorosa con la misma.  “Encarte” es un término muy utilizado en Colombia para referirse a cosas que se interpreten como una carga pesada difícil de llevar, muy molesta e incomoda. 

Verónica Caicedo, actriz, cantante, rapera y compositora de Buenaventura - Colombia, estudiante de Licenciatura en Arte Dramático. Desde el 2018 comenzó un proceso musical que incluía videos y composiciones caseras, se hizo muy conocida en varios lugares del país, y más adelante formaliza su entrada a la industria musical lanzando sus dos primeras canciones, “Don José” y “Yo Soy Dios”, ambas producidas por Colombo, y Sammy el Comandante, estas marcaron el inicio de su carrera musical y hoy con 5 lanzamientos musicales es una de las referentes de la cuarta generación de artistas más importante de su país.

"Encarte" has a fresh electronic sound, but with an intimate background that contrasts the sound of the song, here we talk about anxiety problems, and social anxiety that a person faces all the time, these problems make them afraid of fall in love and let them fall in love with her, causing her first suitor to go on alert before deciding to enter into a love relationship with her. "Encarte" is a term widely used in Colombia to refer to things that are interpreted as a heavy load that is difficult to carry, very annoying and uncomfortable.

Verónica Caicedo, actress, singer, rapper and composer from Buenaventura - Colombia, Bachelor of Dramatic Arts student. Since 2018, he began a musical process that produced videos and homemade compositions, became well known in various parts of the country, and later formalized his entry into the music industry by releasing his first two songs, "Don José" and "Yo Soy Dios" , both produced by Colombo, and Sammy el Comandante, these marked the beginning of his musical career and today, with 5 musical releases, he is one of the references of the fourth generation of most important artists in his country.

Description:
While I continue to grow up and be a teenager, I feel so many emotions all at once. The good, the bad, the crazy. It’s hard to pinpoint where everything stems from. I tend to struggle with how fast time flies by, too busy focusing on trying to slow down the present, that I miss what’s already happened. And there are times where I find people questioning my beliefs, or my feelings towards others. As humans, we are constantly juggling so many different aspects in our life, trying to find a balance. 

Devan and I love this track. We make all our music together and give it our all every time. Magic is the only outcome. I like to think that this song creates an escape for all of us. Or even a safe place to be ourselves. A place to finally exhale. Without judgment, without fear, without stress, and without worries. 

‘Don’t Have to Explain’ spreads a little light on all the flourishing stresses we have. About making decisions, wanting to pause and be in the moment, and even protecting our own space. We should never feel obligated to have to explain ourselves. We should be open and understanding of each other. We should encourage and learn from one another. 

Be present.  
Be mindful. 
Be grateful. 
When you listen to this song, know that you are here. 
And you don’t have to explain a thing. 

- mia lailani & devan ibiza 
<3

'Sundreamer' represents a bit of a rebirth for me. Going through the loss of my father this past year crushed a lot of my creative spirit. My dad was someone I could always send my demos to and he would use his keen ears to give me feedback. Part of the joy I got from making music was getting to share my work with him. Losing him took a lot out of me. 

Even before my dad got sick, I was on a strange trajectory with music. I was pretty caught up in trying to make music that would perform well on streaming services. Often I would optimize my songs to fit Spotify playlists so I could make a decent income. The downside of that was that I was making quite a few creative sacrifices and just wasn’t enjoying what I was making anymore. 

With ‘Sundreamer’ I’m going back to my roots of making music for the joy of it. I’m in a new creative chapter now and am shedding that popularity-centric point of view. Music and creativity are so important to me that I need to let them flourish before I worry about anything else. 

I’m back to basics, making music that speaks to my soul.

Last month I did a free drop for the demo of this song on Sound, and now before releasing on any other platforms, I'm dropping the full song! 

To catch you up to speed on the story of the song: 
Earlier this year, I was in a long-distance relationship with a girl from Florida. Shortly after her and I broke up, I was back down in Florida with Friends and spent a little too much time and money trying to forget I was hurting. I went to bars and casinos and let loose. Weirdly enough, I had started a demo called "down in florida", months prior, that nearly described the exact situation I now found myself in with her. I didn't have the words to finish the song until I was back in Nashville a week later and decided to continue writing the song from my current situation. Hence, the opening of the second verse "i'm back in Nashville..." This track tells the story of how I did anything but face the truth of my reality. I wasn't ready to face the consequences of my actions.

My team and I are committed to growing in the Web 3 space and are confident that your investments in my music will be more than worth it! I've amassed over 200 million streams independently and, as I'm now dropping a song every two weeks, the music will only grow quicker than ever. - Munn

This was one of those songs that took me back to a moment in time when I wrote it...

Early 2010
Hollywood, California
Los Angeles Recording School

I was 17 years old when I graduated high school. I almost immediately moved from Orange County to LA. I couldn't get out of my mom's house quick enough. I just wanted to feel like an adult. To be in my own apartment. To be in college. To just live.

I thought going to recording school was the answer to all my prayers. I would learn everything I needed to know about recording + engineering. I would graduate and start making music. Then get signed. Then... I don't know. That was as far as I thought it through. Everything would go as planned.

Yeah... nope.

School just wasn't for me. Los Angeles wasn't for me. Hollywood wasn't for me. And truthfully, there was a time when I thought music just wasn't for me.

This song is about that time.

Looking back I feel like I needed that experience. I feel like understanding what we don't want is sometimes just as important as understanding what we do want.

And I don't want that life. Of course I want to be able to live and create and provide for my family but I don't believe that the "Hollywood Route" is the only way.

So here we are 12 years later in Web 3 dropping NFTs and just figuring this sh*t out.

And I'm not mad at it...

Thank you to all of you for showing me that there's another way.

All love, always.

In my feelings one night, playing with ableton, this song started to pour out. I was tired of being caught in cycles that never break no matter how painful they become. Patterns in music and patterns in life. Cycles of abuse or misunderstanding that led to pain in intimacy, community and larger exploitative institutions. Infused in this song is a vow: this will be the last time. With this release I am empowering myself as a sovereign artist and individual: alive, human, imperfect, and fully embodied.

After living with this song for a while, I brought it to Segnon’s studio to track some bass from Clark Simz. Clark laid down his brilliant bass and Seg and I watched the song shift directions. This version was asking to be more raw. Channeling being pushed too far, I broke my voice, then sustained that tension until my breath went out and the song could find release. 

I love that the culture and technology within web3 allow us to break free from institutionalized patterns of control. And I won’t come back ;) This is the first drop from MARI season 1.

Description:
I’m Valentina Cy, and I’m an LA born and raised (and never left) artist. I have been singing since I could speak, and I was raised in a house where making music was second nature. When I was 22 I went to a scholarship program created by Mike Posner called Amor Fati, where he took 5 artists and 10 mentors  to Telluride Colorado, and taught each one of all skills that we needed to become better artists. I was taught how to make a demo on Ableton. Since then I have been producing, writing, and mixing all my music. 

I am a self-managed independent artist, and I am gearing up to release an album November 16th. The album is called ‘when you feel like dying’. The first song I am dropping on Sound is a single from the album. It’s called ‘cantaloupe ave.’ and it’s a song that I had to cry a lot to make. I used a voice memo from someone in my past, and I wrote the song about them as well. The cover art is also a picture of the street that they used to live on. This song is essentially very simple. It’s comprised of a cut up voice memo, my friend Gabe Noel on the cello, a kick, some fucked up piano, and vocals. I like when a song is able to hit me where it hurts, and this one did that for me.

A few months ago I almost quit music and I didn’t really feel like I had a purpose in life anymore. It took me making cantaloupe ave., and this entire album, to make it feel like I had something worth living for. That might sound ironic since the name of the album is ‘when you feel like dying’, but sometimes you have to leech all the bad out to feel something good.

There's a yearning for liberation that can only be satiated in private. By recording myself alone, I found the prowess to move and perform freely, capturing moments that wouldn't have existed otherwise. “Private Room” is a song about wanting to share that private liberation with someone. 

I had stopped making music for a while before working on this track. Changing my stage name from Eunice to YUNICE symbolize my recommitment back into being an artist. I moved to LA from Lisbon in June ’22 with four suitcases and my cat. Feeling the bear market struggles, I crashed on friends’ couches while looking for a private room to rent, and took the plunge into the music NFT scene. 

TB, a music producer who’s worked with major label artists, found me on instagram and wanted to work together. I was skeptical at first but took the chance and met with him. We clicked instantly on a profound artistic level. We wrote “Private Room” in our first meeting. It was almost too intense how much he understood my vocals and vision. I wanted dark and sexy and some cello, and we made just that.

Hello!

Everyone of us has a new turn in life we eventually all take. For some it can be warm, tender and harmonious. For others it's rough, dire, and difficult. In this life, everyday, we experience situations that lead us to two things: a choice and a chance. The combination of these two concepts can create a New Turn for the best or for the worst. Living in New York City, I'm constantly witnessing these new experiences unfold. Dreamers come to the big apple for a New Turn to make their dreams come true, their goals a reality, to pursue the life they dream of having, and some come here simply to escape their own reality.

As I grew up, discovering music as a full time career became my New Turn. In the midst of all the noise and ruckus this city brings, I find the most clarity and silence through it all. I met Deffie IRL back in May 2022, though before the real life interaction, we had been connected over Discord during the pandemic. We managed to create an 8 track project consisting of features from MIA GLADSTONE, as well as co-production from myself. Before the collaboration, for years, I was a genuine fan of DEFFIE’s. I remember regularly playing some of his biggest hits on Soundcloud like “Backstroke” & “Gaskethead”. Upon creating this tape, we both were beginning to find a home in web3, and as we're rolling out our own projects a year later, here we are creating a New Turn in the space, hoping this sound inspires anyone to take that leap of faith themselves.

Description: She's a bit of a problem

As somebody who is always moving and shaking, I felt it was a period where God forced me to sit down and reevaluate whats really important in life. The song “Thank You” was inspired by that time. I had a ruptured achilles which put me out of work, and in what I call a “space boot” (cast)  for six months. For the first few months I could hardly do anything. I Even needed my wife to get in and out of the shower. 

  It was starting to get depressing, but then one day at physical therapy I was looking around at people in way worse situations than me. Some we’re probably never even going to be able to walk again. But they were all smiling and doing what they had to do to improve their situation. It was that moment something clicked for me, and I started to look at my own situation in a positive light. 

  I was finally just home. No traveling, none of the constant stresses of work, and most importantly I got to be with my wife and kids everyday. We would take frequent vacations and even though I couldn't walk, I was happier spending time with my loved ones than I had been in years. Time is the most valuable thing that we have on this planet, and it’s expiring from the very second your born. I wrote this song because I was thankful for that time period. My family and friends showed me that even when your out hustling trying to elevate in life, never lose sight of whats truly important. God showed me the real reason to be Thankful. Thank You…

Description:
Hi my name is Cailin Russo. I’ve been a singer-songwriter for almost 10 years. I was raised in San Diego California by 2 punk rock and rollers and a fan of music since the day I entered the earth. My father is in a pop punk band called Unwritten Law, he was the first to invite me into the songwriting space when I was 16. We had just suffered a house fire and were staying at a family friend's house who had the first recording equipment I had ever seen (consciously). From that point on I wrote songs semi religiously. 
 
	I signed to a label a couple years later and began my serious musical journey. I dropped my first song called “September Rose” which did really well and is still one of my highest streamed songs, it is about love coming in at the wrong time. This tone of writing became a staple in a lot of my songs; very melancholic, feminine/ sexy. From there I continued to drop 2/3 more songs in a similar genre then completely switched up everything and started a very no doubt esq feeling band. The band lasted about 2 years and then we broke apart for me to continue to see my solo career bloom. 
 
	After breaking apart from the band and label completely I was on a quest of rediscovery and rebirth. I made a complete body of work compiling all my favorite elements from indie, electronic and r&b. Independent from any label I am dropping my second single off the album “DIE DOWN”. DIE DOWN is a dark electronic song that was made by myself and JJ Scheffy in his basement mid pandemic. The story around the song is about 2 star crossed lovers that take their romance and inhibitions all the way to a point where nothing else exists. Everything else dies down.

Description:
Whatupdoe! My name is Curtis Roach. I am a musician and content creator from Detroit, MI. I've been making music in web2 for about 7 years now, mostly releasing via soundcloud and DSPs.  I’ve been looking to expand more into Web3 with my music. 

Most of my music could be described as “feel good rap” so I wanted to drop the same vibe for my first Web3 release. I made this song while I was working on my last project “the joy tape” -  I just felt good that day and wanted to capture it in this vibe. For my first Music NFT I want to give my collectors a musical hug pretty much! 

I’m excited to dive deeper into the music NFT space.  I have been observing and interacting in this beautiful space for a while and learned so much. I’ve met so many great people and made genuine connections with likeminded people who love art. I've been super excited for my first drop and ready to share with y'all this great piece of work.

Several years ago, seemingly out of nowhere, my mind sort of betrayed me. 

I had developed an anxiety disorder that was, in a word, crippling. 
'Panic disorder', my doctor called it. 
In a nutshell, my mind would play games on me. When explaining it  to people now, I sometimes say to imagine that heightened anxiety or fear you get when something scares you (a feeling that usually dissipates after you realize you aren't in real danger) as a permanent feeling. Like the pit you get in your stomach during the free-fall of a rollercoaster ride, except it never goes away. 

At the time, I felt like I couldn't talk to anyone about what I was feeling because I thought no one would understand- I myself barely understood what was happening to me. It was an incredibly scary and lonely experience, (that fortunately I was eventually able to come out of thanks to therapy and medication), and I really felt like a complete stranger to myself and to everyone around me.  

I wrote 'has anybody seen me?' about that time. 

I really hope you enjoy this record. It was produced by two incredible producers, Mike Daley and Mitchell Owens.

Description: This is my first solo release on sound called "Exhaustin." This song is about taking love for granted and realizing that you can't get too comfortable in a relationship. You have to love like you never had your significant other cause if you don't, someone will. Enjoy!
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BW9tMaJimlU

I feel at peace after my last release.

I feel like there has been a lot on my head + heart lately that I needed to get off before moving forward. Life can throw a lot at us and I know that things can not always go as planned but I'm in a space where I just want to share my music with you all. 

I don't want to overthink it. I don't want to stress. I don't want to wait. So this is the first of my weekly releases to close out the year.

Each of these songs are moments in time and I'm grateful that we can share them together.

I remember recording the hook to this song first which I usually never do. It was like 3 in the morning and I had so much energy but I couldn't come up with the words to fill in the verses so I decided not to force it.

I probably let it sit for another day or two then when I finally came back to it the words just flowed.

"Tell me baby one time at least..."

And this song was born. It also has one of my favorite bars I've ever written:

"I think about you daily, you like my blood you call me 'Bae' I'd rather call you brazy... I saw the red flags early."

Like... come on guys. 🤣

I know I repeatedly say this, but Web³ has completely changed how I think about my music. How I release it. The value I place on it. What I truly want my message and impact to be.

And I will always put the music first. That is my only promise. There may be times where I need to tend to me. Times where I'm not as active on social media or I can't show up in the ways I would like to. But I promise you that if I put a song out into the world that I gave it my all.

Thank you guys for supporting me. For the constant reminder that I am walking the path I am meant to walk. 

All love, always.

Description: Vulnerable" is an emotional awakening in song form. It explores the idea of vulnerability being human nature; something we all go through within our lives in one way or another. Such alien and uncomfortable feelings can make us feel very alone and stagnant. The harmonic arrangements within the vocals help to reflect just how emotionally complex we are as humans and that it can be very hard to switch these emotions off at times. We hope this song connects with people on a deeper level and bring an elements of comfort to those who need it.

Originally lost in the "Great M1 Macbook Migration", this is a bailé remix of the intro track to easily my most masterful work to date, "CHROMA" released June of 2018, finalized and immortalized in, and inspired while I was in Thailand for the very first time.

This project is another of my many releases that speaks to and of my soul, the kind of style of music I wanna hear everywhere, and this particular track (the original) is what birthed the whole rest of CHROMA. After having released 3 of these very rare remixes ONLY on-chain, on another truly dope music NFT marketplace, Catalog, I feel like I inadvertently saved the best of the remixes for last, none more representative of the most evolved of my signature sound than this groove right here, and I want everyone to know that collects it:  light a candle, smoke a bowl or a joint, concoct your favorite libation, and put this one on repeat, and prepare to get lost in this groove, as this was what it was designed for.

For nothing else moves me more than making others do the same 
🙏🏽🕺🏽💃🏽...

An artist's journey 

With every project and musical endeavor I always try to approach it with a different perspective, like all artists I assume, in hopes of creating something new. That journey has brought me to the web 3 space and Soundxyz.
 
Like many artists, I’ve spent the last couple years exploring web 3, studying the use cases and trying to pinpoint just exactly where I fit in the space. I always aim to maintain a sense of quality and authenticity with the content I release, even when it may result in great ideas being left on the proverbial cutting room floor. 

‘White Paint’ was one of the songs born from many sessions, originally supposed to land on an EP I made called ‘Vista”. When Sango sent the original beat, and while writing the song I remember thinking “this is different, this is new”. This is the moment we as creatives strive for right? To break new ground within ourselves, taking a risk on you and it actually working out. 

When going over the tracklist for the project, ‘White Paint’ ultimately didn't make it. It may have been too different from what everything else on the EP sounded like. Which unfortunately, was what a lot of music we listen to now sounds like. I have a tendency to second guess an idea that doesn't “fit”, deem it unworthy of consumption, and ultimately regret my decision. 

As an artist the last thing I want to have are regrets when it comes to my output. So with my genesis drop I’m letting it fly, because in the end it won't matter the excuse, only that I again denied myself the opportunity to be vulnerable in my art.

Get Back Up is supposed to feel like a like a letter to my close friends and family. Music has always been an outlet where I have been able to a show a more vulnerable side of myself and talk about things I normally wouldn't share. Essentially what I'm saying in this song  is even though sometimes life can be hard, and I may feel defeated, I know that there's light at the end of the tunnel. My hope is that whoever hear's this song is able to apply it to their own personal situation and find the strength to keep pushing forward.

This release, it’s a tribute to my Parents. From the hand-drawn cover, to the music, to the sounds that are in the music. Without my parent's support and encouragement, I wouldn’t be here today. In the beat there's half of a speech from my friend saying to follow your dreams and goals and that's something my parents always told me and supported, at the end, she says I miss you chow chow, and as I moved to another state that's how I always feel, I will always miss them but I know that they are right here with me always cheering me on to keep going.

Description:
We’ve all heard stories about the lost city in the depths of the ocean. There’s always been something that’s drawn me into the idea of mystical creatures living under the sea. This song is off of my debut album, a special piece of my heart and soul. A monumental moment of time in my artist career and I’m so excited to share it right here on Sound exclusively. 

Encapsulating my story of coming to America from South Africa, living in LA in the middle of a global pandemic. Atlantis is about finding a safe haven amidst chaos and the bliss of finding a space to retreat. It took me almost 3 years to finally find that feeling again after moving to a new country and going through so much to make it in LA. I made this song with my favourite artist/producer Os Young, lyrically it really flowed so effortlessly that we immediately knew we had something special and meaningful. 

Visually continuing from Black Ice, building the storyline of KAIEN which is a character based on my life experiences. I teamed up with my good friend and graphic artist Alex Rodrigues to create an underwater backdrop with a modern twist on the lost city of Atlantis. 

This is the second drop of many that I’m planning for my debut album and I can’t wait to continue this journey with you all. 

With love always - Kai

Description:
„From Beyond“ comes with a story that I’d like to share. It all started with a reel of quarter-inch tape that I discovered in a box in the attic. After some investigation it turned out to be a recording of my maternal grandfather playing the piano. He passed away before I was born so while we never met, this artifact connected us through time. 

It struck me as a strange experience that somebody who was long gone could reach out through the ether, both emotionally and physically. After all, what is a recording but a vibration frozen in time? These particular vibrations had their points of origin when my grandfather played the piano almost 60 years ago, so in a very real sense we made a metaphysical connection through a reel of tape.

This realization haunted me ever since, only waiting for the right moment to materialize as creative spark for a new project. And with my sound.xyz debut scheduled for Halloween, I knew that this was the perfect opportunity to use the recordings of my grandfather playing the piano to communicate with him across the ocean of time. 

I’ve spent most of my adult life in the studio manipulating sounds and frequencies, but it was „From Beyond“ that taught me how my recordings will be my physical presence long after I'm gone.

WIRED is about living a lifestyle of toxicity and self destruction, because you’re at a time in your life where that feels right. Be sure to watch your back when riding on the edge of that, because one wrong move and the flames will swallow you whole.

Description:
Before Web3 I was 100% dedicated to songwriting, I always liked rapping, it was the first genre I fell in love with! but I put it aside with the excuse that it was a hobby for me, that I liked being behind the scenes. A year ago I decided that in addition to being a composer, I also wanted to release my music, I felt the call to express what I have inside, and this feeling coincided with the moment I met Web3, it was as if the universe was telling me: Hey you have talent and energy, now I'm going to give you the tools. It's funny, because people saw me and thought I was joking until they heard me rapping... Now, I have more conviction than anyone, and I even created my own crowdfund to be able to finance my first album as a rapper, to become the first latin artist to be born with Web3.

This is my first Hip Hop  song in the space, I had to save it for Sound XYZ. I'm serious when I say I want to make a historic album for rap in Spanish. This song is just the appetizer of all the fire that I'm going to give you, and I wrote it in a small room in my house, inspired by the Californian vibe and my life experiences. 

It talks about how this dream doesn't let me sleep, I feel it all day in my chest telling me to keep pushing, because it's not only going to change my life, but also my family, my colleagues and all the people I love. It talks about how I chose art above all else, because this is what I was born for and I just discovered. Rap is in my veins, despite the fact that I wasn´t born in a city totally influenced by hip hop or trap... it was something innate, that was given to me in an inexplicable way.

The music was made by Yogev, a friend with whom I made a lot of music in the past and with whom I met again on Web3... I already had the idea of ​​the lyrics and the melody, I even knew how I wanted to structure the beat, but I needed a person who understood me and could maximize my ideas. I immediately thought of Yogev, because he was one of the people who told me that I should release my rap when I was just a songwriter, And I knew how talented he was musically.

I want to dedicate this song to all my friends from Web3 who have supported me since day one, and who saw potential in me and my vision. Thank you for collecting,  motivating me and advising me, you are part of this. I promise you the best is about to come.

This is song 2 from CACOPHONY, a new project from Reo Cragun and myself. CACOPHONY is a beautiful explosion. Deafeningly loud and chaotic and intimate at the same time. 

FROM REO:
The jig is up is honestly about reading through the facade and people’s BS. 

The road of an independent artist can be extremely difficult at first, but if you put in the work it can prove to be really rewarding. Fortunately now I’m in a position where I don’t have to jump at a major label deal anymore and have the means to comfortably support myself. Oddly enough it’s at that point when a lot of people come knocking to partner. 

We were really just having fun with this record and reflecting on the level we’ve gotten to based off hard work and staying consistent.

FROM CLEAR EYES:

Having fun was so key with this one. Reo and I make a lot of heavy shit together (like the first single from CACOPHONY, HEAVEN) but it’s important to balance that with music that makes you feel good, makes you feel powerful. We love Kevin George’s energy and adding a feature just added to the excellent vibes.

Description:
This is the first track on "Pandora's Box."

In the traditional version of the myth, Zeus gave Pandora a small box but said she must never open it. As Pandora was created to be curious, she eventually could not resist and opened the box. Out of the box came horrible evils such as sickness, death, poverty and sadness that were inflicted on humans.

In hindsight, using "Pandora's Box" to describe a relationship and the effects of it was overly dramatic, but the analogy still stands (in a mental way).

"annabelle" was meant to be soft & made to tug at your heartstrings. Sometimes your mood can be entirely lifted by hearing someone's voice or laughter. Sometimes you find purpose after a series of interactions.

One of my favorite things about music is its ability to take your mind away from everyday life to somewhere new. I love this feeling of being transported. It’s easy to lose track of everything else when you are lost in a song. That is my goal with every piece of music… I want your mind to drift off from the day to day when you listen.

I wrote Clouded back in early July and immediately knew I wanted to save it for a special moment in this web3 music journey. It was one of those sessions without a specific goal in mind, just playing around with different sounds and letting the idea lead. Continuing that line of thought, the name came from thinking about how clouded our view of the future actually is. Of course we should make plans and chase after our goals, but we don’t know what’s going to happen next. And often that is a beautiful thing. Many of the best moments aren’t things we plan for or even see coming. Our job is just to do our best and see where the journey goes.

Case in point for me is this drop. I didn’t see web3 music coming at all, and it has opened up a whole new world for me this year. Just showing up, creating music, collecting music, and engaging with our community here has made me more hopeful than ever for the future as an independent musician. Dropping on Sound has been a huge goal from the beginning, and I’m so happy with where the journey is at right now. I hope this song transports you somewhere, and thank you so much for your support.

I wrote 'In the Leaves' about a dream I had before I decided to quit my stable, full-time design job.

In the dream I kept waking up outside — on the sidewalk in San Francisco, and later in the leaves by a road. I kept choosing that over my bed, and it felt surprisingly calm to wake up outside of my home.

I had a session with Benji Cormack and we talked about this dream and how it seemed to mirror my life choice of staying in the comfort of a full-time job or leaving to focus on music and being satisfied with less.

I quit the job and now I've put out the song.

"I'm waking in the leaves again
Under street signs, never needed more.
Mapping out the turns I take
When I sleepwalk, why's it feel like home?"

Written by: Benji Cormack, Lyrah
Produced by: Nick Booth, Benji Cormack, Jon Wienner, Lyrah
Artwork by: Brendan Lowry

Description:
Emily Lazar is a multi-disciplinary artist fronting the rock/metal transmedia project, September Mourning. She made history as the first female metal/ hard rock musician to mint and sell an NFT on the blockchain. She has spoken about her accomplishments in Web 3/ NFT's at Harvard (2x), NFT.NYC and ETH Denver Conferences.

September Mourning is a transmedia project based on a comic book series she wrote and published through Image/Top Cow Comics with her business partner Marc Silvestri (Batman/Witchblade/Darkness). September Mourning is the title character. As a human reaper hybrid, she  gives expired souls a second chance at life in another body. In doing so, she messes with  the plans of the antagonist, Fate, who is trying to rid  earth of all the good souls and leave the bad so the world will self-destruct and It can start anew. An epic war between the living and the dead ensues. Emily plays the title character on stage.

Emily designed the world she and her band (Rich Juzwick, Kyle Mayer and Aaron Hoover) bring to life on stage, including costumes, choreography, sets, etc. The band has toured with & opened festivals for Rob Zombie, Marilyn Manson, Slipknot, Mudvayne and others across Europe and the United States.

Black Dave is an artist creating at the intersection of anime, streetwear, rap music and sneaker culture. Entering web3 in late 2020, he’s established himself as a thought leader and innovator within it. Having a background in punk and hardcore, as well as rap and production, collaborating with a metal band only made sense.

"Wake The Dead Featuring Black Dave" takes the September Mourning sound to a whole new level by infusing heavy metal with hip hop and trap music. The anthemic song lyrics by Emily reinforce the theme of the September Mourning storyline which is to own one's own voice and make one's own decisions with purpose and intent in order to squeeze every last incredible drop of life from one's soul while on this planet. Black Dave's lyrics reinforce that as well with a call to arms and intense fighting spirit. 

The artwork features Fate, the antagonist from the books and the subject that the song is rallying against.

Description:
Take a step into this Haus (House) that we've built and see this glorious trophy room of ours. 

Navigating through Web 3 has been an interesting and inspired experience. It is a journey that has altered my life (for the better) in a way that will be with me till the end of my time. Web 3 has created the opportunity to for me to reconnect with old family and build a new one. Every week for the past 7 months I commune with an amazing group of "Aliens" in a space we've grown to call home, known as Future Surf Radio. The things we have been able to accomplish together are nothing short of remarkable and I'm grateful to find myself in community with such beautiful collective of people. We laugh, we cry, we sing, we support, we affirm and we create together in Future Surf and most importantly we lead with love. 

"For The Family" is a song I created during our 50th Episode of FSR as an ode to my loved ones and the community we've built. This was directly inspired by all of the members and most specifically my good brother, Miles Ryan Harris, who lit the fire under me. To some this may just be really good "raps" but for those who know (IYKYK), this is a reminder of the power of love. There are so many people who have graced the Future Surf space that I wasn't able to mention or incorporate into the song but know that you forever have my heart.
On days when the weight of the world is crushing me, I know that I have a place to go where I'm loved and embraced and supported. It's knowing this that keeps me ground and keeps me going.

Description:
I wrote this song during a period of my life when I truly felt like a bit of a fuck up. Despite this, the people closest to me continued to believe in my vision, my music, and just ME... even when I didn’t believe in myself. I’d feel like a “sinking ship” at times yet, everyone came aboard, swords drawn high, ready to go to battle for something greater than ourselves. As I continued to write the song, it more or less turned into a prayer to God. I hope you all love the track, it means a lot to me. 

Now that you know about the song, here's how I got here. I grew up in Indiana but currently live in Nashville. When I was 15 I started playing guitar and writing music but didn't take it seriously until my Sophomore year of college.

In the summer of 2018, leading up to my Sophomore year, my engagement with my fiancée fell through, and I lost all interest in school. I was struggling to heal from the breakup, and I had no idea what I wanted to do with my life. It was during this time that I wrote my first song in over a year called I Tried. To this day, I can't describe how I felt after making that song. I had finally found my way to heal, and, from then on, creating music was all I wanted to do.
 
Around this time, a producer that I had connected with in 2017, named Dylan Stiles, was sending me beats every day. I would write and record to these beats every night using an Xbox headset and GarageBand. As time went on, we both decided that the best thing we could do was to drop out of school and go all-in on music. In July of 2019, with less than 4,000 monthly listeners on Spotify, Dylan and I moved to Nashville to do just that.
 
After a failed EP, we realized I needed a better strategy for putting out music. We decided that the best thing I could do was put out a new song every two weeks until one caught traction. On September 6th, 2019, we released the first song following this plan called I Lost Myself.

Currently, I am a fully independent singer/songwriter based out of Nashville. My team and I have been building my fan base over the past couple years and have amassed 200,000,000 streams, over a million monthly listeners on Spotify, 200k+ subs on YouTube, and more, all independently. While our music hasn’t stopped growing by any means, moving into the NFT space for additional support and a new way to connect with listeners was the logical next step for us.

Description:
Releasing this song feels like a necessary detour. I try my best to be as vulnerable as possible in my music but this was something I didn’t know how to say even though I knew it was necessary. I am many things. A man, a son, a brother, a friend, a musician. But above all else I am a father. That is my ultimate purpose. To lead by example for my sons. To teach them how to maneuver in a world not inherently designed for them to win. To break the cycle.

My journey throughout Web 3 thus far has been a time of affirmation (shoutout to Scolla.) It’s been a time of growth, learning, and healing. It’s been a time of not always doing the easiest (or most politically correct) thing, but having faith that it is the right thing as I continue forward.

I feel like I’m at the crossroad of stepping into my future and healing from my past, all while remaining present. I am working through my struggles in realtime - through music - and I hope that anyone who reads this understands that I am not defined by my circumstances, and neither are you. This has been a season that I feel is coming to a close. So although I am excited to share this piece of my story with you, I am equally as excited to have you with me as the rest of the story unfolds.

One thing that Web 3 has taught me is to better vocalize my needs. To not be afraid to say that I am not ok, or that I need help because we are not meant to walk alone.

I have been dealing with a traumatic situation involving my children and my family and I am thankful that I have the love and support to be able to say that I need help as I give this offering. I called this a necessary detour because that’s exactly how it feels. Like stopping for gas on a road trip. Knowing that this path is meant for me but that I had to take a second to address my needs and decompress before driving again.

So to anyone reading this, thank you for supporting me. Thank you for continuing to uplift me and remind me of my worth in the times when I may forget. Thank you for allowing me the opportunity to support my family by doing something I love. And thank you for helping me break the cycle. 

All love, always.

Been holding onto this song. I don't think I was ready to share it with the world, or at least the part of the world that's listening. There was a time where I couldn't even play the song for myself. 

A funny thing I have said before about being an artist is that it's the only profession where your next partner will know all about your last one. What comes with that is everyone else knowing as well. 

Many of you may know me as an extrovert(?) but truly I enjoy keeping to myself and not oversharing outside my close circle. This song was more of a therapy for me so I didn't feel the need to rush it out. I'll start here.

I made this song with Tate Gardner on a day that we were just not feeling it. Even though both our heads were elsewhere, we knew that if we just sat down and got started, the energy would immediately shift because we were doing what we love to do. 

There are days where it's just hard, but through personal experience I have found that when you overcome the resistance, all of your manifestations and new opportunities start flooding in. I am grateful for the process because it is what makes me feel alive. 
Sometimes you really just gotta show up!

I connected with Ayotemi in April and fell in love with his music. I had just made the song and immediately had a gut feeling that he needed to be on this track. The collaboration flowed like water and just like that we created a song together. 

Ever since, Ayotemi and I share a special friendship where we talk about astral projecting and send each other 4 minute voice memos explaining crazy dreams from the night before. It's pretty rad to collaborate with someone who you resonate with spiritually. We align on our values and mission as artists. I believe in his vision and art, so it is so wonderful to share this experience together with the web3 community.

You have purpose. You are capable. You are meant to follow what you are passionate about.

Show up!

Description:
Have you ever gotten to the next level and wondered if you belonged there? Life lately has been what I always imagined it was supposed to be, and yet I still have this lingering unease as I step into the success I’ve created for myself.

  Coming from a single-parent home and contending with the struggles that entailed, I made the commitment to myself that I would transcend my circumstances through my own effort and creativity. I’ve prepared myself to work harder, to do better, to become greater… but one thing I wasn’t prepared for was the feeling of not belonging in the life I had dreamed of.

  Imposter Syndrome speaks to the phenomenon of “arrival fallacy,” in which you’ve achieved what you set out to do… but things but still feel uneasy in the place that your success has brought you to.
Accompanied by fellow artist Rey Morado of ReignCloud Music Group, with production by Dav, Imposter Syndrome is the pure expression of the fear, doubt, and anxiety that comes from leaving behind the patterns of your old life and carving out something new for yourself.

Description:
LNRZ ON SOUND WK 1 

Vaarwell is an electronic duo with a captivating signature sound. We were immediately drawn to the specificity of their writing and the tasteful beauty of the production. 

In their own words:

“IDK” is a UK Garage inspired track about the mystery of life, death and its aftermath. It questions a superior creator and the afterlife beliefs we were taught as kids. The song finds no answer to these questions, with the chorus being an admission of ignorance and eagerness to find out the truth.

 "I don't know what to believe. Am I really here? How?"

VOICES I is about finding moments of relief and escape from your own mind. It's the first segment of a two-part song that was written and produced live on Twitch, and VOICES II will soon follow with another drop on Sound.

Part I was originally created as a new introduction for my debut performance at Red Rocks this year, and the Golden Egg winner will have tickets and backstage access to the show on October 21, 2022 (utility may also be transferred to another show).

Description:
THE FIRST OF THE SERIES
works of progress: dangerous 

WHAT IS WORKS OF PROGRESS
we are tapping into our vault of early demos to release a series on sound.xyz... new drop every two weeks

some of these songs may evolve and be released traditionally and some not.. but these early versions will live forever on Sound and we love them.
we will be creating a guild.xyz to integrate with our Discord for our holders of these “Works of Progress”. this will be a place to chime in and offer feedback & ideas, basically crowdsourcing a braintrust of people invested in the vision of the songs and the Beauty School Dropout project.

dangerous was the first song every written by this band so it seems fitting for it to be the first of the series. 

our sonic style has evolved in so many ways since this session, and it’s important to revisit the early work to see where we came from. there is still magic in here.

one thing we’ve come to enjoy is while learning what this band is and how to make music for it, we made many “mistakes” sonically. we wanted to make big rock guitar sounds but had to learn how to do that first. In the tinkering and toying with sounds, sometimes something new would be created.. obstacles make opportunity and that is where the magic lies. 

here is dangerous.. the first of the works of progress series

Description:
After a hiatus from creating, releasing, social media and even life you could say.. Pearson now finds himself recording and producing his own works implementing layered falsetto-like vocal patterns alongside an acoustic electronica mash-up production style.  

Finding web3 earlier this year allowed Pearson to “finally feel a part of something” and have full control of his own creative output and releases alike. Formerly collaborating with Soulection, RedBull and more. Pearson now looks forward to working with and supporting like-minded artists, collectors and supporters through digital collectables and site exclusive releases.  

 “ “Forget about it” is a track in which I created extremely recently. It's just how I was feeling at the time. I started to almost go back into a negative way of thinking. I don’t know if it’s because it’s so grey and wet in Scotland now, but I was started to feel a way. It’s almost homage to how I was and the style I was creating in 2018/2019 before I had a break from everything. Now I'm on a different wave and decided to create something to say goodbye to. Something to forget about, but also something for a reminder of where I was and where I’m going and maybe also an introduction to those who haven’t heard my music before “ - Pearson  

This is the first of many new tracks coming towards the end of 2022 and is not even the first page of the story.

This song is meant to accompany a walking meditation. Whats that?
Walking Meditation - Choose a foot to start with. Pick it up, move it through space, and gently place it on the ground, feeling the sensations of each part of this process from heel to toe. ...
Walk with intention. ...
Let yourself notice. ...
Focus your attention. ...
Feel your surroundings. ...
Notice when thoughts take over. Send the thoughts telepathically to the outer-most reaches of Space. Aliens will come for you in the form of unrequited love and dreams that seem so real they make u bite your lip. Thats what this song is about.

this song is so simple, yet so special and you’ll feel it when listening.

Description:
I’ve noticed that many of us experience the challenges required to have a healthy relationship. Many artists have made it a point to share their experiences of heartache through relationships. That leads me to believe we are all going through the same thing. It seems most heartache stems from a place of poor communication. The environment for it is neither created nor maintained. That always neglects the elephant in the “RòóM.” Before you know it, the elephant has more room than the two of you.

By making “RòóM,” I decided to face the music...Looking both within and without, I noticed all my experiences put me in a position to be; more self-aware, accountable, and wanting to be my best self. 
Naturally, love, in all use of the word, benefits from this.

The melancholy piano, the muffled drums drowning In space, and the melody all come together to emote what I felt…What I know you may be feeling.
If you do feel this, then it’s for you.

Welcome to our second official drop on sound, "Better Than The First Time." As we grow into ourselves in life and in music, we can't forget to give the girls their flowers. This song is about falling in love with a girl and letting her know how much power her love has over us through all its ups and downs. 

We had the pleasure of working with our friend Reo Cragun who has been nothing but supportive since the beginning of our careers. His presence on this record elevated the song so much and we hope you all agree!

‘Overthinking’ is an eerie, vulnerable, and almost desperate ballad. It captures the exact feelings of being an overthinker. Being swamped with your own bad thoughts that are oftentimes untrue. Needing reassurance from the person you’re thinking about.

This song was so therapeutic and relieving for me to make. The timing of this song was perfect. At that particular moment, I was so overwhelmed with emotions I couldn't make sense of. I couldn't tell if what was going on in my mind was true, or if I was just creating a false narrative in my head. There was no one around me who knew what I’d specifically felt. There was no song for me to play that related to my exact state.

So I made my own.

I started with some simple chords on the keyboard. Just two of them. What caught my ear was the bass within the sound of the piano, and I left it at that. I didn’t know what to start off with lyrically. So I just started recording and sang whatever I felt.

“Why don’t you talk to me”. A simple phrase, yet so intriguing. It makes you think: where was I going with this? I kept up the improvisation and went back afterwards, changing some lyrics and melodies. I didn’t write down one lyric on my phone during this. It was just straight from my emotions. I never want to hold back in my music. I want to say what I feel.

Like many of my songs, they’re personal to me. They all have a story. But like many of us, we all feel heartbreak, desire, longing. And we want to be understood. We want to know that we’re not alone. Words cannot describe how healing this song was for me to make.

‘Overthinking’ is the perfect song for those whose mind wanders. For those whose minds are too loud. For those who need reassurance. For those who want to be understood. ‘Overthinking’ is perfect for overthinkers. I hope you’re able to feel some comfort, and feel some emotion :)

- Mia Lailani <3

Description: Shhhh...

Caesar is an expression - note to self. At this paint in my life, I was swimming through a paradox of success & grief. In the months prior I had lost a lot yet gained so much. It was a cycle, I felt stuck & unable to process what was actually happening. I began to question everything around me - Why do I feel so empty? What’s the point of life if things get taken away? Why are we working so hard?  

I had to change re-focus. I had to reflect. So I linked up with Fuzz, got in the booth & the words began to pour out of me. 

The message behind Caesar is to be able to deal with life and stay true to your purpose no what happens. As things rise, they will fall. Caesar had many accomplishments & at the height of his reign it was all taken away, a similar feeling to what I was experiencing. But I realized my purposed hadn’t been fulfilled, I was still surround by love, there was still work to be done.

Description:
"Fresh Air" is the freedom and relief that arises when you speak your needs. The same tears and unbearable sadness I was feeling the day I wrote this song led me back to myself, to my core needs. What makes me feel grounded and free. I spent the rest of the day at a festival on the lakefront.

 I'm a fire starter, phoenix, lioness, and alchemist with my head so focused on the victory that I'm learning to allow my heart the space it needs to just shed in the moment. Yes I am strong, but these days I have been leaning into my softness, my gentle era, and yearning for ease. 

When we keep telling ourselves the same stories about love, success, friendship, society, relationships, and one another we can create blockages that bind us to the same endings. I no longer believe that I am asking too much and I know that god, the universe, the earth has already provided so much. We have everything we need. I want everyone who listens to this song to feel like giving and receiving good love is possible. 

The heartbeat of the song is New Orleans Second Line drum meets afrobeat (produced by She is the Future collaborator and native son of New Orleans Infinite Eye) featuring the lyrical and vintage visual art stylings of Old Orleans. The soul of the song is nostalgic groove inspired and shaped by Head of Production and Engineering at Creative Minds Coalition, Ashton Woods. Detroit Soul Okkk Motown okkk not to mention the song feats. buttery backing vocals from the Cameroonian Detroit legend Scolla Fungwe as well as my three year old daughter Mecca Selah, no but fr, she was feeling it and it's giving light at the end of the tunnel.

Description:
Hey, I’m Munn. I grew up in Indiana but currently live in Nashville. When I was 15 I started playing guitar and writing music but didn't take it seriously until my Sophomore year of college.

In the summer of 2018, leading up to my Sophomore year, my engagement with my fiancée fell through, and I lost all interest in school. I was struggling to heal from the breakup, and I had no idea what I wanted to do with my life. It was during this time that I wrote my first song in over a year called I Tried. To this day, I can't describe how I felt after making that song. I had finally found my way to heal, and, from then on, creating music was all I wanted to do.
 
Around this time, a producer that I had connected with in 2017, named Dylan Stiles, was sending me beats every day. I would write and record to these beats every night using an Xbox headset and GarageBand. As time went on, we both decided that the best thing we could do was to drop out of school and go all-in on music. In July of 2019, with less than 4,000 monthly listeners on Spotify, Dylan and I moved to Nashville to do just that.
 
After a failed EP, we realized I needed a better strategy for putting out music. We decided that the best thing I could do was put out a new song every two weeks until one caught traction. On September 6th, 2019, we released the first song following this plan called I Lost Myself.

Currently, I am a fully independent singer/songwriter based out of Nashville. My team and I have been building my fan base over the past couple years and have amassed 200,000,000 streams, over a million monthly listeners on Spotify, 200k+ subs on YouTube, and more, all independently. While our music hasn’t stopped growing by any means, moving into the NFT space for additional support and a new way to connect with listeners was the logical next step for us.

Earlier this year, I was in a long-distance relationship with a girl from Florida. Shortly after her and I broke up, I was back down in Florida with Friends and spent a little too much time and money trying to forget I was hurting. I went to bars and casinos and let loose. Weirdly enough, I had started a demo called "down in florida", months prior, that nearly described the exact situation I now found myself in with her. I didn't have the words to finish the song until I was back in Nashville a week later and decided to continue writing the song from my current situation. Hence, the opening of the second verse "i'm back in Nashville..." 

This track tells the story of how I did anything but face the truth of my reality. I wasn't ready to face the consequences of my actions. I hope you enjoy <3
