“Spacecraft” is Amy Correa Bell’s next high energy single from her upcoming album “Correa Bell’.  It’s a bass-fueled journey and intro to the overall attitude Amy exhibits on stage and in life with a heavy production by brother and executive producer Les Les (aka Les Correa).  At the outset we hear the lyrics “Have a lot to say, it’s not the time to wait…” after which she exhorts the listener to turn up and pump up in life.  The chorus intermingles with chants where Amy chimes in on beats with lyrics that motivate the listener to write and make right in this life.  Spacecraft is catchy, motivational and danceable with Amy captaining the craft into uncharted territories."


“This song gave me a chance to write what I’m thinking consciously and sub-consciously at the same time, so you’ll hear my internal dialogue as the song progresses.”

Artwork by Lee Robson Spence.

"Buzzin" is an dark tech vibe beat single created by young music producer Sho. The inspiration for the song came from a nighttime adventure he had during his college years. Sho and his friends decided to attend a secret underground party. The party was located in an abandoned warehouse and was exclusive to those "in the know."

Upon arriving, Sho was captivated by the atmosphere: the flickering neon lights, the deafening bass, and the people around him. What struck him the most, however, was the combination of sounds and light feels like a bee that kept buzzing around the crowd, as if attracted by the music and the enthusiasm of the people.

Sat in his small home studio, contemplating how to translate that night's experience into music. He began experimenting with various rhythms and melodies, eventually finding a musical element that could capture the vibe of that night. He decided to use a synthesizer to mimic the scene hover above his mind and the robust drum set was inspired by opium artists like Ken Carson.

This is the beat of my most recent track, “Wait For Me.” You can stream the song on Spotify, Apple Music, or your favorite platform.

You can also buy the NFT of the song here on Sound.

This beat drop doesn't include the license, but you can buy the license for this or other of my beats on kzenbeats.com or by searching my name on “Soundclick”.

Description:
I grew up in New York City and it feels like my entire life has been spent reclaiming my relationship with the planet. From having to stay on-guard 24/7 to only experiencing slices of green space, it's really difficult to understand what really matters: Sneakers? Fast fashion? The gangster code?

Growing my own food and plugging into resilient local economies has given me more fulfillment than anything I gained in the warped version of city life. This song is a prayer, a blessing for what we can build using these tools that mean so much more than cool collectibles. We are redefining value and who gets to benefit from it. I hope it resonates with you!

The beat is a collaboration with @DanielBonefont on IG and BandLab.

Description:
Hey there, I'm Stan, a music producer based in Brussels,Belgium, and I'm dropping my first track on Sound!

My musical journey began at the age of 6 when I started playing the violin. Later, when my family and I moved to Belgium, I picked up the classical guitar. After years of diving into classical music, I started getting into electronic tunes I heard on the radio. I was completely clueless about how those sounds were made, but with a bit of research and my parents' support, I finally got my hands on my first music-making software at 16.

Once I realized the incredible potential of making electronic music, I made a quick decision to stop my guitar lessons and dedicate myself to it.

During my first year of college, I launched my project as SVDKO and released my debut track, 'Innocence.' A year later, it caught the attention of an audience through some semi-viral moments on Vine and Spotify. That was the turning point when I realized that music could be more than just a hobby; it could become my Plan A.

After releasing several independent songs, having big sync opportunities with the likes of Apple and more recently Dior and crafting a sound that combined rock and electronic vibes during the pandemic - I felt it was time for me to come back to the genre that inspired me in the first place and write a dance and electronic-focused EP.

'SELF LOVE' was actually the first demo I made for that EP, but funnily enough, it didn't make the final cut. SELF LOVE has that rock/electronic blend I liked so much but leans more towards a dance record. I had the chance to collaborate with Akacia on the vocals and ONLYTHENEXT who played a significant role in the production process. 'SELF LOVE' is all about self-empowerment, setting high standards in relationships, and refusing to settle for anything less than genuine commitment and love. At this point in my life, that's the message that resonates with me the most, and I hope you’ll find something in it for you as well ❤️

Description:
"Lonely Cowboy" is a deeply moving song that carries the weight of raw emotions within its beautiful melodies. Through this musical masterpiece, Kayo paints a poignant picture of personal struggle and transformation. The song serves as a testament to the healing power of music, as it was composed during a challenging period in kayo's life, becoming a therapeutic outlet for his emotions.

What sets "Lonely Cowboy" apart is the captivating raspiness in Kayo's voice, adding a sense of authenticity and grit to the composition. This quality, combined with the evocative lyrics and melodies, creates a powerful synergy that has the potential to send shivers down your spine. It's especially heart-wrenching to learn that this song, which holds such profound significance, was the last creation on Kayo's stolen laptop, marking the loss of a treasure trove of music. "Lonely Cowboy" encapsulates the essence of how music can be a lifeline, and its listeners can truly sense the depth of emotion and importance it holds for Kayo.

This track began when I went over to Gaspar's house for lunch a few months back. Both of us had recently gotten pretty addicted to granular synthesis and spent the first couple hours we were with each-other just messing around and making the weirdest noises possible. 

Gaspar then pulled up this beautiful recording of a harpist playing a piece live in this big open space with loads of reverb in the sample. We chopped it up and ran it through a bunch of granular channels until it made this almost digital sounding pluck. I messed about on his Ableton Push creating the beat whilst he cut up some MS-20 white noise stutters for percussion to layer in. 

When I took the track home I sat with it for a bit as I felt it felt a bit too heavy and abrupt than what I usually release but ended up adding a bunch of chords, arpeggios, more drums and arranging it to what it is now. 

The track kind of represents a different space for both of us that neither of us had really ever written in before. It feels much more heavy than a lot of what we make but also very emotional at the same time and I've grown to love the journey that it takes you on.

First started working on the track in early 2021 after being inspired by the opening clip from Adult Swim’s Off the Air “Color” episode - see # 2. At the time, I found myself gravitating toward syncopated drum breaks / jungle and decided to use the Color vocal for a melodic jungle track. The track takes a while to really get to the point, but I wanted to share some influences through sampling.

I made the visual with CRT effects as an attempt to capture the spirit of the Off The Air episode in a way that would work as a live visual for someone performing this, or similar, tracks.

Before you ask, the word 'bololo' is a slang term native to my hometown Barranquilla. we use it to describe a big mess, a brawl, something along those lines. but it can also mean a huge party that is just super out of control.

When I was working on this track initially with The Fund, Mark Johns, and Kate Morgan, they asked if there were any cool spanish words we could write around. I obviously hopped on google and looked up Costeño slang (costeño is what people from Barranquilla are called!) and bololo came up - as you can see we went with it!

I wanted the song to sound like what the word means - hence why the track is pretty crazy production-wise! I also decided to write about a crazy night, I just put myself in the shoes of someone who went out and had one of those nights where you end up in 6 different places, meet 3 people, become friends, and never see them again. I have personally never experienced anything like this so it was pretty fun to just dramatize what this whole ordeal would be like.

We all had the most fun making and recording this song, there are so many little details hidden in it that make it so special, you just have to listen to it over and over again I guess! enjoy "bololo"!!!

The song came about when I was sitting around one day thinking about the old Madden soundtracks and how I should make an alternative rock beat. I went into Ableton to make the beat and began to hear the lyrics for the hook in my head. I recorded my hook and began writing the verse; I wanted this song to be powerful for all ages. I only had my hook and verse when I shared it with Giipson Poet, a local artist in my city, who loved the concept of the song and wanted to record a verse. Throughout the process, he noticed that I didn't have much passion in my verse. He helped me by giving me examples of how to better my delivery when recording my verses. Giiipson Poet, also had the idea to include a bridge in the track. I went back to Ableton Live, copied the intro guitar, and added it after each of our verses to add another catchy melody to the track. After this process was done, the mixing process began which took about 2-3 days. We shared the song with a few people and received a great response back. We must say that this song is one for the books and should be enjoyed by all ages.

Description:
I made The Precipice while getting acquainted with GrimesAI and going through a mini existential crisis throughout the wave of AI news earlier this year. I've always found technology creatively inspiring but its hard not to think about all the unforeseen risks, especially for frontier tech advancing at an exponential rate.

Given my concerns, I appreciate how Grimes has always embraced tech while not losing sight of what is special about being human. She is also an inspiration to me musically, so I was really excited to make a song using her voice.

The title of the song is borrowed from a book of the same name about existential risk (by Tony Ord). It made me think about how our relationship with AI is similar to extremely passionate love: incredibly exciting and potentially life-changing, but could end like a Shakespearean tragedy if we aren't lucky or prepared. 

That metaphor inspired me to make a music video using the 1993 film adaptation of Romeo & Juliet, reimagined through an AI image generator:
https://youtu.be/_WssPKL1vIA

Description:
On a dark and quiet night, I was in my living room, enjoying the tranquility of my home. Suddenly, the sound of a roaring engine shattered the silence of the night. Intrigued, I peeked out the window and was met with a shiny car parked in front of my house. To my surprise, the driver turned out to be none other than Vin Diesel.

Vin stepped out of the car with a smile on his face and a pair of giant headphones around his neck. Without saying a word, he entered my house as if he were a long-lost friend. I was so surprised that I could barely articulate a question, but Vin simply raised a finger in a gesture of silence and pointed towards the living room.

In a matter of minutes, my modest living room transformed into an otherworldly techno party. Vin Diesel, somehow, had brought along a high-tech sound system and began spinning electronic music with impressive skill. Lights flickered in sync with the rhythm, creating a surreal atmosphere.

Vin, with his characteristic calm and intense gaze, seemed completely in his element, as if he had found his true passion in electronic music. The combination of his imposing presence and the booming music created a unique and unforgettable experience.

The night continued with Vin Diesel immersed in the mix of electronic beats, while I and some curious neighbors joined the impromptu party. When the party came to an end, Vin simply nodded, gave me a pat on the shoulder, and retreated as mysteriously as he had arrived.

New music, new distro deal, new me.
Hope you like it

Los Angeles-based producer and DJ, informal., brings a fresh take on music with his EP, "its not that serious." This project emphasizes the simple joy of creating without overthinking, urging listeners to embrace music in its raw, unfiltered form. Having already made its mark in traditional channels, this EP is now being introduced to the sound.xyz community, but with a twist: it's unveiling in reverse order.

"ooh ahh" kicks off this unique release strategy. Originally, it wrapped up the EP, offering listeners a taste of a deeper, late-night vibe. Despite its earlier journey of being pitched to various labels with little traction, "Ooh Ahh" stands as a testament to informal.'s commitment to authenticity. The track delivers with its engaging mix of saw wave bass and rhythmic beats. As the first taste of the EP on sound.xyz (though it's the last in the original lineup), it promises a genuine experience of what informal. has to offer. Dive in and appreciate the genuine artistry behind each track.

# Special Song Campaign

We are also introducing a special contest to thank our fans. Three people who collect the most items each week will get a share of the mint sales. They'll each receive 7% of the mint sales made. So, if you're one of the top collectors in a week, you'll get 7% of the earnings in the following week. If you stay at the top for more weeks, you'll keep getting that 7% weekly bonus. This will happen until the campaign finishes. 

This campaign starts on Sep 18th and ends on Dec 30th for a total duration of 15 weeks. During this campaign, the top 3 collectors of "King of Hearts" will be identified on an ongoing weekly basis at noon PST every Sunday (the "1-week cycle") and will each earn 7% (21% collectively) of total mint royalties generated by "King of Hearts" during the following 1-week cycle. Royalties the top 3 collectors earn will be disbursed directly to their wallet addresses, and they can withdraw shares on Sound.xyz with their wallet.

# Behind the Music

We discreetly invite you to cross through a conscious exploration portal into the concepts of duality and evolution. The King of Hearts card symbolizes the duality of an individual -- an aspirational side and a shadow side -- depending on the context. This song's conception honors the power of uninhibited evolution as a means to more fruitful creation and as a path to acceptance of the full spectrum of one's individuality. 

The first iterations of this song were born during the pandemic when Chris created tracks for his mom to recite Spanish poems. The track "Fiesta" had subtle musical and lyrical references to Celia Cruz. As people collectively underwent evolutions during this isolating time, so did this song. Months later, Chris shared a slower and more sensual version of the song intended to be a B-side version, closer to the style of a steamy Claudja Barry hit. Something resonated, so Matt started singing melodies and charting the song's arrangement.

Eventually, there was a song with only fragments of meaningless lyrics. It wasn't until La Cita traveled to Puerto Rico to celebrate a friend's birthday at a group wellness retreat in the lush mountains of Utuado that they found inspiration for the song's meaning. One day, a card reader at the retreat asked Matt to pick a card, which turned out to be the King of Hearts. The reader said the card symbolized abundant love, wisdom, and humble leadership. But he said to be careful because sometimes, giving this love to just one person is hard. The King of Hearts can immensely nourish -- or hurt.  

This feedback created a shortcut to deeper introspection and reflection over the retreat for both Chris and Matt, where, as part of the retreat, they attended various wellness workshops, including breath classes, spiritual gatherings, and conscious intimacy workshops. The culmination of these activities led to the song's sensual lyrics and androgynous intonations exploring the edges of life, the layered duality of a soul, and the mystery of personal evolution.

Who are Beachcrimes? We’re a duo from LA and we spent the last year making songs in hotel rooms around the world. Beachcrimes is the soundtrack to that adventure.
 
We made a lot of songs, and we’re excited to share them. All of them. This year we’re releasing 24 songs in 48 weeks. If we’re being real, it’s actually two albums – there’s AM and there’s PM. AM is the lite stuff, PM is the nite stuff. Think of it like the Summer Olympics and Winter Olympics, but for dance music.

“Play My Heart On The Radio” is our 16th single this year. The title pretty much speaks for itself. You know the feeling. Where you're fresh off a breakup and every song on the radio seems to have been personally dedicated to your agony. And you’re like, oh that’s nice, the radio DJ has flipped my epic heartbreak into a chart-topping playlist. Well, might as well surrender to the music, have a drink - or three - and don’t let those tears hit the dance floor baby!

Next single will be out 2 weeks from today, and the following single 2 weeks after that.

Description: This track is inspired by Blade Runner and Cyberpunk. Vocals (no lyrics) and music leading to a climax of pure futuristic sounds and melodies that will stimulate your imagination.

The second installment of the Holographic Audio / Visual Series, "Passion" Embarks on a melodic journey through the struggles of what it means to be a creative in this world. 

Feeling like a never ending race to be successful as fast as possible and the weight and self doubt that comes with that. 

Passion takes a more aggressive production style incorporating Dark and Melodic Dubstep. 

* What is the Holographic Audio / Visual Series?

I have been creating a series of demos in exploration of various Electronic music genres. When I started producing, electronic music is what I gravitated to and through time my sound has shifted to more emphasis on my Voice and Songwriting. This series has allowed me to dive back in to my roots and create the music that I know my 14 year old self would be proud of.

Visually, I wanted to combine this eccentric music with Holographic / Iridescent textures as I feel they are a great representation of the world of electronic music. I have something called Synthesia, which means that i experiance multiple senses at the same time. 

In this case, I physically see every sound I hear which has always enhanced my love for music as a listener and a creator. 

Ambient worlds, colourful textures, and hard hitting music that you can dance or cry to... This is "Passion"

Description: DECENTRALIZATION.DIGITAL.UNKNOWN

'Paper Soldiers' is a punchy rap song that takes listeners on a journey through the mind of a confident and fearless artist. Kamre Haze demonstrates a braggadocios swagger and determination to highlight success and prove naysayers wrong. Loyalty and perseverance tend to be overarching themes, emphasizing the artist's resilience through unyielding negativity.

With a hook that serves almost as a war chant, the song's namesake derives from the comparison of adversaries to delicate pieces of paper, displaying high energy throughout. Verse two dives deeper into the artist's psyche, speaking in a condescending tone to those who go against them. Kamre Haze portrays himself to be someone unafraid to speak their mind, regardless of possible repercussions. Harping on authenticity, he continues to touch on themes of danger, deception, and a sense of invincibility.

I grieve because I love. I wrote this song as a heartfelt tribute to my beloved grandma Sofya who passed away unexpectedly three years ago. I didn’t get a chance to say goodbye before she died. Description:
Return From The Pale
2020 Vision - Hindsight Edition
Track 11

This song was primarily inspired by the main character in the game Disco Elysium. That game very quickly became one my forever favorites. This idea - A person, so driven by self-loathing and a desire for a past that never was that they brought themselves to oblivion - then proceeding to find purpose and personal acceptance by putting their disasterous, messy, very fallible self out into the world to "solve" it, one interpersonal "quest" after another. I was very touched by it.

My first album, 2020 Vision was made in 2019 and originally released on Jan 1st 2020. It was a terrific experience, learning as I made, experimenting with all kinds of sounds and genres, but building with a full album experience in mind. The 12 tracks of the album rotate through the circle of fifths, with a track for each major key. It's a rather hopeful album I think, and it is interesting to look back on it, knowing just how much it contrasts with the year it entered. There is also a tinge of loneliness to some of the tracks, perhaps some of that underlying anxiety of seeing covid go down elsewhere in the world and wondering what could happen. This Hindsight Edition was an opportunity for me to go into the state of making these tracks, and feel out how my production has changed. One of the weaknesses of the original album was all the mastering was done with no prior experience, I literally had an ozone tutorial up as I did it. Nowadays I have a much better handle on those sorts of things and this Hindsight Edition is a way to get a new, clean modern master out there while still maintaining the original elements of the release. I hope everyone enjoys!

Amber was the product of fully letting go and trusting the process. I had a session with my friends Zach Ezzy and Cautious Clay one night, and we really eased into it (actual work began 3 hours in after getting tacos and shooting the shit). I had recorded a syncopated drum pattern in my car earlier that day, so we pulled that up and started building sound around it. Zach and Cautious eventually played tandem flute and trumpet over it! We made that into a sample, made it even, and put some paced drums over it. I had been wanting to write a song about how after breaking up with friends or partners we leave a piece of ourselves behind like a fossil or a mosquito trapped in amber, and that night just felt like the right time to flesh it out. 

For a long time I've gone into sessions thinking that I have to make the best song in the world, all the while forgetting that music is supposed to be fun. This song embodies that release and reconnection with the process of making music for fun. I'm so grateful that moment was immortalized in this song.

Unlike a lot of my songs, this song doesn't really have a super interesting story behind it. However, this song was made purely with the intention of being a groovy lil track to get you moving. I started this idea while I was completely sleep deprived at 4AM, and finished it after a solid 8 hours of rest a few days later. The sporadic synth shots, and off kilter noises really capture the state of my mind while being that tired.

It was a beautiful day, but isn't everyday when you'r a child. At least thats what i believed before it happened. I had my favorite starters north carolina blue and purple fit on. My red and black chicago bulls basketball. the air was filled with my families laughter and joy. The sent of grilled burgers and hot dogs covered any other smell on the street. California love had just came on the radio and Tupac was my favorite. I was so happy it felt like my heart was going to explode with joy. Suddenly i see my fathers smile fall off his face. As if it stolen, eyes wide and fixed. I didn't know the world could move so slow, while it happened so fast. The sounds of laugher died, replaced by screams of agony. Pain filled the air that was just thick with bliss. I couldn't hear Tupac over the sirens and police scanners. All of my family was on the ground. Some out of fear, some out of safety. My father was on the ground covering my little sister. My aunt was on the ground, on her knees screaming to God. The word why still echo's in my ears to this day. I couldn't understand, i'm thirty now and i still don't. As a child i lost everything that day. Religion, Faith, Belief, Trust, and gained more fear then i knew what to do with. I never admitted it, But i hated my cousins everyday since. Blood still stains that side walk there is seguin texas. Their brother died, because of a stupid obsession with trapping and false power. He wasn't involved, nor would he be the last. Like a curse sickness, prison, poverty, domestic violence, drugs, suicide, and homicide would haunt my family. Ever since, I've wanted to hunt down change as if it were my pray. Now that im a man i can and i do tirelessly. However as a child, all i could do was PRAY.

I started writing this in March '22. I was practicing scales on the guitar in Am and came across the plucky melody which is now known to hold down Can We Fly. I couldn't stop playing it.

In 2022 I was working with a studio that brought the trippy side of this track out. There's actually a whole different demo to this song that I was so close to publishing.. however I never felt comfortable releasing it because it wasn't an authentic reflection of how I wanted to represent the track.

Come early 2023 I brought both that demo and my rough demo to 'The Fund'. & together we meshed the two to produce the 'perfect' in between. This song is also part of a 3 piece EP.

At the time, I was learning and experiencing about different ways toxicity can form in relationship and was just starting to write music. So birthed, Can We Fly.

Cheers

Description:
Welcome to "HORIZONS", a special album that offers a unique journey. It's made up of seven songs, each representing my growth and experiences as an artist.

It isn't just music, it's an adventure. It takes you through different kinds of emotions, like exploring new places. Think of it as a companion for a special journey, where every song tells a story about my artistic experiences. Let it inspire your imagination.

Tracks:

0:00-3:52 Ephemeral Machines:
You stand amidst the labyrinth of mechanical structures, casting shadows of uncertainty. Embark on a journey where time and form seem to waver. 
The echoes of these ephemeral machines resonate through the soundscape, discouraging you for the voyage ahead.

3:54-8:43 Neon Wastelands:
Delving deeper into the desolate and dystopian city. Cold metal structures stretch toward the sky and neon lights cast haunting shadows across the cityscape. Only robotic remnants can be found in the emptiness. You bear witness to the haunting of a world that once thrived.

8:45-12:25 Rising from Ashes:
The cityscape, once shackled by machines, now stands free. You emerge from the robotic remnants. As the sun breaches the horizon, hope takes wing and humans can once again rise from the ashes of a world that once held them captive.

12:27-16:31 Stardust Reverie:
As the city comes alive, fireworks dance in the sky, mirroring the twinkle from the stars. You can feel the heartbeat of the celebration and you revel in the stardust reverie. A moment ignited by joy and triumph.

16:33-19:16 Beyond the Void:
The city dissapears as you venture into the unknown. 
Guided by determination and courage, you set out to explore the void that holds the ultimate ascent. Embarking on the final quest that takes you beyond the familiar cityscape! Your heart is set on a new horizon.

19:18-21:40 Luminous Horizons:
You continue your voyage, cruising along the open road. The world stretches ahead, promising new sights and experiences. With each passing mile, you draw closer to the luminous horizons, eager for what lies ahead.

21:42-24:55 Ascension:
The culmination of your journey arrives. You stand at the pinnacle of your adventure with a triumphant heart, knowing all the challenges you have faced led you to this point. The world that once confined you is now a distant memory, 
and you’re free to embrace the possibilities that lie ahead. Ascension.

Imagine a universe where we are connected by shimmering beams of light, everyone to everyone. One quirk about this universe is that the beams send emotions between us, one million per minute per pair, clearly and effortlessly. Joy is instantly contagious. A hurtful thought toward another is understood with compassion, seen alongside the place of sadness where it arose. Every feeling triggers infinite empathy, therefore boundless acceptance. (The beams send only the stuff of our souls, not our thoughts — so we still have privacy, interesting conversation, and the ability to prank each other silly.)

Now imagine we already live in this universe except, long ago, we somehow forgot where the beams disappeared off to. But we’ve always kept music with us, because it’s our best way to speak in the old way.

+

Taiwan-born & reared on-the-go between Taipei and the American Southwest, Eric Pan (a.k.a. pandelic) found his musical footing via a jazz mentorship with Ray Brown at the University of California. These studies propelled him onto stages with Jeff Hamilton and Roy Hargrove, plus over a decade’s tenure as New York City pianist & composer. Pan’s compositions and improvisations reveal a relentless pursuit of simplicity, craft, and universality.

Hear him interviewed on-air next to Orson Welles on national radio with PRI’s “The World”, read his exclusive premiere interview in JAZZIZ Magazine, and stream/download his latest long-form interview on the _For a Living_ podcast.

Before she was Party Nails, Elana Carroll was a guitar-toting tween songwriter, playing any open mic she could near her hometown of Chatham, New York. Performing solo or with a band of seasoned adult players backing her up, she wailed lyrics about her family’s divorce, dreams of leaving her small town, and a then-undiagnosed anxiety disorder across biker bars and community centers, often met with tears from patrons moved by her fearless expression of raw emotion. At home she recorded herself with Garageband, instigating a love of music technology which continues to this day.

Years later, her roots in Americana and self-recording serve as foundations for Party Nails. No stranger to collaborations—she has featured on tracks by Getter, MitiS, LUN, Battle Tapes, and Urban Heat, as well as penned an original song for Apple's animated musical Central Park—she is also able to write, record, produce and mix entirely alone. "It depends on the record," she says. When she's not touring to promote her own music, she also works as an engineer and producer for other artists.

Her first US tour in 2017 (with PVRIS and Lights) ushered in a devoted fanbase, and her live performances continue to be a core facet of her artistry, being equal parts Madonna, Hayley Williams, and Sheryl Crow. In the studio, though, her muses are Robyn, Prince, SZA and Dolly Parton, to name a few.

This year started off with a bang with “Like U", a collaboration with Austin-based Boy Sim that PAPER called "reminiscent of '90s and early-2000s rave music". Her second single of 2023, "Bull In A China Shop", was dubbed "chaotically fun", "an irresistible experimental pop meets electronic bop", and "a thrilling, sonically unique arrangement" by the likes of Earmilk, Atwood Magazine and Metal Magazine.

Her most recent and third single of the year, “Someway Somehow” found its way onto Spotify Editorial playlists Fresh Finds, Fresh Finds Indie, and Undercurrents. Paste Magazine called it “brash and rough and imploring, a love letter couched in punky instrumentals and intimate production.”

After wrapping a Pacific Northwest tour with San Francisco’s Gloomy June, Party Nails is back in the studio mixing, producing music for her artist clientele, and working on her third album.

Description:
Outroselo's genesis is an introduction to Nebula Dogs


The debut of this young Brazilian band is a multimedia art project. Their concept album contains 10 songs that we’ll release till the end of the year one at a time: audio, lyrics and illustration. Yes, because every song has been visually interpreted by an artist: 10 songs, 10 illustrations, 10 artists. But what is the album? And who is the band? Nebula Dogs is a progressive and psychedelic indie band, founded in 2012 in Florianópolis – (capital city of Santa Catarina state, on the homonymous island bathed by the Atlantic Ocean, in the South of Brazil) – by André Zanella (synthesizers/vocals), Conrado Emerick (bass), Kauê Werner (guitar/vocals), and Paulo Pfutzenreuter (drums/vocals).

"Our repertoire is influenced by bands with a psychedelic vein as the Pink Floyd, MGMT, Radiohead and Supertramp, that seek sound diversity and often use elements taken from other styles, such as blues and jazz, always maintaining a tune with the contemporary scene."

"As the album has a story behind the songs, we thought that maybe some artists would like to represent them with an illustration. Some of them are our friends and some others heard and joined the project. This exchange between music and art was born from pure passion. We have selected 10 artists and everyone will show you their own vision about the concept, lyrics and music. This way, they have visually interpreted our album; so you can listen to it and see it."

Description:
The Demo Days: Hold On To Me (May 30th, 2018)

I actually wrote this song before I met David. I almost never take lyrics and put them over a new beat, but when David played me this later that year, the chorus jumped right back into my head. The melodies and lyrics fit perfectly.   

David is a great guitar player and that melody he cooked up on this one is like walking on clouds before a storm.

Lyrically, I think the heart of this song is the bridge. Acknowledging the fact we will eventually lose everyone we Love, or that they will lose us, is devastating. Yet, most of us continue to Love deeply, because all the inevitable pain is worth the beauty our Loved ones bring into our lives. What a magnificent tragedy it is, to be human. 

Hold On To Me is out now on Spotify, Apple Music, etc. Link in Bio. Thanks for listening❤️

Welcome to my Genesis NFT release, Beautiful Tragedy.

This one has been a long time coming. It’s inception beginning during the early days of lockdown in 2020. Everyone was losing their minds, but for me it felt like the first time I took a breath after a 5 year sprint.

In the chaos I was rediscovering this sleeping giant in me. For 5 years I was working non-stop. 12 hour days, occasionally 21 days straight. All to pay for degrees I didn’t believe in but somehow that version of the American dream was what was sold to me and shoved down my throat. A different story for a different day.

I can’t remember exactly when during those months of lockdown but an old friend reached out and asked if I wanted to join this “songwriter’s circle” he was putting together each week on zoom. It became something to look forward to each week. A way to work on art each day when the days blurred together.

Beautiful Tragedy was one of the songs from those sessions. I was trying to ramp up both my lyric writing and production skills at that time. This is the first time I fully had my hands in the production pot, outsourcing things to friends when I felt I had reached my limits. Lyrically this is the first time I explored the idea of writing stories that were not my own. Funny enough Taylor Swift released albums that year along the same lines.. Folklore and Evermore. If I remember correctly for the same reasons.. pulling material from your own life is exhausting. And what if you’re a sad songwriter and your life is going great? Do you.. stop creating? Self sabotage?

As the world “returned to normal” this track ultimately lived on my laptop. It’s as if we hopped right back into the rat race and forgot that we “slowed down” for this moment in time. The days passed, the months passed and here we are. But at the end of it all, I think the timing of this release is happening when it was meant to happen.

Beautiful Tragedy is best listened to with headphones, or better yet.. in your car; on a night drive when you want the world to slow down and you’re purely soaking in the vibes.

Thanks for supporting me in this journey, looking forward to this next step.

Going Nowhere (Enjoying the Ride) was my first album and 'Time is Amazing' is one of my favorites from that album.    
    
I've poured all my passion and my experiences as a young man into every note of those tracks. Recorded over 2 days in the spring of 2014, with some incredible Italian jazz musicians.  
  
Recording and releasing this album was a milestone moment in my artistic development. A journey that spanned continents, cultures, and emotions.

At that point in time I had graduated from the "G. Rossini Conservatory of Music" and traveled through most of Europe and Australia, meeting hundreds of incredible musicians, busking on the beautiful streets of Sydney, London, Paris, Rome, etc.
I also played each and every gig I could find, with all kinds of bands, musicians and DJs. Little by little expanding my musical horizons, acquiring knowledge, feeling and taste.  
  
My journey then took me to Berlin, where I refined my jazz chops.
I played hundreds of shows around the world with my quartet and supporting other amazing musicians.  

Then, in 2020, when live music went away, I took that as an opportunity to search for new avenues to release and monetize my music. I found an answer in blockchain technology.
With no limitations imposed by traditional standards, I let my creativity run wild.

I released my first album on Ethereum in March 2021, 'Nifty Sax Genesis', followed in September 2021 by 'Spheres', which was a ground-breaking success.  
  
My success inspired me to co-found Nifty Music, a music NFT incubator helping fellow artists create their own successful projects.
Nifty Music projects collectively generated over $1 million to-date for our independent artists and their communities.

And here we are now at the present moment, with yet another important milestone, the first music NFT I release to include music from my back catalog.

My first day traveling to the UK, my ears were cold. I bought a beanie and gravitated towards the pastel-purple one. My dear british friend said, "how cute, lavender in London!". With no hesitation I coined the phrase in my Notes app (amongst countless other random names and phrases).

This was my virgin trip to Europe/UK. After traveling through the Swiss mountains and flirting with the palpable history in London, I had no doubts I would naturally be inspired. Within a couple weeks of arriving home I sat down to play around with my guitar, there was no pretense. 

xxx creation xxx

The chord progression was first to arrive. I think I was purposely fooling around in a key I don't usually gravitate towards, it landed pretty quickly and felt very animated. I knew I was in the mindset to turn it into something.

I tried the cymbals on the upbeat and didn't look back. It just worked. I was itching to write a song with a groove like such anyway.

I love the hypnotizing drone bass on this track.. I did have another great bass line in the chamber - it danced with the kick. On paper it probably would have worked better but I was at the point in the creative process where I was exerting excess energy and I knew I should just move on and let the track be what it is.

The introduction is a combination of a rain storm I recorded when I was in Hilo, Hawaii, & a train crossing from San Diego, CA. I accidentally recorded the latter sound through my AirPods so it came out funky. But I liked it.

After my first session of building the song out, I had to name it before saving. I looked through my "list" of names. It was as if 'Lavender In London' was 10x the font size to the rest of the list. It was a no brainer.

I knew I was writing an abstract story in regards to the structure of this song. I enjoyed it and had no interest in re-working it to make 'more sense'.

Once I was finished & brought it to The Fund to mix, I could tell they were absolutely ITCHING to re-work it to be more digestible. But this was a time where I wanted it to stay 100% 'weird'. They did help me build a bridge to literally "bridge" the two parts of the songs before the main vocals come in.

Joshua_Squashua on Twitter did me a huge favor and commissioned the cover art. He is a true artist, I love(d) working with him.

That's the birth of my psychedelic-beach-indie-feel good track. Thanks for listening :)

Description:
The Snow Level, Playing As The Child Sleeps
2020 Vision - Hindsight Edition
Track 10

This song is caught between two moments in time. To be the child, enraptured in a small wonderful world until sleep takes you while it plays on. And to be older, the witness to this and understand it is still wonderful, just in different ways.

My first album, 2020 Vision was made in 2019 and originally released on Jan 1st 2020. It was a terrific experience, learning as I made, experimenting with all kinds of sounds and genres, but building with a full album experience in mind. The 12 tracks of the album rotate through the circle of fifths, with a track for each major key. It's a rather hopeful album I think, and it is interesting to look back on it, knowing just how much it contrasts with the year it entered. There is also a tinge of loneliness to some of the tracks, perhaps some of that underlying anxiety of seeing covid go down elsewhere in the world and wondering what could happen. This Hindsight Edition was an opportunity for me to go into the state of making these tracks, and feel out how my production has changed. One of the weaknesses of the original album was all the mastering was done with no prior experience, I literally had an ozone tutorial up as I did it. Nowadays I have a much better handle on those sorts of things and this Hindsight Edition is a way to get a new, clean modern master out there while still maintaining the original elements of the release. I hope everyone enjoys!

ABOUT THE RECORD
Frerick den Haan's masterpiece 'Les Heures du Jour' (Four Times of the Day) is a suite of four brand new compositions for solo piano named after the poster tetralogy by Alphonse Mucha. Heavenly inspired by Ravel's 'Daphnis et Cloë Suite' and 'Une barque sur l'océan' (Miroirs), 'Les Heures du Jour' proves that impressionism still has new paths to explore and thus is still relevant today. 

The decision to create a impressionistic suite comes from multiple inspiration sources. First of all, he fell in love a long time ago with the impressionistic approach where colouring the music seemed much more important rather than the focus on melody. The French composer Maurice Ravel seemed to have a great influence on Frerick's composing style throughout this suite.

Secondly, he recently visited a Mucha exhibition where he saw the four posters. Beautifully illustrated it reminded him of an alternate version of 'Vivaldi' Four Seasons'. While Ravel and Mucha were contemporaries and both lived and worked in Paris, they never met. Thus, also inspired by the fairytale illustrations of Mucha, Frerick decided to (in their honour) bring them together in a new piece of art. The artwork from the record is the actual tetralogy brought in new dotted perspective by illustrator Sanne Sprengers (NL). A2 - Éclat du Jour (Brightness of Day)

''Mystics view the daylight as a manifestation of divine truth and wisdom. Just as physical light dispels darkness, spiritual enlightenment brings clarity and understanding to the mysteries of existence.''

ABOUT THE RECORD
Frerick den Haan's masterpiece 'Les Heures du Jour' (Four Times of the Day) is a suite of four brand new compositions for solo piano named after the poster tetralogy by Alphonse Mucha. Heavenly inspired by Ravel's 'Daphnis et Cloë Suite' and 'Une barque sur l'océan' (Miroirs), 'Les Heures du Jour' proves that impressionism still has new paths to explore and thus is still relevant today. 

The decision to create a impressionistic suite comes from multiple inspiration sources. First of all, he fell in love a long time ago with the impressionistic approach where colouring the music seemed much more important rather than the focus on melody. The French composer Maurice Ravel seemed to have a great influence on Frerick's composing style throughout this suite.

Secondly, he recently visited a Mucha exhibition where he saw the four posters. Beautifully illustrated it reminded him of an alternate version of 'Vivaldi' Four Seasons'. While Ravel and Mucha were contemporaries and both lived and worked in Paris, they never met. Thus, also inspired by the fairytale illustrations of Mucha, Frerick decided to (in their honour) bring them together in a new piece of art. The artwork from the record is the actual tetralogy brought in new dotted perspective by illustrator Sanne Sprengers (NL). The suite has been pressed on 10' inch vinyl and will limited distributed as from October 1st 2023. The date and merch channel will be updates when ready.

With the company of a blend of electric and acoustic timbres and lead by an oboe, you may wander around in a chilly night until the sun rises.

“Oil and Water” is the second act of the instrumental suite opening the Tableaux Électroniques album. This track is marked by some stark contrasts: between acoustic and electronic instruments, between fast and slow sections, between swing and straight rhythms.
These contrasts won’t blend, but they will come to a sort of uneasy cohabitation, just like oil and water sometimes do. All the melodies you hear are played by a clarinet, at times heavily distorted and effected.

“Oil and Water” emulsify two themes taken from previous "Moods and Modes" pieces: Marilyn for the slow section and Geronimo for the fast one. "Moods and Modes" is a neverending collection of short instrumental pieces that traverse genres, an open playground I use to remix, reshape and recreate.

Sugar Daddy is an exhilarating rap anthem sure to captivate the listener with a beautiful soul sample and unapologetic lyrics. Kamre Haze holds no punches, delivering hard hitting bar after bar as he narrates and navigates the complexities of life, friendship, and relationships. The track dives deep into themes of authenticity, hypocrisy, and the struggle to maintain personal integrity as you move up in the world. 

With lines such as "Thinking sh*t's sweet, little b**** I ain't no sugar daddy", Kamre Haze quickly establishes his no-nonsense attitude and demeanor. As the verse unfolds, themes of social pressures and personality are explored, showing a vulnerable side of the artist all the while maintaining a striking level of self-belief and confidence. 

'Sugar Daddy' is an anthem for those who dare to stand their ground and speak their truth, regardless of the challenges that may come their way. If you enjoy hard hitting lyrics over soulful hip hop beats, this song is perfect for you.

I wrote this back in early 2020. It was cold outside, so it was probably around January in New Jersey. The seasonal depression was at an all time high lol. Anyways, this song is about feeling like you are not good enough for someone because they are so good in every way. You want to be the best version of yourself but you're just not quite there yet, or at least you think you aren't. I think we all unintentional self sabotage moments in our lives at times because of our own personal struggles. I think its very normal to feel like we aren't good enough for someone. It's a natural part of personal growth. It's human. Appreciate what you have in your life while you have it and feel blessed for the people who are in your life. :)

Much love.

Tommy

verb
1. allow or enable to escape from confinement; set free.

noun
2. the action of making a movie, recording, or other product available for general viewing or purchase.

I debated releasing this record. Not because I dislike it. Not because it doesn't mean a lot to me. I just feel like it's something that I've been struggling to find peace with and when I listen to it I'm reminded of exactly how I felt during that time. 

But maybe that's exactly what a release is meant to be. Releasing all of the pain and trauma and finally finding peace with it. Moving forward.

Lately I've felt like a shell of myself. Dwelling in the ashes of a house that I desperately tried to keep from burning down. And it's not who or where I want to be anymore.

I want to get back to myself. I've missed me. So I'm doing something that I love again: releasing.

To anyone who listens, collects, shares, etc. thank you. Thank you for the grace you all have given me as I find my way back to myself. Thank you for loving and supporting me. Thank you for allowing me to just be me.

All love, always.

- MRH

The song "You were my rose" is inspired by the book "The Little Prince" by Antoine de Saint-Exupéry. In this book, the "Rose" is a character whom the Little Prince encounters on his planet and falls in love with. The Rose becomes a symbol of love and tenderness for him.

In the context of "The Little Prince," the phrase "You were my rose" means that the Rose was particularly important to the main character. Sunsets have called me to accept endings and new beginnings; to develop a loving detachment that permits me to enjoy a moment and not hold onto it past it’s expiration date. 

Earlier this year, when I released “Golden Hour”, I was ready to quit in many aspects of my life and artistry, but received an outpouring of love, support, and affirming energy that gave me the creative courage to start again. 

In my musings about endings and new beginnings, I was reminded of something I once read. “Quitting is a fundamental part of being an artist. The only difference between an artist that quit and one that is still making art is that the latter had the courage to start again.”

My entire life has felt like a cycle of dying and being reborn, though, it wasn’t until now that I’ve attained such a peaceful perspective on that process. 

I now welcome the small deaths that occur on a day-to-day, week-to-week, month-to-month, and yearly basis. 

I welcome the space that is being created for experiences and connections that I’ve longed for deep in my being.

Each song on “Play This at Sunset” represents a readiness for birth in a different aspect of my existence. 

The EP also exists in company with a visual collection entitled NEARSTALGIA BAY (NBX for short). NBX is a city in the Surf Noir region. 

There, a unique phenomena occurs in which the city is bathed in an eternal sunset.

The NBX Collection will give insight into the people and places of this locale.

Love can heal the world.

Turn it up in your car, your house, your party, everywhere.

Description: GET THE GEM song

🚨This song is part of a crowdfunding and every collector get very cool benefits, read the text bellow so you can get to know more about me and my project better 🚨 MUCH LOVE 💕
Hi there! Although some of you might know me as Yaxx, my real name is Yagna. That's what my mom calls me.

I'm a singer-songwriter from Havana, Cuba. I'm a mother to an amazing 5-year-old boy. My favorite color is purple, and I recently turned 27.
I wanted to be a doctor for a short time, but I honestly can't remember when I wasn't dreaming about performing my heart out on stage.
I started working with a band as a singer when I was only 18 years old and bought my first acoustic guitar on my 19th birthday by saving up my earnings. I've been writing songs for as long as I can remember. The first time I played my guitar, I wrote the song that changed my life, "Mercedes Benz." Yes, I tend to personalize things as abstract as a song because honesty is what unlocks the soul in my music. Working with a "cover" band has taught me a lot in the past seven years. I gained stage presence. Performing Led Zeppelin songs helped me improve my vocal abilities, but nothing compares to the feeling of standing on stage and singing the stories I've written.

In 2020 with the quarantine, all I had was my guitar, so I took that forced break from my routine to improve my songwriting. I helped two Cuban artists finish their albums (for legal reasons, I cannot share their names). I discovered some magical stuff about writing in Spanish (which I am now obsessed with).

I released my first song in Spanish on all digital platforms on September 18th, 2021, called "Deja Vu," since then, my life has been an incredible roller coaster.

I joined Twitter in January 2022 to help promote a collection, and little did I know, I was heading to the warmest place I'd been in forever.
My journey as a Web 3 artist started on the Tezos Blockchain, where I released three singles that were somehow related but weren't part of a collection. These songs were all acoustic performances recorded on my cellphone. My most successful song of those three was "Viernes," my first to sell out and which later became my first collaboration with my now producer and partner Caueiro. This collaboration became my debut on Catalog, a 1/1s music market on the Ethereum Blockchain, collected by Xcelencia. For that, I am eternally grateful.

I am a "me and my guitar" kind of performer when it comes to my music, but with the profit of my latest collection on objkt.com, "Yaxx's Nine Lives," I was able to switch things up and gather other musicians, I admired for a long time. This gave life to "Numerología," my own little band, which we debuted during a concert on my 27th birthday. Needless to say, it was a dream come true!

I can proudly say I now have enough material to record and release my first full-length album: NUMEROLOGIA: THE ALBUM, a 9 tracks love story.
I'm super excited to share this album with the world.
Being a full-time singer in Cuba is a constant struggle financially. Life in Cuba can be challenging even for people that are not professional artists.

For context, selling one edition is listed at
0.005 eth (~9 USD) equals a two-month concert salary. I won't mention the daily living expenses because this is NOT about that. This is about music and art and love!

So, I am releasing a crowdfunding NFT. I've written a beautiful, soulful song called "Lights on Me," which encompasses everything I am attracting and manifesting for this new career era. This will be a limited edition, 540 editions (yes, I have a thing for the number nine, and I can tell the number nine has a thing for me as well). 

The Lights on Me NFT will be listed at 0.01 eth (approximately 20 USD at the time of this article) and is available from August 27th
Our main goal is to collect at least 540 editions before November 25th (90 days) to release the full album on April 27th.

Below are the details of the benefits of being a holder:
All the holders get access to Metaverse concerts and behind-the-scenes content of the album process and receive merch! This care package will include a personalized hand-written note expressing my gratitude and some fabulous album material.

The maximum amount of mints per wallet will be 5 editions. The more editions that are minted means more benefits to the holders:
1 minted= access to presale to the album with a 50% discount.
2 minted= access to presale to the album with a 75% discount.
3 minted= 1 free copy of the album.
4 minted= 1 free copy of the album AND  a custom NFT cover song
5 minted=  free copy of the album AND  a custom NFT cover song and a 25% discount on future mints, no matter the Blockchain.
Follow me on all social media platforms (@yaxx_castillo), and be sure to turn on notifications, as there will be many spaces and performances over the next 90 days. I'm always glad to connect and get to know my followers and supporters. Thanks for reading. Much love.

Picture this: "Cerulean City," a sonic voyage that sprung from the fertile crossroads of serendipity and digital connection. It all began when I stumbled upon Garrett's sonic sorcery on Instagram. A virtual baton-pass of beats and verses ensued, forging a harmonious bond that could only be defined by wavelengths and wavelengths of music. But here's where the plot twists into the unexpected: I found myself en route to Los Angeles, that sprawling canvas where dreams brush shoulders with reality. Garrett and I seized the moment, deciding to turn our pixelated synergy into an in-person crescendo.

Now, close your eyes and imagine that day: the City of Angels draped in clouds as if to cast a cinematic filter on our creative convergence. The overcast sky wasn't just a backdrop; it was a bridge between LA's cosmopolitan glitz and the gray-tinted memories of Detroit's weather. Amidst this weathered symphony, the verses poured forth like a torrent, my pen racing across paper as if propelled by the very raindrops tapping on the windowpane. Fifteen, maybe twenty minutes, that's all it took to channel the essence of blue-collar reveries and the gritty aspirations that play second fiddle to the 9-to-5 grind. And just like that, as if the universe had queued it up, the hook echoed in, a chorus that resonated with the anthem of moonlight hustles and the stubborn pursuit of aspirations against the odds. "Cerulean City" isn't just a song; it's a resonance, a fusion of backgrounds and dreams that beats at the heart of both the verses and the producer behind the soundboard. Garrett and I? We're comrades in the midnight pursuit of our dreams, and that spirit, that very electricity, pulses through every note and rhythm of this track.

It's Alright, I Just Need a Moment to Myself
2020 Vision - Hindsight Edition
Track 8

This one is a response to the theme of the previous track. I am one of those people that really does handle issues best by allowing myself quiet and space. I try to be thoughtful on my responses to tough situations, and if I let my mind wander for a bit I'm usually able to steel my resolve and push forward with energy.

My first album, 2020 Vision was made in 2019 and originally released on Jan 1st 2020. It was a terrific experience, learning as I made, experimenting with all kinds of sounds and genres, but building with a full album experience in mind. The 12 tracks of the album rotate through the circle of fifths, with a track for each major key. It's a rather hopeful album I think, and it is interesting to look back on it, knowing just how much it contrasts with the year it entered. There is also a tinge of loneliness to some of the tracks, perhaps some of that underlying anxiety of seeing covid go down elsewhere in the world and wondering what could happen. This Hindsight Edition was an opportunity for me to go into the state of making these tracks, and feel out how my production has changed. One of the weaknesses of the original album was all the mastering was done with no prior experience, I literally had an ozone tutorial up as I did it. Nowadays I have a much better handle on those sorts of things and this Hindsight Edition is a way to get a new, clean modern master out there while still maintaining the original elements of the release. I hope everyone enjoys!

Description:
One Last Night Terror
2020 Vision - Hindsight Edition
Track 7

I used to be a much more nervous, anxious person. If I went to sleep while under a lot of stress or somewhere unfamiliar there was a not insignificant chance I'd have some very real seeming dream and act it out some even after waking. Usually a "someone is in the room" or "there's snakes everywhere" type dream (I'm not even afraid of snakes). As I got older I learned to stop letting things weigh on me so heavily and I got really good at squashing the fear of failure. Sometimes I wonder what the current me would do if caught in one of those old dreams.

My first album, 2020 Vision was made in 2019 and originally released on Jan 1st 2020. It was a terrific experience, learning as I made, experimenting with all kinds of sounds and genres, but building with a full album experience in mind. The 12 tracks of the album rotate through the circle of fifths, with a track for each major key. It's a rather hopeful album I think, and it is interesting to look back on it, knowing just how much it contrasts with the year it entered. There is also a tinge of loneliness to some of the tracks, perhaps some of that underlying anxiety of seeing covid go down elsewhere in the world and wondering what could happen. This Hindsight Edition was an opportunity for me to go into the state of making these tracks, and feel out how my production has changed. One of the weaknesses of the original album was all the mastering was done with no prior experience, I literally had an ozone tutorial up as I did it. Text by William Blake.

lyrics.text:
Children of the future age,
Reading this indignant page,
Know that in a former time,
Love, sweet Love, was thought a crime!
In the Age of Gold,
Free from winter's cold,
Youth and maiden bright
To the holy light,
Naked in the sunny beams delight.
Once a youthful pair,
Fill'd with softest care,
Met in garden bright
Where the holy light
Had just remov'd the curtains of the night.
There, in rising day,
On the grass they play;
Parents were afar,
Strangers came not near,
And the maiden soon forgot her fear.
Tired with kisses sweet,
They agree to meet
When the silent sleep
Waves o'er heaven's deep,
And the weary tired wanderers weep.
To her father white
Came the maiden bright;
But his loving look,
Like the holy book,
All her tender limbs with terror shook.
'Ona! pale and weak!
To thy father speak:
O! the trembling fear,
О! the dismal care,
That shakes the blossoms of my hoary hair!'

Description:
Who are Beachcrimes? We’re a duo from LA and we spent the last year making songs in hotel rooms around the world. Beachcrimes is the soundtrack to that adventure.
 
We made a lot of songs, and we’re excited to share them. All of them. This year we’re releasing 24 songs in 48 weeks. If we’re being real, it’s actually two albums – there’s AM and there’s PM. AM is the lite stuff, PM is the nite stuff. Think of it like the Summer Olympics and Winter Olympics, but for dance music.

“Fahrenheit” is our 15th single this year. At the risk of disappointing our European metric system fans, Fahrenheit just sang better than Celsius. Our PM album is chalk full of tech house bangers and this one is no different. We knew we needed a pregame song about feeling hot and this song only needs about 10 words to get the job done. So take a look in the mirror and tell em “Fahrenheit, I’m hot sh**”.

Next single will be out 2 weeks from today, and the following single 2 weeks after that.

This song is being released as a FREE MINT minus the cost of the platform and network fees.  We're not getting anything other than the satisfaction of your enjoyment.  Hopefully, people will find it inspiring to listen and share with others to mint as well!

About Neo Soul:

Finding that special someone, your soulmate can be elusive.  When you find that person, everything feels, tastes, looks, and smells better.  Life has a perspective of renewal.  More than a helpmate, your spiritual twin makes life harmonious.  Ask those that have found their soulmate.  Their soul is found...it is new again.  Neo Soul.

When I wrote this song, it was precisely the right moment that I found so many of my friends and relatives searching for their soulmate.  I wrote this for all of them.  It was quite an easy song to write.  The feeling was so intense inside me that the lyrics flowed and resonated with my imagination.  The arrangement and production took time as we dressed the song in different 'clothes' until we realized it had to be emotively deep, raw, and sweet simultaneously.  

About Ransom Kong:

Ransom Kong was initially comprised of lifelong friends Richard Zeuch and Ransom Kong from Kihei, Maui.  They wrote some stinkers early in their career including a laugher called, 'Essence of Cesspool Scum' (Punk genre of course).  Ransom went to LA and Richard to Baltimore among other places to pursue music, performing with bands and writing songs.  After many years, they reconnected upon their return to Maui to hone their songwriting style and sound.  Some of their songs have been commented on having inklings of Death Cab for Cutie, The Pixies, The Beatles, Harry Styles among others.  They're fans of most genres and let their eclectic tastes shine in the music.  Later, Sylvain Audet, bass extraordinaire and hard working engineer-producer joined them to bring an extra polish to the sound.  Likewise, he is a lover of many music genres, especially funk.  Sylvain has played and studied with master bass teachers and serves as music director for side music projects.  This trio creates studio delights and are just itching to stretch their combined creative powers.  New music is slated for release in late fall to winter of 2023.

About the cover art:

As a one time and short lived moderator of a NFT generative art project, I was gifted this from one of the main artists.  It reminds me of the Pueo or Hawaiian white owl.  It is my sky amakua or sky spirit animal that protects and guides me.  I see it often when I drive the Maalaea area of Maui.  It's infrequent to see them at night but it usually flies over my car when I drive past there at night!  Kind of like part of my Neo Soul flying high.

Chilled electronic love.

“Love is a Gun” melds minimal electronic instrumentation with a cold, almost ethereal sonic palette. 

The lyrics delve deep into the duality of love, portraying it as both a weapon and a refuge. As the words unfold, love is personified as a force that can empower, seduce, or devastate, underlining its unpredictable nature. 

The refrain "Love Is a Gun" contrasts the concept of love with the cold steel of a firearm, suggesting love's ability to captivate or destroy. 

The piece, both in its sound and message, becomes a meditation on the complexities and paradoxes of human emotions.

"Elements of Life: A Musical Journey Through Life’s Struggles and Finding Serenity & Solace"

In a world plagued by the chaos of the pandemic, two resilient brothers found solace, creativity, and a profound connection to their emotions through music. "Elements of Life," a captivating EP crafted by Nitish (Chalk) and Harshit(El Khefe) , encapsulates our journey through the unprecedented times. Comprising four mesmerizing tracks - "La Lluvia," "A Walk in the Park," "Eve," and "Youniverse" - this EP transcends mere musical compositions. It's a poignant narrative that emanates from the depths of our hearts, painting a vivid picture of their struggles, triumphs, and unbreakable bond.

"La Lluvia" - Echoes of Calm Amidst the Storm
The opening track, "La Lluvia," ushers in a sense of tranquility amid the storm. The croaking of toads, the gentle pitter-patter of rain, and the distant rumble of thunder create an atmosphere of deep calmness. Synth pads intermingle with melodic keys, mirroring the entangled nature of life itself. Despite the chaos that surrounds it, this track stands as a testament to finding balance and harmony amidst the turmoil.
Been a bit down lately but this song can always pick me right back up. I hope it does the same for you!

In the twilight's embrace, beneath a sky brushed with the hues of time, there unfolds the sacred Rite Of Passage. It is the hushed symphony of souls in metamorphosis, a dance betwixt realms, where innocence and experience entwine.

***

There's no denying that this song holds a special place in my heart...

Written during a period of personal turmoil, when my life was moving neither forward nor backward, I felt stuck where I was. I lacked the courage to move on while at the same time, I feared retreating back into the past.

I didn't know it at the moment but I was in the process of reinventing myself, and my life. And as so often is the case, for something new to emerge something old must die. Only once we let go of the old, can we truly appreciate our newfound path.

Through it all, this song emerged as a testament: an ode to the unyielding spirit within us. It stands as a reminder that no matter the tempests that life sends our way or the labyrinthine passages we navigate, a path forward is ALWAYS waiting to be discovered.

May this music serve as a beacon of courage, illuminating your journey as you forge ahead, crafting the beginning of a new chapter in the story of your life!

It narrates the yearning of a lover, constantly on the move, lamenting the moments lost away from his beloved. This enchanting piece has been graced by numerous renditions. Among them, maestro Homer Dizeyee's interpretation stands out as exceptionally poignant, while maestro Shamsula Rahmani's vocal rendition resonates deeply.

'In The Smoke - Eligh's Version' is a collaboration between Scottish singer-songwriter Emma Miller and LA-born artist, musician and rapper Eligh. Both artists have decided to use this drop to contribute to the relief efforts in Hawaii since wildfires ravaged communities this August. 

This NFT also grants you access to the stems of Emma's original arrangement as well as future allow lists for Emma Miller. NFT holders will be invited to a special, token-gated livestream on August 31st with Emma. 

Eligh, a self-described “genre-breaking, obsessive bass fiend” has continued to sustain himself as a salient figure for over twenty seven years within the increasingly fickle and rapidly revolving world of hip-hop. The Los Angeles native has maintained his respected status by fearlessly veering from a traditional trajectory which is often limited to beats and rhymes. Instead, Eligh has chosen to fabricate projects that incorporate the gritty sounds of the UK dub scene, the unorthodox styling of indie rock, the lush guitars and honesty of folk music and the complexity of jazz, all without losing the listener in a musically esoteric composition.

"My goal with remixing Emma's already beautiful song was to have no goal at all, just to ride wherever the energy took me. I did want to change the vibe in a sense of movement with the drum patterns and speed, but maintain the mood because both of us are very moody artists in our own right! I had to add a verse because the topic and the idea of shifting her song into a dark/moody hip hop song were irresistible."

Holding the NFT is your proof that you were here first for this debut collab and moment in history. September 1st will see the song released across streaming platforms - stay tuned for how to pre-save and support the launch. 

Original artwork by Eligh.

Colours Dancing, working title (All Day I Stare At A Wall And That's OK), was written during the time of isolation during the pandemic.

After losing my job due to the shut downs I was faced with despair, overwhelming pressure to find a way to survive and the overall sense of hopelessness and absurdity.
Confronted with various tragedy and losing many good people in my life, one day I just decided to sit down and reflect on everything.

Finally taking a day to relax I managed to have a breakthrough, hence the original title "All Day I Stare At A Wall And That's OK". I was literally sat with my colour projectors on in the dark looking at all the colours on the walls thinking about how I could move forward.

I mind mapped, spoke everything through out loud and decided I was going to start taking music seriously, because to me it's something that invariably connects everyone, gives us all hope and most importantly it always brings me a torrent of positive emotions. There's nothing quite like having a vague thought in your mind and watching it become this whole world.

So Colours Dancing became the first solo project track I had written using Ableton and it was through this track I learned production from the ground up. It took over a year to get it to a place I was finally satisfied.

As time moved on, I found blockchain and AI art, I'd finally found a home for these worlds I had been creating. I realised that they had all been a reflection of my reality and my Web3 journey. I'd never felt more at home.

Imagine a universe where we are connected by shimmering beams of light, everyone to everyone. One quirk about this universe is that the beams send emotions between us, one million per minute per pair, clearly and effortlessly. Joy is instantly contagious. A hurtful thought toward another is understood with compassion, seen alongside the place of sadness where it arose. Every feeling triggers infinite empathy, therefore boundless acceptance. (The beams send only the stuff of our souls, not our thoughts — so we still have privacy, interesting conversation, and the ability to prank each other silly.)

Now imagine we already live in this universe except, long ago, we somehow forgot where the beams disappeared off to. But we’ve always kept music with us, because it’s our best way to speak in the old way.

+

Taiwan-born & reared on-the-go between Taipei and the American Southwest, Eric Pan (a.k.a. pandelic) found his musical footing via a jazz mentorship with Ray Brown at the University of California. These studies propelled him onto stages with Jeff Hamilton and Roy Hargrove, plus over a decade’s tenure as New York City pianist & composer. Pan’s compositions and improvisations reveal a relentless pursuit of simplicity, craft, and universality.

Hear him interviewed on-air next to Orson Welles on national radio with PRI’s “The World”, read his exclusive premiere interview in JAZZIZ Magazine, and stream/download his latest long-form interview on the _For a Living_ podcast.

Description:
My Hometown Empties
2020 Vision - Hindsight Edition
Track 6

Every autumn, my hometown holds a riverside festival that brings in a lot of people. The streets are absolutely packed body to body and there's lots of energy. I always use it as an opportunity to visit family. This song is about the day after. The morning where the road is lined with people leaving, and the day shows in stark contrast just how few people are left in the town itself. All the young leave, it's an aging, dying place.

My first album, 2020 Vision was made in 2019 and originally released on Jan 1st 2020. It was a terrific experience, learning as I made, experimenting with all kinds of sounds and genres, but building with a full album experience in mind. The 12 tracks of the album rotate through the circle of fifths, with a track for each major key. It's a rather hopeful album I think, and it is interesting to look back on it, knowing just how much it contrasts with the year it entered. There is also a tinge of loneliness to some of the tracks, perhaps some of that underlying anxiety of seeing covid go down elsewhere in the world and wondering what could happen. This Hindsight Edition was an opportunity for me to go into the state of making these tracks, and feel out how my production has changed. One of the weaknesses of the original album was all the mastering was done with no prior experience, I literally had an ozone tutorial up as I did it. Nowadays I have a much better handle on those sorts of things and this Hindsight Edition is a way to get a new, clean modern master out there while still maintaining the original elements of the release. I hope everyone enjoys!

This song is based on traveling between my hometown and the city I live in. I love visiting my family but somehow the drive down always dragged on. Heading back was opposite however, something peaceful but still energizing about the return home.

Heading North
2020 Vision - Hindsight Edition
Track 5

This song is based on traveling between my hometown and the city I live in. I love visiting my family but somehow the drive down always dragged on. Heading back was opposite however, something peaceful but still energizing about the return home.

My first album, 2020 Vision was made in 2019 and originally released on Jan 1st 2020. It was a terrific experience, learning as I made, experimenting with all kinds of sounds and genres, but building with a full album experience in mind. The 12 tracks of the album rotate through the circle of fifths, with a track for each major key. It's a rather hopeful album I think, and it is interesting to look back on it, knowing just how much it contrasts with the year it entered. There is also a tinge of loneliness to some of the tracks, perhaps some of that underlying anxiety of seeing covid go down elsewhere in the world and wondering what could happen. This Hindsight Edition was an opportunity for me to go into the state of making these tracks, and feel out how my production has changed. One of the weaknesses of the original album was all the mastering was done with no prior experience, I literally had an ozone tutorial up as I did it. Nowadays I have a much better handle on those sorts of things and this Hindsight Edition is a way to get a new, clean modern master out there while still maintaining the original elements of the release. I hope everyone enjoys!

So if you're a world traveler that loves to embark on new adventures or you just want to enjoy the present moment you've had and leave your phone for a bit, this song is a must in your playlist.

While I do love collaboration and working on music with and for others, there's so many factors that go into releases for other artists that are beyond my control and it can sometimes feel easy to lose your own creative identity in knowing what you like for yourself when you are constantly trying to blend in like a chameleon to other artists visions.

This was one of the first songs me and my good friend Joshua Apple made together. I had asked him to send me over some beats and he threw this one in the pack, not expecting me to use it for anything. Lo and behold, this song became my first single. Originally, it was called Count Me Out, but we had to change the name so we didn’t confuse anyone because of Kendrick Lamar’s release (or get into any legal disputes with the man himself).

The Demo Days: On a Comeup (March 9th, 2019)

All the beats David, the producer of the record, sent me in that pack were fire, but this one stood out to me immediately. It sounded like a sunset in August.

At the time, David and I were working together pretty frequently. I’d drive down to his place in Hawthorne, like an hour away. We’d do a 4-5 hour session, and then I’d drive an hour back, straight to the bar I worked at for the night shift. It was music all day and the bar all night.  I had been in LA for a little over a year and was in the heart of the grind, so I wrote a song about it. 

There’s actually an original version, where the verses have different, more melodic lyrics.  There was a pretty awesome alternative post chorus on that as well. It didn’t matter though, the song needed bars, so this version was born. 

It’s odd listening back to it. The first thing that strikes me is “kid”. I was 26 then, and it felt fitting to call myself a kid. Now, not so much. I also feel bad for that Joe in a way. The whole song feels like it’s written by a kid nearing the end of the comeup, as if all it would take is one more push for the problems to melt away. Just a little more grinding. Little did he know.
