Description:
The song refers to the orixá Iemanjá. This deity is part of the African-rooted religions in Brazil, being a female orixá, recognized as the orixá of salt waters, patroness of fishermen, characterized by motherhood and issues related to the head and decisions of individuals. She is the most syncretized and worshipped deity in the African pantheon in Brazil, with her worship widespread from north to south, with many festivals and holidays in her honor in the country. 


An artist with extensive experience in Afro-religious-Brazilian musicality, in “Festa pra Iemanjá,” Libertu evokes the deepest elements of the tradition. The artist rhythmically constructs the song on the drum beats of Umbanda yards, especially on the "Ijexá," "Cabula," and also "Alujá" rhythms.

The arrangements prioritize percussion elements, which lead the music through the sections. The harmony is provided by a guitar coupled with counterpoints performed by saxophone, flute, and a choir of female voices. In the recordings, Libertu played all the percussion instruments and the guitar. "Canção pra Iemanjá" can be categorized as a prayer-song and is part of the MPB tradition that recognizes, praises, and evokes the strength of ancestry.

Moroccan Oranges is a song about the summer I traveled to Morocco and Paris with my dad and sister after my mom passed away. It’s about the dissonance I felt looking at my dad trying to hold it together and make us feel okay, knowing that even though we were seeing stunning views, and trying new foods, and were there together, we felt completely shattered. After my dad passed, the trip took on even more significance as the last time I really had with him. 
The artwork is a photo of my dad and I. My sister took it after we fell asleep on a train after visiting Monet’s gardens in Giverny. 
The song is intentionally upbeat to juxtapose the lyrics.

I don’t think there's a concrete reason as to why I associate Joshua Tree to self reflection and mushrooms. But ..

One of the reasons may be the open landscape of Joshua Tree that gives it such a peaceful setting. The absence of heavy development and the quietness of the desert create an environment perfect for peace of mind. 

This was the perfect place to end the tour. No service. No Netflix. No TikTok. Just thoughts of reflection and gratitude for the trip. At certain parts of the trip, it almost felt like I was on cruise control - things were going just as scheduled (I made an hour by hour schedule for all 5 days of the journey).

But that schedule ended after this last performance at Joshua Tree, leaving me at a loss for words or action - just thoughts. Bringing this idea to fruition is why I make music and create. The sense of accomplishment is priceless. But I couldn’t help but have a yearning for the things I was depriving myself from all year - family, stability, the present.

The next move was always on my mind. But here - the road ended. And how coincidental, that on this night, there was a full moon - a symbol of deep emotion, completion, and spiritual growth. Looking up at the full moon, I sat in awe as this trip was nearing its end.

In this performance, you will hear Two Worlds Collide, Future, Nimbostratus, and One Life. The deep reflection in these songs - touching on human life on earth, mortality, decision making, keeping a positive outlook - all felt like topics fit perfect for Joshua Tree.

As you watch this performance, imagine the stillness around -  traffic, police sirens, notifications on your phone - all silenced.

'House Music' is a dynamic and vibrant song that blends elements of hip-hop and the pulsating rhythms of dance music. The lyrics are a reflection of a high energy, carefree lifestyle filled with partying, hedonism, and romantic escapades. The song starts with a relaxed, inviting tone, suggesting a laidback setting to unwind and enjoy the present moment.

As the song progresses, it delves into themes of lavish spending habits and a gift giving love language. With vivid imagery and metaphors, Kamre Haze paints a scene filled with ambience. In contrast, there are moments of intimacy and vulnerability, with lyrics suggesting a deeper longing for genuine connection amidst the superficiality of the party scene.

The song was penned at the age of 19, reflecting a love for a distant partner. Despite the awareness of our toxic dynamic and acknowledging my own youthful flaws, I couldn't resist baring my heart on my sleeve and embracing the painful experience of love.

Standing 750 feet from the ocean that it stands in, the Golden Gate Bridge is a “larger than life” monument that leaves you in awe. The bridge goes on for about 1.2 miles (about 3,000 steps to get from one end to the other). The bridge weighs 840 million pounds…. Lol (heavier than the Empire State Building)

Below are my thoughts post-performance at the bridge.

“I’m feeling extremely blessed. Not many people get to see what I’m seeing right now. I’m from Connecticut. I’m a long way from home. I miss my family’s warmth and acceptance. Music is the vessel of exploration for me. I don’t think I would have come here if it wasn’t for music. Trying to soak it in before I have to focus elsewhere.”

I made it out of the harsh streets of Guilford, Connecticut lol. In all honesty, it is not normal to pursue a creative role in life where I’m from. But it never really seemed different while I was and am doing them. Maybe it’s because the internet has exposed us to so many other people doing crazy things. Maybe I’m delusional and need help. Either or, I traveled 2,000 miles from my home - to - perform the music I made in front of the Golden Gate Bridge in San Francisco. 

In this performance, you will hear Cutie, Sunny Day, Green Converse, and You Can. These songs have a very light feeling, which is the feel I get when I think about San Francisco. Most likely influenced by my childhood favorite, Full House. 

So, as you tune in for the upcoming performance, let the magic of the Golden Gate Bridge transport you to a place where engineering brilliance meets artistic elegance. It's not just a bridge; it's a symbol of possibility, a beacon that has stood the test of time, welcoming all who pass through its majestic arches.

Interesting fact. This is not the bridge pictured on the Golden State Warriors logo. I thought it was until corrected. :( oops.

This track has been inspired by the tree, l'arbre in french. 

The whole track is build as an ascension, from the seed to the universe, from the roots to the sky, from the ground to the cosmos, from the human experience to a united consciousness. There are different layers of representation throughout the piece as the physical tree and the cosmic tree are always interwoven. Thus there is a continuous movement between the apparent reality and the surrealistic world.

It has been created in three distinctive parts. 

The first (0:00 to 10:40) is an acousmatic piece, starting with the cracking of the seed, and figuring the growing of the tree. It has been composed by a microediting technique of only microphonic sound, mostly wood pieces and branches. 

The tree grows towards a forest, and the second part represent the forest itself (10:30 to 20:00). It was again composed by mostly microphonic sound taken from the primal forest of Sarawak on the Island of Borneo.
The sound of the forest is slowed down, and underlined with very specific pure tones (analog sine waves) to create a beating effect between the organic forest and the synthetic analog sounds.

The third part sees the arrival of music instruments, such as piano, vibraphone, guitar and voices. This is the introduction of the next section (L’ARBRE 2) which will later be released later this year as an orchestral piece of a song which can already be heard in a live version here 
https://youtu.be/QkFewHnGWtk?si=hjeziqpwT2EPX5jB
This third part respresents the journey towards a unified consciousness.

Close your eyes and let "Starlight Forest" wash over you, a tranquil balm for the soul. It's the perfect escape from the everyday, a sonic sanctuary where stress melts away, and peace reigns supreme.

Citadel is the RŌHKI theme song - first debuted on rohki.xyz

It’s been the cornerstone to our world and a moment we’ve patiently waited to release until now.

A full, newly scored version of the track is being shared as our submission for Optimism’s onchain art competition - and as a tribute to the end of Season 1 and an ode to Season 2.

Over the course of the past year and a half we’ve become fluent in what it means to be onchain while becoming fluent in what it means to use AI and emerging technology to tell our story.

We started Season 1 with our Genesis Keys on Mirror - a collection which has served as the bedrock to our community.

Our first two songs were done completely independently - bringing our community to our site where they were greeted with Citadel before experiencing a curated mint experience.

This was an extremely warm welcome - and we were honored to learn that our first song of Season 1 - Desperado - had inspired the creation of one of the most prominent collector communities in onchain music. (check out Lạc Đà for more on this)

It was over time that we realized releasing on Sound was about something bigger than just us - it was about being a part of a collective and an intention to share our music with the world in a novel way while making a conscious impact on our relationship with our community.

Fast forward to Horizon - our first release on Optimism and one of the first songs on Sound Swap.

We were shocked to watch 5k editions be minted - clearly showcasing the power of the superchain and the importance of L2s.

This led to our next L2 singles Demon, Lạc Đà and our CERULEAN EP - all of which were minted on Optimism and released exclusively onchain.

In total - we've been blessed to have minted 9,825 editions on Optimism across 9 songs to 1725 unique collectors.

This impact has given us the confidence to take our story to the next level - which is exactly what we plan to do with any potential winnings by expanding our team for Season 2.

So in closing thoughts - we’d like to thank our community for joining us on this journey.

For being such an integral part of what makes RŌHKI so special.

We have very ambitious plans for Season 2 - so we wanted to give it our all for this competition.

We hope you enjoy this free mint and look forward to sharing much more with you in the coming months.

The music of Art History 101, a collaborative Stable Diffusion Deforum music video created by null_hax and Vnderworld.

Throughout the course of human history, from our primal ancestors to the present day, art has been a constant and essential part of our cultural expression, evolving through the hands of Homo Sapiens, masters of paint and sculpture, counter culture icons, and street art nomads alike.

"Art History 101" is a compelling exploration of the intersection between the past, present, and the future of creative expression. The piece reflects on the evolution of the artist. With a deft hand, Null Hax and Vnderworld weave together the traditions of art history with contemporary techniques and technologies to create a work that is both timely and timeless.

Sequoia National Park, home of the largest trees in the world. THE WORLD!! INCLUDING ALL OF THE CONTINENTS!! While some of the trees can grow up to 300 feet in the air, (the size of the Statue of Liberty), the width of the trees can grow up to 30 feet. Thats about 20 people standing side by side. The feeling of being in the presence of these trees is pretty indescribable, but here’s a journal entry from my time spent there. 

“I made it. I just finished the performance. I thought I was doomed for a moment, but we did it. 1 take. And the sun is down. I wish I got to take in the trees more, but as I sit here at this sunset I'm feeling very thankful once again. I wish I could share this moment with somebody else. The camera isn’t capturing the beauty thats for sure. I hope I make it back to the hydrogen station. We'll see.”

Walking by trees taller than the buildings in LA, NY CHI - just made by…. Nature?? God?? Aliens?? Who knows. Makes the little things in life feel a bit less significant. 

In this performance, you will hear All Me, Break it Down Freestyle, Airplane Mode, and WYA. These songs all have a low, dark tone to the production. But are all have a powerful feeling. Some of my personal favorites of my whole discography. 

So, as you join me for a performance amidst these giants, envision the majesty of Sequoia, and let the magic of this place enrich your experience. Together, let's celebrate the wonders of this natural sanctuary.

Description:
“In Your Mind” explores the mysterious, elusive, and magical nature of creativity, emphasizing how artists connect through their shared ability to dream up new worlds and creations. Throughout parallel universes these creative minds inhabit, wonders unfold from the subconscious realm as they sleep. The lyrics reflect the delicate dance between risk-taking and cautious contemplation. “In Your Mind" is a reminder of the infinite possibilities that unfold when one embraces the magic of their own creativity.

I have been an artist my entire life. At age 8, I was exploring all the creative mediums I could: visual art, singing, piano, animation, acting, dance, etc. I’ve always been a daydreamer fantasizing about other worlds and realms within my imagination. I’ve used creativity as a way to escape and distract myself from the struggles of depression and anxiety. As I’ve grown, I’ve discovered that I can use creativity to sink deeper into my feelings and heal, rather than escape from them. I’ve had to learn to find my own sense of balance between my fantasy worlds and reality: “Row row row / Your boat will sink if she thinks only of the dreams.” 

I recorded all the instruments and vocal layers on my own. My setup is pretty simple: I plug in a USB microphone directly to my laptop recording and mixing in GarageBand. I am very passionate about composing songs with many layers. For this particular song, I played various instruments including xylophone, accordion, melodica, electric piano, and shakers. In addition, the song artwork paired with the track is an original drawing that I drew using my iPad and Procreate software.

Description:
"One Life" is about embracing the unknown, taking a leap of faith toward one's dreams, and ultimately experiencing transformation rather than succumbing to the fear of the uncharted. The harder the journey becomes, the closer one is to discovering a magic that transcends imagination. 

My inspiration stems from a deep connection to mental health and the transformative power that our times of adversity can hold. I've witnessed a recurring pattern throughout my life – the moments that feel insurmountable often precede significant growth, leading to a greater sense of inner peace. This song, "One Life," serves as a reminder to persevere through the toughest of times, to commit wholeheartedly, and to trust the process. When we listen to our intuition, our innermost self will always guide us in the right direction. Learning to listen to and trust my intuition has been a lifelong journey. I have dealt with seasons of severe depression and anxiety. There were stretches of time when I felt completely paralyzed, overwhelmed, and detached from my core self. With each life experience, I practiced noticing my intuition. Slowly but surely, I began to develop an actual connection to my intuition. My depression started to lessen in length and intensity as I listened more closely to the voice within myself. I could finally trust my emotions, in fact, my core self was strong. 

“One Life” is an anthem for the moments when emotions run high and the weight of stress feels overwhelming. It urges us to hold on amid chaos because it can be challenging to perceive the broader picture that unfolds just beyond the horizon. As I grow older, the sense that ‘life is short,’ becomes increasingly real. I now set the intention to make the most of each day, of each moment. We all deserve the right to pursue the life of our dreams. I will not let my fears limit me. I will not let my depression or anxiety hold me back. I will listen to my intuition. I will heal. I will transform. I will fly. We will fly.

I recorded all the instruments and vocal layers on my own. My setup is pretty simple: I plug in a USB microphone directly to my laptop, recording and mixing in GarageBand. I am very passionate about composing songs with many layers. For this particular song, I played piano and shakers, and mixed in samples of a thunderstorm to create a surreal atmosphere. In addition, the song artwork paired with the track is an original drawing that I drew using my iPad and Procreate software.

Description:
Each of us is on our own unique journey living and growing up in the strange world we all find ourselves in. We start out as children freely experiencing the world with wonder and no labels, but we tend to build our own cages from labels and definitions of ourselves that we subconsciously let slip into our mind while navigating the structures and patterns of society. Great Time To Be Human asks us to question everything we think we know in hopes of getting back to the childlike wonder in each moment and learning to trust our own internal compass. 

Our internal and external worlds have been shifting, but it truly is a great time to be human

Navigating the path of a musician or artist is asking to embarking on a challenging and unpredictable journey, riddled with various adversities that test one's resilience and passion. Here's a metaphorical glimpse into the hurdles we often face:

The aspiring musician or artist sets sail in a fragile vessel, their dreams and aspirations unfurling like sails in the wind. However, the tides of uncertainty and competition are fierce, creating waves of self-doubt and industry challenges that threaten to capsize their artistic voyage.

The first wave, aptly named "Financial Rapids," crashes against the boat. Limited resources and the high cost of equipment, studio time, and promotional efforts can feel like a relentless current, requiring artists to navigate carefully to avoid drowning in financial woes.

As they sail farther, the fog of "Recognition Obscurity" blankets the horizon. Breaking through this mist is a formidable task, with countless talented artists vying for attention in a sea of anonymity. It becomes a struggle to emerge as a distinct voice, desperately trying to be noticed amidst the cacophony of the creative realm.

The storm of "Creative Blockades" looms ahead, thundering with self-doubt, artistic blocks, and the pressure to conform to trends. Artists battle against the gusts of conformity, attempting to stay true to their unique sound and vision, fearing that their creativity might be swept away by the storm.

In the heart of the journey lies the whirlpool of "Industry Challenges," a maelstrom where artists must contend with complex contracts, exploitation, and the elusive pursuit of fair compensation. The risk of being swallowed by the currents of exploitation is ever-present, demanding a delicate dance to navigate the turbulent waters of the music industry.

Yet, despite the tempests and turbulent waters, artists persist. They adjust their sails, weather the storms, and find inspiration in the moonlit calm between challenges. The journey, though arduous, is a testament to their unwavering dedication and passion, steering their artistic vessels toward the distant shores of recognition, accomplishment, and the fulfillment of their creative destiny.

Description:
Brooke and I met up one day to make music and she had been ruminating on cold showers. It's noble to do the right thing even when it sucks, avoiding temptation and pushing past distractions. Cold showers are great in theory, but what if they don't really give you what you need? What if the healthy thing bores you to death, strips away any sense of risk and adventure?

We tried to draw that parallel to relationships in this indie DnB / stutter ukg crossover. That toxic relationship is wrong for you - but it feels so right. Practice moderation in moderation. Let the intrusive thoughts win for once. It's only human to lean in to the dark side once in a while and toss the angel on your shoulder.

This song was recorded in a single live take amongst the incredible acoustics of Clyde Hall, South London. 'Life Song' will be the final track on Belle Mt.'s debut album 'Mean World Syndrome' coming January 26th 2024 and this unique performance of the song captures all of the magic and raw emotional power behind it's meaning. Performed by Matt from Belle Mt. with Anna Pancaldi on powerful harmonies & Ben from Belle Mt. on atmospheric ebow.

------------------

Belle Mt. are a 3-piece indie Alt-Pop band from the UK fronted by Singer and Songwriter Matt Belmont, with Ben Worsley on Lead Guitar and Chris Burgess on Drums. Their cinematic, ethereal but driven sound is rooted in deeply crafted insightful lyrics and infectious melodies. They have amassed a devoted fanbase with over 60 million streams across platforms since their debut EP self-release in March 2018, receiving top tier play-listing across platforms including on New Music Friday in multiple countries and two top 40 US alt radio releases (Hollow in 2020 and Famous Son 2021). They were signed to Warner Records LA in February 2020 and went fully independent in February 2022. 

Their most recent live shows include a sold out London headline show at The Courtyard Theatre in April 2023 and UK tour supports for RAG’N’BONE MAN, KALEO, LARKINS & JUANES in 2022 (with sell out shows at London’s Hammersmith Apollo and Shepherds Bush Empire). In 2019 they created a huge buzz on the new music showcase festival circuit playing packed out slots at SxSW, Eurosonic Festival and Reeperbahn festival. 
Returning with an evolved sound; Belle Mt. have been collecting serious momentum and attest that their Charlie Andrew produced upcoming debut album ‘Mean World Syndrome’ constitutes a watershed moment, their best work yet.


Anna Pancaldi; an enchanting and noteworthy London-based singer-songwriter influenced by the likes of Joni Mitchell, Carole King and proves a rare talent and an artist to remember through her wondrous vocals and thought-provoking songbook. Anna’s exquisite latest musical offerings are effortlessly honest, touchingly relatable and is a performer known for her deeply affecting live performances. 

After a sold-out London headline show at Folklore in May 2023 after the release of her rousing new single, Where Do I Lay All the Love I Have Left, Anna then released her anthemic single, Stay This Way, in September with more songs to follow shortly. Anna embarks on a full headline UK tour, including another sold-out headline show at London’s The Waiting Room on October 20th.

2024 marks a poignant new epoch for Anna having musically remerged from her chrysalis with her most inspired music yet and a pivotal turning point in her career. 

With an impressive catalogue of music placements in film and TV including the globally acclaimed Grey's Anatomy trailer, Focus Feature film, Every Body, Pretty Little Liars, Love Is Blind, Famous in Love, Paramount film, The In Between and has featured in and soundtracked an adrenaline filled Levi's campaign. 

With three Top Ten's in the singer-songwriter iTunes charts, Anna has gone on to captivate audiences headlining across the UK, Europe and the US. Headlining shows in NYC, LA, Chicago, and Nashville. Anna has captured audiences with TV appearances on CBS LA and London Live and toured the world opening for heavyweight artists such as David Ryan Harris (John Mayer's guitarist), Jake Isaac and Fatai. 

Gaining momentum and traction with nod of approval from print and online press, radio and editorial playlists. Anna’s music has been featured in Spotify playlists giants such as New Music Friday, Easy, Most Beautiful Songs in the World as well as receiving support from the legendary BBC on shows such as BBC Radio 1, 2, 6 and BBC Introducing in London and Essex. 

"Anna Pancaldi has long been in possession of a voice that reaches for emotional highs and swoops into emotional lows with equal intensity. the raw beauty of that voice shines through like never before." - The Line of Best Fit

Description:
Where do I even start....probably with the truth. Someone Else is a story about how time can change people. I was in a relationship with someone for a decade and in a matter of months, in the end, she completely turned into this version of herself that I knew deep down was not true to her spirit.

It's hard trying to be there for someone when you see them making decisions that not only impact themselves but, people around that care deeply for them. In this case, it was new friends that had a certain lifestyle and she wanted to be a part of that. A rift grew between us after a while that wasn't able to be mended. It's sad and unfortunate but that's life. All we can ever do is our best and hope that the universe is removing things that aren't meant for us and that there's a bigger reason for it.

Description:
Listening to the track "A Walk in the Park" from my upcoming EP titled "Elements of Life", transports me into a deep awareness of the present moment and to cherish the privilege I have in life. 

I'd started creating this track by curating pieces from my memories of long walks with my brother around the city of Bangalore during the first Covid lockdown in 2020, wherein the streets that were once bustling with people, had transformed into avenues of introspection into the harsh reality of life being so fragile. 

The ethereal soundscapes, echoes, and delays in the track create a mesmerizing aura of peace and reflection. Soft bell rhythms intertwine with slow-paced beats, offering a respite from the non-stop chatter within our busy minds that most of us tend to nourish with hope for a better future.

A few years ago, I went through a breakup which marked the end a six-year relationship with my ex. I was emotionally devastated... and was by no means looking to meet someone new. About 3 months later, I met my now girlfriend and we hit it off. I felt myself falling in love with her and wasn't sure if I was ready for that. I was Nervous that I'd end up getting my heartbroken once again, but ultimately took the leap of faith. I decided that a chance at true love is worth all the risk in the world.. and thankfully I was right. This inspired "Nervous". 
My girlfriend and I have been happily together ever since and this song has become a sort of anthem for us. Although this song is extremely personal to me, it's message is universal. This song is for anyone who has been Nervous to allow themselves to be vulnerable again after getting their heartbroken.

"Party (Like It's 1999)" was created by Merv xx Gotti's hip-hop/R&B boyband project, Samurai Champs, in collaboration with Canadian rapper, Jeah. The single is an ode to the '90s and the golden era of hip-hop, as well as to their Southeast Asian heritage and the communities who raised them.

Upon release, the single was playlisted on JASMINE, Spotify's official editorial playlist highlighting emerging Asian artists. The official music video for "Party" features other Asian-Canadian artists from Western Canada's Filipino, Vietnamese, and Cambodian communities and can be watched here: https://youtu.be/rNiouD79wY8

Samurai Champs has been featured in press outlets such as CBC Canada, VICE Noisey, and HipHopCanada. They have been playlisted on Spotify’s official Just Vibing, Jasmine, & Fresh Finds playlists and have garnered well over 100,000 streams.

Having toured internationally, Samurai Champs have performed at festivals such as SXSW (Austin, TX), NXNE (Toronto, ON), Music Matters Live (Singapore), Reeperbahn (Hamburg, GE), The Great Escape (Brighton, UK), Tallinn Music Week (Tallinn, Estonia), Upstream Music Fest (Seattle, WA), Sound City (Liverpool, UK), BreakOut West (Edmonton, AB), and many more.

Leading up to their JUNOfest performance, Samurai Champs were featured in CBC Music’s "Samurai Champs: Meet the Wild, New Hip-Hop Group Revolutionizing Saskatchewan Music." This was the first installment in CBC Music’s “Beyond the 6,” an online editorial series highlighting Canada’s most notable hip-hop artists creating communities around Canada.

Samurai Champs have also won numerous awards and honors, including multiple nominations for Western Canadian Music Awards’ Hip Hop & R&B Artist of the Year, TD Bank’s Creative Entrepreneur Incubator, and winning Hip-Hop Artist of the Year in SaskMusic’s Saskatchewan Music Awards.

Jiujitsu is the first single from Merv xx Gotti's upcoming 2024 6-song EP, "Guitar Songs." To date, the single has garnered over 34,000 streams on Spotify, been playlisted on numerous influencer playlists, and was picked by CBC, Canada's national public radio and television broadcaster, on 21 separate radio shows—the largest syndication pickup by a Western Canadian artist in 5 years.

Jiujitsu was written in LA and Singapore during a time of deep internal struggle, serving as a metaphor for one's own grappling with their multiple "selves." 

The song was created minimally, featuring only Merv xx Gotti's androgynous vocals, a single travel guitar, and a lead guitar recorded through an analog tape player. Underneath the primary layers of the song, the single features ambient work by acclaimed ambient & jazz artist Michael Scott Dawson.

Jiujitsu garnered critical industry acclaim, earning Merv xx Gotti’s first festival performance, as well as debut performances in LA, Toronto, and New York City in the same year of its release. Jiujitsu speaks to the internal struggles we all face, particularly through the trying times of unprecedented change that the world has experienced in the past 3 years.

Album "Meridian 68" is a unique album by the Polish-Ukrainian band Dagadana, which combines four cultures: Polish, Ukrainian, Mongolian, and Chinese. On the album, the group turns to fresh interpretations of timeless folk music pieces, which sound like a unique fusion of genres, mixing jazz, ethno, and electronics.

The album includes traditional songs from various regions of Poland, Ukrainian and Lemko folk songs, Mongolian poetry that can be heard here, as well as one unique song recorded in Chinese together with the Mongolian-Chinese band North Lab. "Meridian 68" was nominated for the "Fryderyk" award in the Album of the Year: Roots Music category.

Dagadana band has been brilliantly combining elements ofUkrainian and Polish culture through jazz, electronica or world music for fifteen years. It was founded in 2008 by Daga Gregorowicz (Poland) and Dana Vynnytska (Ukraine). Today, Dagadana is already a quartet, sometimes expanding to include a brass section and even a symphony orchestra. Dagadana was the only band from Poland and Ukraine to play at one of the world's biggest music festivals in 2019 - thelegendary Glastonbury Festival in the UK. Among others, theAmerican National Geographic wrote about it. The group hastoured in more than 30 countries, including the largest festivalin South America and a number of tours in China. Dagadana hasso far played on a raft, in a mine and even in the desert.

Description:
In early 2023, I embarked on an ambitious journey with my major project, Krash World, aiming to create an astounding 1,000 songs. This endeavor was not just a test of creativity but also a testament to my commitment to exploring the depths of music production. After six months of relentless work, layering vocals and honing production techniques, I found myself with enough material to surpass my initial goal. However, amidst this plethora of creations, I realized that quantity couldn't compensate for the essence and soul I sought in my music. Most of the tracks didn't resonate with the vision I had for Krash World, leading to a rigorous selection process. Despite this, a few songs distinctly stood out, embodying the spirit of what I had set out to achieve, though it was not ultimately chosen to be included in Krash World. 

This particular track, with its unique blend of punk and hip-hop elements, explores themes of fear, regret, getting lost and falling down a hole you don't know how you're going to get out of. This song feels like falling down a deep hole and grasping. to no avail, for solid ground. I wrote this song purely from a journalistic stand point at the time and chose to have a bit of fun yelling out my feelings dramatically. Sometimes you just need to scream! hehe

In creating this song, I poured my heart and soul into not only writing and recording but also engineering it myself. 

The cover art, crafted with the innovative Dall E, visually encapsulates the song's themes, mirroring the intensity and emotional depth of the track. 

This song, though not part of Krash World, stands as a powerful piece in its own right. It's a reflection of my artistic journey and evolution, and a reminder that sometimes, the paths not taken can lead to unexpected, resonant creations that connect with people in profound ways.

This is from the same color (red) as my previous single "AIN'T NO PEACE" and features a new take on the same production.

As the tension builds, the drums morph into a relentless breakbeat, before the track erupts into an unforgettable drop that'll leave you breathless. This tech-funk fueled banger is pure sonic adrenaline, guaranteed to ignite any dance floor.
Stand with your bro, through highs and lows, facing whatever life throws.

Dive into the intense and raw world of "Dead People," a track that delves deep into the struggles of sharing personal space, coping with emotional stress, and confronting the demons of life. This song is not just a melody, but a journey through the complexities of human emotions and the harsh realities of existence. The lyrics paint a vivid picture of internal battles, societal pressures, and the feeling of being surrounded by lifelessness even in a crowd.

Lyric Highlight:
The song kicks off with a powerful line, "Fuck my bitch then go to sleep, but I hate sharing my bed," setting the tone for a raw and unfiltered narrative. The chorus, "I see people but they dead," echoes the theme of disconnection and the paradox of feeling alone in a bustling world. The artist's struggle with caring too much despite a hardened exterior is explored in lines like, "I tell myself that I don’t care, but I be caring way too much."

🌟 About the Artist:
This track showcases the Kamre Haze’s talent for storytelling and his ability to transform personal experiences into relatable art. His journey, marked by resilience and self-awareness, reflects in his music, offering listeners a mix of vulnerability and strength.

dreams(act i) is my 9th drop on sound.xyz and the first release from "untitled iii" a multistory ep produced in collaboration with Philly legendary producer and songwriter, HEZEKIAH (founder of Beat Society, Johnny Popcorn) 

The two of us met while celebrating 50 years of hip-hop in VA late summer 2023. The headliners were DEAD PREZ, the G.O.A.T.S. iykyk, who closed their set showing love to all and intentionally giving me my flowers, not as the only woman emcee on the bill, but solely because of my gifts and handling of this craft. Wow, full circle moment to be witnessed and affirmed by true giants like blueprints for the culture for real. Shortly after that moment, I could hear the opening lyrics of this song ringing out over the sound of the festival's closing. "Reaching for the highest heights of my highest destiny and whats more, days later, HEZEKIAH sent me a pack! The "untitled iii" collaborative project was born. 

Over the course of the first quarter of 2024 we will release music in three acts, three mediums of sharing story as creators. The first is dreams (act i) a music visual & song that reflects on what it's like to navigate the industry as a woman, as an independent artist, as well as a creative legacy, and the walls artists hit sometimes when seeking to have their creations valued. This year as an artist in residence at the New Orleans Museum of Art I am continuing to actualize my belief that music is fine art for all, and that hip-hop/rap is this generation's true authentic American art form (more on that later). This year is for the dreamers. Cover art by Supermit! a collector evolved into collaborator. 

stay connected as we share more of our dreams, nightmares (act ii), and invite you into new worlds (act iii) this year. 

may the inspired stay inspired, 

<3 CHARM

The song tells a story of a person in Kuala Lumpur who desires a sophisticated lifestyle and seeks a partner who can provide materialistic gifts rather than someone involved in music. The lyrics express a sense of longing and dissatisfaction, as well as the feeling of being misunderstood and not fitting in. The protagonist reflects on past experiences and the changes in their life, expressing a desire to move on. The song conveys themes of materialism, longing, and societal expectations.

Released under the artists moniker of SLATAN on digital streaming platforms, this project
consists of participation from a total of 19 artists (12 singers/rappers and 7 composers) with names like Gard, Quai, Offgrid and Wuzgut which names are no stranger to the label roster as well as a couple of up-and-coming composers like cyndaquil, Dafreakinaz, henrii,
Khodi, LastKhalif and many more.

The album cover art is a visual representation of their idea of blossoming, growing and
contributing to a greater cause rather than just personal motives. The label decided to
commission a painter based at Central Market, Kuala Lumpur (MY) to visualise the artists references as a form of support to the oil-paint artists in this digital era.

In early 2023, I embarked on an ambitious journey with my major project, Krash World, aiming to create an astounding 1,000 songs. This endeavor was not just a test of creativity but also a testament to my commitment to exploring the depths of music production. After six months of relentless work, layering vocals and honing production techniques, I found myself with enough material to surpass my initial goal. However, amidst this plethora of creations, I realized that quantity couldn't compensate for the essence and soul I sought in my music. Most of the tracks didn't resonate with the vision I had for Krash World, leading to a rigorous selection process. Despite this, one song distinctly stood out, embodying the spirit of what I had set out to achieve, though it was not ultimately chosen for Krash World. 

This particular track, with its unique blend of punk and hip-hop elements, delves into themes of violence, anger, and socioeconomic inequality – issues that are profoundly relevant in our current times.

In creating this song, I poured my heart and soul into not only writing and recording but also engineering it myself. To bring the final touches to life, I utilized Songmastr AI for mastering, taking inspiration from Green Day's iconic 'American Idiot' to capture the raw energy and rebellious spirit of punk, while infusing it with the rhythmic complexity of hip-hop. 

The cover art, crafted with the innovative Dall E, visually encapsulates the song's themes, mirroring the intensity and emotional depth of the track. 

This song, though not part of Krash World, stands as a powerful piece in its own right. It's a reflection of my artistic journey and evolution, and a reminder that sometimes, the paths not taken can lead to unexpected, resonant creations that connect with people in profound ways.

Over the past 10 years, us brothers have been through a tough joint family separation and an emotional turmoil moving away from Jamshedpur - our hometown and permanent residence in a small industrial town in East India. Music has been an integral part of our healing from these wounds and has given us hope in times of despair. We spent a significant time curating music for our DJ sets, warming up the dancefloor for headliner DJs at club gigs and sharing our emotions as expressions in our curation.
The encouragement and support we've received from old friends who've attended our gigs, and new friends we made on the dancefloor, has been our guiding light in this journey.

This track was co-produced by a very dear friend of ours - Sandeep Chowta, who's a veteran in the music circuit in the Indian subcontinent and beyond. He's been a great pillar of support for us brothers. Sandeep runs an independent collective called Namma Music and has released over 40 albums in the past 3 years, which y'all must check out :)

After several years as a DJ in pubs and parties in my city, and with the recent global pandemic, including lockdown in house, I had the wonderful idea of downloading the trial version of FL Studio. After watching some videos on music theory, I ventured into creating my first song (if you could call it that), and after several hours of tinkering, it turned out like this.

Obviously, the song has as much artistic value as a slice of bologna, but as I believe that sharing your work is always valid, whether it's of quality or not, I uploaded it to a platform, and within a few hours, a stranger paid $1 for the song. This event sparked in me a crazy desire to learn to create more and better music, to the point of becoming somewhat obsessive.

So there's the (personal) value of this song. I upload it just as I left it in 2021.

I take this opportunity to thank my over 1000 collectors and more than 2000 followers. Together we grow!

Pretty Traumatized is my origin story. It's the first record I've written about everything I've been through medically. It's not a coincidence that it's the happiest sounding song I've released, with the darkest subject matter. I wanted to bring a fantasy element to the horrible things I went through. This song is at the root of my escapism approach to music. It helped me establish my superpower of creating these fantasies to save myself.

By Borja Moskv

Earlier this year, I was in a dark place and contemplating life choices, experiencing regret, you name it; I had a lot going on, and to be honest, as I write this, I still find myself fighting the urge to return to my dark place and let the chips fall where they may.

But one day, I was journaling after therapy and randomly wrote, "Every dent has its own charm, but I’m not made out of glass..."
"I’m not made out of glass..." I kept repeating it over and over again. As I kept saying it, the better I felt. Through the tears, "I’m not made out of glass..." I kept repeating it until I believed it.

To anyone who feels that life is getting too heavy or something seems too hard to bear, remember you aren't made of glass and won't break, even if it feels like you might.

𝑯𝒐𝒔𝒕: "Welcome, music enthusiasts, to the exclusive behind-the-music scoop on the quirky and uproarious track, "FROGSMAS VS. X-MAS" by the dynamic duo DCoop and Patty Mack! This satirical masterpiece dives headfirst into the wild world of Web3, NFTs, and the contrasting chaos of Christmas versus the blissful mayhem of Frogsmas. Let's peel back the layers and get the lowdown on this musical rollercoaster."

𝑫𝑪𝒐𝒐𝒑: You know, when Patty and I set out to write this song, we wanted to capture the absolute madness of the Web3 space during the holiday season. It's like the crypto winter wonderland meets a blockchain nightmare.

𝑷𝒂𝒕𝒕𝒚 𝑴𝒂𝒄𝒌: Absolutely, DCoop! We started with those hilarious grievances – a doxxed team MIA, a roadmap with less utility than a snowflake in July, and let's not forget the PFP without a community. Classic Web3 stuff, right?

𝑯𝒐𝒔𝒕: Classic indeed! But then the song takes a turn towards Frogsmas. What's the deal with that?

𝑫𝑪𝒐𝒐𝒑: Ah, Frogsmas, the antidote to the Web3 chaos. We stumbled upon this gem of a project, The Plague of Frogs, providing decentralized opportunity in the midst of all the madness. And what better way to express that than through a catchy, holiday-themed tune?

𝑷𝒂𝒕𝒕𝒚 𝑴𝒂𝒄𝒌: And let's not forget the Frogsmas gifts! Chompies for fixing your teeth, Swamp Water sweet and Hoppy, a Henhouse with $EGG, and the list goes on. We wanted to create a whimsical world where even Moark becomes the Plague MVP.

𝑯𝒐𝒔𝒕: Moark as the MVP? That's a twist! What inspired that?

𝑫𝑪𝒐𝒐𝒑: Well, Moark is just this charismatic figure in the Frogsmas universe, leading the charge against Web3 chaos. He's like the Santa Claus of decentralized opportunities, and who wouldn't want him as the Most Valuable Plague? I mean who is this Pons ETH guy anyways?

𝑷𝒂𝒕𝒕𝒚 𝑴𝒂𝒄𝒌: And, of course, we threw in a nod to Wenswap and Making Coffee, because what's Frogsmas without a bit of caffeinated joy? 

𝑯𝒐𝒔𝒕: True that! And the finale, a Hikeshi Japanese tee? Tell us about that!

𝑫𝑪𝒐𝒐𝒑: It's all about embracing the unique and eclectic, just like Frogsmas itself. The Hikeshi Japanese tee is like the grand finale gift, a symbol of individuality and style in the midst of this crazy Frogsmas celebration. PS !WEN

𝑷𝒂𝒕𝒕𝒚 𝑴𝒂𝒄𝒌: And there you have it, folks! "FROGSMAS VS. X-MAS" – a musical journey through the ups and downs of Web3 and the enchanting world of The Plague of Frogs. We hope it brings a smile to your face and a hop to your step this holiday season!

𝑯𝒐𝒔𝒕: Well, there you have it, the inside scoop on a tune that's as catchy as it is comedic. "FROGSMAS VS. X-MAS" – a festive anthem for the crypto enthusiasts and frog lovers alike!

I wrote "Airport Beer" for a friend, wishing I could be there with her in the airport as she flew across the country to bury a loved one. I return to it often when attempting to process loss.

Felt like time to put it out since the holidays can be a difficult time for many, and with such unimaginable grief in the world today.

To every beautiful friend who's held me close when I needed comfort, 

To every hurting soul who needs comfort now, 

This one's for you. 

Xx
Wallace

50% of the proceeds will be donated to the PCRF (providing medical and humanitarian aid to youth in Gaza) and the Trans Santa mutual aid (supporting trans youth in need)

Artist and designer Kathleen Warner, who performs under the moniker Lyrah, breathes new life into a classic on her irresistible new track “Everywhere” – track eleven on HIGH FREQUENCY Volume 2.  Written by the late Christine MvCie and originally released in 1987 on Fleetwood Mac’s 14th studio album Tango in the Night, “Everywhere” lends itself perfectly to Lyrah’s dance-focused sound and show stopping vocals. 

Drenched in reverb, adding an otherworldly, cavernous quality to the immediately recognizable 80s’ synth intro, Lyrah’s topline dances across a lush chord progression and the pulse of a heavy kick drum while angelic harmonies fill the track with celestial choir of her own making.

Prompted by a request  to cut vocals for a version of the song a friend’s label was planning to release, Lyrah recorded the vocals while in London this summer.  After learning the label had gone in a different direction, Lyrah found herself returning to the song’s potential. “Anytime I was on the train commuting to sessions in London I was working on it and on the flight home. I didn't know if I'd put it out, I just wanted to see it through and make the version of the song that I heard in my head. The immediate thing was different chords. And because my background's piano, that's what I normally start with. The chord shapes the world of the emotion, and I wanted to hear a little bit darker of a twist on it. Then I was like, “I love the song. I should probably put it out.”

-----

Album "Meridian 68" is a unique album by the Polish-Ukrainian band Dagadana, which combines four cultures: Polish, Ukrainian, Mongolian, and Chinese. On the album, the group turns to fresh interpretations of timeless folk music pieces, which sound like a unique fusion of genres, mixing jazz, ethno, and electronics.

The album includes traditional songs from various regions of Poland, Ukrainian and Lemko folk songs, Mongolian poetry that can be heard here, as well as one unique song recorded in Chinese together with the Mongolian-Chinese band North Lab. "Meridian 68" was nominated for the "Fryderyk" award in the Album of the Year: Roots Music category.

Dagadana band has been brilliantly combining elements ofUkrainian and Polish culture through jazz, electronica or world music for fifteen years. It was founded in 2008 by Daga Gregorowicz (Poland) and Dana Vynnytska (Ukraine). Today, Dagadana is already a quartet, sometimes expanding to include a brass section and even a symphony orchestra. Dagadana was the only band from Poland and Ukraine to play at one of the world's biggest music festivals in 2019 - thelegendary Glastonbury Festival in the UK. Among others, theAmerican National Geographic wrote about it. The group hastoured in more than 30 countries, including the largest festivalin South America and a number of tours in China. Dagadana hasso far played on a raft, in a mine and even in the desert.

Description: I started writing this song back in 2018 with the intro guitar melody. I kinda played around with the guitar pattern for a few years trying to understand what the song was making me feel. After a break up the song really made sense. It was the idea of willingly waiting around for someone to be better for you or even yourself being better for someone else, because all you ever wanted was that person and no one else. Sometimes though, the desire to be better will never be enough for either individuals and accepting the reality that action for change is the only truth to definite love.

A tree growing inside a dark square is chosen as the cover for a new music track - as a metaphor for inner creative energy breaking through limiting conditions and circumstances. Just as a fragile tree sapling can burst into the light even through asphalt, human imagination and creativity can thrive even in seemingly harsh and barren conditions of the surrounding reality.

This image shows us the creative power of growth and development residing within every person, able to overcome those obstacles imposed by societal norms, conformism, fears and anxieties.

With my music, I sought to convey the artist’s zeal to pursue his dream. The zeal allowing to break all barriers in the way, to overcome moments of decline, difficulties and lulls. And then - to fight those limitations again for the sake of achieving the dream.
The end of summer: a bittersweet transition marked by fading warmth, lingering memories, and the anticipation of change.

With strange times behind us and don't know what to expect in the near future, it felt as the right thing to record the first three Gnossiennes by Erik Satie.

The world is balancing on the edge. Whether we should go left or right. What is right, what is wrong? As I see it, these extraordinary pieces balance along. Strange but beautiful, minimalistic but rich, sad but optimistic in a way.

This was recorded at a time in my life when so much was uncertain. I had just lost my job, and my wife, Olivia was due to have our baby soon. Our security felt threatened, and we didn't know what the future held. I wanted to play something that would wrap Olivia up in a warm wash of sound and serenity, a musical cocoon amidst the tumultuous winds of change.

The instruments this song was played on are called RAV Vast. I combined a G Pygmy and an A Integral RAV Vast to create a more complete scale recorded with two microphones to make an immersive stereo recording. I played with mallets to bring out an especially calm and beautiful tone from the instruments.

"Snowbird" transcends being merely a composition; it's a soulful lament dedicated to Whiplash Ash's lost love, referred to by the same poignant moniker. The melancholic strums of the guitar resonate with the longing of her heart, each chord a tender call to the one who flew away from her life, leaving behind a trail of cherished memories and unspoken promises. The music ebbs and flows with a wistful grace, capturing the solitude of her days and the chill of the absence she feels in the night's quiet. Yet, within its somber melody, there's a delicate hope, a whispering wish for her snowbird to return with the spring, to rekindle the warmth that once filled her world. It's this blend of yearning and love, etched deeply into the song's essence, that makes "Snowbird" an elegy to lost love and a testament to the enduring hope that love leaves in its wake.

Learn more about Whiplash Ashes' story in Train of the Century, a railroad tycoon game on the Wax Blockchain.

Delving into the creative process behind the birth of a Christmas song has always fascinated me. There's something extraordinary about the way this season encapsulates a diverse range of emotions—be it the somber, the melancholic, the fiery, or the jubilant. Often, these contrasting sentiments seamlessly coexist within a single composition.

As I embarked on crafting "Christmastime," I drew inspiration from a verse tucked away in a yet-to-be-released song, a fragment from a time when I navigated the depths of a profound darkness. The words echoed, "searching through these snowy streets for some kind of miracle." In that moment, I realized that the quest for a miracle is a universal experience, transcending religious, creed, or societal boundaries. It's a sentiment we've all encountered—a yearning so intense that only a miraculous intervention could rescue us.

My creative journey involves a continuous exploration for those subtle miracles that serve as poignant reminders of a time when I reveled in awe and wonder. I believe we could all benefit from seeking out these small wonders, rekindling the enchantment that resides within us. My earnest wish is that this song resonates with you, meeting you exactly where you are. May it reignite the magic of being surrounded by loved ones and evoke memories of those who, though absent, have profoundly impacted our lives. Merry Christmas!

“Can We" is a healing track that I made in reaction to the crazy events that occurred in the summer of 2020. I was stuck at home with my parents in quarantine at the time, and learned about the tragic death of George Floyd. I felt powerless and hopeless about the world and the hatred that was dividing us as a species. I sat down that day to make something that would soothe the pain and anxiety I was feeling; a sort of plea to the world for love to triumph over hate. It represents what I love about music as a whole; the ability to heal wounds and make the tough times a little bit better.

This song was written and recorded by myself over a many month period.The original demo was recorded in one night but it took many more to complete it. I feel like the chords and melody have that tension of the sentiment of the song.

It was a Sunday afternoon in early fall during the pandemic. I’d left NYC to stay at a wildlife refuge in Delaware, and my bedroom / makeshift studio window faced an expansive marsh on a wildlife refuge.

I was working on writing a new album. Instead of being attached to any one particular song, I started approaching the process in a more zen-like way, just showing up for the work and being open to what would come.

I was putting the pieces together after leaving a bad relationship and processing the awakening to the depths of hard personal struggles.

As the sun reflected off the marsh water, bits and pieces of the beat, bass, melodies, and chord progressions started to fall into place.

Imagine manipulated vocals and fx playing around like ear candy, mixing it up with jazzy chords and beats inspired by UK garage, all leading to this open-beat Jersey bass party. It's a whole mood—melodic, groovy, and simply good times.

This song flowed into being quickly like a glimmer of light, a voice calling out that it’s time to step into your future self. 

"I know the answer's in your eyes. I feel the beating of the truth."

Mad love,

x Alarke

I have always loved Christmas music. Songs such as "White Christmas" and "Let it Snow" paint beautiful pictures of snowy days that are so commonly referred to in Christmas narratives. Jimmy Buffett's version has been played in my house for as long as I can remember and after his recent passing I wanted to pay tribute with my own take on it.

An outtake from his cornerstone project Raver Realm, “Asleep at the Switch” showcases the heavier, trap-influenced side of Jadyn’s musical repertoire. “I've made over 100 songs during the last year to get the final nine for the Raver Realm project, and “Asleep at the Switch”  was one I made while creating the underground realm – the realm that encompasses that type of music.”

Overtop heavy trap 808s Jadyn approaches the beat with confidence finding a grungy flow amid the experimental soundscape. Resulting in what he aptly calls a “heavy mosh pit vibe,” “Asleep at the Switch” is a departure from Jadyn’s more pop focused material, shifting the focus to one of his first musical infatuations. “It’s a heavy trap song, which is kind of the foundation of my music career. That's how I got into the love of making music, and I was like, “Man, I need to stop trying to cater towards what other people will like and just put out something that I like, because that's what matters the most,” says Jadyn. “It was very fun making it. I made it in New York with a couple of friends. They were just getting lit, jumping up and down in the studio. And I was just really just going crazy on the song–heavy trap drums, 808s–and it's a vibe.”

"Hasselhoffmaskoff" by Awesomeisjayell is a musical narrative that immerses listeners in a realm of uncertainty, where the ticking clock of time threatens to unveil concealed realities. The track weaves a tale of revelation and self-discovery, as the artist, Awesomeisjayell, confronts the impending disclosure of profound truths.

As the song unfolds, the heartbeat of Awesomeisjayell reverberates through the rhythmic pulse of the drums, creating an intense and immersive sonic experience. The drums play out like the pounding of a heart, symbolizing the artist's inner journey and the emotional intensity of embracing one's ultimate truth.

The lyrics paint a vivid picture of a time when facades crumble, and authenticity takes center stage. Album "Meridian 68" is a unique album by the Polish-Ukrainian band Dagadana, which combines four cultures: Polish, Ukrainian, Mongolian, and Chinese. On the album, the group turns to fresh interpretations of timeless folk music pieces, which sound like a unique fusion of genres, mixing jazz, ethno, and electronics.

The album includes traditional songs from various regions of Poland, Ukrainian and Lemko folk songs, Mongolian poetry that can be heard here, as well as one unique song recorded in Chinese together with the Mongolian-Chinese band North Lab. "Meridian 68" was nominated for the "Fryderyk" award in the Album of the Year: Roots Music category.



Dagadana band has been brilliantly combining elements ofUkrainian and Polish culture through jazz, electronica or world music for fifteen years. It was founded in 2008 by Daga Gregorowicz (Poland) and Dana Vynnytska (Ukraine). Today, Dagadana is already a quartet, sometimes expanding to include a brass section and even a symphony orchestra. Dagadana was the only band from Poland and Ukraine to play at one of the world's biggest music festivals in 2019 - thelegendary Glastonbury Festival in the UK. Among others, theAmerican National Geographic wrote about it. The group hastoured in more than 30 countries, including the largest festivalin South America and a number of tours in China. Dagadana hasso far played on a raft, in a mine and even in the desert.

Description:
Damn...this song is so fresh that it still hurts when I listen to it. 
-----.......

I don't usually put out songs so soon after recording (4 days ago in Paris) them because it's my personal preference, but I'm making an exception for the OP contest that I'm submitting to. 
-----.......

I was inspired to step out of my comfort zone...and let me tell you..I'm very uncomfortable.
-----.......

Something I know about myself is that I'm very chronological lol. My mind almost NEEDS to work in order. Of course I've been challenging this part of myself for many years haha, it's a daily practice. 
-----.......

Especially when It comes to my music, I am very much like this. I have a few songs I've recorded before this one and I almost feel like I'm doing them wrong by releasing this one first 😂
-----.......

BUT FUCKKK IT! 
-----.......

this is a very telling song of where I have been in my human experience as of late. I have been on a solo journey for over a month now. I traveled all the way up through Italy and am currently submitting this in a cafe in London,England. 

I didn't realize why I needed to have this journey when I started, I just knew I had to do it.

"I thought I was enough for us" is literally me realizing that I am not the only person who's responsible for making life "right". I've always had this feeling of needing to help someone or feeling like someone needed my help. Of course, through my travels, I have unmasked the true foundation of this feeling. In part, it's a trauma response to being rejected by my father and having my innocence taken away from me at a young age.

This trauma caused a co-dependent mentality to grow, feeling like I needed to be needed in order to have importance or value. 

I can't even explain how much this realization has given me clarity on all the questions I've had in regards to the people that have been in my life or the type of relationships I've harbored (or have been unable to harbor). 

I stepped into these travels with a deep desire to finally get a full understanding of why I couldn't be the person I wanted to be in relation to others. Not only have I discovered the root cause, but I now have a direction. 

I am far from "healed" or "complete", but within the laborious work required to get past the dirt, down to the root, I'm coming away with a vigor and strength like I've never had before. 

I am not enough for us, WE are.

Description:
“Relief (Solo),” off Heno.’s upcoming album "I'm Tired Of Being Hypersurveilled," marks a turning point in the poignant narrative of the artist, producer, and innovator’s larger concept project. Accompanied by the RELIEF pixel game where arcade tickets minted on ZORA unlock power ups, “Relief (Solo)” soundtracks Heno.’s character’s pursuit of an escape. “Dealing with a topic like surveillance, there's a lot of nuance, and a lot of ways to go–different topics or subtopics to speak on. But I knew escape, relief or pursuit of being free was a sentiment that needed to be on an album like this,” says Heno. 

Speaking to Heno.’s personal experience as a black man in America–the project’s allegorical storyline was introduced by a three-part short film released last January in which Heno.’s character attends a PTSD Anonymous meeting that turns out to be a ploy for the S.Y.S.T.E.M. (Securing Your Safety Through Extreme Means) to spy on attendees. Eventually, his character is kidnapped (as depicted in the “Neybors” and “SIMMER DOWN” videos) before being thrown into a simulation seen in the interactive RELIEF pixel video game at which point Heno.’s character realizes he must find relief and escape. “This is the point where I recognize I need to get out of the simulation one way or another, even if it means I have to burn the establishment down. I needed to get out. And I wanted to capture the frustration and the feeling of being gaslit while dealing with surveillance and people invalidating your experiences.”

Written, produced, and performed by Heno., “Relief” –the ninth track off HIGH FREQUENCY Volume 2–viscerally captures the feverish and exhausting feeling of being chased. “It started with the production–playing around with different synthesizers, and then I came across certain sounds that sounded like a chase. The beat sounds like I’m running from something, I'm literally trying to get the fuck out of there, and that urgency of being in pursuit.” 

Both futuristic and retro, the industrial nature of the track is perfect for the addictive video game, while simultaneously drawing attention to the very real experience that fueled its creation. “You gotta make this shit make sense for you but for me, freedom from it all (as well as relief) is what I really want.

Collectors of “Relief (Solo) on Sound will receive 1 airdrop for RELIEF arcade tickets on Zora that unlock power ups within Heno.’s RELIEF pixel game, will be added to the allowlist for the song’s upcoming lyric video drop on Zora, and be added to the allowlist for Heno.'s forthcoming album "I'm Tired of Being Hypersurveilled", dropping in January 2024

In the ethereal realm of emotions and experiences, "Half Life" emerges as a poignant melody that weaves the tale of a love suspended in the delicate balance between presence and absence. The song's genesis lies in the aftermath of a profound connection, where the echoes of a past love linger like a haunting melody, refusing to fade away completely. The title, "Half Life," serves as a metaphor for the enduring trace of that once-intense connection—a love that, despite its conclusion, still pulses within the veins of the songwriter.

As the lyrics unfold, they paint a vivid narrative of a soul grappling with the aftermath of love's departure. The phrase "having her still in my system" captures the visceral nature of the emotional residue left behind—a love that has become an intrinsic part of the songwriter's being. The song becomes a musical diary, chronicling the bittersweet journey of navigating life with the indelible imprint of a past love. Each note is a brushstroke, and every lyric is a page turned, revealing the complex layers of emotions that come with holding on to the half-life of a love that once illuminated the heart.

"Yarayım" is a Turkish song that unfolds its emotional narrative through a live performance on classical Spanish guitar and vocals. The song delves into the intricate facets of love, exploring the profound impact it can have, even when accompanied by pain. This heartfelt composition was performed and recorded as part of the live album project titled "Guitarology."
Guitarology is the name of a music album that carries deep feelings and messages related to reality. This Album composed and performed by Omar Alkilani (Syrian artist refugee in Turkey) . This album was able to touch the hearts of many audiences, as the music was able to influence them and they clearly responded to it.
The Guitarology album has been presented on Guitar Live for 5 consecutive Guitarology themed shows.

The birth of "The Chips" was a serendipitous journey, a fusion of individual talents that seamlessly came together to create a masterpiece. Yacoo D.B.H.S, the visionary behind the track, stumbled upon a captivating beat produced by Kamoshun while scouring the internet. 

Downloading the beat, Yacoo found himself inspired to sing a melody, inadvertently drawing from the vibes of a classic N.W.A track. Realizing the potential, he wasted no time and loaded up Protools, crafting the infectious hook that would become the heart of "The Chips." With the foundation laid, Yacoo knew something special was in the making. 

Enter Swendal, the bro with the lyrical prowess. As Yacoo was perfecting the hook, Swendal pulled up to the lab, and the magic unfolded. Sharing the track with Swendal, the response was immediate - "Can I get the first verse on that?" Swendal's earnestness was undeniable, and the collaboration took a new turn. Yacoo, recognizing the synergy, gladly accepted, setting the stage for Swendal's killer opening verse.

Amidst the creative buzz, curiosity struck. "Yō, who made that beat?" Swendal inquired. Upon learning it was Kamoshun, he wasted no time reaching out, and negotiations for the use of the track were swiftly underway. The collaboration was cemented, and the trio was ready to elevate "The Chips" to new heights.

The final piece of the puzzle fell into place when Fatso Loso, the missing ingredient, made his entrance. Catching wind of the track as Yacoo mixed Swendal's vocals, Fatso couldn't help but add his own flavor. Mumbling bars under his breath, Yacoo urged him to speak up, unveiling the gem that would become the second verse.

With all the verses in place, the trio wasted no time. They tracked Fatso Loso's verse, fine-tuned the mix, and unleashed "The Chips" onto all platforms. A visual masterpiece accompanied the release, etching the track into the annals of history. The journey from a chance beat discovery to a collaborative triumph marked a chapter in the musical legacy of Yacoo D.B.H.S, Swendal, and Fatso Loso.

Urban Melancholia is the second studio EP by Sarah Krimson. Through the EP, Sarah narrates how her physical journey to London turned out to be a journey of self-discovery and healing in solitude. The journey of Sarah conveys an important underlying message that home is not always the place where you are born but where your heart is. In London, Sarah found her independence and the courage to pursue a career in music. 

Tracklist:

1. September '15 🚄 (00:00)
'September '15' symbolizes the start of the journey (New Chapter) of Sarah in London. The intro track showcases the sound a person new to London hears when wandering through the big city at night.

2. Urban Melancholia 🌃 (01:23)
'Urban Melancholia’ is a brief autobiography about Sarah’s experience when she first moved to London years ago. Despite the cultural shock, setbacks and lack of support from people around her, Sarah takes the enduring journey in pursuit of her dreams, all alone. 

3. Combo 💊 (04:12)
In pursuit of her dreams, Sarah embarks on a personal journey of self-discovery. ‘Combo’ describes the early stages of Sarah’s career; from trying to find her unique sound to battling her inner demons. Amid the chaos, Sarah temporarily lost herself to fear and self-sabotaging behaviours and found herself back again 5 years later. 

4. Call Me Back 📞 (07:03)
The dreadful thoughts of not being able to return to London reopened the old wounds and deepened her depression and suicidal thoughts in Sarah. 'Call Me Back' is a scream of pain, written in hopes of getting the attention of someone else who can come and save her while she wallows in pain. But that someone else will never 'call back' because there is no one else besides herself.

5. Spine 🥀 (10:10)
Through ‘Spine’, Sarah talks about the end of a 10-year-long toxic friendship filled with fights, hurt and co-dependency. It symbolizes the inability of people to maintain healthy connections with others when they do not like themselves.

6. Bleeding Heart 🩸 (14:26)
‘Bleeding Heart’ is a personal note by Sarah after spending years in therapy. She reflects on constant emotional triggers while battling her childhood traumas and the need and inability to express herself. But, her journey of self-discovery came full circle when she received her first guitar and started writing songs.

"

"Keep My Distance" was crafted while David D’Angelo was living in San Francisco, CA and MayDay was in their hometown of Durham, NC, during the first year of a global pandemic. We were forced to go through the creative process distanced from each other, yet we believe distance is also healthy for creative growth. We empathize with everyone trying to find that balance between isolation and social connection. We brought forth this project with a goal of finding and creating community, no matter the physical distance between one another. 

We invite you to simultaneously get closer to our music while keeping your own energy at a distance from anything that does not serve your personal growth. We see your Ultimate Potential ! We Invite you to see Ours !

East Journey To The West - David D'Angelo & MayDay journey to the Bay (2021)

Distance. Space. Time. Something That We All Need & Something That We All Share. We’ve ALL Been Entangled Within These Concepts, These Energies Even More Directly Over The Last NEARly 2 Years. As Artists, Whose Purpose Is To Channel, Express & Magnify The Current Feelings Of The Collective Conscious, We Experienced This Entangling Intensely. Being The Organic Artists That We Are, This Was Nyooooot A Viiibe!!! Couple That With David D’Angelo Being Freshly Landed & Expanding In San Francisco Whilst I TerraFormed In North Carolina, SHHEESH! So Of Course We Had To Add Sum Musical Alchemy To That Frustration & Thus Arrived: Keep My Distance!

In The Most Mystic Fashion, This Song Truly Became A Bridge Of Distances! Allowing Us To Travel West…Towards The Future! Enter…KIN DAO!!! 

Upon Being Invited To The Bay 4 Other Performance Opportunities, Our Timing Aligned To Desire A Peek Into The Future And As It Happened, KINDAO Had A Panel @ Maker’s Mart in SF…The Very Day We Landed in Ramaytush Ohlone Territory! 

Maneuvering through the City was a deliberate crawl…yet the Instant that the Flower Of Life Geometry Was In View, Our Pace Quickened! Immersing Into Space with KINDAO Felt Like One Of Those Family Reunions Where You Started Tentatively To Grab A Plate, Then Rounded Out The Night With Joyous Laughs And A Drink In Hand! Incredible!! That Energy Reverberated & Transformed and thus our connection to KINDAO Has Continued 2 Flourish & Grow !

Flash Forward - Full On Solstice & Full Moon - Back 2 Back 2 Frame Our 1st Of Innumerable Entries Into The MetaVerse Through This Auspicious NFT ReLease! So Much Appreciation & Gratitude Forward To KINDAO !

This NFT Represents The Journey Of Our Collective Feelings Between Space & Time Through FadeLess Memories We All Are, Have & Will Embark On.

Fresh back from an expedition with the Neon Cave Pirates, an assembly of psychedelic spelunkers engaged in an annual excavation of their buried treasure, the artists deemed the trip an ideal foundation for the story embedded within the lyrics. The piece not only evolved into a captivating interplay between the literal and metaphorical, but also emerged as an anthem encapsulating the ethos of these earth penetrating psychonauts.

Description: Know Thy Self -Thanos

Who are Beachcrimes? We’re a duo from LA and we spent the last year making songs in hotel rooms around the world. Beachcrimes is the soundtrack to that adventure.
 
We made a lot of songs, and we’re excited to share them. All of them. This year we’re releasing 24 songs in 48 weeks. If we’re being real, it’s actually two albums – there’s AM and there’s PM. AM is the lite stuff, PM is the nite stuff. Think of it like the Summer Olympics and Winter Olympics, but for dance music.

Producer, engineer, vocalist, multi-instrumentalist, and entrepreneur Dot reconnects with her roots to, once again, find her creative spark. “I've been going back to the piano, and playing jazz standards again, studying harmony again, and transcribing Bill Evans solos–going back to my roots as a pianist, and not even thinking about Ableton or anything digital, just playing the piano. That led me to start sampling the piano, and start working some of that back into my production.”

“Begin Again,”–track eight on HIGH FREQUENCY Volume 2”–catapults Dot to a breakthrough. “It's hard to get that energy and that momentum to start again. This track is really representative of how that feels.”

The sound of piano invites the listener with a comforting ease and beautifully romantic quality before the beat hits, steady and unassuming, introducing Dot’s ethereal vocals singing “feel your love again.” While the track builds, it ebbs and flows creating waves of sound that eventually crash into an infectious dance break. “That's a lot of resampled piano, from crappy iPhone recordings, not even using any nice microphones or anything to record it, it's very off the cuff,” says Dot. “I'm trying to capture this moment of finding the inspiration to take those first steps again, towards a new direction, or into a new project or a new chapter.”

Unfiltered and raw while still exemplifying Dot’s impeccable attention to detail in her engineering work, “Begin Again,” exudes both the magic of playful creativity and the excellence of studied perseverance.

"Memento Mori" is a personal note to my darker side, my alter ego.

I firmly believe that each of us carries a mix of good and bad within; absolute purity is unrealistic. What truly matters is which side we allow to take over. There may have been times when our darker selves won the battle. I know mine did.

The song serves as a testament of my journey toward self-redemption—a message from me to my other self. Writing the line "Why should I be paying for your crimes?" felt like a declaration of war against living a life imprisoned by my own darkness. It's unfair to claim that it defines who I am; it might be who I can become, but it's not my core identity.

The Latin phrase "Memento mori" means "remember that you will die". That's why the last lines of the chorus really capture the heart of the song: "All's memento mori/ So it's time for me to finally be alive". It's a reminder that as long as there's even a single drop of life, death can't take over. The worst within us cannot triumph as long as we preserve the light.

The chest, an ancient artifact woven from strands of starlight, was said to encapsulate the very essence of their ethereal wings—the source of their boundless grace and power. Legends whispered of its existence in the mortal realm, hidden among the enchanting landscapes of Earth.

The Council of Angels decided to embark on a quest, leaving the celestial abode to traverse the mortal world in search of the magical chest. With a serene hum, they descended from the heavens like gentle rain, their wings folded as they assumed mortal forms.

In the earthly realm, the angels encountered the beauty and complexity of human existence. Their celestial presence blended seamlessly with the natural wonders around them. As they journeyed through ancient forests, crossed cascading rivers, and explored bustling cities, the ambient sounds of their surroundings blended with the soothing harmony of their quest.

The melody of the ambient track mirrored the ebb and flow of their search—a combination of wonder, determination, and a touch of melancholy. Soft notes resonated through ancient ruins and vast landscapes, reflecting the profound connection between the angels and the world they explored.

As the angels delved deeper into the mortal realm, they discovered that the chest was not merely a physical object but a symbol of self-discovery. It represented the eternal dance between the celestial and the earthly, a harmonious balance that resonated with the ambient notes echoing through their journey.

In the end, the angels realized that the magical chest was not a destination but a reflection of the beauty within. The ambient song, now infused with a sense of fulfillment, accompanied the celestial beings as they returned to their heavenly abode, their wings glowing with newfound radiance.

And so, the story of angels searching for a magical chest became a timeless melody, echoing through the celestial realms—a testament to the eternal connection between the divine and the enchanting tapestry of the mortal world.
