'Best Kept Secret' is a hard hitting, braggadocios rap song that sees Kamre Haze embracing his status as an underground artist. The lyrics unfold into an intense exhibition of confidence, and raw, unfiltered energy. Proclaiming himself to be the best kept secret, Haze blends his self assured demeanor with a dark, haunting allure. He paints a vivid picture of an enigma unbothered by the lurking presence of mortality.

The verses possess a gritty, confrontational tone, juxtaposing references to mortality and fearlessness. A striking blend of wordplay and imagery is coupled with slight social commentary and a cynical, but realistic perspective. Kamre Haze draws a strong distinction between his unique style and poised demeanor compared to the fickleness of others.

Overall, 'Best Kept Secret' is a potent blend of lyrical prowess, vivid imagery, cunning wordplay, and unapologetic self belief.

“This was actually originally written for the Netflix “Spy Ops” show during the “remote times” of the pandemic, but did not make it into the show (other scores did which I may release as a side project soon). Even though what the show called for was very different from what I have previously done as a composer, a lot of the music I submitted was low-key similar compositionally to where my head was at for the trio for some time - I was trying to sneak jazz into a spy TV show haha. This song is built around a funky variation on the infectious Chaabi groove from Morocco / Algeria, and lately we’ve been opening live shows with this one. I love West African music and Chaabi music is interesting to me because it seems to have started around the same time as jazz - it’s a newer genre - and the various grooves which could be considered Chaabi are some of the trickiest to improvise over in my opinion. I’m always seeking to challenge myself.”

Produced by DEEGAN, Eldar Zey, and Matt Allen, “Make It Better” sparkles with ethereal soundscapes, pop earcandy, and DEEGAN’s uncanny creativity in weilding his multidimensional vocal chops as his lead instrument. 
 
After a session with Matt Allen who had written the song’s chord progression, Deegan and Eldar burned the midnight oil to follow a stroke of inspiration. “It was one of those where you download it from the universe and run with the momentum the second you’re inspired,” says DEEGAN. 

Before calling it a night, DEEGAN took a voice note with an experimental idea for the chorus. 

“I was like, ‘I’m going to say each word individually, and then auto tune it really hard and chop each word short,’’' says DEEGAN. “I thought if I go to sleep and don't at least get some proof of concept, it's gonna escape me and fly off to someone else. I was able to achieve the next day with my microphone and in the DAW exactly what I said on the voice memo. Most times it's like, “I said I was gonna do this and then I started playing with it and became something else.” But I remember the satisfaction of saying it out loud and then following through with that idea and it coming out exactly how I heard it.” 

Letting the lyrics pour out over the beat, DEEGAN made room for the song’s thematic concept to reveal itself. “The overall theme, once I started letting it spill out of me was like, ‘through dark times your partner can be the stronghold or the rock for you. Other lyrics are the contrast of that when you become codependent dumping all of your trauma onto your partner. It's about the healthy spectrum.”

Finding its center in the infectious hook, “Make It Better,” finds blissful balance.

Maya Randle makes dance music that carries an emotional weight.  Debut EP ‘Focus,’ the producer’s first for Pack Records, is a collection of pop-imbued drum and bass that’s both packed with irresistibly catchy tunes and wistful melancholia.  Hailing from Birmingham, UK, where she still resides, Randle grew up listening to the grime of the midlands, before cutting her teeth DJing at house parties with friends and teaching herself the basics of production.  Initially making drill and rap-type beats as well as dabbling in house music, once she got to know the essentials “since then, I’ve never watched another tutorial,” she explains, preferring to trust her own intuition while expanding her knowledge and confidence as a producer.

Story of the Song: "Sleepwalking"

In a haunting nocturnal journey, the protagonist finds themselves wandering aimlessly, driven by an unseen force. Despite the unfamiliarity of the wasteland around them, they feel a strange sense of déjà vu, as if they've been here in the past. The vividness of their sleepwalking state blurs the lines between dreams and reality, making the world appear in a different, more luminous light.

As they traverse this dreamlike realm, they feel a strong compulsion pulling them further away from the comforts of home. While a part of them yearns for awakening, another part revels in the freedom and boundlessness of this state. There's an exhilarating sense of invincibility, as they realize they can achieve feats they never thought possible. Yet, underlying this thrill is a nagging fear that they might become forever lost in this trance, turning into an unfeeling stone.

Throughout their journey, the sleepwalker grapples with the duality of their situation. On one hand, they embrace the liberation of the dream world, feeling unstoppable and uninhibited. On the other, there's an urgent plea for someone to awaken them before they drift too far and lose themselves completely.

This song paints a vivid picture of the internal conflict between the allure of escapism and the grounding pull of reality. The recurring refrain serves as a reminder of the dangers of getting too lost in one's mind, highlighting the importance of staying connected to one's roots and reality.

Description:
As a writer and ever-evolving human being, most of my songs come from real experiences. Whether they be my own, or somebody else’s. Although they’re all widely open for interpretation, some are a little more transparent in the details. 

Unforgettable is one of those songs. 

As most women do, I have a deeply loving but equally as complicated relationship with my mom. I love her more than I’ll ever love anyone, but she also knows how to twist the knife so effortlessly in ways nobody else does. And when a lot of those wounds continue to open back up time and time again, it’s difficult to not be reminded they’re there every day. 

When something is so prevalent and reoccurring, it tends to interrupt the peace I continue to try and culminate in my life. Sometimes my closest friend in moments of pain is my piano.

'Unforgettable' was born in a studio on Sunset Boulevard with a couple of my closest collaborators, Paul Phamous and Bailey Lindley. It was a slow burn to completion and took almost two years of going back in to refine the tiniest details til I was satisfied with it. It’s a testament to how powerful this song is, for me at least, because it resonates with the same intensity as it did when i first wrote it."

The song is a reflection of those lonely nights when my thoughts seemed to echo in the stillness, unable to find the solace of slumber. 'Insomnia' captures the raw vulnerability of those moments, drawing the listener into the intense emotional turmoil that accompanies a restless mind. 

The haunting melody and evocative lyrics speak to the universal experience of struggling with the relentless grip of sleeplessness, creating a connection between the listener and the artist's own turbulent nights. Through 'Insomnia,' I hope to provide a comforting soundtrack for those who find themselves trapped in the relentless embrace of the sleepless night, a reminder that they are not alone in their restlessness.

Each verse unfolds as a tapestry of gratitude, extending warm accolades to the cohorts and confidants who've been the wind beneath the artist's wings. The lyrical voyage transcends mere transactional interactions, delving into the profound realm of relational kinships born out of mutual respect and shared visions.

"WAGMI" isn’t just an acronym; it’s an emblem of collective aspiration, embodying the essence of ‘We All Gonna Make It.’ Through verses that echo with sincere acknowledgments, the artist iterates a promise of relentless pursuit towards a shared dream, making the song a heartfelt homage to every kindred spirit in the web3 domain.

Who are Beachcrimes? We’re a duo from LA and we spent the last year making songs in hotel rooms around the world. Beachcrimes is the soundtrack to that adventure.
 
We made a lot of songs, and we’re excited to share them. All of them. This year we’re releasing 24 songs in 48 weeks. If we’re being real, it’s actually two albums – there’s AM and there’s PM. AM is the lite stuff, PM is the nite stuff. Think of it like the Summer Olympics and Winter Olympics, but for dance music.

“For A Minute” is such a special song to us. It is the 20th song we’ve released this year, and captures that nostalgic feeling of trying to get over someone, having it almost work, until the moment you think of “us for a minute, your touch for a minute, your love for a minute”. This one has felt so special to us since the moment we wrote it, and we hope it resonates with you, too. Even if it’s only “for a minute” ;)

Next single will be out 2 weeks from today, and the following single 2 weeks after that.

*SONG FROM THE ARCHIVES*
Tears Me Apart is a song that I wrote and produced in 2013 about the anger I felt over a broken friendship. This is the instrumental. I actually vividly remember creating this track, so I guess I'll tell the story...

I was in my DAW playing around with chord progressions and switching through sounds when I came across this buzzy sound that you hear when the beat first drops. I hadn't made any drum sounds for the song yet, and I just played with that buzzy sound using different chords. The buzzy sound sounded... sickly...? Sick and tired... pissed off... 

Then I started going through kicks and layered a few together, and after that I found an old-school sounding snare. I made a very *pocket* beat with them. Just a very... BOOM... POP! ..B-BOOM... POP! ..And then I sequenced that drum beat with the tired-and-pissed buzzy sound, and played it back.

As soon as I heard it played back, I stood up from my chair and just let the newborn piece of music start speaking to me. The track was disgusted and exhausted. I started remembering how I felt when my ex-friends ghosted me, only after hearing a rumor about me. Didn't even come to me and ask about it. Just... gone. 

I had never started writing lyrics so fast up until that point. The lyrics just poured onto the page. I knew it was going to have to be a rap, because I had an entire RANT inside me.

As I was writing the first verse, the sadness came. That sadness was at the root of it all. Yes I was angry... but I was angry because I was heartbroken, and I knew things didn't have to turn out that way. That's when I added the weak and airy piano, and the song took and emotional turn. The rest of the creation of the song was me continuing to explore this juxtaposition between sadness, anger, and knowing that I would eventually need to just let it all go and move on.

Description: The second single from Shilly, first released in February 2023.

Recording Angel was a very fun and interesting process. Darius Alexander Baharlo and Elie Samouhi began writing it in July 2023, meeting up in Calabasas, California. After the main writing was done, Darius went off to Syracuse University to study at The Bandier Program for Recording and Entertainment Industries. From here, he was bouncing sound files, tracks, and notes from to Elie in Los Angeles and vice versa. The shared vision, dedicated hours, constant and honest communication, and overall love and passion for making music between Darius and Elie is what allowed for such a fun and meaningful result in the form of a song. We hope you love Angel just as much as we loved making it.

10) [NOT LEGAL ADVICE.  NOT FINANCIAL ADVICE.  THIS IS ALL AS I REMEMBER IT, BUT MY MEMORY MIGHT BE FAULTY IN PARTS.]

11) I'll get to what happened.  But for now, let's talk about where we are today.

12) To the best of my knowledge, as of post-11/7, with the potential for errors:

a) Alameda had more assets than liabilities M2M (but not liquid!)
b) Alameda had margin position on FTX Intl
c) FTX US had enough to repay all customers

Not everyone necessarily agrees with this

13) My goal—my one goal—is to do right by customers.

I’m contributing what I can to doing so.  I’m meeting in-person with regulators and working with the teams to do what we can for customers.

And after that, investors.  But first, customers.

14) My goal:

a) Clean up and focus on transparency
b) Make customers whole

15) A few weeks ago, FTX was handling ~$10b/day of volume and billions of transfers.

But there was too much leverage--more than I realized.  A run on the bank and market crash exhausted liquidity.

So what can I try to do?  Raise liquidity, make customers whole, and restart.

16) Maybe I'll fail.  Maybe I won't get anything more for customers than what's already there.

I've certainly failed before.  You all know that now, all too well.

But all I can do is to try.  I've failed enough for the month.

And part of me thinks I might get somewhere.

17) I know you've all seen this, but here's where things stand today, roughly speaking.  [LOTS OF CAVEATS, ETC.]

Liquid: -$8b
Semi: +$5.5b
Illiquid: +$3.5b

And yeah, maybe that $9b illiquid M2M isn't worth $9b (+$1b net).

OTOH--a month ago it was worth $18b; +$10b net.

---

18) Truth and Beauty

19) Once upon a time--a month ago--FTX was a valuable enterprise.

FTX had ~$10-15b of daily volume, and roughly $1b of annual revenue.  $40b of equity value.

And we were held as paragons of running an effective company.

20) I was on the cover of every magazine, and FTX was the darling of Silicon Valley.

We got overconfident and careless.

21) And problems were brewing.  Larger than I realized.

[AGAIN THESE NUMBERS ARE APPROXIMATE, TO THE BEST OF MY KNOWLEDGE, ETC.]

Leverage built up-- ~$5b of leverage, backed by ~$20b of assets which were....

Well, they had value.  FTT had value, in EV!  But they had risk.

22) And that risk was correlated--with the other collateral, and with the platform.

And then the crash came.

In a few day period, there was a historic crash--over 50% in most correlated assets, with no bid side liquidity.

And at the same time there was a run on the bank.

23) Roughly 25% of customer assets were withdrawn each day--$4b.

As it turned out, I was wrong: leverage wasn't ~$5b, it was ~$13b.

$13b leverage, total run on the bank, total collapse in asset value, all at once.

Which is why you don't want that leverage.

---

24) Shrapnel

25) Last night I talked to a friend of mine.

They published my messages.  Those were not intended to be public, but I guess they are now.

26) Well, that gives some color, I guess.

It sucks.  I'm really sorry that things ended up as they did.  And as I said--I'm going to do everything I can to make it more right.

27) A few thoughts:

a) It's *really* hard to be a regulator.  They have an impossible job: to regulate entire industries that grow faster than their mandate allows them to.

And so often they end up mostly unable to police as well as they ideally would.

28) Even so, there are regulators who have deeply impressed me with their knowledge and thoughtfulness.  The CFTC has; the SCB, and VARA, too.  And others, scattered.

But most are overwhelmed.

29) Which means that interacting with regulatory structures can be really frustrating: a *huge* amount of work--much of it arbitrary--and relatively little customer protection.

Fuck that.  You all deserve frameworks that let regulators protect customers while allowing freedom.

30) (Some of what I said was thoughtless or overly strong--I was venting and not intending that to be public.  I guess at this point what I write leaks anyway.)

31) And in the future, I'm going to care less about the dumb, contentless, "good actor" framework.

What matters is what you do--is *actually* doing good or bad, not just *talking* about doing good or *using ESG language*.

32) Anyway -- none of that matters now.

What matters is doing the best I can.

And doing everything I can for FTX's customers.

Description:
What started as an effort to capture beauty, turned into a container for grief as electronic music duo KarmaVioletta approached the making of their song “Humanity”–the fourth track from HIGH FREQUENCY Volume 2. 

“I started the initial idea on a plane looking out the window during sunset feeling like, “I want to capture this emotion somehow.” I made the soundscape, and then we wrote the rest of the song this weekend,” says Karma.

“The past week, we’ve had a ton of emotions about things happening on the global scale,” says Violetta. “We tend to put our emotions into our music, and kind of process in that way.” 

The brainchild of Miami-based artists Karma.wav and Violetta, KarmaVioletta often serves as a vehicle for catharsis for the musical duo and couple. A focus on shared humanity has always been core to the duo’s message and music, and “Humanity” is no different. “It’s a reminder that there is some continuity between us,” says Karma.  We're all one species.”

“Maybe we're just hopeful dreamers, but we believe in humanity, and we dream of a time that there's peace on our planet,” says Violetta.

---- 

This is the fourth track from HIGH FREQUENCY Volume 2 — a compilation album curated by NOISE and the web3 music community.

Description: This song was actually an afterthought for the EP. But it just tied everything so nice. The first time i listened to it in context of the rest of the EP, the last few seconds sent chills down my spine. Thats when i knew this one was a wrap.
This is one of my favorite songs off the album. The vibe is on point and the drop just hits so nice. Its also the only song I've ever put my voice on.

I wrote this back in Colorado where I grew up last summer about a night out I had with a girl in July right after graduating High School. It’s funny because I didn’t really love country music back then, and she was playing me all these country songs when we were driving around. Now, a few years later, I’ve incorporated a banjo, harmonica, and steel pedal guitar into my music. It’s almost like she was the first to truly introduce me to country music, and that’s become the sound I’m chasing now!

Who are Beachcrimes? We’re a duo from LA and we spent the last year making songs in hotel rooms around the world. Beachcrimes is the soundtrack to that adventure.
 
We made a lot of songs, and we’re excited to share them. All of them. This year we’re releasing 24 songs in 48 weeks. If we’re being real, it’s actually two albums – there’s AM and there’s PM. AM is the lite stuff, PM is the nite stuff. Think of it like the Summer Olympics and Winter Olympics, but for dance music.

“Oh Na Na Na” is the 19th song we have released this year. This song was born on a late night in the hot tub. We had just been in the studio making a bunch of beats, and we wanted to keep working, but we ALSO wanted to go in the hottub. We bounced the beats from the session and brought our speaker to the hot tub. We started singing random melodies until boom. We came up with the hook for Oh Na Na Na. We knew if we could remember the hook after another hour of singing random melodies over the beats we had just made, it was something special. And we did.

Next single will be out 2 weeks from today, and the following single 2 weeks after that.

Description:
I wrote this song back in 2019. It happened so quickly. I made a quick drum beat and then started playing the acoustic guitar and mumbling nonsense that eventually sounded like I was saying "i don't wanna be your lover" lol. The song was fully realized within an hour and by the following week I had my close friend in Brooklyn play some live drums on it. The song is about that in between place we eventually find ourselves in while navigating a toxic relationship. You're in between a place of wanting to be with this person and not wanting to. You can't tell if they are your lover or your worst enemy. I think that comes with the territory of any tumultuous relationship. This song is always a lot of fun playing at shows! Anyways, hope you enjoy. 

Peace and love

I created this song after grieving the loss of a dear friend of mine. I was going through a lot at the time and when I got this beat from my producer Joe Dirt I became obsessed with it immediately. It took me a while to get my thoughts together and finally rap on this beat, because I was lost for words and didn't know how to express myself at the time. Eventually I knew I needed to go ahead and get back into my comfort zone, and once I started with the first bar of this song the rest of the lyrics came to me effortlessly. Although I loved what I did, I was planning on a few other projects at the time of this recording and didn't release this song immediately because of that. After holding onto the record for a little over a year, I eventually started to wonder if I ever wanted it to be released. The emotions I get from listening to this recording bring me back to the day I was in my room listening to it on repeat and coming up with no words at all, only memories all flooding into my brain at once. Eventually, going on tour with my hardcore band "Inner Peace" in August, I decided it was time to drop this song along with another two that I made around that time as well. I am very happy that the world has been able to hear and enjoy this timeless music with me.

No matter how many songs i make, 'Broken' will always be very special to me because it was the first song I released...

I wrote this song as an open letter to my parents, asking for forgiveness for the all the pain I've caused. We’ve all been in that cruel tug of war between our guilt of staying the same, and our paralyzing fear of change…and we all have days when fear wins, but through “Broken” I want to remind you to keep believing in your own breakthrough.  

'Broken' was also my genesis music NFT, which I initially released on Open Sea, and those collectors are the ones who you see in the "special edition" section. 

But because this song is such a special part of my journey, I wanted you guys to be able to collect it....forever!

Produced by the brilliant Poly Armour, with whom I have been doing collaborative songs for about 5 years now - our symbiotic experience just continues.

This track is part of Poly Armour's solo album "Fusion with Metal" released in summer 2023

Backstory: He sent this beat to me in a time when I felt like all the protective illusionary shields I set up as a child to protect myself, bursted at once and left me all naked. I didn't feel distant anymore, I didn't feel like I was surrounded by this stone-cold wall anymore, I felt free. Soft and unformed, couldn't grasp anything at all - I was starving. The definition of the "me" was gone and I needed to hide from everyone for a few days. When I stepped into the sunlight, the sunrays felt like they were flashing through me into every cell. It recharged my body with its frequency, warmth and intensiveness and I never felt it that strong ever before. The beat felt like the bursting sunrays and the flashes that were so sudden and intense. Rushing in and out of the system, flushing through every vein and nerve of the system. It was perfect. I hope you enjoy this one <3

I wrote this song back in early 2021. At the time I was flat broke and my mental health was at an all time LOW. I thought it would be a good idea to stop taking my meds my doctor prescribed me because I believed I could handle my depression and anxiety. I was wrong lol.

It was mid January in New Jersey. Freezing cold night. I decided to take a drive to clear my head. I live ten minutes outside of Philly and normally I drive down to the beach to clear my head. However, for some reason I decided to drive to New York City. Idk what compelled me to do it but I just did it anyways. So as I'm driving on the highway for what seems to be an hour and a half I see a big city and get really pumped up. But for some reason it wasn't New York. I ended up in Philly somehow. I took the same road I always take to NYC and I was right where I started after driving for an hour and a half. I was terrified but also wildly inspired to write a song so I went into my studio and went at it. Deja Vu was born that night.

Hope you enjoy and hope you take care of yourself friends. Life is shortly and it's a blessing to be here. 

Peace and Love

Allow me to take you on the journey of "Cabin in the Woods" - a song that was born out of pure longing & love.

Two years ago, during one of our countless Zoom meetings, my long-distance boyfriend, Satwik (whom most of you know as this incredibly talented and charming artist, songwriter, and producer), started humming this hauntingly striking melody. It was then and there, right in front of my shameless tearful eyes that "Cabin in the Woods" was coming to life. It was coming strong, almost as if it was making a statement that it was here to take over our lives.  It did. And damn, was it beautiful.

Fast-forwarding a couple of months later, the song was all finished and wrapped up in a giant bow spelling "ready for release". But I was the voice on it, not him. After completing the songwriting process, Satwik unequivocally decided that "Cabin in the Woods" belongs to me, and that it has my name written all over it. So now, here we are. After 2 long years of sitting on the Spotify shelves, that bow still spells the same words. The only difference is the 2 words added at the end of it: "in Web3". Who would've even imagined?

"Cabin in the Woods" has become an extension of myself, being the song I always start our live concerts with. In a way, long before it even reaches hundreds of thousands of streams, fame, and all the weird twisted good & bad that comes on the side, it already became a legend. 

Today, you're not only minting a song;  you're becoming the owner of a symbol marking the beginning of our 2 year-long journey that led us all the way here. All the way to you.

In 2018 I had released 3 songs under my new moniker Divorce Court. I was writing my 4th single, unsure of what it would be about or what it would be called. I had a rough demo of sampled chords and drums playing in my headphones on a long flight from Utah to Florida. It was the middle of the day and I was alone sitting in the window seat. The sun was shining and I was looking down upon a bed of the fluffiest, most beautiful clouds I had ever seen. I was feeling a bit introspective (travel and flights always puts me in that place), and my mind was wandering around every aspect of my own life and the current state of the world. 

I was thinking a lot about interconnectedness and how we treat each other. I wrote down one line, which ended up becoming the first lyrics of this song... "this sea of white, won't support us all.." It represented beauty and worry at the same time. How can we all co-exist comfortably on this planet? How can we all feel supported by each other and experience the beauty around us? 

The next line says "I'll be there soon, to catch you when you fall..." It's this idea that no matter what happens, somebody will be there for you. Even if it's not the person that you expect. These two lines sat in my notes app for a few months and I continued to tweak the track endlessly. 

The next thing I know, I am standing in an old church in Idaho at my Grandfather's funeral standing over his casket. As I examined his frail structure, I thought about how strange life can be; managing these bodies temporarily, and endlessly worrying until one day it all ends. It didn't even look like him tbh.. without his spirit lighting up his eyes - his movements and way of speaking. 

It was a lot at once, so I went out to get some air and jotted down some thoughts which ended up being the next two lines of the songs.. "break through the clouds, gazing down on you.. empty and still, a vessel we forget." This concept of bodies or vessels just being vehicles for experiences hit me really profoundly that day.

In the chorus, the song just repeats the words, "I just wanna get away.."

I guess the point of this whole story is - no matter what, you are never alone, and things that seem overwhelming might not be so bad in the grand scheme of things. 

Much love,
Lynden

Description:
Written, performed, and produced by Sara Phillips, “Angel City” shows versatility and range from the LA-based, Montreal-born singer-songwriter known for her keen songwriting and impeccable vocals. An honest rumination on the disillusionment of romanticizing the pursuit of an artist career in Los Angeles, “Angel City” notes fair weather friends, vapid parties, FOMO and other soul-killing agents as causes of metaphorical death in the city of angels. 

A minimal, moody, synth-laden beat shows off her blossoming production skills, while her intentionally pretty and appropriately angelic vocals let her clever lyricism take center stage. “Everybody’s dying here, that’s why they call it Angel City.  Everybody’s lying here, my god they make it look so pretty,” she sings, later offering the line: “All this young forever is getting old.” Sara says she actually likes LA, but struggles at times to find her boundaries within the pressures of the culture. She sings, “I’m sick of the parties but I still want to get invited.” A painfully relatable line for anyone who’s chased success in Lala land, Sara strikes a nerve. 

“It’s the dichotomy of being tired of it, but also wanting to still be a part of it,” says Sara. “You're still caught in the middle, not completely over it, frustrated and kind of jaded by it, but you still have this need or feel this pressure to show up because you feel like if you don't go, you're missing out, or they'll stop asking you.”

Over the years, I've recorded the song several times, but it's only recently that I feel I've captured the perfect version that truly does justice to the essence of the song. Sometimes, songs age like fine wine, gaining depth and meaning with the passage of time.

This song was born from my visit to the Vatican and the awe-inspiring beauty of Michelangelo's frescoes in the Sistine Chapel. "Heavenly Angels" is a heartfelt exploration of compassion, redemption, and forgiveness. It delves into the idea that we all make mistakes, and as painful as those mistakes can be, everyone deserves the chance to be forgiven and liberated from the burdens they carry.

Looking forward, we realize that the pain we've experienced only serves to shape us into stronger, more resilient individuals.

I'm proud to say that "Heavenly Angels" is a collaborative effort between myself, and my dear friend Ed Prosek, who worked together on the writing and production. The artwork for the song is a creation of my talented father, Giuseppe Zironi, who, despite his usual work drawing Disney comics, took a break to collaborate with me on this project.

YO I'm Ramzoid, an artist/singer/producer from Prince Edward Island, Canada.

I've been exploring the Web3 space for around a year now, starting with a sold out collection of 10 audio/visual pieces on opensea, I then dropped a series of 1/1 songs from my discography on Catalog which have mostly been collected up until this point as well. Have loved watching what sound.xyz has been doing from the sidelines and very stoked to be officially dropping on here!!

This is the first single from my upcoming debut album that I've been working on for the past few years. Oddly enough, this was the first song I made in my album process that felt like it encompassed the "vibe" I was looking for. It really set the tone for the whole project, & after I wrote the demo for it, the album started to really take shape and have direction with each following song I created. During the creation of the song I was very inspired by visuals. I wanted the song to sound like how a desolate, dark field would look (if that makes any sense lol)

So yeah very excited to share it with you all, hope you enjoy :)

Description:
It’s crazy how time flies. It feels like yesterday that we started writing songs together in high school, recording our songs at Clemens’ house and just uploading it for the world to hear. But already almost ten years have passed since we released our first album and we are grateful for every single step in our journey till today, honored that we are still here and able to do what we love.

And we’re hoping that we can do this for much longer, but while writing ‘Synchronize’ we did have some apocalyptic images in our heads. We liked the idea of coming from the „smoke in the sky“  image - that was there first - and to pair that with the comfort of being totally in love/synchronization and the absurdity it creates. Even though this world seems to be going down slowly, if you find yourself in sync with a person you love or in sync with the world around you, it resembles the blind feeling of love and how that can make you „blind“ for other real happenings. Like seeing everything through rose-colored glasses. Making you feel good endlessly.

We are so delighted that RAC, an artist we always admired for his unique sound and creativity, took our song and made his own version of it. RAC really did a beautiful job on reinterpreting our song. The Song structure itself didn‘t change but the world he built around it, so it feels more like a remake than a remix. His guitar playing and new harmonies take the song to another level in a more dark and melancholic way and we really love how it turned out. From bottom to top a little masterpiece.

Miracles is a life affirming psychedelic disco banger about the magic of the universe. 

Written, produced and performed by Ging (fka Frank Dukes)

This record is dedicated to my brother.
River Naim Harris

We all process our trauma differently, and the past few years of my life have been quite traumatic. On one hand I understand that I am not defined by these traumas. They are a part of my journey but they do not make me who I am. Yet, on the other hand I understand that in order for me to heal I need to address them. To process them. To find acceptance. To find forgiveness. To find peace.

The fact that songwriting is a gift is not something that’s lost on me. I am grateful every day to be able to express myself through music in a way that helps me heal. I don’t know a better way to communicate. I don’t know a better form of therapy than being completely vulnerable: on record. 

I wrote “Be Here Long” at one of the lowest points in my life. At the time I didn’t realize how many emotions I was suppressing and how much of an impact it was having on me. It’s funny how art reflects life because I feel like I was in autopilot both mentally and musically. I didn’t need to force this record and truthfully, I don’t feel like [I] wrote it; it wrote itself. I just remember pacing around my apartment in tears and finally looking down at a finished song.

One section in particular resonated with me at a core level:

“You halfway through a sentence, and it’s harder to keep dreaming.
I’m halfway through a sentence, and it’s harder to keep reading.
Letters feel like packages whenever I’m receiving… heavy.

I feel the distance, the dissonance
The disconnect from your innocence
The tears, rain…
The pain in your eyes, the resemblance
Liquor in my cup, a deliverance
And liquor on the ground in remembrance”

It reminded me that we’re all fighting our individual battles. Together. We are all fighting to maintain our light. To keep going on days where it may seem hopeless. To find love in all that we do. I am not physically with my brother but his battle is my battle. His light is my light. His peace is my peace. And we will find it together.

I thought a lot about what I wanted my initial offering for this platform to be. Full transparency, it gave me a lot of anxiety trying to pick the “perfect” song. I never set out to make any type of record. I just create what I feel called to create. But I found hope in this record. And that’s something I’d love to contribute to my people in any way possible.

I love you guys. Thank you for changing my life. Thank you for reminding me of my worth when I forget. Thank you for loving me. Thank you for supporting me. Thank you for uplifting me. Thank you for showing up for me. Thank you for helping me provide for my family. Thank you. For everything.

All love, always.

-MRH

The single most important thing right now is that the youth believe in ourselves enough to truly unleash our creativity.

I am an artist, teacher, student, world builder and I am a vessel by which the higher dimensions flow into this one. I create these compositions of high frequency vibration for everyone, but specifically the Indigos. There is a shift happening and the Indigos are here to usher in a new world. A world that operates on the love frequency. I believe music is our strongest tool for this purpose.

My name is Ayotemi and I am a 25 year old, groovy, full-blooded Nigerian born in America. The rhythms and the soul of my African ancestors are my root lens. The lens through which my divine creativity is unleashed. My subconscious sits above this root and is as a file cabinet. Every sound, whether a cricket chirping, a buckle-seat-belt beep, jazz standard harmony, black church choir, voice of my mother, voice of a stranger, is stored there. Input in a database. Soil nutrients to a tree. The fruit is my song.

Doo Doo is my saddest song so far. It’s about the toxic side of self-love. Self-love without balance. As people with purpose. And goals and ambitions and shit. [in love with the thought of the taste of flight] it can be easy to lose touch - with the ground. On this episode of toxic self-love, I push her too hard. Does she leave? Listen for yourself. Doo Doo.

Emily Lazar is a multi-disciplinary artist fronting the rock/metal transmedia project, September Mourning. She made history as the first female metal/ hard rock musician to mint and sell an NFT on the blockchain. She has spoken about her accomplishments in Web 3/ NFT's at Harvard (2x), NFT.NYC and ETH Denver Conferences.

September Mourning is a transmedia project based on a comic book series she wrote and published through Image/Top Cow Comics with her business partner Marc Silvestri (Batman/Witchblade/Darkness). September Mourning is the title character. As a human reaper hybrid, she  gives expired souls a second chance at life in another body. In doing so, she messes with  the plans of the antagonist, Fate, who is trying to rid  earth of all the good souls and leave the bad so the world will self-destruct and It can start anew. An epic war between the living and the dead ensues. Emily plays the title character on stage.

Emily designed the world she and her band (Rich Juzwick, Kyle Mayer and Aaron Hoover) bring to life on stage, including costumes, choreography, sets, etc. The band has toured with & opened festivals for Rob Zombie, Marilyn Manson, Slipknot, Mudvayne and others across Europe and the United States.

The high energy hard rock anthem, “Personally” slaps you in the face with driving guitars, percussion and vocals fueled by rage. The lyrics mimic the anger September feels towards Fate in the story  but can very easily be relatable to any listener’s real life frustrations as well. 

Wes Henry brilliantly captures the energy and emotion of the song in his album artwork.

Album Art: Wes Henry
Song Credits: September Mourning Collective

“If you were given the ear of every living being on this earth for 5 minutes, what would you say?” 
This is a question that (whether consciously or unconsciously) lingers at the back of my mind every time  I create any art. I operate in a space of gratitude and abundance, thankful for the gifts I’ve been given from the source. Thankful for my journey, my story and for the ancestors that came before me. I’m nothing without my community. I’ve learned that true growth doesn’t occur in a vacuum and I know that I’m constantly being poured into because I pour into others. It’s a cycle of love. I know all too well the importance of my purpose (while here in the physical) and the exact responsibility I have to live in that purpose. I’m a builder, simple as that. It's that ideology that's driven me since I was a kid and the ethos that acts as the fuel to my fire as a Cameroonian-American, multi-disciplined creative, an advocate for my community and a bridge between the diaspora and the motherland.

“Affirmations” is self love personified and a real time case study for the power of community. This happens to be the first song of five that I recorded during a live stream with the incredibly talented June Jissle and two of his frequent collaborators, Big Racco & Tito G. I had the pleasure of meeting June (via my good brother, Cam Murdoch) back in March at the start of what we now call Future Surf Radio and I instantly became a fan. Fast forward 6 months later I know have the pleasure of calling him my brother. June called me with an idea one night that I was immediately down for. He wanted to do a challenge where he would have 15 minutes to star production and pass it along to the next person who then had 15 minutes to contribute and then finally I would have 20 mins to load the production and create a song. We did this process live and in a little under 3 hours we ended up creating an EP full of self-love, confidence, culture and vision.

I’ve been in a state of flow and this process documented that stream of consciousness. June is nothing short of a genius and this record would have never happened with out him. I’m grateful to be able to use this song as an opportunity to bring not only, Tito & Racco into the world of Web 3 but my brother, Ashton Woods, who mixed and mastered the record. This song reminds you that no dream is too big and you deserve to have good things. Please set the tone for growth and success in your life by calling to it.

I hope you enjoy.

With Love,
Scolla

How To Be Us was Written, Produced and Arranged by Saint Rien.

About me? Man, I just fucking love creating and consuming art. I'm unhealthily obsessed.

I am a 5th generation performer and have jumped into all the creative endeavors that have presented themselves to me. I grew up acting, joined a band when I was 16 and at the same time I was modeling commercial, runway and editorial. I then switched to creative directing and styling in fashion too. 

After the band split up I slept on couch pillows for six months in my friend's studio and learned how to produce before spending every cent I had on a visa to move to America. Two weeks before my flight, I met her…

She was and will always be the most beautiful person I’ve ever seen, Stephanie… Even a french name! From the day we first met, we didn’t leave each other's side for over a week. It felt impossible to imagine not being together, I had real thoughts of struggling to remember life without her even though that reality was merely days prior.

How To Be Us is a retrospective song looking back at every moment of those first months together. Falling for her, feeling like we wouldn't be able to be together, moving across the world and finally proposing to her after six months… I wanted to capture the duality of how it felt to meet the love of your life as you were planning to leave and never come back. I hope you enjoy. 🥀

My relationship with music is always changing. I picked up the guitar 10 years ago out of necessity; life was beginning to flood with new emotions and experiences, and I desperately needed an outflow. With time, songs eventually became a second language, lending me the keys to new friendships and identity within self expression. In 2018, I had all but sold my soul to the medical field for a doctorate in physical therapy when music exerted it’s force on me again, this time pulling me away from medicine and into the thicket of my creative journey. Nowadays music is my religion, and songwriting feels a lot like meditation. The creative process is both merciless and vigilant—it casts it’s light into my darkest corners. What started as an outlet has become the setting for confronting the parts of myself I fear the most.

This demo of ‘Back on the Fence’ is a testament to the power of songwriting as a spiritual guide. I have trouble following through on positive change, and I think writing this song helped me gain a sense for when I start to regress into old thought patterns and behaviors—things like self-isolation, splitting hairs over the smallest stuff, or ironically losing weeks of life at a time to the thought of eventually dying. I’m really so thankful for the opportunity to rediscover this demo and share it. Letting go of it has allowed me to honor and appreciate every step in my creative process.

Hiii, we are KarmaVioletta! We're a traveling music duo couple, involved in the Web3, creator & wellness spaces. We believe in a world where a kid can tell their parents, "I want to be a musician, artist or creator," & there's a viable path to that. We were formed in 2019 in Miami, after we fell in love and started creating in our home studio. We feel that we are all in this human experience together, so let's dance :)

Karma, born in Vancouver, raised in Hawaii & Miami, comes from a musical family, having learned to play the drums at age 3, followed by guitar, singing & piano. In 2012, he first discovered Ableton and that took him down the rabbit hole, which he re-surfaced from as a producer, singer/ songwriter, sound engineer & DJ.      Violetta (Vee-oh-letta), born in Germany, raised in Russia & America, learned to play the piano & guitar at a young age. She’s been singing her whole life & started songwriting in 2017, which also led her into co-producing & DJing.

This is our very first drop on Sound.xyz from our duo project. We got into Web3 via Karma.wav red-pilling Violetta at NFT NYC last year, Nov 2021. During that trip, we met up with the Songcamp fam IRL & had our first studio session together. We are now both a part of their most recent camp of 77 members, Camp Chaos, the headless band. Right around that same time we started wavWRLD, through which we are building infrastructure to enable unique musical experiences that connect artists with their true fans.

We wrote this song in the beginning of our relationship, about 3 years ago. It encompasses those moments of butterflies & excitement, but slight fear at the same time, when you realize that you’ve already fallen so deeply for this person, your person. “So Deep” also represents gratitude for all that has come beforehand, including past relationships, as they were filled with hard lessons that prepared you & got you to where you are now, with who you are now. They got you to a much better place. Only you know what’s best for you, so trust yourself & remember to do you & love YOU first, then everything else will fall into place.

Thank you so much for listening, being a part of our journey & collecting.

Hi! My name is Brij, I’m a producer, DJ and music teacher from Mumbai and I’ve been making tunes across genres for close to 7 years, mainly under the name Three Oscillators. I’ve been influenced by science fiction, dystopia and electronic music ever since I was a kid, and I bring out these influences in the music I make.

While being a producer, I also DJ under the same name and have played some of the wildest gigs in my home country of India, a place with a small, niche audience that absorbs everything from techno, drum n’ bass and RnB to even more experimental genres.

Dreamy, introspective and emotional are some words I’d describe most of my music with, and I see every tune of mine as an inward journey into your consciousness. Submersion is my first tune on Sound and marks almost a year of being into web3 and music NFTs, something that has changed my life and I’m truly grateful for. This journey has had its ups and downs but that’s a story for another day.

Submersion is about immersing yourself in your thoughts and letting them consume you completely. I went on a trip to Goa last year and experienced bioluminescence for the first time in my entire life; watching the ocean glow while you swim in it is an unparalleled experience. A few tunes I’ve made after that trip attempt to encapsulate that feeling, and Submersion is one of them. I haven’t decided on what to do with these tunes yet - it might be a single or end up becoming an EP. As a collector, you’ll be the first to know what I do with them!

I hope you enjoy the music and I hope it makes you feel something. Now close your eyes…

Until next time <3

Hi I'm Luca. I used to say I was just a producer, then just a DJ, but only now do I feel like I fully encompass the role of an artist. I've spent the last 10 years navigating the electronic music space to varying degrees of success while using SoundCloud and digital distribution platforms as a digital diary to share my eclectic productions with the world. Through a series of fortuitous events, persistence and a dedication to the craft I found myself touring the globe over selling out hard ticket shows a world away from my tiny apartment in Brooklyn where it all started. 

That all came to a screeching halt with  the pandemic, although covid gave me a much needed reprieve from touring nonstop and allowed me to re-evaluate what it was that I wanted to do with music. I briefly pivoted into more rave centric music with a project centered entirely around speedhouse music but, without any raves to play the tour we had scheduled around the material was postponed until outright cancelled. 

During this period of particular financial uncertainty I was introduced to the NFT space through my friends cooper and Kris (wuki). I became heavily involved in several project, teaching myself JavaScript and python in order to fully dive into generative art and music creation. At some point I realized that despite my enthusiasm for learning a diverse new skill set I was drifting farther away from the thing that gave me true purpose in life - that of creating and sharing music.
 
It was during this time I penned Crystal Caverns. I hadn't touched upon the style that had so fortuitously brought me to this point in some time - after years of production experience I was coming back with both a fresh ears and a fresh heart to fully embrace the sound. Although I have since pivoted out into more mature techno leanings I felt like a more melodic superfluous future bass romper was the perfect fit for a sound.xyz drop.

Versions of me is the realization of it all.

So much of my life, I’ve dedicated everything I’ve had to others. Which isn’t always a bad thing…unless you never refill your own cup.

This song acknowledges out loud that all of the good coming my way, from years of hard work and pouring my heart and soul into making sure people are taken care of, is well deserved.

I acknowledge where I fell short countless times trying to be perfect and look forward to a bright future that will give me everything I need and desire because of the love I have sown. I no longer desire to be anything but the imperfect masterpiece I have been designed to be.

My name is Pat Dimitri. I’ve been a professional touring guitar player, composer, and producer for 10 years. I’ve played for numerous artists, some you know, many you don’t - this career has taken me all over the world as a performer, and more importantly made me into the musician that I am. Despite having played in front of millions of people, 10 years in and I still found myself struggling for financial and creative freedom - Web3 provided a solution to this problem I have been trying to solve since before I knew blockchain existed, and that's why I've been all in on it for the past 18 months.

This record was written in 2020 where my personal frustration with misinformation was at an all time high. I felt like I needed to explore the idea of seeing things so clearly while others had obvious revelations obscured. In short, the past 5-6 years was a mind bogglingly thorough example of Dunning-Krueger, and this song proved to be an outlet for that anger - and an outlet for the legend Kwudi to drop a flawless verse.

For those that are unaware, Kwudi is one of my closest friends and has a list of accolades that would take up the entire page - most notably being an amazing solo artist and a producer for Childish Gambino. He recently found himself in a serious motorcycle accident - part of the ethos of this song is making sure that him and his family get all the help they need. Half of primary sales are going to his gofundme.

The more we know the more we know we don’t know.. but what we do know has to count for something, right?

Have you ever watched a movie where the masterful swordsman was simply nowhere to be found? He was perhaps tending to his garden, or building a cabin, until the people in need of rescue finally contacted him to pick his sword back up? this song is that return exactly. 

Until now, Seattle rapper, producer, cartoonist, etc. J’von had quietly stepped away from releasing music, though still recording & practicing everyday. With the successful release of Loser Club, an NFT art project designed by the man himself, he has found himself drawing more, whilst obtaining more resources than ever to really push his creative mind further. But what does he have to say? Exactly how much of himself does he have available to give now?

“BOOK” is a rap song, where j’von discusses the past, the present, and the future of who he is & is destined to be. Esotericism ensued, where only a select few will be able to resonate with his messages. j’von speaks of his bouts with depression, identity, relevance, and sabotage, but with such a slyness, who would really know?

j’von is currently recording his next album. if “BOOK” is to be any signaling of where the man is headed, then brace yourselves. It's going to be a long adventure.

So I’m a DJ.

My job is to make sure you're having a good time. I select different sounds and mash them up and people actually pay me stupid money to do it.

I live for sampling. Everything is a remix.

The first time I heard “D.J. Girl” by Katalina was at a rave. For the next 10 years, I whole-heartedly believed that was the original song. (DJ Caffeine)

It wasn’t until this year that I discovered the original and as a house-head you can imagine my excitement!

I immediately started playing it in all of my sets. I found the acapella and made an edit that felt more aligned with what I play today.

I played it out and people really liked it.

I made a TikTok and it went moderately viral (for me)

Me to myself: Hey I think I might have something big here!

Me to record labels: Hey guys do you like this song?

Record labels: [Silence]

So I made another TikTok with an updated version. And it happened again.

Cool cool cool, so I guess I’m doing it on my own.

This is my version of I’m With the DJ.

Hello hello, I’m Kathleen! 

I’m a Boston born independent singer/songwriter (go pats), currently residing in Nashville, TN (yeehaw?) I’ve been actively releasing music for about 10 years, but really just got into my own groove over the past few. Growing up in Massachusetts, I was deeply inspired by Irish and folk music. My dad introduced me to Alison Krauss and I’ve been writing sad shit ever since. 

This is my very first drop with Sound.xyz but my introduction to web3 came a little over a year ago. During the pandemic, I had a few sessions via zoom with my friend Matthew Chaim. At that point, his idea for Songcamp was really brewing and I could tell how excited he was for what web3 could become for independent artists. I didn’t want to miss out. I was then a part of Camp Elektra as well as the most recent camp, Camp Chaos. Songcamp became the ideal playground for me to learn & experiment in this space alongside this group of people, whom are now my family. 

I wrote this song a few months back while on tour in The Netherlands. I was experiencing, for the first time, being away from a partner and having it feel really healthy. Before this, I wasn’t used to the idea of someone fully supporting my wandering spirit or the fact that my career can take me elsewhere for weeks at a time. I also hadn't found this time away in the past to be very successful.. had been cheated on multiple times by the first guy I ever fell for, blah blah good timesssss my dudesss

“best or worst?” is my talking through that pessimistic side of me.. when I don’t mean to self sabotage, or talk myself out of enjoying the present moment.. but I do! At times when my life is going really well, I find myself being scared to get tooooo happy. It’s like my “what’s the catch?” mentality creeps (hey, therapy!!). Anyway, life is full of the push & pull of inner thoughts and I wanted to be honest about that. 


Thank you so much for being here,
and thank you Sound.xyz team for the platform x
KR

As a kid growing up in South Jersey my main music of choice was trap and club music, but as I developed as a musician and started to study other genres of music I learned to appreciate all different styles. Being a Nigerian man growing up in America, sometimes I felt like my house was Lagos Nigeria and as soon as I stepped out those doors I entered back into America and that's because of the music and culture my father gave me as a kid which helped me be the producer, dj, songwriter, and artist I am today pulling from all styles of music. 

Wa Nibi is a song I produced, wrote, and performed to simply make people dance and feel good. In the song I use some yoruba words such as “dide” (which means get up) or wa nibi which means “come here”. The song mixes in multiple styles of music such as ama piano which is a sound coming from South America but also has different renditions all over Africa. At the end of the song you can also hear some Spanish guitars I played with. 

Hopefully people can feel the same energy I felt when I made the song. Regardless if you understand the words or not, Wi Nibi is supposed to feel euphoric, sexy, and dangerous.

I made all of these sounds except for the vocal from scratch using the Pulsar-23 and AlphaBass. I downloaded the vocal from Splice (not really sure who it is)

Unreleased on DSPs for now because it takes longer to process (and I literally made this today), but I will upload to other spots like Audius, Soundcloud, etc after the drop.

Thanks for being a part of my experiment fr

I wanted to create a song that I havent heard before. Something that was weird but cool. With this song the quality of music was very important to me, and above all, I wanted the track to feel big. BLKMN and I both had a crazy feeling and energy after creating FortysSeven. There are multiple meanings and stories in this song but we hope the listener and collector get a chance to discover it on their own.

“Joke” came to me after an unwanted encounter I recently had with my old Honor’s Chemistry teacher from high school (who I NEVER got along with). He often made passive aggressive and patronizing remarks about my passions because they were different from his. While working an odd job in May, I bumped into him, and thus came the passive aggressive remarks that he would so often make 10 years prior. He continued to insinuate that my career, work ethic, and overall presence was laughable. I played the bigger man in person, killing him with kindness, and when I got home I spazzed. But “Joke” became more than your corny “diss track to the teacher who never believed in me” type song. It became a work of art that encompassed an everlasting theme in my life. Being Yourself, and being proud of who you are. 

I realized that I have spent so much of my life here on earth wearing masks, trying to fulfill other people’s perceptions of me, only to burn out some days wondering why I’m this way… wondering who I am in general. Subconsciously, I have surrounded myself with so many people that are unapologetically themselves no matter the situation, and I’ve always admired that skill. A lot of those people have said that I exhibit that trait as well, but I’ve never felt that way about myself. Maybe I am mirroring their energy and I feel comfortable enough to shine in front of them because they showed me the way. This year, I started really listening to what THOSE people have said about me… really taking in why I am loved by my friends and why I am unique as a person. 

With “Joke” I wanted every aspect of myself to shine through the song’s production. I performed a sketch with funny voices during the intro of the track, I produced an 8-bit video game styled instrumental, I sampled my grandmother and mother, and I added an instrumental and tonal shift midway through the track. That being said, I love doing funny voices, I love video games, I love my family, and I love beat switches and moody contrast. So why not put all of those things in a song, regardless of what other people think? These are just some of the things in a long list of interests that make me: ME! And I plan on showing the rest of those special attributes throughout the rest of my career.

Hey, I am San Holo, an artist, producer, DJ, and songwriter from The Netherlands and currently living in LA! I started making music when I was 13 years old and played in different bands throughout high school with my best friends. I grew up loving punk and alt-rock music which inspired me to learn how to play the guitar. I studied guitar at Rotterdam’s Codarts University of the Arts which is also where I also started to develop a love for beat making and music production.

I started producing electronic music and making remixes of songs like Dr. Dre’s “The Next Episode” which exploded on Soundcloud and YouTube. I released one of my first original San Holo tracks “We Rise” in 2015 and “Light” in 2017 along with many other songs that I still play in my shows to this day. I’ve had the opportunity to tour around the world and perform at incredible venues and festivals since then. In 2018, I released my debut album titled album1 on my record label, bitbird. I spent months at an Airbnb in Los Angeles producing the music, writing the lyrics and singing on many of the tracks myself, alongside great friends and collaborators such as The Nicholas, Thorwald, Bipolar Sunshine and more. I found myself back in the same part of town (Echo Park) years later while I was recording my second album, bb u ok?.

One day when I got back home after a long tour, I felt inspired and I spontaneously made a little beat on my phone while laying in bed. I found this phone beat on my computer recently, I almost forgot that I made it! I really like the raw nature of this beat, it’s very unpolished and definitely not perfect... But somehow a very strong emotion shines through all the imperfections. About 95% of what you hear on this track was recorded and produced on my iPhone, including the vocals! I wanted to share this raw version with you (which will be exclusive for Sound.XYZ) and hope it inspires you to make something special, whether that’s music or any other form of art! - San Holo ↑%

Everyone goes through their own lows and highs in life, and in a way, that’s such a unifying thing. I’m obsessed with the word “Sonder,” - the realization that each random passerby is living a life as vivid and complex as your own—populated with their own ambitions, friends, routines, worries and inherited craziness. Every person you pass by in life has their own story, in a way you might think this separates us… but actually, the opposite is true: It connects us. 

I wanted to write a song about sonder and remind myself to embrace everything that life throws my way, whether I might think it’s good or bad. Sometimes the lows in life end up being an incredible lesson that actually turns out to be a high after all. Which brings the question: What if the lows aren’t actually that bad, if you learn to accept what is. Everything you go through in life shapes you as a person. In a way you can say your memories are always a part of you… Our memories on rewind… All The Lows, All The Highs. - San Holo ↑%

‘Higher’ started in a very unusual way for me. A very, very, unusual way. My friend Salvador Breed sent me a video of a parrot vocalising / imitating a percussive rhythm. It sounded like the parrot had been hearing drums and was imitating those sounds. But something in the rhythm immediately triggered me. It sounded like the parrot had been hearing some pretty complex rhythms, it sounded to me like it was switching between straight and triplet time in every bar. (In non technical terms, within four counts it would constantly switch between two completely different rhythmical feels.) When I heard this and realised what kind of opportunities this complexity could give, I immediately ran upstairs to my attic studio and tried imitating / reproducing the groove that I thought the parrot must have heard and was imitating / reproducing.

The triplet feel has something very non-european to it, I’ve been into exploring different takes on rhythm a lot. I’ve been cratedigging on Bandcamp for South American club music, and also been listening to African pop and club music quite a lot. As with every obsessive listening period I go through, it’s only a matter of time before this really starts translating in my output. The same influences are very clearly audible in my ‘Ugly’ remix for Big Dope P and Mighty Mark, I think. ‘Higher’ goes a bit further in rhythmical complexity than where I left off with ‘Ugly’. But as always, my goal with club music is not to make something that sounds complex. The complexity in the groove and the sound has to come across intuitive and immediate, that’s always been the goal, both with Noisia and in my solo work.

I started it in the attic studio upstairs in my house. Then I worked on it in LA from my covid isolation room, because I wanted to play a more finished version at my Brownies and Lemonade show, which was recorded and an early version of Higher appears around the 25 minute mark: https://soundcloud.com/iamthys/thys-brownies-and-lemonade. I mixed the tune in the studio, and then worked on it in airplanes (thank god for noise cancelling headphones!) and hotels travelling to shows and holiday destinations. I finished the track in a full-on heatwave, on a laptop and headphones, in swimwear with a fan pointed at me, while on vacation in Italy :D It’s got quite a story, this one!

The artwork is a collab between Shy1 (one of Amon Tobin’s many pseudonyms) who made the weird golden bird statue illustration, and Tom Jager, who does a lot of the art for my label Eccentric O and also does a lot of amazing work for Noisia and Vision.

"Myōken" is the Pole Star - that guiding light which, in ancient Japan, was the focus of a Taoist movement in the 7th Century. I love the idea of mythical and folkloric symbolism tied to creative expression and narrative - the idea of old stories being one with futurist stories and using the wisdom of all that to guide us as we venture into a new reality...

This instrumental broken-beat track dips into so many things I love - freeform harmony, piano and synths painting the introspective opening - the Pole Star shining bright and universal... then the intro music gets resampled and flipped as we sidestep into the samples n beats world of my early 00's London underground club years - the urgency and intention of machine-gridded rhythms juxtaposed with the resampled organics of the intro. 

When it comes to tribalism in music, Fela Aníkúlápó Kuti is a perennial inspiration and I wanted to bring some of his vibes into the mix, writing a Fela-influenced melody hook and topping it off with breakbeats and jazz improvisations on the rhodes, bringing us full circle to all the things I love to blend... soulful harmony, syncopated rhythm and free-wheeling improvisation - the jazz soundclashed with something for the dancer's dancer.

executive produced by sunny b aka bizzle bizz

this song is so insane to me, and the best part is how its creation was such a journey

pt. 1 conception (5.18.22)

mood swings started may 18, 2022 when i had an in-person session with rohan (roho), we had already made two or three songs together virtually but had never met in person and wow he is very tall. also one of the kindest, easiest to get along with, and most effortlessly talented people i've worked with. we started the session the same way all my favorite sessions start, with about 2.5 hours of talking. i think this was before eth went down such sweet and innocent times.

eventually, we started working and the first thing that rohan played was the piano chords, we went through a few versions before we landed on the ones you hear (first time they come in is when i start rapping). he plays all his drums by hand on a keyboard, which is why they feel so human. i've seen very very very few people do it in person, and nobody as well as he does. he talks and makes jokes while he comes up with the craziest shit its insane. there are like 3-4 different drum patterns throughout this song its insane.

as the instrumental started to take shape i started having ideas for raps. i wrote a very long verse (cut it down by about 12 bars in the final version) and felt like i was truly in the 'flow' for the first time in months. i had been struggling with feeling a lot of self-judgement whenever i created for a while but working with rohan unlocked a playfullness and free-spiritedness that i hadn't tapped into for a while. kind of a similar feeling i get from yelling on twitter honestly.

i recorded my verse in one take as well as a hook idea that was very different from what this song ended up being. we left the session with a verse and a hook recorded and a super rough layout of the instrumental.

from there i took it home and worked on it that night, adding the distortion to the bass and developed out the arrangement and my vocal mix a little more. i was in my studio at my house with a couple friends who were gassing me up.

pt.2 may-july 
(forgot about the song)

it didn't fit on the new album i'm working on so i just put it to the side and didn't think i'd come back to it. i would listen to it from time to time and play it for people and the reactions were always super positive but i didn't know where to 'put' it in my discography.

pt.3 july 2022
i traveled 6 times from june 19th - july 26th and the song was finished while i was still living out of my suitcases

at this point jon and i had been talking about working for a couple of months, and i had sent him a different song i wanted him to get on. i think i had already sent this song to another artist and showed it to jon on a whim. but he connected with this one instantly and said he was writing to it.

a week or two passed and he sent me his vocals. i started working on them in miami and finished them in san antonio in sunny's apartment. after i mixed his voice i spent a day or two changing the production around his verse to fit what he was saying. i recorded some vocals / adlibs over his verse to add to it and added that skit between hook2/verse2 while sunny was studying at her table.

at this point sunny b's executive production really kicked in. she told me i needed a new hook, and made a few changes in production to jon's verse and later mine. very key addition of the tire screeching sound in jon's verse by bizzle. 

i bounced a version of the song with the hook taken out just so i could imagine new ideas in its place. sunny's in medical school and is doing clinical rotations now so i dropped her off every morning at 5:55am. on the way back one morning i started playing "Mood Swings v.8 [no hook]". I wasn't trying to write to it, but when the hook came around i started singing the melody for the new hook and i got really excited.

if u are reading this tweet "mood swiiingiiiinnggggg" and tag me or jon on twitter and one of us will send u a customized selfie response it'll be great. this is to reward u for really reading this long-ass thing.

it came about really effortlessly after that. i wrote the hook parked in her car, playing the music too loud at 6am and spent the next hour or so figuring out how to record it, and deciding that the intro needed to just be the hook with the distorted bass.

a couple days later sunny mentioned how my verse felt too long and helped me pick out 8-12 bars that needed to get cut out. the pitched up swearing ending of the verse was always there with the beeps but it didn't have context so i added in the 'talk show' skit and that was pretty much the song.

my favorite song i’ve ever made.

it was an unexciting saturday morning in my south florida suburb. i’d spent the majority of my life moving around but this specific street had been around for enough years to start to feel like home. if you’d had live footage of my street at 6:00 am, you’d see a series of peaceful front lawns and one with a flurry of movement. a little guy (me) excitedly shoving every last household item into my car as i prepped myself for the 14 hour drive to nashville.

months before, i received what i had interpreted as a series of divine signs to take a chance on myself. i’d saved up some money that i hoped would sustain me for the following year. i was going to go after music full time for the first time ever.

i’d arranged to stay in a friend’s spare bedroom for cheap. my plan was to deliver food a few hours each day and work on music the rest of the time.

i promised my parents that if i didn’t make it big in a year, i’d move back home and take up my career as an airline pilot that i’d put on hold for music. i didn’t think i’d have to, i’d always believed so deeply in my ability to make shit shake. 


the next 12 months were some of the most blissful and painful months of my life.

the best moments: i made music with people i’d looked up to for years, made huge strides towards finding an audience, and found a new community in web3.

the worst moments: a lot of shame, feeling like i’d disappointed the people closest to me, spending nights paralyzed unable to figure out my next steps.

on month 11, i was processing the impending reality that despite all my progress and work i wouldn’t be able to make my 1 year deadline. 

i had to readjust.

Since this beginning of this year, I’ve been living in the new me. The new me that has had time to heal, grow spiritually, mature emotionally, and feel on a deeper level that I didn’t know a man could feel. Prayer and therapy have beyond good to me.

On the week of February 6th, I was set to experience some of the most emotional moments of my life and I had no clue. Moments that would seem regular to someone else. These were good emotional moments on the way, of course.

On Thursday, February 10th I would release my Genesis NFT alongside some friends (virtually). A special moment for me because I truly enjoy my tribe and doing great things with them. These aren’t people I just release music with. These are close friends who I love and care for deeply.  We brought our lifestyle of intentional community to the Blockchain.

On Friday, February 11th I would celebrate my Birthday with my close family. Me, my mother, my wife, my sister, and her boyfriend all went out to eat at one of my favorite restaurants. Dinner was great but the conversation and laughter was food for the soul.

On Saturday, February 12th I would celebrate my Birthday with my close friends. We played games, drank, ate good and just enjoyed each other’s company. During our time, my wife called for a toast to acknowledge me. I didn’t have many words…which is different for me in moments like those. Just, “thank you all for coming through. I love you all, salud!” I went to bed late that night not only warm and tipsy but my soul’s cup was filled to the brim.

That week is what birthed me writing and producing this song. All the moments I described may be normal to other people, especially on the week of one’s birthday. But I felt the love on such a DEEPER level than ever before because of my healing experience.

All the healing I had been doing allowed my cup to be overflowed with a level of love I never felt before.

Hi, I’m Kacy Hill. I’m from Phoenix, AZ, now based in Los Angeles. 

Back in 2014, I signed to G.O.O.D. Music and released my debut album, “Like A Woman” three years later.  While I’m thankful for the crash course in the inner workings of the industry my major label experience gave me, I ultimately wanted out (badly). After almost a year of quite literally following Kanye West around to try and get a meeting, I was finally dropped and have been releasing music independently since 2018.

With each of my subsequent album releases I have experimented more with production and the amount of freedom I give myself to make mistakes. In my second album “Is It Selfish If We Talk About Me Again”, I was able to dictate the sounds I heard in my head to collaborators, though rarely sitting down at the computer to dig into the engineering of those sounds. My most recent album, “Simple, Sweet, and Smiling”, was a window into engineering and producing my own music, partially fueled by lockdowns and the inability to actually collaborate in person. 

“If I Could Say” is the first song I’m putting out into the world that I’ve produced and written (and played saxophone on!) entirely on my own. I’m less focused on perfection these days and more interested in what feels most fun and fulfilling to me. I love making music and at this point in life, I pursue whatever will allow me to keep loving the process.

Waterfalls is one of my best performing songs on DSP's with it currently sitting just under 1 million streams. Where Loaded was more of a fun song without any deep meaning, writing Waterfalls was a far more cathartic experience for me. It's about trying to let go of the things the subconscious holds onto, which I think anyone with neurotic tendencies will be able to relate to.
