I was born and raised on a farm in Candelo, Australia, about seven hours from Sydney. I’ve lived in the states for the past ten years making and releasing music whilst performing around the world. In 2017 I decided to take a break from the industry, since then I have grown as a producer, and my artistic style has changed. Being off the road gave me time to focus on creating again and I honed in on a new goal of learning to sing. Singing has completely changed the way I think about and create music, I am incredibly excited to share this new journey with you all! 
 
This new era begins with my first new single, “Sandman.” The song slowly came to life over a four-year period, adding all the elements bit by bit to finally create the full track using an array of vintage synths and a live drum kit. I was influenced by rock & roll music at this time so wanted to give the song a more aggressive edge, filled with a huge bass line and melodic leads to create the full experience! With the lyrical meaning of the song I prefer you to take away your own interpretation as that's truly what art is. But if I had to describe it in one word it would be unification!
 
Over the past few years, the industry landscape has changed drastically. Even so, no shift has been more compelling than the power of the NFT community and web3. Being new to the NFT community, this is something that I’m really excited about! There is no better time to enter the community than on the heels of new music, it feels like the perfect storm!

this song child of mine, called "out of focus", is particularly special because it represented a much-needed return to form for me at a very difficult time. music creators can probably relate to the idea that your creative process evolves drastically as you become deeper enveloped by the industry. although i can stay busy with sessions every day sometimes weeks will go by and i'll realize i haven't touched a piano once. songwriting was born as a sacred, solo activity for me: sitting, emoting at the piano, having no idea what i was doing. so although i am grateful that now i can create a song in a multitude of ways, i can start burning out or feeling inexplicably lost if i spend too much time away from the form that brought me to love this expression in the first place. fuel that with a tasty breakup, and this song had everything i needed. i sat, and wrote this top to bottom at the piano, no pre-conceived concept, or melody, or worry if the chorus was "lifting" enough, or if i was being original enough... just did what my instincts wanted to do. i wrote this about feeling pushed away by a person, but as i listen to it now it takes on a new meaning feeling often shoved aside with my career as well. she's truly one of my favorites, and i hope you it makes you feel something🤍

The Initial idea for “No Landing” started with a grungy bass line made on an old vintage Memorymoog. This bass line sparked my creative energy, and I started to build out the track with drums, synths and continued expanding on that initial bass line. I arrived at a sound that seemed simple, but still sounded crisp and full-toned. The track was pure, so I didn’t feel it needed to be overcomplicated and oversaturated with wasteful production. To the ear, the elements of “No Landing” are stripped back, which helps encapsulate the energy I wanted the song to exude. 

This single started with production, and I eased into the lyrics, letting the smooth gliding beat serve as the track’s core concept–never forcing a single word. Ultimately, this track has a sonic, unhurried sound that makes listeners feel like they’re floating, never worrying about landing back on the ground.

Remember that thing you couldn’t free yourself from? The habit, the relationship, the mindset. The one that you know will crush you if you stay in any longer.. this is Assassin.

Shortly after signing our deal with the new venture between Mark Hoppus, Pete Wentz, and Sherry Saeedi called Verswire we began a month long stint of writing sessions geared toward creating new music for our next project so we could come out of the gates swinging. In these sessions Assassin was born.

Assassin came from a session with a writing and production group called the Four Horsemen (Aerosmith, Ozzy Osbourn, Highly Suspect, Carrie Underwood, Buckcherry, Kelly Clarkson, etc.)

Going into the process, we said our goal is “Bieber level hooks with the heaviest guitars you can get” and Assassin was born. It was one of those songs that wrote itself. It felt easy, and that is not always the case. 

When it came time to produce the record we had a roadmap in our heads of how we wanted the sonics to come across. We’ve been practicing getting a song written in entirety before adding any production elements. It’s like our ultimate test to see if the song is good or not… if it can it hold up being playing with just an acoustic guitar then we know it's a good song.

“Crypto ₿oy” is a wake-up call for all the chart-watchers, candle-counters, and JPEG-flippers that find a way to bring crypto into any conversation, no matter what it’s about.

We all know them — checking OpenSea like it’s instagram, obsessing over prices, hodling this, shorting that and unable to focus on anything except Discord.

As exciting as crypto is, and as likely as it is to revolutionize finance in the coming years, I want to shift our attention to a very urgent issue, which is the possibility of SCOTUS overturning Roe v Wade. This attack on reproductive rights is something we should be talking about as loudly as a crypto boy talks about NFTs*. It’s imperative that we band together and fight to protect our fundamental rights. To help bring this together I partnered with Nadya Tolokonnikova of Pussy Riot, who I love and respect, to create the custom art for this NFT.

100% of the proceeds of the sale of this NFT will be donated to The Center for Reproductive Rights (https://reproductiverights.org), a legal nonprofit that is able to accept donations in cryptocurrency.

hi. i’m sad alex. i’m from delaware, which is a real place other than that wayne’s world line. i have been doing music since i was a very small human and professionally in both nashville and la for the last 9 years. 

i think my biggest strength and weakness in this industry has been my versatility. i can wake up one day wanting to write a sad introspective folk song about my life’s failures, and the next day i write a song about my tits (for real, you can see it on my tiktok and dsps, it did quite well). this makes me a valuable writer and producer in the room for other projects, but can often make decisions about my own the most difficult. because that would require defining the hardest question of all for me, “who am i?” 

but occasionally i make a song baby that defies all that doubt. it flows out effortlessly, i don’t follow any rulebook or try and mold it into something it isn’t. and as a result, it finally feels fully me. it was a no brainer for my genesis sound release to give you one of these precious bbs. this one is partly about a guy that i have written probably 200 songs about, one of those beautifully catastrophic heartbreaks that turns you into an endless bubbling well of emotion. if you haven’t had one of these, i 10/10 recommend for your full experience as a human. but the majority part is about how when you hold onto someone that tightly, after they’re gone it can be hard to figure out where to put that love. the manic titling of this song represents that little voice inside screaming the bitter tired truth that for me, it’s unfortunately often easier to love someone else than to learn to love myself. something i’m working on, shoutout free kaiser therapy. 

i’m very grateful for my experience in the industry the last few years, that same aforementioned epic heartbreak ended up getting me a pub deal and record deal, and as a result i’ve had the opportunity to work with some incredible people, had many cool and fun times, etc. however a few months ago (by choice) i left both in an effort to build the career i want from the ground up. this is my first solo release since leaving my deal, which i wrote and produced fully myself. i’m so excited to connect with all of you and share what i have planned for the future. it is some of the best music and art i’ve ever made, which by saying that i guess means i AM in fact learning to love myself a little bit more xx

Welp... 
This songs inception came after an evening that could have been written into a coming of age Shakespeare dramedy.
Sparknotes version... 
Finding a love interest canoodling with a friend.. in your own house... only to turn around and say, it's you they're really interested in... 
The confusion!!

The beat for YEAHYEAHYEAHYEAH... was actually conjured up over 6 months prior to it being written while living in the old Hollywood home of famed director Orson Welles (Citizen Kane), and Frank Sinatra among other notorious names.
After our aforementioned incident.. the beat was pulled up again, and the lyrics "you make me depressed" were penned giving the original demo the title "DEPRESSED" before renaming it to "YEAHYEAHYEAHYEAH..." for the album release.

The Body Talks. Picture yourself walking through a crowd of people with a group of friends and hearing the most outlandish bids being called out like an auction. Primitive energy coming at you like hot breath inquiries on a loop. Dysregulated emotions brewing up in your space. A reflection of disunity within your mind,body,and environment. I feel at that point you’d be wanting some fresh air.  After 2020 I really missed dancing out in the city of Miami where I grew up, after being isolated for so long it felt foreign to be out. Reminiscing on my friends and I dressing up to impress ourselves to be quite honest, stepping into a party but by the time we’d arrive I am thinking “I should’ve done a few more reps at the gym” because I am now the protector of the group. The token masc femme needing to step in to interrupt that hungry energy for some peace just to dance freely and safely. Sheesh!

Fresh Air is like a nightlife manual I wrote,  a mantra to repeat before heading out for the night. It is quite comical preparing for a reaction from people when they get rejected. Feels like these days physiologically people are on a clock out here ready to tie something down for the moment. Anxiety and anticipation combined is a rude cocktail before the night out.
Call this song the energy protector! There are ways to respectfully approach the person you want to dance with.
On the contrary - there is something mysterious about non verbal connection and there’s nothing wrong with attention. I feel the most empowered when I am dancing and in my body so there’s this push and pull you’ll here in the song even melodically. The words “Back it up” I have heard in so many songs growing up so I decided to give it multiple meanings. Back it up, meaning Back up so I can Back it up. Also, make room so my shawtys can comfortably back it up on me as well. Ha! It was a lot of fun creating this with Jesse Boykins III with us both growing up in Miami. He fully understood the assignment sonically and morally! I am here to bring awareness to our 5 foot body with audio visual experiences. I have always been intrigued by the conversation between the brain and its podium. So, whether you’re at the gym or going out whatever city you are in allow your body to speak and enjoy the moment.

Summer of ‘21, Bordeaux, France. It rained, it rained, the sky and I didn’t stop crying. Today I call it cleansing, but back then I couldn’t even call it. My love at the time couldn’t call me either - he was slipping through my fingers by the day. Our relationship slowly died like a campfire that gets smaller while everyone sits around and watches the flames go down, quietly observing. As life would have it, the more we died, the more myself and my music came alive. A whole world opened at the expense of the demise of what I thought was my whole world.

I have good and bad news about heartbreak. The bad news is that it sucks. The good news is that in such deep waters, you can be nothing but honest. The urge to reclaim my identity washed over me and I decided it was time to bring every part of my being to life. With the love & support of my wonderful friends and producers Dean Woodson, Jean Castel, and Edouard Algayon, every sound, language, culture, flavor that makes up my DNA found its way to my fingertips and Boded was born. 

BODED (pronounced Bodèd), Hebrew for LONELY, sings the pain of the man I loved slipping away from me. His body was there, but his heart and spirit were no longer around. “BODED, wanted alive not dead.” When I lost him, I found myself and my sound. This song is a concoction of dying love, living beauty, the Israeli music I was raised on, many languages, few words, all united in harmony between the creaking walls of a castle in the south of France. I hope you enjoy my he(art) as much as I enjoy giving it to you.

The My Head In Your Hands drop featured an original drawing, animation and music. The project became the first NFT drop with a musical artist to ever gross over 1 million dollars, something that I am really proud of. “Tell Me The Truth” is the first song I have written since “I Feel Like I’m Drowning” that really stemmed from my most vulnerable honest self. Last year I moved from LA back home to NYC - the city where I wrote my first EP and album. “Tell Me The Truth” was the first song I wrote when I moved back. NYC just has a darker vibe that always leaks into my music when I am producing in the city. This song is definitely the song I am the most proud of on my new album. -  Two Feet

We made this song almost two years ago now. One of us had just exited a long term relationship and was going through it, bad. This was the first song we recorded following that situation. It felt like a message. it wasn't planned. it all just came out, with ease. It was like a "hey, don't feel bad for yourself. fuck her. fuck everybody at that point really. Keep your head up, things are starting to happen with this music shit. Just keep going and getting better, you don't need anybody," type message.

This song just created itself basically. I think it was written in like 10-15 minutes. One of those special pieces that felt like it was made in a blackout. Those only tend to come together when you're going through some serious shit. And then without even realizing it, you're probably coping with it by creating that piece of art.

Little did we know, this was the beginning of what would become our album: 'PAIN MUSEUM'. Unconsciously, this song birthed an entire project. It wasn't until later that we made the correlation, but what we did know at that moment, was that we both were in pain. Under completely different circumstances, the one thing we knew we had in common was pain. We were both simultaneously dealing with depression and anxiety, for different reasons. But the glue that kept everything together was the fact that we were hurting together.

Pain became a central theme around all the new material we were creating, and then one day everything clicked. We're building an album. We're building a museum. And we have to credit "PNTHR" for giving birth to this entire concept and credit to the circumstances we dealt with for birthing this universe. We've nearly lost our minds on multiple occasions while building this museum, but it's finally yours on May 13th. No better way to open the museum, than with the exhibit that started it.

Hi I’m Cameron and this will be my first release in over 6 years. I can’t tell you how grateful I am to sound.xzy for giving me the opportunity to release a song.  About 8 years ago I bought a grand piano from Paul Kostabi in upstate NY. Even though he gave me a deal I emptied my bank account doing so and could barley afford to move it back to Brooklyn. For the next two years I had nothing but that 6’8” conservatorium grand piano, which only fit in the freight elevator by a couple millimeters, a bed and a white shag carpet rug. That piano really altered my life. I think I played it for about 5 hours a day. Eventually I felt like I wasn’t doing the thing justice so craigslisted some piano lessons. My teacher knew I couldn’t read music so I would send him songs I wanted him to learn and teach me every week. Either that or he’d help me re-voice the backward songs I was writing at the time. Eventually he taught me how to split a chord across octaves, sounds so simple but it really opened my mind to melody and harmony. I started moving chromatically down scales with this newly found technique and let my ears go where they wanted to, if that doesn’t sound too pretentious. That’s where this song was born. It’s been rattling around on my hard drive since then until this year where I had a conversation which free’d me, in way, to let this song happen.     

Airport Beers is about being in flux. The consciousness of transit or a change,  between places or somewhere more metaphysical, creates instability which can be embraced or feared. It depends on whether you’re intrigued by uncertainty or not. Beginnings and endings have always seemed recurring or cyclical to me. Everything in between is never the same. It’s as much about what you do with your time in flux as it is about beer.

There’s a lot of good that’s going on in the music NFT space and I’m so happy to see and be a part of it. I’m honestly glad that I’ll be able to connect directly with my supporters of my art and continue to change lives with my music.

I’m originally from Jacksonville, Florida. I’m a military brat, my dad retired in Florida and me and the rest of family settled there. I couldn’t stay still, so when I graduated high school, I moved to New York City to live my dream of becoming a recording artist. I lived out my dream there for 8 years and right after me and my ex broke up after 5 years together, I decided I needed to move to Los Angeles, California 2020 before the pandemic. I remember this place being one of the stops during the tour I was on back in 2019 with Samoht. I came here   and I can recall saying that LA reminded me of a tall glass of water it was so refreshing and I needed this because I got a chance to take a break from my thoughts.
I’ve been here for two years now and my experience have been  great in so many ways. I finally get a chance to sit with myself and get to know who Devin Tracy is. I’m glad for what New York has taught me and I do miss the food honestly.

The song AMAZING is a beautiful piece about being sexually free. When I wrote this song I was on cloud 9, high as a kite and I didn’t want to come down. Lost in my apartment slightly depressed and still questioning where I was in my life and my relationship with self at the time..I kept smiling at the fact I was beginning to feel free. All I can think about was the night before and the lyrics started flowing. The song is about having intimacy with a person you really like, and you haven’t had that in a while or for others you haven’t had it in that capacity at all. It also speaks about feeling free from judgement and wanting to have that feeling over and over again. That feeling you get where you think can touch God, that feeling you had when you’re on a vacation in Turks and Caicos Island and you dive in the water, and you feel how clean and beautiful it is as you swim to the surface. The adrenalin of you getting on your favorite roller coaster ride and in the beginning, you see the drop before the ride starts and once it starts you have no other choice but to commit.  That’s the  feeling, I had the feeling  again and again and again and when I wanted it I got it. During the pandemic we all know  some people haven’t had the correct intimacy from the right person. I would hear stories of people having amazing sex which is great but afterwards there was no recollection of it happening again or of this person staying. My experience was a bit different I can remember every piece, every placement, the smell, the sound, the colors I saw. It was almost like a musical cinematic movie but with a lot of drama and live action. In other words, a bunch of passion between two special individuals. The song is also therapeutic and calming because to me that’s what it was felt like in the beginning. I’m a cancer so my emotions run real deep.

I really hope this song resonates with you and give you therapy like it did for me. I want others to see the importance of being sexually free and being themselves.  It’s ok to have an experience with other people and do what your heart desires. As long as the intentions are in the right place there’s going to be good that comes out it regardless of where you are. Just make sure you protect yourself and continue to love yourself. Ok Im done !

Love You, 
Devin Tracy

My debut release ‘everything sucks’ had a huge viral moment which helped it spread globally, hitting the #1 spot on the viral charts on Spotify and staying there for several weeks. I’m a pretty emotional guy and that seeps into my music and lyrics. ‘Disaster’ is no exception to that. I wrote this song as a part of a songwriting challenge where I try to start and finish a song in 77 minutes. This was the first song of the challenge and I have been surprised to see how much people relate to it! Disaster is about the type of person it hurts to love. Someone who’s problems are often self-inflicted and ends up hurting the people around them: even the people that love them the most. I’m really proud of it, especially as I wrote and produced the song by myself in my home studio. I really hope it resonates with you in someway!

A year ago I moved back to my country of origin, Georgia. I had been living in the Netherlands for most of my life and felt like I needed to reconnect with home.

A lot happened in the course of a year while being there. I’ve been fortunate enough to spend time with family, make the best music I’ve ever made all while being surrounded by the mountains.

One of the songs I’ve made in this period is “Hurt Nobody”. A song about trying to be righteous in a world that isn’t. A song about honesty. 

This song was set to release on a NFT music platform earlier. It unfortunately didn’t go through because of them being very focused on selling out which went at the expense of the relationship they were building with me. We’re doing it right this time.

I made this song at a time in my life where I really feel the world doesn't know. They have no idea what I've been through, and they have no idea what I'm about to do. You see I've been at the top for throughout it all and here to stay, life had crazy plans for me and just as quick as something can go good, it could go bad too, and it went 7 years bad. 

Yeah alot of time has passed since the world has heard from me. A lot has changed too… But not me I’m still the same live wire everybody loves, I’m still smiling ear to ear, and I’m still dancing for the girls making the people laugh. 

No matter what life throws at me I’ll always find a way to smile through it all. Locked away for years in prison didn’t break me… So they tried a little harder and locked me up while being locked up but that didn’t do it either. 

They try to dim your light when they put you in those dungeons. They try to make the time hard, but I knew that one day I’d be free again.

I sent out a batch of instrumentals I produced to someone close to me. she said she liked one beat in particular. I had already tried recording to it but wasn't happy with the result. After I spoke with her I decided to have another go at it and made this song to it. 

Hideout is about taking time to yourself and putting your energy towards things that are really important to you. The title of the song also is a nod to the place I'm staying at currently which I refer to as my mountain hideout.

It feels good to be making use of Sound.xyz in a way were I can freely drop whenever I feel like. the artwork for the golden egg is a signed picture taken at the mountain hideout.

My name is felly.  I’m from Connecticut originally but stay out west in Los Angeles. I found a lane in the music scene a few years ago after years of putting out albums/mixtapes/projects on bandcamp, soundcloud- really whatever was available at the time.  We’re talking 5-6 years ago.  During the golden days of indie platforms I hit a chord in a scene I’m still trying to understand. It is wild to think about how things have evolved since.  

In the early days at school at USC in Los Angeles I helped to form a collective called 2273- named after the dorm room my friends and I would create in.  I kept putting out albums/mixtapes and eventually found myself on multiple nation-wide tours as a headline.  Just my friends and I, selling out large rooms all across the United States.

Fast forward a few years and I’m back living in Los Angeles, after making a pit stop in Brooklyn.  I signed to Sony who I dropped a couple projects with, and then most recently signed with 300 Entertainment.   Throughout this journey of creating the art that speaks true to me and my fans, I’ve met and connected with thousands of people across the US and shared this love for music, life, and we’ve all gotten closer to a feeling of oneness.  I’m filled with gratitude to be a creator and be able to play.  The shows are crazy and my team and I get more inspired to create timeless music by the day.  

Bad Radio is the first single off an invisible project I have that is entirely self-produced.  I say invisible because I’m not sure if it will ever come out, though it contains some of the most personal, true to me songs.  There is no reason for why it won’t come out, but the time for it hasn’t come yet.  I’m thankful to Sound XYZ for providing the first glimpse of this album that the public is able to see.  The songs on this EP are folky, dark, driving.  Very different from the sunny light hip hop sound that I’ve been known to come with.  

To sort of spoil it, the idea behind bad radio is a reflection of how I felt about love at the time.  It’s like, when you hear your favorite song on the radio, but the signal won’t quite come in.  Do you stay there in the static, waiting to hear whatever notes you can make out.  Or do you bash the fucking radio and drive off a cliff?  

The choice is yours.

Young Fel.

When I started writing songs on bass in 2011 I felt like it gave me some kind of power, I really believe just holding a bass makes you emotionally stronger, you just feel instantly like a badass, the weight of the instrument that you’re holding feels substantial, the depth of the tone, the simplicity in the notes. There’s weirdly so much in that stuff. It’s an incredibly empowering instrument and a useful tool when finding your voice and getting in touch with your feelings. I found a new voice for myself when I started writing on bass, it was writing on bass that led to songs like this. I found it such an important way for me to express myself and lots of the heartache I was going through during my 20s. 

So many songs about bad choices, bad love, bad endings. ‘Try to forget’ feels like the Girl Talk (my 3rd album) era to me. There are still songs from the Girl Talk era coming out of me and still so many locked away in a chamber. It’s a time that was so formative for me, I was dealing with true independence, facing demons, facing bad guys, making bad choices. It felt a bit like Buffy season 5. I felt I was facing the world and was seeing it’s dark underbelly, realising I was an adult but still just a girl underneath. Music has always been the best way for me to deal with my life and this was never more true during this era. I love still being able to access that moment and feeling, it’s youthful, rebellious and angsty, it’s still in my stomach.

‘Try to forget it’ was written in a rehearsal room, there’s a ton of songs written in dingy dark rooms with dirty old amps and microphones, sounds of drums coming through the walls from other bands, cold damp rooms, bad lighting and bad air. I love spending time in these caves and playing for hours, sometimes nothing comes of it but every now and then you catch onto something you’re playing with and it becomes a song, that’s what happened with 'Try to forget it', it was just an afternoon in a rehearsal room jamming on the bass. 

‘Try to forget it’ is a punk love disaster song, written on bass about the car crash you know is coming. In love with someone that doesn’t have respect for you? in love with someone that has hurt you already? You try to forget it, try to make excuses for them and their actions despite knowing better. You make your own bed and you lie in it, you’re aware you should change the sheets, you should probably burn the bed and move house, but you’re not ready. Something is making you stay. Somehow you’re stuck. Only you can choose to walk away. Is it hedonism or self destruction that keeps you entangled? Is it your own sickness, some kind of addiction. I feel like for so many years I put myself in situations and relationships that I couldn’t seem to escape from. I knew they weren’t going to end well “I see you in my rear view mirror” I knew what was coming, yet I’m not sure I was aware I could change anything. So I stayed until the bitter end. This song was written in the middle of those feelings, the midst of my own struggle with personal boundaries, self respect. I clung to my bass as it made me feel powerful and I feel like it helped me release a lot of these thoughts, I just couldn’t quite hear myself. This song feels like a driving song to me, written about toxic love, a car crash you know is coming. You just keep trying and eventually you realise you can walk away, but until then, find a punk love disaster song that brings you some comfort.

Hello all,

My name is RIZ LA VIE, and this is my song, NITELITE. I began making this song in Malibu in May 2021, with my long time friend and creative partner Daniel Hartzog. I had brought Dan with me to Malibu after a shared traumatic loss of a friend, to create, swim, and heal, together. Out upon the hillside in Malibu, during our first weeks there, overlooking the expanse of ocean, we would see a giant full moon rise every night. A spectacle. My love of the moon is certainly not new but these felt like special views. I wrote the song about all things celestial, captivating, and endearing, the moon being the mascot of those qualities to me, and the chances of experiencing these qualities at all. I wrote about how, like a partner with an empathetic ear may hear out the woes of their loved ones from time to time, and may even occasionally lend guidance, the moon will listen like you are the only two in the universe, and how, like many instances in this life, if you take a moment to listen to it and give it the space to communicate, it just may reflect something you need to hear.

We continued working on NITELITE and the album at Dimension 70 Studios in NYC’s lower east side throughout June 2021, recording some sections just a couple days after broken collarbone surgery. It's a song that has always existed through and because of healing, support, and a bit of help from the cosmos. With a fresh coat of paint bringing it into 2022 and beyond, one of the guiding lights of my debut album is ready to see the light of day, and we’re very excited to present it to you all. 

Space therapy,  cosmic prayer, or shouting to the heavens, Nitelite is for moonlight lovers, chill thrill-seekers, and web3 natives. Y'all are amazing thanks for being an active part of this. If you ever need to yell something into the night sky, and don’t know what to say, don’t hesitate to use these words.

Falling in and out of love music
Being set free and being held captive music
Making and losing money music
And then making it back 2 fold music

Either way this life is a gem
This is my soundtrack to it

I'm very excited to be premiering my newest song Wonderland here on Sound. I think the premise of the lyrics and the sonics lend themselves very well to this new wonderland that is Web3. Being an independent artist coming up in this new age of technology, there are so many middlemen that stand between you and your potential fanbase and I'm so happy that I'm getting the opportunity to connect directly with supporters of art and lovers of music alike

I was born in Inglewood California and spent half of my childhood in Cali, and then my parents moved my brothers and me out to Louisiana where I finished high school. music for me has always been an escape from the world around me, and an outlet for a lot of internal conflicts I hadn’t yet learned to articulate as a kid. The day I picked up a guitar I felt something change inside me, it was a change that gave me hope in knowing there was something out there that could quell even the most vicious storms that were going on in my heart and in my life around me. 

Wonderland feels like a peaceful escape from reality, but the lyrics are a cry out to the world about mans (hu-man) relationship with themselves, and with the environment around them. I talk about how some people view a tree as a source of shelter or kindling to be burned for warmth, while others may view a tree as a living being and as a source of the very air we breathe. Now we all need shelter, but having an understanding and respect for nature is paramount because the earth can only give us exactly what we need. Any more than that throws the world out of balance, a lot of us live lives of excess without thinking about how every action has an equal and opposite reaction. Whether you look at things from a yin-yang perspective, or you view things like Newton, it's the same concept. 

I hope that this song brings people peace, even if for a few minutes and shows us that stillness and reflection are important for growth - we must be focused more on the natural progressions of life rather than the constant production of goods and services. Community is the only way forward in my mind and heart, and I am grateful to be a part of this community full of pioneers blazing a new path into the future! 

Peace 
~ Brandon ~

When making the music I love, I tend to keep my head down, and the volume up as music keeps me going. Music has played a significant role in my life, being my primary form of therapy. I was very insecure, introverted, and struggled with social anxiety as a kid. I still, to this day, enjoy my alone time much more than going out with others, but I no longer struggle the way that I used to because of music. 

As always, there comes a time when you have to look up and step out to take yourself to the next level. In doing so, you often receive a lot of pushback from people around you who don't agree with or understand your vision. This is entirely normal and expected when you're doing something great. One thing I personally didn't expect was for others' insecurities and traumas to get in the way of their support for what I do. I recall being very insecure in myself and my craft at one point, and as a result, I studied those that I felt were much better than me. This never made me not want to support what they were doing; It only attracted me more. As I venture deeper into the music industry, I notice that some people will know who you are and what you do but choose to ignore you because they don't want their shine taken away. This song offers a form of support while also addressing the issue at hand so that we can continue to grow as artists.

The song gives off a fun and groovy vibe to represent my understanding of dancing. I compare the issue to dancing because that's exactly what it is, a rhythmic (repeated) sequence of steps taken by multiple parties resulting in the form of entertainment. While the matter can be entertaining, the main focus is the conflict that can arise between both parties if they are not on the same rhythm. Insert the title, "Stick and Move," a boxing technique that I consider a dance representing the conflict between both parties. 

In the first verse, I express my interaction with some of these individuals who have slighted me in ways they may not have noticed and how it made me feel. Though it can get to me at times, I tend to be very forgiving and understanding which keeps my confidence up, igniting the fire within. The second verse goes deeper into the issue, explaining my thought process on understanding what's really happening and how to solve it. Ultimately we all need a little patience. Even when frustrations are high, the conversation can still be had in healthy ways so that we all can thrive and flourish within this industry.

WHY WEB3
Growing up queer in a small town meant it was always easier to talk to people online that I could relate to. Platforms like tumblr played a big role in cultivating a space & community, where I could connect with like-minded people. I have found this same sense of connectivity & community in Web3.
After the success of my independently funded & pushed EP, I went on multiple different label runs, meeting execs from every major label. I quickly realized that a lot of people in the music industry didn’t understand the vision of what I was trying to create, not allowing me to have full creative control and reins on my future. Technology, music & entertainment go hand- in-hand, so naturally, I have a big interest in creating a community on Web3 that can be a part of my journey & career as an artist, while simultaneously creating a blueprint for aspiring artists that want to retain creative control as well.
I want to encourage others to stop fighting for a seat at a table that was never built for them and instead create their own table, specially curated to their needs, interests and passions!

"Crashing" is the instrumental of my single "Again" w/ Juliana Chahayed, released Aug. 12th via Friends of Friends. The two songs were released as a double single as the lead for my upcoming EP "Always Less". 

I started on "Crashing" somewhere around a year ago while in the midst of a major identity crisis regarding my music, and abandoned it when I wasn't able to confidently flesh it out. Almost a year later, Juliana and I got in touch, and right away I knew I had the idea for her. I sent her what was then the demo version of "Crashing" and she quickly sent me back a vocal idea which instantly inspired and excited me. There's not a lot of vocalists I connect with or enjoy the sound of, but her voice so flawlessly fit over the instrumental, and I knew that was all that I was missing. 

Once the process began of finishing the song with Juliana's vocals, the instrumental came together much more naturally. Having that inspiration and foundation of the vocal layers really helped me see it through. I'm extremely proud of this instrumental which so vividly conveys the calm essence I wanted to communicate when first beginning the instrumental a year ago.

So... the last time I was here, I was trying to convince myself that I wasn't done working towards the "Finish Line". Thanks to the awesome supporters and engineers here at sound.xyz, we sold out instantly. Since then, I've been stretching between attempting to maintain relationships with extremely talented friends, working on heds.app, and generally keeping my head as down as possible. More recently, I've started to explore what it means to be a creative. When you start out your career with absolutely zero sense of infrastructure and a job title that doesn't exist yet, it's easy to feel overwhelmed by the stress of simply trying to survive. After 15 years of linking & building, many of my friends in the creative field struggle to find a tangible direction for them to go. I'm here to argue: there really is none. Winging it is truly the answer. Out of every decision in the creation of a record, the most exciting to me are still those "happy accidents". A knob slightly tweaked can add so much emotion, changing the direction of your process completely. That's the beauty in creativity to me. The ability to paint with your decisions, to maximize your creative return in order to create more, to increase your footprint in the culture of your choice. Bob Ross was really onto something.

Hey y'all, DLG. here 👋 

(You can call me Dave though, we're homies like that).

I started playing guitar when I was 6. I played classical guitar, with nylon strings. I loved the warmth of the instrument, how I could feel each note resonate in the wood grain against my chest. I spent many years taking lessons and playing in classical guitar recitals, freezing my ass off in a church somewhere on the edge of town. I would wear a black turtleneck and sit up straight as an arrow. 

As time passed, I decided that sometimes I wanted to hunch over when I played the guitar. I wanted to hum along to the notes, play random chords until something stuck, experiment more. I was always very adventurous with the rest of my art (mainly drawing, painting, and origami at the time), so writing my own songs felt like a natural step to take. 

I began to try properly singing when I was about 12. Prior to then, my singing experience was mainly singing along to Cake and The Beatles on road trips. I was angsty and I needed an outlet, so I would sit crosslegged in my living room and belt out whatever lyrics crossed my mind.  Garageband entered the picture a couple years later, and the songs I was writing in my living room (and with my rock band, Fat Boy and The Midnight Snackie) could be immortalized on my hard drive. 

I kept writing songs throughout high school, as well as creating physical art. Drawing, painting, printmaking, origami, and sculpting have always been very important parts of my life, and my music is heavily influenced not just by other musicians, but by painters & illustrators as well. My favorites include Joan Miró, Dalí, Peter Sis, and Chris Van Allsburg. 

Near the end of highschool, I discovered Ableton, and formed a band with my close friend and collaborator Josh Mosier. I eventually explored producing on my own, and began to tinker with an EP during my freshman year of college.

I spent a lot of time during college locked away in my room, in a manic daze, determined to finish songs. I was addicted to getting better. I released songs with no intention of having them heard or being a successful musician; I just needed to get them out there. It was my form of therapy.

For my artist name, I chose DLG., the initials of my last name and the nickname that everyone in college already called me.

One song after another, and I started to get some recognition. Suddenly, the hours locked away in my room didn't seem so crazy. I realized I should take music as seriously as I always wanted to, and the rest is history. 

This song, Runnin' Back, is the first track I've finished since moving to LA from Austin a week ago. It was written, recorded, produced, and mixed by me in my living room. The artwork (as with most of my recent album artwork) was painted by my mom Joyce Rosner, an award-winning artist & designer.

Thanks for listening 🧡

Growing up, I played drums and guitar in rock bands and then shifted to a singer-songwriter sound as I started writing and recording my own music. I’m currently based in San Diego and have been leaning into a nostalgic, upbeat 80’s sound. I love creating music with huge punchy drums, reverberated guitar lines, and layered vocals.

“Sober” is an anthem for that sober friend at a party. When I wrote this I was so over people acting like I owed them an explanation for why I didn’t want to drink. There was a long time that I felt isolated because of this and I wanted to explore that feeling. 

This is the most proud I have been of a song’s sound quality and writing to date. I’m so excited to share it with the world, alongside a music video shot on 65mm film by No Storage Productions. I appreciate those who want to join me on this journey and am especially grateful to be on a platform with so many other talented artists!

Hey, I’m Munn. I grew up in Indiana but currently live in Nashville! When I was 15 I started playing guitar and writing music but didn't take it seriously until my Sophomore year of college.
     
In the summer of 2018, leading up to my Sophomore year, my engagement with my fiancée fell through, and I lost all interest in school. I was struggling to heal from the breakup, and I had no idea what I wanted to do with my life. It was during this time that I wrote my first song in over a year called I Tried. To this day, I can't describe how I felt after making that song. I had finally found my way to heal, and, from then on, creating music was all I wanted to do.
     
Around this time, a producer that I had connected with in 2017, named Dylan Stiles, was sending me beats every day. I would write and record to these beats every night using an Xbox headset and GarageBand. As time went on, we both decided that the best thing we could do was to drop out of school and go all-in on music. In July of 2019, with less than 4,000 monthly listeners on Spotify, Dylan and I moved to Nashville to do just that.
     
After a failed EP, we realized I needed a better strategy for putting out music. We decided that the best thing I could do was put out a new song every two weeks until one caught traction. On September 6th, 2019, we released the first song following this plan called I Lost Myself.
     
Currently, I am a fully independent singer/songwriter based out of Nashville. My team and I have been building my fan base over the past couple years and have amassed over a hundred million streams, a million monthly listeners on Spotify, 200k+ subs on YouTube, and more, all independently. While our music hasn’t stopped growing by any means, moving into the NFT space for additional support and a new way to connect with listeners was the logical next step for us.

Before dropping out of college and leaving everything behind for music, I was attending a small college alongside my then-fiancé and many hometown friends. When my engagement fell through, I was crushed, and everything about that town that I once loved became insignificant to me. In fact, I started to hate all of it. I couldn’t bare to be in that place any longer, so I left it all behind; I had to. I’d go back from time to time to visit my friends that still lived there, but something about that place would always have me unsettled, feeling anxious and genuinely sick to my stomach. From all of this, my song “the reason i hate home” was born. I knew when I was writing this song that it was something special because it would be something so many people resonate with. My ex fiancé ruined that town for me, and she’s the reason I hate home.

Music is a universal language--truly loved by all. Through creating this song, both Morgxn and I were able to find some peace during these tumultuous times.  

The origin story: The introduction actually began at a Halloween party hosted at Charli XCX's home. Fast forward to the pandemic, Morgxn sends me a very special vocal he had written in London just before the lockdown. The message and lyrics resonated so deeply that I had to create a song that truly represented how I felt.

Though the song was written before our society shutdown--it had more meaning during.  This song is about the idea of craving touch that feels euphoric and cathartic. After dealing with 2 years of physical separation from our loved ones, this song is a celebration of togetherness and our love for each other.

"Wrong Way" is about being unsure. It's about not knowing if the path you're choosing is the right one, but continuing along it either way. It's about the feeling i get when i have 5 different feelings clashing at once (or something like that). It's like reaching the top of a hill, only to find a greater challenge ahead of you. It's an unexplainable feeling, and i hope the mood of this song will convey it to people. 
I want to be able to express more of my roots musically, and express the things that sit on my mind usually. I'm not good at writing how i feel out, so im hoping this will help. This is such a small piece to the puzzle, but i hope the picture will start to show with a few more pieces coming soon.
What's most important is that i appreciate everyone and anyone that is/ will be apart of this. I can't wait to show whats next.

hi, my name’s alaina castillo. i’m 22 years old from houston, currently living in los angeles. for me, music started in my bedroom in texas when i was by myself either after school, work, or sneaking away when life got stressful. i was in choir throughout my school years, but was always told to focus on my studies and things that would put me on a secure path in life. when i was about to finish highschool, i realized that all i wanted to do was break the cycle and make something for myself. i wanted to make those around me proud so that they could see the dream i had in mind was achievable. to them, not being able to see the end result was an immediate red flag for me to stop, but to me it meant that i could create whatever outcome i wanted. 

i started making covers on youtube, trying different things, & meeting the amazing people who supported me from the start. i still talk to a lot of them to this day & don’t know where i would be now if it weren’t for them supporting me and hyping up each upcoming video. starting with a small community was the part that i remember enjoying most. they saw my first video blow up, my channel start to grow, & eventually my move out to los angeles where i started doing small tours and festival performances. it was something that i had always dreamed of while making videos with just a camera and an instrumental track on my computer. 

when i started releasing music as an artist, there were moments where i thought i had found myself, but always had to ask if it was really me because i had no clue who i was or what i wanted to say. i would find it in lyrics of songs or melodies that made me feel something, but i always felt a disconnect. i didn’t realize until recently that the person i was looking for inside myself was hurt, broken & hiding. expressing myself was never something that came easy and i forced myself to forget my own problems to please the versions of myself that other people had. before the start of 2022, i went back to houston with this new mindset, recorded music in my spare room, & went back to the reason i wanted to start making music. the reason for wanting to desperately create a world that i could escape to. it came from sadness & trauma, regret & emotional abuse, but also from optimism. a desire to do more, achieve more & show people that i could make it because there was nothing that made me feel more like myself than making music. 

my new song, “sad girls always finish first,” was the first song i wrote when i got back to la in january. i was sitting in the studio and we had a beat on repeat and the words, “troubled girl,” came to mind. i had always told myself i could be the happy artist that writes about overcoming problems, but when i started to write “sad girls always finish first,” i realized i didn’t wanna lie. i didn’t wanna act happy, i just wanted to feel the emotions however i could so that i could stay sad and eventually come to terms with whatever demons i had. to everyone who listens to this song, whether happy or sad, i want you to know that being sad doesn’t mean you’re gonna stay that way, or miss out on things, or lose. it means you’re gonna experience the feelings that come with the sadness. the anger, the mania, & the confusion & it’ll push you to grow into someone who finally has a voice of their own. i wanted to create a sad world with a dark side of confidence because we all need to escape to that place once in a while. or everyday, u decide. i hope you enjoy it & i hope you’re excited for the art to come.

My name is Alex aka Boys Noize, DJ & producer from Berlin, Germany. I started to DJ in clubs when I was 16. As a teenager I was working in a house and techno record store, so when I started to make my own music I decided to create my own label to be 100% independent. The music was released through limited presses of vinyl - it was music for DJs only. You were only able to find the music in a select network of house & techno record stores around the world. 

After the first few releases, well known DJs started to play my tracks in their sets, and I suddenly was getting booked both as DJ and to remix the likes of Depeche Mode and Daft Punk (!!). Out of the 100 remixes I’ve done there were indeed some hits, and these propelled me to big stages like Coachella and Glastonbury and studio sessions with A$AP Rocky, Bon Iver, Frank Ocean and Lady Gaga.  It still feels surreal to think about where it all started.

This brings me to my release today. “Cwejman“ is a classic Boys Noize banger - unreleased until now - and it’s a big one in my current DJ sets. The name "Cwejman" comes from one of my modules in my modular system that I've used to create the main sound of this track. 

Bringing limited editions to the digital age gives me the same vibes I had in my early days when I spent all my money on limited vinyl presses. Every DJ knows the feeling of dropping something rare in their sets, something that few others have. Offering DJs that feeling again while supporting artists is the magic of Sound.xyz

Suki Waterhouse catalogs the most intimate, formative, and significant moments of her life through songs. You might recognize her name or her work as singer, songwriter, and actress, but you’ll really get to know the multi-faceted artist through her music. Growing up in London, Suki gravitated towards music’s magnetic pull and always saw the medium as a way of expressing creativity and telling stories. Suki has drawn comparisons to the Paisley Underground sound of Mazzy Star and to the 60s influenced girl group reimagining of bands like Stockholm’s The Concretes and Glasgow’s Camera Obscura.

On “Wild Side,” Suki wonders aloud if her love would return to an ex if they came calling, particularly because the excitement and lust of a prior relationship can be so enticing. Suki sings, “when you got that ex who’s crazy, they’re always running through your mind / remember when we had a wild side?”

“Wild Side is about recognizing each other’s past, the beauty and the fear that comes in reminiscing about who you used to love,'' says Suki about the record.

Love is the most powerful force in the universe.

In our world, love can save lives, end wars, and heal hearts. 

"Touchdown" is a song of two souls who discover interstellar travel, willingly leave their world and take their love on a journey beyond our solar system. 

After their travels, they return to earth as celestial beings. With their light shining beyond comprehension, they reveal the blueprint to build a utopian world and revolutionize the structures of civilization forever.

Hey I’m Alexander 23 an artist/songwriter/producer from Chicago who lives in LA but still roots for the Bulls. I started making music when I was 9 years old after seeing my dad play guitar. I knew instantly that if I wasn’t gonna make it to the league that I had to make music for the rest of my life. I played in bands in high school and dropped out of college after my freshman year while studying engineering to tour as a drummer/bass player.

I originally moved to LA in 2018 to write/produce songs for other artists. It was cool to start to try to make a living doing in the studio, but I couldn’t help but feel like something was missing. I was working with talented artists, but I wasn’t feeling creatively fulfilled. I called my manager and told him to cancel all of my sessions. I wanted to be an artist and make my own music.  I wanted to exist musically outside the studio.

Fast forward a little bit and I was able to release my first music as Alexander 23 in 2019 and was fortunate enough to go on tour with Omar Apollo and Chelsea Cutler that same year. When the pandemic hit in 2020, everything changed, as it did for everyone. Tour was cut short and I went back to LA feeling defeated. That initial isolation brought me back to a time in my own life when everything was going wrong: personally, professionally, romantically. It was that same feeling that something really important was missing.

This feeling inspired me to write “IDK You Yet” and this song changed my life. This year I was able to go on tour opening for one of my heroes John Mayer, was nominated for a Grammy for co-producing ‘good 4 u’ by Olivia Rodrigo and just last week “IDK You Yet” went platinum (three things that don’t even sound real when I say them outloud). I wanted to share the original demo of  “IDK You Yet” because hearing it in its original stripped form is such a strong reminder of the power of a single song. As fans of music I think we all understand that and it’s what keeps us coming back for more.

RIP You and Me was one of the first songs I wrote for my debut album Aftershock. Ironically, it ultimately became the clear and obvious choice to be the final song on the album (more on this later). I hadn’t really written any songs since my previous EP “Oh No, Not Again!” and didn’t know exactly where I wanted to go with the next round of music which I think is both the scariest and most freeing time for a songwriter. I booked a spontaneous trip to Miami to get inspired and that’s where this song started.

While I was in Miami, I realized that although a relationship of mine had ended, there was still a lot I wanted to say to her and things I hoped she knew. I began to think of this song as a kind of eulogy for a relationship and that’s where the title was born. After I had the working concept and some of the lyrics I sat down at the piano and that chorus melody line was one of the first things that came out. It was really funny working on this sad piano song while all of the other studios were bumping insanely loud reggaeton. I actually think this weirdly ended up inspiring the bridge, in that I knew the song had to dial up to 10 at some point to really capture the emotion.

When I got back to LA, I lived with the song for a little bit and really loved it, but it felt like something was missing to really put it over the top. It felt like one of the most harmonically sophisticated songs I had ever made and I really wanted to lean into that. I called Charlie Puth and had him not only replay all of the piano I had played but also add that outro solo which I could not be happier to have as the last moment on the album. 

This song had to be the final song on the album because to me this song is closure personified. It’s looking back at all the highs and all the lows, exhaling, and saying ‘we gave it our best shot’. I think of the duality of the really intense bridge and the outro piano solo as kind of the perfect encapsulation of that feeling. I think this song defines the Aftershock era and I’m so grateful for it.

This song is for several things. It’s for my girlfriend, my family, and my friends for being there for me when we all got stuck inside; for the feeling of being at shows, looking over to the person next to you and knowing you both feel the same thing; and for the nostalgia of times spent together when you’re away.

I’m really excited to be an independent artist for the first time since I was 19. Over the past five years, I’ve put together a catalog that didn’t quite fit in with my major label releases; “When I’m With You” is the first of these. Lately, I’ve built a modular synth, and many of the sounds I’ve been crafting songs around have come together so much more organically. The newer records feel personal and intimate.

After being a supporter and collector of sound.xyz songs since the beginning, I’m stoked to be able to drop this record with them as a series of NFTs. This release will help fund future projects, as well as give the fans a collectible to hold on to. Owning an edition will also provide access to a secret section of the MELVVille Discord.

My official debut EP “Shift In Momentum” will be released later this year. This is the first single from that project. Sit back, space out, and enjoy.

Almost exactly 3 years ago, in the early spring of 2019, we were beginning to release songs from our debut album, komorebi. It was our first time releasing a full fledged record, on a major label. It was our first time releasing videos alongside our work, and our first time really diving into the whirlwind that the music industry can be. 

We always tend to create far ahead of our next release, so as we began to show komorebi and ourselves to the world, we were processing our experiences and beginning to craft what we believed to be our next release. The earliest of songs were written in hotels ranging from Berlin to the Florida panhandle. We dreamed of a sleek, groove driven record, where subtle polyrhythms gave the listener a distinct head bop. We strove to expand our manipulations of guitars beyond the licks, lines and textures we’d established. For all of these inspired intentions, this record never saw the light of day, as our vision didn’t seem to resonate with our team at large.

‘night dive’ is such a meaningful song to bring to sound for our first drop here. it’s about the frustrations of the conventional music industry, where money and metrics seem to dictate movement more than an artist’s vision does. it’s a song that details how being fresh and new in a pre-existing system can be a toxic affair and a fast ride, leaving a person confused when they get out of the proverbial car. 
it’s a song that wasn’t able to surface back where we were, but has found a home here in web3 where art and community are valued. and for that we are very grateful

this is ULTRA 1

i made this back in 2019. i had recently turned 21 and i was in the midst of my 5 month long journey around asia. i was staying in Bali and i had just started engaging in mindfulness. it was an interesting time where i was starting to get to know myself better. i was questioning the reasons as to why I do things and what I ultimately want out of life. I guess this is my version of keeping journal entries. 

ULTRA 1 was a form of therapy and it represents me finding ways to express myself through art, which is surprisingly something I rarely did at the time. I was always focused on making the craziest beat possible or what would have the most impact in a club setting. this song will always mark the beginning of me growing up and letting the music document the progress. 
<3

Hi, I’m msft, Italian bass music producer and web3 enthusiast. My Sound debut will be with my song Take / Back.
This song represents somehow a shift in my production workflow towards a groovier/drums-oriented approach. After releasing my EP in January which got completely sold on Catalog as well, I wanted to dive deeper into my production techniques, finding new ways to implement my skills and eventually become a better producer.
I’ve been inspired by my peers in music, especially camoufly who’s one of my best friends, a source of self-challenge and, of course, motivation. He made me start my web3 career months ago and he always pushed me to make whatever I want, constantly encouraging me to be and feel artistically free.
This song aims to prove how I want to keep on exploring genres/styles that I wasn’t used to make years ago. Somehow, I believe this experimental approach embodies my web3 journey: building, experimenting, trying, understanding, and eventually assimilating.

Pollen is a project that originally started as a series of Zoom sessions and blossomed into 20 songs over the course of a few short months.

Collaboration can be a very hit or miss experience. Sometimes the vibe in a room can be off, sometimes the styles of genres simply don’t align. But when Lucas (Bloody White) and I (Daniel Allan) met, we immediately found a balance in working together. We quickly realized that we were both good at the things the other was bad at, so we began setting up sessions twice a week to work on as much music as we could. The music we were writing felt frictionless, honest, and timeless. It felt like we were exploring the dark side of my production and the light side of Lucas’.

After making an absurd amount of music, we came to the realization that we should start a band together. We started mood boarding, making even more music, and writing mission statements. We came up with our cross pollination strategy - the belief that the more genres we could intersect the less we had to bind ourselves to any one sound in pursuit of creative happiness. 

As $OVERSTIM started to change my life, Lucas began finding his early footing in Web3. Our attention became spread thin, and the timing of Pollen became more and more out of reach. But if there’s one thing we’ve both learned about Web3 it’s that overthinking can be a true Achilles heel, and good music deserves to be out in the world instead of locked on a hard drive.

Jealous is a song about paranoia in an unstable relationship.  Everybody knows what jealousy feels like in whatever form it may present itself.  It's a harsh, primal feeling.  The contrast between the lyrics and instrumental, for us, paints a picture of what it feels like to suppress and play off those doubtful thoughts.

To More.

For those of you who don’t know me, my name is Jayden and I write music under TWERL. I’m originally from Perth, Western Australia but just relocated to Bali.

‘wherever you go’ is a track that’s extremely close to my heart as it’s an emotional collaboration with my partner Pauline that is about being in a long distance relationship and having to leave each other. I still remember the moment we were in a studio session in seperate rooms and she came in to play me the demo, I instantly teared up.

This is also a special moment as it’s my genesis Sound NFT and a further dive into web3 which is something that I’m extremely passionate about. There is such a high level of toxicity in the music industry right now and web3 is truely changing the game for artists, we finally have the control and value we deserve without labels manipulating and using us. I had completely lost my drive for making music due to these issues but web3 has brought back the spark along with a new direction for my sound/branding and this song is a perfect example that.

Sometimes we live in denial because we don’t want to admit that we’re settling for sub-standard circumstances and are missing out on potential opportunities for greater happiness. This song encourages everyone to face the possibility that they have the potential and take action to improve their own situation.

Description: To me, "New Dawn" represents the neverending quest for abundance and happiness. Though you might be going through something, they say it's always darkest before dawn. Here's to a new dawn!

Beyond stoked to be back on Soundxyz with my release 'drowning', an emotional garage piece I've been chipping away at for 2 years.

I've been laying low over the last few months, due to working on the ASTRO project, a full length web3 album with some amazing artists such as Daniel Allan, Reo Cragun, Pauline Herr, Mark Johns, Tisoki, Camoufly & more.

Drowning is just the beginning of a massive amount of music coming over the next few months, I can't wait to share with you all!

I made this exclusively for my show in Stockholm but decided to share this with the world. It gave people so much joy that night so I wanted everyone to hear it. Also I'm uploading this on my birthday today :) This one is for the steppers!

Hey everyone! I'm delighted to have my second drop on Sound, premiering a very special song.

I originally made The Only back in May 2022, right before my trip to LA. I was (and still am) heavily inspired by breakbeats and I wanted to combine those vibes with electric guitars, reese basses and acid synths. Being able to blend modern sounds with iconic rhythms has been my major goal for the whole year; this song aims to prove that.

The artwork is made by DVRS, my go to for any 3D visual I need and long time friend. I've been releasing many projects in collaboration with DVRS as I strongly believe in the importance of the audio / visual relationship. It's safe to say my music would impact way less without his art.

The Only will be premiered on Sound on September 5th, then it will be available on DSPs the day after, on September 6th. All collectors will get an invite link to join my secret Discord.

hey i’m alec. from denver, in los angeles. this song is called jojo. it’s a first class seat on my train of thought through the rollercoaster of heartbreak. i’ve always wanted to do a song structured like this; a full beat switch. it’s an a side & b side of jojo. the perk of finally being an independent artist is that there is no chatter in my ears telling me “4 minutes is too long!” “jojo isn’t relatable enough for a song title!” “don’t use demo vocals” “why would you have a pig on a leash as the artwork, it doesn’t make sense!” i can keep going because this is fun but you get the point. i think this song encapsulates the experience of dealing with heartbreak while simultaneously having a career where you make those feelings very public. there is no other job where your next partner will know exactly how you felt about the last one. that’s jojo.

Over the past 8 years huge range of different styles of music, and at times I’ve struggled with what to do with the ideas that didn’t quite fit the directions my artist project has taken. Music NFT’s have given me the space to share music that otherwise might never see the light of day with fans, and showcase other styles of music I love to make.

This track earned the title Skyline because when I listen to it I imagine floating around a snowy mountain or New York City at night, watching the world go by. Whenever writing music one my main focuses is to have contrasting moments - dreamy verses with soft, warping pads and then stripped, gritty choruses. I think this tune captures that perfectly.

I really miss when Ludacris was in every DJs rotation. 'Peanut Butter Cherry' is me explaining how I am really missing everything that is nostalgic (for me, the late 2000s/early 2010s) while making sure the song (& myself) still feels good. 
PBC opens with my brain saying, "I been at this function, I been smoking something, idk who this is, guess we some hooligans, it's hard to get thru this shit, can you play some more Ludacris, cus it's hard to get through this shit" in a low pitched voice. Not sure if it is the devil or angel on my shoulder, but it is definitely telling me to leave this party and spend my time doing what I actually enjoy.
Shout out Luda

& again, thank you soooooooo much for making being an independent artist possible. this is very real

Sunrise is the third to last song on my upcoming debut album Dreaming of Flying. It feels like clarity after the dust settles, insight after heartbreak. I made it with Ty on the first day we met.

Every session I’ve ever had with another producer starts with a getting-to-know-you beat. We either sync up our DAWs or take turns on one computer and try to feel out what collaboration with eachother is like. Often these are sloppy and it takes until the second or third beat of the day for us to know how to best trust and compliment eachother. I still can’t believe this is the first thing we ever made together. It felt so easy and also fresh and new. I think that’s why I called it Sunrise.

This is the biggest step I’ve taken so far in building Dreaming of Flying. I make music everyday, therapeutically. So much of it never leaves my hard drive. Collectors of this project will have access to a monthly tape of my latest creations. Curated just for them. It means so much to me that you’re here. Thank you for listening.

yo! i’m peter! i’m an artist from the bay area, now livin in la! i make pop music and try to spread mental health awareness through everything i do! i’ve been playing guitar since i was 7 and grew up on literally everything from worship music, to classic rock, blues, pop, etc. i’m heavily inspired by people like john mayer, the 1975, lewis capaldi, and honestly all of my friends. during my senior year of high school i made my first song and put it out for my friends and family to hear. it ended up getting on some pretty cool playlists and hit 100,000 plays on Spotify alone within the first couple months of its release, and it honestly changed my life—the response i got from the song was just insane… i received hundreds of dm’s from people saying how much the song had affected their life. it wasn’t until that song came out, that i had realized how much potential there was to make an impact on youth culture through my music. a few months later though, i had ended up losing my brother in law to suicide in 2018. the last thing he posted on his facebook page was a link to stream my first song. it was an insanely rough time for me, my family, and everyone around me. it broke us. as i kept making music over the years though, i’ve received thousands and thousands of dm’s, mostly from random people saying that my music had really helped them. at this point, i’m still thinking to myself that maybe if i wrote some of these songs earlier--that maybe my brother in law would still be here?  those dm’s i received, conversations i had, etc. have really put a lot on my heart and a ton of purpose in my soul to continue doing what i'm doing. i truly hope that you can connect with my music and that it can give you an escape to help you build new perspectives. 

this song i am dropping, “wishing”, is one of the more recent songs i’ve made. i wrote it about the idea of being in a relationship where BOTH of you are toxic. you're always breaking up, getting back together, acting like you don't care when you really do, etc. and for some reason you can't seem to make the final decision to just walk away and end things. i wrote it in hopes of inspiring you to stop letting yourself stay in pointless situations where you're constantly hurt, over & over. i hope you stop "wasting your life" away with unnecessary BS… whether that be your relationships, your job, etc. 
also i’m wishin that you’ll dig this song <3

I am a multi-disciplinary artist from Chicago; my primary medium is hip-hop music. I was born and raised on the South Side with family roots in Ghana, West Africa. Growing up I was a skateboarder first, a graffiti artist second and a rapper third, music quickly becoming the fabric that tied all poles of my life together and gave me contextual meaning. The ethos of my creativity is truth telling; to share my unique perspective through the various mediums I employ.

The song King Of The Slum was made during my recent stay in Ghana in January. I titled it as such in reference to the slum in which my family resides and my father was born, known as Asokore Zongo in Koforidua. Zongo settlements are largely poverty stricken areas in West African towns comparable in ways to the Black American ghetto, albeit much less resourced. Much of the lyrical content of this song speaks to the juxtaposition of these different sides of my existence. My uncle, who lives in the zongo, is a legendary Ghanian musician named Chief Kofi Sammy of the Okukuseku International Band, and a pioneer of a style of music called High Life. For this record, which I also produced, I took influence from the music of my ancestry while I was physically in my homeland to manipulate some traditional melodic elements within the framework of my own personal style.

The photograph out of which I made the cover is of myself in the Zongo with my nieces and nephews. Despite the extreme poverty experienced where my family lives, there is immense power in culture and spirituality that I have sought to express through my practice in both photography and music.

The “Amen break” is one of music’s most beloved and essential samples, ranking up there with “Funky Drummer” and “Think (About It)” as the most used breaks in hip-hop and electronic music. However, the primary songwriters behind the track – the Winstons’ Richard L. Spencer, who wrote the arrangement for the song and owned the copyright on the track, and drummer Gregory Coleman, who died homeless in 2006 – never received royalties from their indispensable beat.

I always wanted to find a way to credit the creators behind the samples I was using in my own productions. It’s easy to do so on a vinyl sleeve (and I did), but the music streaming industry doesn’t care, and makes it almost impossible to share informations about a record and how it was produced, apart from the main artist’s name. Most of us know that there’s more to a record than just a singer, a rapper, or a techno producer. Music is inherently collaborative. Music is the fabric of communities. Music is made of shared moments, connections, and interactions. 

The Stems & Twigs Mix is an experiment in collaborative creative processes, using smart contracts to ensure that all creators are credited and get a fair share of the sale, based on how much they’ve contributed

Following the Ensemble Mix (the first ever techno DJ set minted as an NFT back in March 2022 on sound.xyz), I decided to push forward by putting together a mix based, not on finished songs, but on stems (individual instrumental tracks). 

After announcing the idea on Twitter, I received around 550 different stems, uploaded on a shared folder : drum loops, basslines, vocals, guitars, synthesizers, sfx, or even modular and generative experiments. Each stem file’s name needed to include a twitter handle and an ETH wallet address 

I spent the next week assembling these components into a 25 minutes piece of music where almost every sound has been sourced from this collective sample pool. From the 550 stems originally received, 46 have been used in the mix (I only included 4 of my own stems). The final mix will be sold on sound.xyz as an NFT with multiple editions. Each producer will receive a percentage of the NFT sale, based on how many of his stems have been used (1 stem = 1%), with 50% of the sale going to the stem producers, and 50% to myself for building the mix and designing the concept. 

What’s interesting is that, even if 92% of the building blocks I used were produced by other musicians, the mix sounds a lot like a typical Maelstrom DJ set. But the process still pushed me into unexpected territories, where I had to find ways to include elements that I thought were essential, but didn’t sound at all like something I would have recorded myself. The result is truly a collaborative one, a dialogue between different voices, coming from specific places around the globe and different cultures, but sharing the same desire for a better future than the one that is currently being pushed down our throats by the music industry.
