I've been back and forth for a long time now on what my next move in life is gonna be, which has coincided with some setbacks on many levels recently that effectively solidified that I had to make it now, or I never would.

Long story short, I'm going back to school to get my Master's degree in music, with the plan to teach/educate folks about electronic music from a Black perspective, and our history in revolutionizing all music with just a handful of musical devices and techniques, or through developing musical styles that dominate popular music to this day.

I digress, though: I've been feeling defeated until recently because I failed elsewhere in my life. I tried, really hard, but maybe just not hard enough. I'm tired. Exhausted. Sometimes from just being a Black man living in this world we live in, most times from just not being where I expected to be by now, which is really where the idea of this song originated.

This is for my peoples who are ready to give up. To stop chasing for a minute, and to accept where you're at and how you feel, instead of propping up your ego and your pride, and say out loud that you really did try. We all have, we've all been there, too, so you're not alone, and this isn't the end. Enjoy it while you can, enjoy it here in this moment I created, and find catharsis in knowing you have to fail at some point, to one day eventually succeed. 

Right?

Right...

This song is about getting up and following your dreams... The search for something greater. This applies specifically to my life, being a first generation immigrant, moving around a lot as a kid, and being an artist/entrepreneur. I've always been on a search for something bigger than myself. My very conception was between 2 people who left their native countries of Tanzania and South Africa, to fly across the ocean in search of something more. 

There's a "Buzzin" feeling you get when you know your potential is greater than your physical environment. I think a lot of small towners and midwesterners who seek to make an impact in the world can feel me as well. After Brady Watt and I connected we finished this song probably in 2 hours tops, and he played every instrument on it. This was really fun to me because I came up performing to a band way before I ever had a DJ. A band / natural instrument setting is probably the most natural way for me to write and perform. 

I moved around mainly out of necessity as a child, but as a young man I had the pleasure of choosing to live in some of the greatest cities in the world. What's crazy is that everything came full circle. Everything I learned from all of the cultures and places I've been, have taught me how to give back, build, and make my hometown of St. Paul, Minnesota a greater place to live for myself and my whole community.

Last year was a year full of high anxiety and depression. It took a strain on my mental, and for the longest time I haven’t been able to cry, no matter the situation that emotion was completely cutoff! After multiple trips to help deal with my emotions it felt like I unlocked a whole new part of myself!

I managed to create Lifted Demons out of darkness and this record made me feel light, it made me want to jump around and enjoy myself again. Like, it literally had been so long since I’ve seen my true self and once I did it felt like my demons had been lifted!

“It’s been a long time since I seen you man, fuck is going on”

We have all dealt and maybe are still dealing with some type of darkness. I’m here to tell you keep fighting, no matter the battle. You have only yourself to prove something to!

This will be the first song on our first album in 4 years. 

It almost didn’t happen. 

Before the pandemic we had gotten so exhausted and jaded for a moment it felt like we might walk away. Then the world ended. And for the first time in 8 years we were apart. In those lost months we remembered how much Marian Hill means to us, and means to all of you. How the connection we find through our music is literally magic. And we knew we needed to finish this record.

Marian Hill gave both of us the lives we'd always dreamed of, and kept us going during the worst year of our lives. When Samantha found herself turning 30 in her childhood bedroom and Jeremy suffered an onset of chronic pain in both of his wrists, the music we made gave us moments of joy to hold onto in a world full of uncertainty. For a few moments each day, we could get lost in a song, and pretend we were playing it for you.

This song in some ways feels like a message from that time to eternity. When we started thinking of the lyrics we were really thinking about us as a band, us as songwriters...will we be remembered? Do people still care? Will anyone care in 5 years, 10 years, 20 years?

It’s also about wondering if an ex will remember you once the relationship is far in the rearview.

And about if any of our art will last as climate change escalates to world-ending levels.

When you listen to this song, you are with us, wherever you are. 

We invite you to share your own memories in the comments - together we’ll build a wall of memories forever immortalized through music.

someday when everything’s underwater
and all our memories are forgotten
there’s nothing
as far as you can see
i wonder in all that…
is there a trace of me?

will you remember me?

I met DEEGAN my first week living in Los Angeles. I was at a show watching a friend perform when I got a tap on the shoulder - I thought I was going to run into one of my other friends who recently moved cross country with me but instead I was greeted by a total stranger. He introduced himself and I immediately recognized him after having worked with his cousin months prior.

The next day I did a deep dive on his catalog and invited him over to my place for a session. I remember being blown away by the weird noises he could produce with just his voice alone. I realized he was the type of creative that wouldn't try to structure out the perfect song - he would let me do whatever I wanted to do. And creatively that's exactly what I needed. 

Over the years DEEGAN and I have worked on so many records together. From our early days making bleeps and bloops on my computer to his 2 features on Overstimulated, to the writing camp I put together in Malibu, DEEGAN has consistently been one of my favorite people to work with - not only for his musical abilities - but for his undeniable personality that lights up every room he's in. 

Bittersweet is a record that I started on last summer and sent to DEEGAN at the end of last year. When I was looking for a song to drop on Sound, I came across this topline but the production felt outdated. I ended up manically sitting with it for 72 hours and this is the result that came out. It's a preview of my new direction sonically.

This song is about the mixed emotions one feels after a breakup: The happiness of not having to deal with their toxic behavior anymore, and the sadness in losing all of the good parts about them.

This track is for all of my peoples who have to wake up before the sun comes up to make ends meet, the early risers who found their beat to start the grind for the life that they want, a soundtrack to contemplate your next move, whether it’s to secure the bag, realize your dreams, or just tear up the asphalt to as you dance your way to the finish line, when the rest of the world is seemingly non-existent. As if there was no one else but you out there…

I wrote this during the pandemic, working as an essential worker the entire time, something I was not accustomed to as a career musician/DJ/producer for so long before. I thought for a while I couldn’t even make the same music as before, because I wasn’t living like I used to, head in the proverbial clouds and blessed to do what I love for a living. I had a whole different grind, a different perspective that put me out of my usual, ideal state of mind, that working 40+ hours a week wasn’t going to get me to.

Instead, though, I learned over time how much this motivated me to persevere, be patient, and wait for my next “cubic centimeter of chance” as I call it, the chance for me to break back through and find momentum, back into that state of mind that brought me the musical workflow I became successful with.

Dance Like No One Else Exists (or “5:55am”, the time I remember finishing this beat) is me, dancing the dance of the early grinder, ready to take it all on so I can get to my real work, making music that moves people, and reminds them that you and you alone can move mountains, let alone yourself. So dance like no else exists, move to your own beat, and don’t ever forget who you know and believe you are.

This one is for my late father who passed last April, Gary Nash, my inspiration to keep making music everyday, any way I can, anywhere I’m at.

Rest in peace, Pops…

This is the oldest song on our upcoming album "why can’t we just pretend?"

We wrote it exactly three years ago during one of the sessions for our "was it not" EP. 

We started writing it in a way we never had before - in the room, no beat.  Sam sang a melody as Jeremy snapped his fingers softly. And then we just had fun.

"Trippin out" felt too weird for the EP. Its hard to justify a strange intense record without a catchy chorus on a five song project in the streaming era. Through the years our most experimental songs have often seen the fewest streams. So we added it to the pile of oddball MH outtakes and moved on.

The following year as we put together our fourth album in the middle of a global pandemic we found ourselves compiling a list of song contenders and stumbled back onto "Trippin Out". It was still perhaps the strangest thing we’d ever made. And together we decided that no matter what anybody else said, this song needed to be on our album. 

We are so grateful to platforms like Sound for building a music experience where peculiar curiosities can flourish. We hope you enjoy this ear candy as much as we do - thank u, as always, for listening.

Heart attack came about from three separate events that all had the same effect on me more or less. I’d really hurt the girl I was seeing in the months she was away, and I went to her house to talk through everything. I realized pretty quickly it wasn’t going to be a favorable discussion though, she’d made up her mind and I wasn’t in any place to try to convince her otherwise, so I left with my eyes full of water and cried in the car for the better part of an hour. Weeks went by without seeing her, but then I eventually did at a friends birthday and it was like getting sledge hammered in the chest. I’d started seeing someone else around that time, which in hindsight was really irresponsible because my heart wasn’t nearly settled, so it just led to a lot more stupid sadness for everyone involved.  Really all this music from the first half of Cherry is just the product of me being an idiot boy that couldn’t see beyond his own nose too well. Like this song is so sad but you can’t really pity someone that orchestrated their own pain. But don’t worry, the room gets brighter the further you walk into it and we have a lot of room left.

This is the version of Heart Attack I was originally going to go with before I sat with it for a few weeks and completely reproduced it from the ground up. It didn’t feel right to not have this version exist somewhere so I’m glad you’ll have it here. All holders of this drop will be airdropped an edition of the final version when it’s released on my site later this year.

A lot has happened these past few years. Some things beautiful, most things painful, but all of it necessary. 

I've given much thought to the words I want to say here and if there are any that could possibly convey what I feel. For a long time it felt nearly impossible to find any words. I had to go through hell and back before learning how to navigate the turbulence of my sea of emotions. On that journey I found that creation was always my compass. Then my son was born, and he became my reason to stay. 

Almost all of my life has been spent creating things to be my anchor. It's my way of making sense of a world that feels alien to me, to process my experiences and to connect with people. Connecting has always been the thing I've desired most, and in my immaturity I sacrificed a lot of myself to have it. From my mind and my body, to my time, integrity and emotions.      
I lost many things in my pursuit of a connection, hurting myself and others in the process. A scared kid pretending to know everything. 

My childhood is where I stayed.

I wrote those words in the summer of 2017 during a period of severely exploitive label deals, poor management, a terrible break up and my own narcissistic and toxic self-destructive behavior destroying everything around me. 

My childhood was where I went to escape, reminiscing on the beauty and ignorance of being oblivious. And for a while it was safe. 

But life went on and I had abandoned those words and sentiment for years, blind to how important they really were. When I eventually found my way back to them, they had embodied a completely new and much more emotional meaning. They were no longer a door, but a mirror instead.

And when my son began his own childhood, that changed everything. 

The love of my life, our greatest creation and the most perfect gift from god. He gives me reason and resolve, the connection I've so desperately craved my entire life, a chance to break the cycle of pain that has plagued my life since I was his age. 

Still, nothing comes without hardship. 

I spent a long time fighting to know him, to be with him and to love him with everything I had in me at the time. But for reasons controllable and uncontrollable I was an ocean away from him for what felt like a lifetime. Logistics, lies and love lost orbited what was meant to be completely beautiful and so it seemed to be the end of the world, another failure of my own doing. But the love he filled me with didn't allow me to quit.

No matter what the obstacle was, or whatever opposing force I encountered, I found my way back to him. Being in the presence of my gift from god has taught me how to truly grow up, and now the beauty of his childhood is my duty to maintain and a second chance at healing from mine. 

This is for you, Mateo. Thank you.

Time is the greatest currency.

A lot of things lead us to believe that we don’t have much of it, but that couldn’t be further from the truth. We constantly see ourselves running out of time, losing it, instead of the beauty and experience that time gives us.

It’s true that you can never get time back, but what you spend that time on might just be infinitely more valuable.

For as long as I can remember I have always felt the clock ticking, never stopping, impartial to everyone. That filled me with fear. I tried for so long to get those seconds, minutes, hours and days back, wasting even more time in the process. It never worked.

I realise now that holding onto what has been lost will only offer you the same fate. Being lost in times gone by will have you learning the same lesson over and over again.

So now I decide to move forward, regardless of how much time has been lost, because there’s much more time left. How you choose to spend your time is your decision and yours alone… just remember that you have more than enough of it.

We all have ample time to love, lose, learn and live through.

I got into music later in life than most would assume. Being raised in an immigrant household, I didn’t have the opportunity to join a band, sing in a choir, or play multiple instruments. The entirety of my childhood was engulfed in school and sports, and I never really had the opportunity to pursue what I was passionate about as it didn’t fit the mold of what felt traditionally acceptable to my family.

I was introduced to music when I was seven. My brother - who is 15 years older than me - gave me his iPod classic, and for the first time I felt enamored. I was exposed to songs that most kids my age weren’t listening to, and in large part I attribute that iPod to getting me through elementary school. I was never a popular kid growing up, and it didn't help that I was struggling as I developed my English skills and navigating my way through a brand new culture. Most of the kids around me had seen life through a lens that was foreign to me, and that iPod helped me escape that reality and find meaning amongst the uncertainty. 

I knew then and there that I loved music, but I always approached it tangentially. In high school I became a self-proclaimed audio engineer, recording local artists in my bedroom closet. Eventually some of the artists I was recording asked me for beats but I wasn’t at all ready to recognize myself as an actual musician. I feared rejection and more importantly - being bad at something I aspired to be great at.

During my freshman year of college I decided to be intentional about what I wanted and take my life seriously. While studying pre-med and being an athlete, I decided to 180 my life’s trajectory and unapologetically go all in on learning how to make music. And I did this in the most extreme way possible: Every morning at 4 A.M. I'd start my day by taking notes on music production. I began my journey by taking every session I could across the street at Berklee School of Music - always being the worst producer in the room. I stopped caring about school entirely. My life became a big game of catchup - I lived on the margins to work on music in every crevice I could find, to catch up to the artists I was surrounding myself with. And while I’m grateful for those years of my life, they did come with a cost. 

All of us have bad habits, and mine is being selfish to a fault. Over the course of the past four years, I’ve cut so many people out of my life. Childhood friendships, relationships, and even family members have fallen by the wayside as a result of my manic approach to furthering my career. I figured that the easiest way out for me was never getting close to anyone in the first place, because all that would do is put them on a fast track to eventually leaving my life. And while I don’t regret the choices I’ve made in the process, that doesn’t mean they’ve been easy to accept. 

"Too Close" is my manifestation of that feeling. Everything you hear - from the softness of the chords to the delivery of Bloody White’s vocals - feels like a reflection of the thoughts I’ve experienced along the way. In a way, writing this song helped me sort through them and gain a better understanding of myself.

My Journey From Music To Crypto  Four years ago, I was a full-time music producer and global-traveling DJ. I had been working in music for nearly a decade, was getting millions of plays on streaming platforms, and had produced a couple songs that landed in the Billboard top 40. But despite having a career many people dream of, by 2016 I was feeling uneasy. My career had started to plateau and my attention was increasingly turning toward topics far afield from music, particularly the existential risks of technology.  To understand the source of my anxiety, it’s necessary to travel back to my childhood. I grew up watching a lot of Star Trek: The Next Generation with my dad. And looking back, the techno-optimist vision of Gene Roddenberry had a big influence on how I viewed human progress. My music tastes followed a similar theme. I vividly remember hearing Daft Punk’s Around The World the first time, and how excited I was when I bought my first synthesizer. This all led to a more serious interest in futurism in college. I started reading books like Ray Kurzweil’s The Singularity Is Near, and hard science fiction from authors like Stanislaw Lem, from whom I eventually took my DJ name, Gigamesh.  I released music and performed under that alias full time from 2008 onward, growing a modest global fan base. In the first two years, I achieved commercial success and started touring without a management team or agent. This was all possible thanks to the decentralized nature of pre-Spotify music discovery. I would post bootleg remixes and original songs on Soundcloud and send the links to a list of music blogs. The blogs would feed via RSS into aggregators like Hype Machine. There were very few gatekeepers so online music discovery was an organic, beautiful mess. It created a long tail of musicians like myself who wouldn’t have been able to make a living from it years earlier.  Another thing working to my benefit during the early years of my music career was that social media was still in its pre-monetization infancy. During this time, it was relatively easy for motivated, talented artists to cut through the noise and find a niche audience without doing constant self-promotion. Words like “content” and “algorithm” hadn’t become fixtures of every musician’s vocabulary.  By 2015, my career was cruising along at a steady clip but the road was getting bumpy. My old tools for promotion were no longer viable. Spotify had supplanted Soundcloud as the dominant music discovery platform, and Facebook’s advertising revenue model was making it increasingly more difficult to reach my fans, as their attention was now being auctioned to the highest bidder. I found this frustrating, but I wasn’t fully conscious of the impact it was having on my career until much later. Ironically, the algorithms were also turning me into a news junkie with an addiction to political content.  It has taken me years to fully understand what was happening, but my optimism about humanity and technology was transforming into existential dread. The exponential technological progress I previously had religious faith in seemed to be in a doom loop with the master algorithm of unfettered capitalism. After the 2016 election, I was just as convinced technology had the potential to make humanity self-destruct as it did to create vast abundance — possibly more. This realization made it difficult for me to rationalize spending my time making dance music. It was causing instability in both the world and my life. I felt creatively unmoored, which led to spending more time consuming news, which created more anxiety and less musical output.  Nevertheless, I still remained hopeful about technology’s potential for good, which is where cryptocurrency enters the story. In early 2017 I noticed Bitcoin was in the news for having reached a new all time high. I had bought some at the peak of the previous cycle but hadn’t paid any attention to it in the intervening years. Like many people, I thought the ideas behind it were interesting but only had a cursory understanding of the technology and mainly thought of it as a high-risk investment. That all changed when I learned about Ethereum.  Around February of that year, a musician friend named André (RAC) and I started chatting over whatsapp about crypto. At some point, one of us mentioned Ethereum and we were both intrigued. After listening to some podcasts and an interview with Vitalik Buterin, I fell down the rabbit hole. I quickly moved my BTC to ETH, which then proceeded to go up about 10x over the rest of the year. André went even deeper, positioning himself as a leader at the intersection of music and crypto.  By the end of the year, I was starting to think I was a financial genius. It was making me considerably less worried about my music career. Life was pretty good! But then four events conspired to throw my life in turmoil in less than three months: crypto entered a brutal bear market, my manager quit the industry, my touring agency was acquired and subsequently dropped me (along with many other artists), and my wife moved out.  Suffice to say I quickly adopted a much more aerial perspective over my life and concluded I needed to make a big change. Despite the price crash, my conviction in cryptocurrency was unshaken. I thought I might be able to forge a path toward a career in the industry. I had always thought about learning to code, so decided to give it a shot. After going through a free intro course online, I realized coding hit a lot of the same pleasure centers in my brain as making music did, so I kept going.  It was a long transition and unfortunately didn’t save my marriage, but coding did start to make me feel like I could potentially have a higher-leverage impact on the world than what my music skills afforded. After spending about 8 months learning everything I could, I found some freelance web development work. I also volunteered for an organization called RadicalxChange, which has developed a reputation for innovative solutions to the problems in tech I've been concerned about. All of this culminated in landing a full-time role at Left Field Labs, a digital agency that contracts for big tech firms like Google.  While I enjoyed the esteem of contributing code for some of the biggest tech companies in the world, I also had misgivings and remained focused on getting into crypto. By the fall of last year it was clear a new bull market was taking shape, so I decided it was time to make the leap. I quit my job and soon launched a business based on an algorithmic crypto trading strategy I developed in my free time. I called it FinFren. I was able to attract subscribers with minimal promotion, however I primarily viewed it as a side-hustle and was still eager to find a position where I could level-up my skills and feel like I was contributing more directly to the industry. I started applying for jobs.  A few weeks into my search, I dropped a message in the Optimism discord server asking if they needed any front end development help. Like most people invested in the Ethereum ecosystem, I knew Optimism to be one of the most ambitious and anticipated infrastructure projects. I estimated my odds of getting a job there to be pretty low, so I was very happy to get immediate independent replies from both the CEO, Jinglan Wang, and CTO, Karl Floersch. They charmed my socks off and offered me a contract gig for a minor redesign of their website. The contract went well, which eventually led to a full-time position. I had arrived!  Why crypto? Cryptocurrency has helped me regain my faith in the future. Why am I so optimistic about its potential to improve the world? I could go on about this at length, but I’ll try to be brief:  First, I don't believe cryptocurrency by itself will change the world significantly. What I think will have the most impact is something Ethereum has but Bitcoin doesn’t: a Turing-complete virtual machine. It enables an internet of programmable value in which users can easily gain an ownership stake in all the platforms they interact with. My preferred term used to describe all the applications built on this distributed computer is Web3, to contrast with the Web2 internet in which advertisers are the customer, and users are the product.  A common metaphor for the internet is a digital global hive mind. In that framing, every computer represents a synapse, and Web3 is a way of improving the connections between all the synapses. Rather than arbitrary data passing through the network via centrally controlled, rent-seeking intermediaries, smart contracts enable anyone to attach value to their data down to 18 decimal points of precision. This all happens on a network that is massively difficult to hack or shut down.  It should be noted the programmable value isn't purely financial. By managing the complex relationship between incentives, smart contracts also enable the expression of ethical values as well. All of this will enable us to design better social networks and governance systems to conquer coordination failures. In short, Web3 is a better global operating system.  ****************** December 2021 edit: The text above is from a piece I wrote after joining Optimism.io back in February. I definitely recommend following what they’re up to, particularly their work on retroactive public goods funding. I find them to be one of the most inspiring group of builders in web3.   I have since cofounded Sound, and this essay seemed like an appropriate way to kick off our internal test run on mainnet. Thanks for reading, and for supporting musicians! ✨

Until then you’re just a kid with extra responsibilities. Cherry was the discovery of and exploration of that realization, and I tried my best to organize it not in the order that the events happened but by the progress of the emotional growth. 

Jersey was the infancy of it all. I had in my hand the heart of a really sweet girl and I wasn’t ready to give her mine fully cause it belonged to someone else. I had spread myself too thin. “ROGUE” was made in the fall of 2021, live on twitch in about an hour for a beat battle. I was living in Boston at my parents house. (I moved back home during covid to start fresh, creatively and mentally.) It had gotten to a point where I was nearly paralyzed artistically… living in LA and touring for the better part of 5 years. I didn’t know where I wanted to go and the fast paced industry combined with not taking proper care of my mental at a young age really affected my art.

Removing myself from the social aspects of music was necessary in order to get back to myself creatively and I think ROGUE is a fitting title for what I was feeling while going through a lot of that mental turmoil.

All of the music on my new project “sObeRRRRR” is me at my truest just doing what I love and not caring about where or when these songs will get played. I’ve always enjoyed a weird mixture of rhythmic and melodic semi-club ready music, and this lays into my heady electronic beats side much more than the festival and club sounds. It’s a more personal electronic journey but still has the wonky maximal character that a lot of my music in the past retains.

I moved to Los Angeles in January of 2020. I had just finished up classes at Boston University and proceeded to take the biggest leap of faith in my life and move across the country to pursue a career in music. Up until March of that year things were going pretty well: I got some of my first mix clients, started doing my first sessions, and met some new friends along the way. Then the world fell apart and I had to move back to my parents’ basement in Louisville, Kentucky. For the first time I started to question my decisions. How can I make a living off music? I love doing it but how can I have a sustainable career?

After a few months of sitting in the basement in Kentucky I decided to book a one way ticket back to LA in early May. Still in the height of the pandemic, I figured that if I could be scrappy I could formulate some sort of a viable career off of my music. And if I could do it during a pandemic, I could definitely have an easier time when the world returned to some semblance of normalcy. Between mixing clients, production lessons, and taking some production fees here and there, I managed to do this for almost a year.

Then in April of 2021 I played a show in a friend’s backyard and invited a bunch of A&R’s and music industry people to swing by. Over the course of the next few months I got on the phone with major labels and one of the reoccurring themes I heard was that it wasn’t just about the music in today’s industry - I had to have the full package. I was told that I had to have a way bigger social media presence, that I needed to blow up on Tik Tok, that what I was doing wasn’t enough, even if the music was there.

Hearing a bunch of voices pulling me in different directions made it seem like I had to focus on everything but the music, and that became incredibly toxic - especially to me as someone who has built meaning in life around making songs. 

Overstimulated is a project that comments on my personal journey and its overwhelming nature. When life gets hectic, my primary coping mechanism is to lock myself in a room and work it out with music. Sometimes I don’t really know how to communicate, so I suppose this project is my way of sharing that experience with the world.

every album needs an intro, and nothing i'd written while traveling quite felt like the welcome mat for the front door of the estate that is daddy's money. back in march daniel allan, bloody white and i booked a studio in town during ETH Denver and messed around til 3 or 4am. i always came back to one of them, and realized that if i flushed it out it really did set the tone for the rest of the album. i had come back to LA to finish Cherry with plans to ship back out into the world the following week, but i met this girl that diverted my flight path.

she was new in town to work for the summer and didn't really fuck with the egos in a lot of the people she met.she just had a different vibe in a really refreshing way. she was made out of sunlight, and i wanted to surround myself with it. i wanted to give her the best experience possible for the short time she was there, and it felt really good to want to make someone's life feel cinematic. sort of how life had felt for me traveling solo in Europe. and so i'd found my welcome mat.

Chuki Chuki and many songs of mine are inspired by music that I would hear at family gatherings as a kid growing up in NYC, so they hit very close to home for me. Chuki Chuki was made in Dec 2022 with Ex Mañana, a friend that I haven't worked with in a while and was excited to get back in the studio with. I told them that I wanted to make a track that was rooted in Merengue but also melds my American knowledge of Hyperpop. Once I heard the dry opening chords, I laid down my hymns and just started having fun with it. It’s not often making a track comes that easily so I knew we had something special.

Being a first-generation Dominican American, I think it’s important for me to pay homage to and spotlight creatives of my culture. The word “Chuki” is derived from the children’s diabolical doll “Chucky” and is used in some Dominican households to describe kids being up to no good. I wanted to make a track about having a night out with my friends so I took the slang word and made it more lighthearted but still mischievous.

In defense of love.

Almost immediately after getting into a relationship I started to push the person I loved away because I was scared that if they decided to leave me one day, I would essentially be emotionally destroyed and never get over it. I didn’t want to tell the person that I felt this way and so out of fear of being left or getting in too deep, I would go cold suddenly and withdraw and intentionally shut down. When I did open up, I was told that my mood swings were like an ocean and I realized how hurtful I had been while trying to “protect” myself. The song is about wanting to do better and not be this way.

Don't fall
Into me
The sting of yesterday

"New Pigs On The Block" is an electronic music track that fuses hypnotic synthesizers, pulsating melodies, and intense rhythms to create an unforgettable rare party-like atmosphere.

Generally, my method for naming purely electronic and instrumental songs is as follows: once I have finished the creation/production process of a song, I pause my mind for a few seconds, and whatever idea, name, or anything that comes to mind first will be the title of the track (and consequently, the theme of the artwork).

I enjoy creating music and digital art equally, and in this case, since the artwork is dual, it's double enjoyment!!! For this track, whoever finds "The Golden Egg" will discover who the second pig is.

"Everything is Fine" is a captivating downtempo electronic song that radiates a sense of serenity and tranquility. From the first chords, you are immersed in a world of soothing sounds and enveloping atmospheres.

The song begins with a soft and ethereal melody that delicately floats over subtle layers of electronic textures. The slow and steady rhythm envelops you, inviting you to disconnect and immerse yourself in a state of introspection. As the song progresses, electronic elements intertwine gracefully, creating an ethereal and mysterious atmosphere.

The vocals glide gently above the music, conveying a sense of calm and acceptance. The lyrics, though minimalist, evoke a feeling of inner peace and remind us that despite the challenges we face, everything will be fine. Each word is whispered tenderly and seamlessly blends with the instrumentation, creating a hypnotic and comforting listening experience.

Over time, the song unfolds with additional layers of subtle electronic sounds and understated sound effects. Underlying rhythms evolve slowly, adding a sense of progression and depth to the composition. As the climax approaches, the song reaches its peak, flooding you with a sense of release and euphoria.

"Everything is Fine" is a song that transports you to a state of inner peace and invites you to savor the present moment. It's a sonic journey that envelops you in a downtempo electronic experience where you can escape from stress and find calm amidst the chaos.

MINI-ESSAY: 

The social decay; how smartphones create a disconnection between us humans.  

Finally I had time this summer to record some new music which I gave the name 'the social disconnection'. You might ask yourselves; is this guy in social decay? No, I am not, but I feel the world is most of the times.

Let me explain. Last year I taught marketing and entrepreneurship on a school for theatre and producer students. I rode a metro three times a week back and forth between my home town and a city near me, and after having binged everything on YouTube (that's the hypocrite part), I started to look around. Looking at people literally glued to their phones the whole ride, including the people on the platform. 

I taught kids whom on average are spending 11 to 14 hours doom scrolling on TikTok and Instagram, having a hard time to connect with friends in real life. 

Over time, and with every ride, I started to observe people. I felt like people around me acted as zombies, completely lost into their own bubble.
Was it a bad thing? I don't know. I was one of them I guess. 

Fall 2023. I'm bringing my stage piano to school during rush hour for a show at school. Taking up one and half seats and no way to use my phone, an older lady sits next to me. If it wasn't for the piano, we probably wouldn't have engaged into a conversation. I exited the metro for the first with a smile on my face. I guess there is still hope for humanity. :-)

As soon as I heard this particular beat, I was immediately inspired and knew exactly what I wanted to convey through my music. The melodies flowed effortlessly, and the concept for a summer-themed song quickly took shape.

This song holds a nostalgic essence, as it speaks to the memories of a past relationship and the emotional ties that linger. The lyrics reflect on how the gentle ocean breeze serves as a poignant reminder of the moments shared with a significant other. It's a heartfelt expression of longing and reflection, capturing the bittersweet essence of reminiscing about a lost love.

With its warm melodies and evocative lyrics, this song is a tribute to the summer season and the emotions that it stirs within us. It's a musical journey that invites listeners to immerse themselves in the nostalgia and emotion of a bygone romance, making it a perfect soundtrack for those summer moments of reflection and introspection.

Hope you guys love it!

Bruenor Frostbeard
Mountain of Gods (Vol 1)

The four strangers, now having faced danger together, decided it was time to share with each other their stories. Eager to share his tale was Bruenor Frostbeard, the dwarven paladin. Bruenor was young member of dwarven clan famed for its smithing and craftsmanship. Alas a terrible act wiped his entire clan out. Who did this, how did they do it, why did they do it? Any memory that could answers these questions eludes Bruenor. And so he swore an Oath of Vengeance and travels the land looking for answers. Called to hammer and anvil, every time he works a new piece, whispers enter his mind. A message from his god or perhaps the spirits of his clan. He will do whatever it takes to find out.

The piano solo piece 'Farewell' emerged from an idea that
lingered in my mind for several years. 
During this time, I experimented with it, exploring different
variations until, finally, in 2021, the composition took its
definitive form.
Only the original motif remained, serving as the heart of
the completed piece.

The title of this piece came to mind after reflecting on its
completion. 
While a 'farewell' often evokes feelings of sadness or melancholy, 
there are also moments of reminiscence about the beautiful times
shared, leading to brief glimpses of brighter moods. 
Ultimately, parting is inevitable, and the music in this piece aims to
reflect this emotional journey.

The cover art depicts the bark of a tree, symbolising a comforting
blanket that shields us when we feel vulnerable, as we yearn for
the strength of the tree itself.

The Golden Egg is the 'natural' version of the cover art.

Description:
As a software engineer (IRL) the concept of /dev/null was always interesting to me. A virtual blackhole you could send anything to where whatever data was sent to it ceased to exist. Earlier in life I had always wished there was an equivalent where we could send our past failings, hurt and betrayals to a /dev/null to have them disappear from us forever. Only if we could “control” the hurt that happens in our lives.

Fortunately, we have been given something similar…forgiveness. Forgiveness for ourselves and others in Christ where we can lay everything at His feet and walk away renewed. 

Let’s talk production. I wanted to create something rough and raw but still show a level of refinement. The breakbeat is a jungle break that was slowed down and chopped up to give various rhythmic feels. The simple bass is provided by a Neutron bass synthesizer with a single oscillator with the LFO rate at minimum to sustain. Diva for pads. The detuned French horn during the Chorus is courtesy of the Dawesome KULT put through distortion. The mid-tone bells during the bridge were also put through tape distortion. The guitar was played live with a Fender Strat captured through a mic’d Fender Blues Deluxe using a modified rotary from Eventide’s H90 effects pedal. The guitar tuning was in drop-D. The mic used was a BeyerDynamic M88 into a Neve1272 followed by an 1176 compressor.
 
Produced, mixed and mastered by agablis.

"The Sun Never Sets" is a call to increase your faith and remain triumphant. It is the title track for my upcoming album, "The Sun Never Sets - Start From The Sky Vol. 1" 

The reason it gets dark at night isn't because the sun gets dark but because of the Earth's movement on its axis. I find this to be a great analogy to life. When we face challenges and tough times, there is always a bright side to look on, a positive perspective to behold. 

There is a light inside of us that is always shining and even when things look bleak we can always tap into the resilient part of us. We can adopt a growth mindset, knowing that we have a constant source of inspiration which encourages us to see challenges as training, as a means to elevation, to learning, to improving and overcoming.

I have been away from social media and web3 for almost a year and this is my first inscription on the blockchain since then. My enthusiasm for blockchain technology has only increased and I never stopped working on music. It was music that provided the healthy outlet for me to traverse the past year.

In a nutshell, I met in two car accidents which unleashed a sequence of events that forced me to take some time away. My living situation also became quite unstable. Things are improving, especially because i've decided to follow through on my plan no matter what. 

I am still trying to secure a place of my own and I am confident this will happen. Currently, I'm working out of a co-working space, which I am super grateful to have because it allows to do my favourite thing: be creative, work on my music, my writing, my education, my content.

I literally just woke up at the co-working office and got straight to work, completing my first SoundXYZ drop and first Music NFT drop, of the year. I am continually making music and also embarking on some additional endeavors namely: a Newsletter, a Youtube series and podcast based on my journaling called "I&I: Journals of a SkyStarter", also a new Poetry/Freestyle series called "The Floetic Bar" that will have a blockchain component, here on SoundXYZ.

I want to be more and do more and I am being more and doing more. I aim to exercise my talents and gifts to their fullest. I believe one gift that we are meant to give to others is the gift God gave us. It is my duty to utilize my gifts. 

Thank You for your support and for listening. I really don't want to do too much talking and want to let my actions speak. I want to let my work, speak.

"This story begins a long time ago when I was still a child. At that moment, I didn't know, but it captivated me, engaged me in various ways. Everywhere I went, she was there, and I couldn't resist. Later, in my adolescence, she stirred my emotions at parties, in bars, in the gatherings in the backyard of my grandmother's house, until I realized it was time to embrace it, and I joined a 'Escola de Samba' when I was just 14 years old. I was completely captivated and enchanted by music, but especially by the genre of samba and its close relatives, choro, and pagode. Some time later, I had an intense love affair with someone, and this relationship made me reminisce about my history with music, with samba, and from there, I composed "Mina Firmeza" because, after all, everyone wants to samba."

The song features an artist deeply immersed in samba. Libertu, who honed his samba skills in samba circles, carnival associations, and neighborhood pagode and choro groups, presents a song that moves between different urban samba styles. It touches on Samba-gafieira, flirts with Samba-maxixado, showcases percussion rooted in Samba-de-curimba, and culminates in a Samba-enredo with hints of improvisation on the Rhodes keyboard that brings a Samba-jazz atmosphere to the music. The lyrics celebrate the empowered woman who, in her strength to "handle all her affairs," so diverse within the experiences of a brown-skinned woman, a teacher, a single mother, and an activist, is multifaceted in her interests and social circles. She is socially recognized, admired, and desired.

__________________________________________________________________________________________


"Essa história começa há tempos atrás, quando eu ainda era criança. Naquele momento eu não sabia, mas ela me cativou, me envolveu de várias formas. Em tudo quanto é lugar que eu ia ela estava, eu não resisti. Depois, na adolescência ela mexeu comigo nas festas, nos bares, nas rodas no fundo do quintal da casa da minha avó, até que eu percebi que era hora de assumir e fui tocar numa escola de samba e eu tinha só 14 anos. Eu estava completamente refém e encantado pela música, mas especialmente pelo gênero samba e por seus parentes próximos, o chorinho e o pagode. Tempos mais tarde eu vivi uma relação de amor intenso com uma pessoa e essa relação me fez recordar muito da minha história com a música, com o samba e daí eu compus Mina Firmeza, porque afinal de contas, todo mundo quer sambar."

A canção  apresenta um artista com os dois pés no samba. Libertu, que se formou sambista nas rodas de samba, grêmios carnavalescos e grupos de pagode e de choro de bairro, apresenta uma canção que transita entre diferentes sotaques do samba urbano. Passa pelo Samba-gafieira, flerta com o Samba-maxixado, mostra uma percussão que explora a raiz do Samba-de-curimba e chega num Samba-enredo com pitadas de improvisação no rodhes que traz uma atmosfera Samba-jazz para a música. A letra exalta a mulher empoderada, que na força de "fazer todos seus corres", tão diversos dentro da vivência de uma mulher parda, professora, mãe-solo e militante,  plural em seus interesses e ambientes que circula, é socialmente reconhecida, admirada e desejada.

Description:
‘Gold in Autumn’ is a study in contradictions: It’s simple and delicate, yet textured and lush. It’s an instrumental track, yet tastefully-arranged vocal samples add humanity. It’s electronic and computer-y, yet graceful piano and a guitar-driven emotional release lead the way in its final build and climax. Despite these contradictions — or, more likely, because of them — “Gold in Autumn” is cohesive and impactful, equal parts art piece and feel good, dance-in-your-bedroom banger.

For Carter, finishing the track did not come without its challenges and roadblocks. The intro sat as an unfinished draft for months, until he realised he always got a “strong sense of excitement” from that snippet. “When I eventually approached expanding upon the intro, I wanted to maintain that feeling throughout the whole song. I quickly smashed through writing most of the track until it came to the final chorus. I must’ve made at least 3-4 different versions of this section - some felt awesome but most just weren’t right for the song,” explains Carter. “Inspiration usually comes from the process of creating as opposed to before I begin creating.”

Description: Introducing 'Beta Tauri,' the latest track from my Landscape Collection. This piece continues the journey we began with my last release, adding another layer to the musical landscape I've been exploring.

King Baw, originally from Tolyatti and living in Israel, presents his new melody, which tells the story of a meeting with a unique woman who turns his fate around. Each line of this work reflects his deep feelings and amazing experiences. King Baw describes how his hands were entangled in her beautiful locks and her scent permeated every corner of his home after her sad departure. He also notes that she changed the shade of her locks, symbolizing the change in their bond. King Bow's song is a story of passion, loss and self-discovery, making his music truly unique and moving. Listeners will be able to feel and share his emotional state after hearing this deeply touching song.

Do you love discovering new music that truly moves you? We've got a brand new melancholic electronic/hip hop release that you need to hear.

Introducing "The Way" - a hauntingly beautiful track dedicated to the passing of loved ones. This experimental song seamlessly blends electronic and hip hop elements into a powerful listening experience.

From its stripped down beats to its raw, evocative vocals, "The Way" will stir your soul. This is music that connects on a deep emotional level.

We especially recommend this song if you're a fan of melancholic electronic or experimental hip hop. The production quality is superb - you can tell no expense was spared in crafting this moving work of art.

This is music made to be felt. We hope it provides comfort and catharsis during difficult times. Thank you for supporting this special independent release.

"Neon Echoes in Italian Rain" was a single I produced entirely with very few resources during a backpacking tour around Africa and Europe. This song was composed right after a Paul Kalkbrenner concert in Italy. It was a summer and rainy day, but the folks didn't care about it and danced through the night. That inspired me so much I had to do my own version from that gig. An electronic music, composed with few tools. An acoustic guitar, my headphones and a laptop. Only those were used. The headphones were plugged into the mic spot of the laptop and I attached them to the guitar and recorded it. The rest was composed using an ordinary audio workstation in my early days of music production. Very intuitive and passionate about this creation. First time going online after twelve years. The possibility of submitting this exclusively through sound.xyz platform and We Love The Art contest is what makes this piece a genuine form of art. An original music work, produced with a lack of resources, now held by vanguard technology providers. That is what I love about Art.

Step into the "Love Elevator," an electrifying new track from the innovative producer G2, featuring the soulful voice of Chip Days from The Senate. This musical journey is a blend of vibrant beats and heartfelt melodies, elevating the listener through layers of rhythmic ecstasy and emotional depth. Each note and lyric in "Love Elevator" is crafted to resonate with the soul, making it more than just a song – it's an experience.

Immerse yourself in the rich tapestry of sound, where Drew Scott’s masterful keyboard skills intertwine with Randy Razz’s soul-stirring guitar riffs, creating an auditory landscape that is both complex and captivating. The track comes together in a symphony of sound, expertly mixed and mastered by Stan Green and J. Eldon, weaving a sonic masterpiece that transcends genres.

As a pioneer in the music NFT space, G2 brings a fresh perspective, infusing blockchain technology with artistic creativity. This NFT is not just a piece of music; it's a digital asset that represents the intersection of cutting-edge tech and timeless artistry. // Station 5 // Biography

Imagine a universe where we are connected by shimmering beams of light, everyone to everyone. One quirk about this universe is that the beams send emotions between us, one million per minute per pair, clearly and effortlessly. Joy is instantly contagious. A hurtful thought toward another is understood with compassion, seen alongside the place of sadness where it arose. Every feeling triggers infinite empathy, therefore boundless acceptance. (The beams send only the stuff of our souls, not our thoughts — so we still have privacy, interesting conversation, and the ability to prank each other silly.)

Now imagine we already live in this universe except, long ago, we somehow forgot where the beams disappeared off to. But we’ve always kept music with us, because it’s our best way to speak in the old way.

+

Taiwan-born & reared on-the-go between Taipei and the American Southwest, Eric Pan (a.k.a. pandelic) found his musical footing via a jazz mentorship with Ray Brown at the University of California. These studies propelled him onto stages with Jeff Hamilton and Roy Hargrove, plus over a decade’s tenure as New York City pianist & composer. Pan’s compositions and improvisations reveal a relentless pursuit of simplicity, craft, and universality.

The song that accompanies this image is about the speculation that Sergey Nazarov, the co-founder of Chainlink, might be Satoshi Nakamoto, the mysterious creator of Bitcoin. The song explores the various clues and evidence that some people have used to support this theory, such as the fact that Nazarov registered the domain smartcontract.com six days before the Bitcoin white paper was published.

The song also expresses the curiosity and fascination that many people in the crypto space have with the identity of Satoshi Nakamoto, who has remained anonymous and silent since 2010. The song wonders if Nazarov is the one who started the crypto revolution and the master plan behind it, and if he is hiding his true identity behind his work with Chainlink, a decentralized oracle network that connects smart contracts to real-world data. The song ends with a plea for Nazarov to give a sign or a hint that he is Satoshi Nakamoto, or to reveal the truth once and for all.

I wrote this song while crying and feeling some of the deepest emotions I've ever felt. The whole song came out in under 2 hours, with just me and the piano. Long story short, it is about loving someone else so much that you forget to love yourself. 

I am someone who loves deeply, who feels deeply. When I fall in love, I give everything I have to the other person, and I forget to nurture myself, to love myself fully. I give so much that I quite literally have nothing left to give to myself. If anyone hears this song and can relate, I hope you can be reminded to love yourself fully. By doing that, you will be more capable of loving those around you properly.

Description:
This is "Les Cerisiers en Fleurs" an album by Maeki Maii. The opening track of his heartfelt album, is now available on sound.xyz under the CollabHaven Records label. This album, originally released on August 3, 2023, is a masterful blend of hip-hop and rap, characterized by its peaceful and emotive melodies. The project is especially significant as it aims to raise funds for Maeki Maii's sick child, imbuing each song with profound personal meaning.

This first track, "Les Cerisiers en Fleurs", sets the tone for the album with its serene vibe and is later gonna be followed by the bonus version by John Volatyl. Other tracks like "Accattone" featuring Italo IDL (prod. Konstruk and Gaty) and "Shiryu" (prod. Uezurii) will be released weekly, each adding a new layer to this musical journey.

"Les Cerisiers en Fleurs" is not just a collection of songs; it is a narrative of resilience, hope, and dedication, echoing Maeki Maii's commitment to his family and his craft. Each weekly release on sound.xyz is a step further in this deeply personal story, inviting listeners to be part of a cause that transcends music.

Perfect Day is not just a song but a soulful reflection encapsulating the journey and essence of my life. Born from a desire to share personal insights and unveil the core of my identity, the song delves into the fabric of my experiences and the pursuit of a perfect day. In a musical landscape constantly evolving, I will boldly step forward and present my debut release PerfectDay. 

The melody and lyrics intertwine to weave a narrative of self-discovery and aspiration, inviting you the listeners to resonate with the emotions and stories embedded in the composition. This inaugural piece is not merely a musical endeavor; it's a heartfelt invitation to connect, and I earnestly seek your invaluable feedback, believing in the power of shared experiences. With a wish for peace, love, and light, I open a door to my world through the harmonies of Perfect Day.

A journey through space and time, where every ray of light witnesses the death and birth of new planets and stars. 

Echoes of the distant past, revealing the secrets of our future.

Deep house is a subgenre of electronic dance music known for its smooth, mellow, and atmospheric sound. Characterized by slower tempos, deep basslines, and soulful vocals, it often incorporates elements of jazz, funk, and soul. The genre creates a laid-back and immersive experience, with its emphasis on rich melodies, intricate rhythms, and a generally relaxed vibe.

"Parasite" tells the story of a toxic partnership Emily had with a producer she used to work with. She alludes to how he manipulated and gaslit her for two years, but has now embraced the attitude that if he ever tries to fuck with her again, she’ll do whatever she has to do to get rid him from her life. He sucked the joy and vitality she had for her career and life and replaced it with fear and anxiety. He was a narcissist and a parasite.

Emily brought the initial idea to rehearsal one day (then called "Criminal") that had a riff and a vibe to it. Over the course of 6 months, it became known as "Parasite" and morphed into what it is now a genre-bending journey of ambient melodies, hard rock, and soul. "Parasite" has become one of our favorite songs to perform live, by far.

Introducing the DEBUT single 'Run Baby Run' by Johnny Woog and CODA MACC. 'Run Baby Run' is a track deeply rooted in our profound mission to inspire individuals to confront their fears and take action towards their dreams. 

'Run Baby Run' is about moving head first towards your fears, rather than attempting and ultimately failing to run from them. The fears that we face internally are often the things that we should put action towards. We hope that this track inspires others to realize that moving towards their fears is, in fact, the way. 

CODA MACC (Community of Developing Art, Music, and Conscious Collective) was created by two life long friends that have been playing and writing music together for most of their lives. Johnny and David are both classically trained musicians that started a band in high school. That band had success in their genre and was active for 7 years. From there David went on to receive a PhD in Music and is now a symphony conductor and Music Professor. Johnny took a different path into finance and the crypto industry but found that his life lacked fulfillment during the pandemic. It was during this pivotal moment that he resolved to learn music production and made a call to David explaining that he wanted to write music together again. David responded "Johnny, I've played music with a lot of different people over the years, but I've been waiting and hoping for this call."

CODA MACC's long term mission is to build a community of creatives across multiple art forms that help make the world a better place through their respective art forms and give back to youth music and mental health programs. In the long term, we aim to partner with music and mental health programs to foster positive life experiences for youth in underprivileged areas. 

This track is our first release together in over a decade and stands as a testament to our rekindled creative partnership. We are so thrilled to bring it to the sound.xyz community first! 

This track was born in a basement in Nebraska. No one involved with the song actually currently lives in Nebraska. 

Performed and produced by Johnny Woog
Written by Johnny Woog and David Galant of CODA MACC

Bored Ape Richard Vagner and I recorded this piece** in a live session at his LA home. It's a nod to the special moment we're currently in as early adopters/experimenters in the Audio NFT and Metaverse performance space.

Although we work in different genres (I'm a classically trained vocalist in 14th century Sufi tradition of North India, and Richard is a virtuoso violinist rooted in the Western tradition), we found common inspiration upon meeting in person after having known each other awhile on the Clubhouse app.

I visited Richard at his LA home during my first visit from NYC, an eventful trip that convinced me to relocate to LA. The impromptu jam and recording/mixing of Sufi vocals, Ukulele, Violin, and Electronic soundscapes in the hours that followed is a testament to the creative power of this time we're in, particularly as the rest of the world catches on (VISA bought a CryptoPunk just a few days ago, which makes us laugh because (a) VISA had to  become a single digital wallet, but it also makes us think because (b) we have to be careful not to let centralized institutions steal our JPEGS! NFTs are a paradigm shift and this is just the beginning.

The album art is a derivative of Richard's Bored Ape trained via AI at Playform.IO using my Alien Boy as visual inspiration.

This is a song I wrote after going through a really lonely point in my life and being surrounded by the wrong people in LA. It often felt like none of my friends really knew me and I always felt like an outsider. Luckily, my luck has changed in that aspect and I have the best BFF, boyfriend, and pup in the world.

This song was one of those instances where I had the idea for the skeleton of the song for so long, and just hadn't sat down to properly try recording it. I'd been playing so many of the chord voicings when I wasn't recording, just practicing, just feeling out how some of them fit together - or didn't fit as well. I'd spent months figuring out some of those voicings in an alternate tuning on guitar, because it sounded and felt better than playing in standard tuning at the time. I could reach different combinations of notes that I couldn't in a regular tuning. Certain notes were closer together, or further apart, and it changes your playing in ways you can't be certain of until you spend some time experimenting with it. 

So many of those things wouldn't have been properly jotted down if I'd let them remain as nebulous ideas that I only played with while practicing. It's so easy to be like "Ahhhh is this good? Does this suck? Should I record this?" when really - sitting down and recording anything is better than not. Even if it sucks, you wouldn't have spent hours thinking in your head how cool it will be - only to be disappointed when you realize it doesn't work the same way it did in your head. And sometimes something you think isn't special ends up growing into something beyond what you could imagine. It just seems important to stay open, and record everything you can within reason. You never know what might work.

Originally recorded and released in 1996, Concept 1’s monthly releases documented a year of sonic experimentation. Each month I would record as much music as possible with a strict and limited selection of technology.  Gone were the typical “Hawtin” combination of TR808, TR909 and TB303’s which had driven the techno tracks I had become known for under my F.U.S.E. and Plastikman aliases, replaced by a striped down selection centered around three Doepfer MAQ 16/3 sequencers and 5 panels of Serge modular racks. This year-long experiment ended up being the beginning of a new minimalistic phase and set the foundation for the Plastikman Consumed album.

This unreleased exploratory groove, "96:11 00:00”, was written on November 19, 1996 and was a testing ground for the shuffled 909 programming that appears on the released Concept 1 "96:11 21:00" track, as well as featuring the feedback textures that appeared on the final Concept 1 release "96:12 24:00”.

As the original Concept 1 release was limited to a specific number of physical releases, I thought that it would be an appropriate continuation of its concept to release this track as an edition of 1 NFT, using it as another exploratory move in this developing eco-system.

Lastly I want to extend gratitude to  @jzs (Jeremy Stern) and the rest of the Catalog Team for going above and beyond to help ensure my legacy/story could exist in it's intended chronical long form existence.

Backstory:

Last album released rapping as Dutchmassive was released in 2007 on Rawkus Records.

Social media and life kind of killed the magic of words for me. I see too many thoughts daily, So I shifted my creative energy into expression without words. beats, keys, sample manipulation, experimenting with creating new worlds from nothing, or evolving a sample into the unrecognizable just music in general, just speaking without using words.

Hip Hop stopped inspiring or surprising me, with minimal exceptions. The fun aspect of being an emcee or making music kind of fell out of style. where up until about 2011, it was everywhere, so accessible. such a vibe, easy to bounce that creative energy back into the world.

but I still am an emcee, passionate, over talkative, TMI, super expressive human IRL.

but losing chronologic timelines on social media (yep I'm going there again) really changed how humans communicate online. Expansive conversations don't happen by design, everything is fragmented, and anything long form is taboo, especially using your words to communicate on these apps. you see a paragraph, you think rant. Crazy right? I'm the crazy one? nah this new fragmented, A.I. manipulated timeline we all living in doesn't want nor allow for expansive dialog to happen in real time anymore. Everyone's on a soap box, trapped, reacting, and dunking basically always in offense or defense mode. hahaha I grew tired of battle rap in the early 2000's, now soccer moms, senators and the whole worlds has battle rap energy haha.

You think this discouraged me, nah. I let that lil light shine in private haha, I missed when hip-hop was fun, so I had fun with hip-hop in private, got all my venting out and recorded it every time. Freestyling and flipping samples is all do, while rebelling publicly, hoarding insane amounts of beats, and albums, I got super addicted to recording everything in real time.. The rawest and truest form of expression.... having fun, being introspective on autopilot.

Absolute freedom.

but this stuff was never intended to be heard by anyone. DailyRambles is me loading up a batch of beats on the Tascam DR-05 that I haven't listened to yet, and blindly freestyling and seeing which ones move me enough to make me wanna sit and write, and having fun with the ones that don't fit my voice or style and have fun trying to make it work.

I had zero intentions to make any of these freestyles public,  but due to severe health complications, I might not always be here and even if I am able to somehow course correct by pure miracle and insane amounts of debt,  it would alter my ability to speak the same and/or articulate the way I do now. 

There may never be another well thought out, written and recorded "Dutchmassive" album in the future. But there is 6 years worth of "DailyRambles" right now.
I'm reluctant about even dropping this as Dutchmassive, even though polls on all "social media" unanimously chose it over the alias "Reluctant Clap"

I won't always be here. I'd rather this silly introspective gibberish be out in the world, then locked away on my hard drive.

Reluctantly,  INCOMING!

Waiting on Genius had been floating around Ché's head for years. Half written but always present, Waiting on Genius is the soundtrack of a long and laboured musical journey. Through years of waitressing jobs and side hustles, it was as much of an outcry as it was a confession of worries and self doubt.

It took a pandemic to revisit it. Ché found that all of the angst that had surrounded the song for years, was now long gone. Finally able to separate herself from the character in the song, Ché was able to tell the story of a young girl waiting in the wings, waiting on a moment of genius.

With additions from her musical peers Morgan Agren (Mats/Morgan, Frank Zappa), Scott Reeder (Kyuss) and Diego Tejeida (Haken), all geniuses in their own right, she finally found the inspiration to move forward and put to bed the worries and self doubt. 

This is a song for anyone who has ever crossed this threshold. Who has taken the time to craft something, even in the face of their own neuroses. All the while holding onto the hope of a finish line.

Welcome to the Drifter Series. Every Monday I’ll be packing up my backpack with a laptop, a pair of headphones, and a disposable camera and hitting the road to write and record a unique piece of music. Each piece of this series - from the recording and making of the beat - to the pictures and creative direction - are all conceptualized and created in the same day.

For this song I had a hard time getting started for the day. I was lacking inspiration and spent a lot of time debating where I should go. For whatever reason I went through my old photos and found a picture from August of 2018 where I was standing at sunset at an overlook at Griffith Park. At the time I was a junior in college and I remember so vividly the overwhelming draw I had to figure out a way to move to Los Angeles one day. I put my things together and drove to that same spot.

Backstory:

Created in my Los Angeles apartment in Fall of 2013. This track began the same hour Addison Chase (of Cosmic Compositions) reached out to me to be included in their next Avant Garde Series for Sun Ra.  After telling me my track "Astral Traveling" for **Cosmic Compositions Avant Garde Series Vol.1 [Pharoah Sanders]** was one of his personal favorite tracks as well as one the fan favorites, I was pretty inspired to jump into this flip without a moment's delay.

**Reference**

Avant Garde Series Vol.1 [Pharoah Sanders] Digital / Vinyl Release:
https://cosmic-compositions.bandcamp.com/album/cosmic-compositions-avant-garde-series-vol-1-pharoah-sanders

"Astral Travl'n" would later be featured on the 120 minute cassette "Chill Gawd Chill" 
https://dutchmassive.bandcamp.com/album/chill-gawd-chill

Both of these Artists we were paying tribute to were some of my biggest inspirations musically over the years.  Hearing their music always made me feel like my creative intuition to embrace the abstract and create contrasts between chaotic moments and peaceful/harmonious moments either  through sudden unpredictable shifts that would feel jarring to most people or through slow builds that tell a story that may or may not have a resolve, This was something I always got pushback on from friends but was something I myself was proud of.  Methods both Sun Ra & Pharoah Sanders both implemented often. So when the chance was presented to pay official tribute to & honor these legends, I made absolutely sure I came with my A game and made tracks at least I could be proud of.

"Spring Chops In The Fall '' was created in Ableton Live, but it was also the 1st song I used the Original SP404 compression and isolation on.  I really wanted to flex the art of micro-chopping and show off my ability to turn entire songs into a instrument, rather than cherry picking the obvious part(s) most people would usually gravitate towards. So I flipped my chosen track multiple different ways while still finding a way to sequence all the change ups in a way that told a cohesive sonic story.  Honor A Legend, Create A Journey. This remains one of my personal favorite tracks to date. 

The song also landed on the B-side of my album "The Uproot"

https://dutchmassive.bandcamp.com/album/the-uproot

Which will hopefully one day see a physical release, even if in the Demo form in currently exists in.  =)

Welcome to installment number four of the Drifter Series - where I pack up my backpack with my laptop, headphones, and a disposable camera and see where the day takes me.

This is a special song. 

When I woke up to make this song, I had a weird inkling to go to my first apartment in LA; my friends still live there and I thought it would be a cool thing to come say hi and make a beat on the roof.

What I didn’t realize is that one year ago - almost to the day - I moved to Los Angeles to pursue doing music full time. Making music and living here has been a dream of mine since I was a 16 year-old kid producing rap beats on my barely-functioning laptop. I’ve never really taken a moment to appreciate that, and this song felt like that moment to me. I put myself in the shoes of my teenage self and imagined what words of encouragement I could offer if I could go back in time. In writing the song I also realized that if you really love what you do, it will always be a dream.

Description:
Desiderium is a piece I began composing by accident. I had just inherited a painting by Gino Hollander, a painting that I had grown up with and loved dearly. I placed this painting in front of me at my studio, and before I could think, a series of soft eighth notes escaped my fingers. I spent the following 3 months turning that initial idea into the piece it is today. This is my genesis NFT as well as my first true example of art music, as the majority of my compositions have only danced around the idea. This concept of art music, and its origin within the concept of ekphrasis, is one that I’ve been gripped by... I personally find nothing more rewarding then to seek out meaning within the story, and transliterate that into music. So, this piece, Desiderium, after Gino Hollander’s 1994 ‘Untitled’, is the story that I hear. I hope it touches you.

Special thanks to Elliot Cole [elliotcole.eth], for the guidance within this burgeoning space and for making my genesis drop on Catalog a reality, as well as Siri Hollander, for granting permission to use images of her late father’s work.

Perspective was written during the same season as my last EP, Breathing Tides. After a long, difficult year, I wanted to try and process everything through a collection of recordings. What came out was an hour or so of very quiet, peaceful ambient music; rather than express the anxiety and depression that I felt so strongly during 2020, I feel like these songs expressed some hopeful optimism. A truly refreshing feeling.

I wanted to keep the official release short (it's only three songs), knowing that I had a LP coming out later in the year. This left me with several unreleased tracks.
